# Velora Frontend: Completed Goals (Archive)

Archive of finished work split out of [`goals.md`](./goals.md) to keep the active roadmap
short. Same section numbers as `goals.md`, for cross-reference. This is a historical record,
don't edit past entries except to fix a factual error; append newly-finished items here
(compacted) when they get checked off in `goals.md`.

The third file is [`docs/goalsDetails/`](./docs/goalsDetails/): long-form detail for items that are still
**open**. When such an item ships, fold its detail sheet into this archive and delete it there.
Full rules in `CLAUDE.md` → "Roadmap files".

Last archived: 2026-07-19.

---

## 1. Playback & Audio Engine
- **Normalization on by default, no blind boosts (2026-10-05).** `loudnessNormalization` defaults on for new installs (no migration, a stored `false` stays). `maxBoostForPeak` allows no boost without a known peak, so the live-measured and session-cached paths only cut: nothing downstream limits the output, and the old +6 dB blind boost could clip a quiet, dynamic master. ReplayGain with a peak still boosts up to its headroom. Compressor stays off by default (it changes the music's dynamics, a situational tool). Check: `tests/services/loudness.test.ts`.
- **Louder normalization target (2026-10-05).** Default -22 (broadcast quiet) became -14, the streaming level, and the slider now reaches -6 instead of -9. Audio settings v3 moves a stored -22 to -14; any other value was a choice and stays. The description says higher is louder. The blind boost was removed the same day (entry above). Check: `tests/services/customEq.test.ts`.
- **Normalization uses ReplayGain (2026-10-04).** `Track.replayGain` (track gain + peak) comes from OpenSubsonic `replayGain`, Jellyfin `NormalizationGain`, local tags (`trackGain`/`trackPeak` columns, `METADATA_VERSION` 4 rescans) and the Velora backend (tagged, else measured with ffmpeg). The engine applies it before the first sample, the peak capping the boost (`maxBoostForPeak`). The live fallback is now K-weighted with per-channel meters over the whole signal, starts at the previous track's cut (never its boost) instead of unity, and remembers a finished measurement (2 minutes, not radio) for the session. Album mode was dropped on purpose: one toggle, track gain only. Check: `tests/services/loudness.test.ts`.
- **Android no longer takes the audio back (2026-10-03).** When another app (YouTube) took the audio, the WebView paused the slot and the recovery path restarted it, pausing the other app. On Android an OS pause of a loaded, unfinished slot is now sent as a `pause` command, from the slot's `pause` event and the recovery tick alike (`OS_PAUSE_IS_FINAL` in `audioEngine.ts`), and a resume Android makes itself (after a call) is sent as `play` so the UI follows, never the engine's own start (`starting`). Check: `tests/services/audioOsPause.test.ts`.
- **A paused phone no longer starts by itself (2026-10-03).** Three paths did it, all fixed in `audioEngine.ts`. (1) The OS-pause sync above was Android-app only, so in a phone browser the 5s progress tick kept calling `play()` on the paused slot (its 4s backoff window reset between ticks); the sync now runs everywhere and recovery only resumes a suspended AudioContext. (2) The WebView restarts the slot once the other app lets go of the audio; that was synced as `play`, now it is paused again. (3) The real trigger with the desktop app open: the playback state is shared, so a play on the PC (Electron registers the Windows play/pause key as a global `toggle`, which Bluetooth headsets send too) started the hidden phone, which Android won't let back into the foreground, so it stuttered over TikTok until its service died. A hidden device whose state turns paused to playing now stays silent (`heldOff`), without pausing the device that is playing, until a press on its own media controls (`handleMediaAction`) or opening the app; the notification shows paused meanwhile. Electron pins visibility to visible, so the desktop is unaffected. Check: `tests/services/audioOsPause.test.ts`.
- **Hold-to-preview in the palette, search dropdown, Spotlight and artist header (2026-10-02).** Palette and search-dropdown result rows preview through the shared `HoldCover` (`primitives/holdPreview/`, which the nav rows now use too); the Spotlight artwork previews its track or a random song of its artist; the artist header previews the artist from an `artistHeroHold` layer under its content; the content lets presses through to it everywhere but its controls. `useHoldPreview` reads `holdToPreview` itself, so call sites only pass a source.
- **Hold-to-preview in the queue and the nav (2026-10-02).** Queue rows pass `preview`, the now-playing row stays out. Nav rows (playlists, favorites, pinned artists and albums) draw their own cover through `NavRowCover`, which binds `useHoldPreview` and plays a random song of the row (`utils/cardPreview.ts`); the nav cover CSS targets `.navRowCoverImg` so the hold mark's glyph is left alone. A row's reorder drag starts by hand (`useDragControls`) only past the hold's `MOVE_TOLERANCE` and never under a fired hold, so a previewing row can't be dragged. `useHoldPreview` is generic over its element.
- **Right-click a hold preview to play it (2026-10-01).** While a hold's clip plays, a right-click plays its song through `usePlayTrackNow` (an empty queue seeds all songs at it). `audioEngine.commitHoldPreview` cuts the clip and drops the pending resume, `holdPreview`'s `onReady` now hands over the clip's track, and the right-click's own menu is swallowed once at window level since it fires on press or release by platform.
- **Playback speed (2026-10-01).** `playbackSpeed` (Settings → Playback, 0.5x to 2x, pitch kept) multiplies the special mode's rate, which alone still shifts pitch; radio stays at 1x. Quick access: an opt-in speed button (`player.speedButton`, off by default, in the Player buttons picker) in the player bar and the BigMusic utility cluster (submenu in the mobile more-menu) that opens a stepped slider over the presets, numbers under each notch and the fill growing out of 1x, unbound `speedUp`/`speedDown`/`speedReset` keybinds and palette rows. Two things a free rate broke: the 1x position extrapolation in the controllers and backend outran the 3s re-seek threshold at 2x (progress now reports every `progressIntervalMs(rate)`), and the crossfade trigger compared media time to a wall-time fade (now scaled by the rate). Also fixed: slowed/nightcore reset to 1x on every track change, since a src load resets `playbackRate`; the engine sets `defaultPlaybackRate` too.
  - ↳ files: `audioEngine.ts`, `utils/speedMenu.ts`, `primitives/speedButton/`, `player.tsx`, `bigMusic/useUtilities.ts` + `utilityButtons.tsx`, `keybindActions.ts`, `useKeybindDispatch.ts`, `commandPalette.tsx`, `userDataScopes.ts`, `tests/services/playbackSpeed.test.ts`, all 9 locales
- **Drop a song on the player to play it (2026-10-01).** The desktop player bar is a `useTrackDropTarget` like the nav and the queue: a dropped song plays now through `usePlayTrackNow` (inserted after the current one, the rest of the queue kept; an empty queue seeds all songs at it), and the song already playing is refused. The surface restates the drop fill in `player.css`, since `.uiContentContainer`'s `background` shorthand resets it.
- **Faster hold previews (2026-10-01).** The clip starts loading 120ms into a press (`useLongPress` `onPress` + `audioEngine.armPreview`/`disarmPreview`), so the 250ms hold only starts it; a tap or a scroll start loads nothing. On a server reporting the OpenSubsonic `transcodeOffset` extension (probed in `SubsonicProvider.connect`, new `streamTimeOffset` capability) a transcoded clip is requested with `timeOffset`, so the server starts at the anchor instead of transcoding up to it. Velora too since backend 2026-10-01: `VeloraProvider` reads `features.streamTimeOffset` from `GET /api/v1/server` after connect/resume (a missing key or failed fetch means off).
- **Preview quality (2026-10-01).** `previewQuality` (Display → General, under Hold to preview, default `low`) picks the stream tier for hold-to-preview clips, so they load fast whatever the main quality is; the games keep `audioQuality`. `preparePreview` and `buildStreamUrl` take the tier as an argument. Travels with the audio export scope.
- **One hold-to-preview setting (2026-10-01).** The row and card toggles were the same feature, so `holdCardToPreview` is gone and `holdToPreview` (Display → General) covers both; an old profile or import holding the card key just ignores it.
- **Hold a card to preview (2026-10-01).** A second setting, on by default (`holdCardToPreview`, Display → General). Holding a card's cover plays the same 15s clip: a song card its own song (Home's recently added/listened, an artist's songs, the playlist grid, search), an album, playlist (Favorites too) or artist card a random song of it (Home, the grids, an artist page, search), through `audioEngine.holdPreview`, which now also takes a lazy source (`utils/cardPreview.ts`) and drops the hold if it is released while the song is still being picked. The row and the card share `primitives/holdPreview/useHoldPreview.tsx` for the gesture, the scroll lock and the loading ring. Smart playlists and radio don't opt in.
- **Hold a cover to preview (2026-10-01).** A setting, on by default (`holdToPreview`, Display → General). Holding a song row's cover for 250ms plays a 15s clip from a random point past the intro, with playback paused under it; letting go fades the clip out over 0.3s and resumes playback half a second later, only if the hold paused it and only after the last of several covers held in a row (the half second is what lets the next cover's hold claim the pause). It reuses the guess games' third `<audio>` slot (`audioEngine.holdPreview`), and the pause and resume are real `sendCommand`s, so a server-authoritative queue sees them. Wired on the shared `Playlist` rows and the jar, not on the playing row, in select mode or in the queue. On touch the hold owns the long-press, so holding the cover previews and holding the rest of the row still opens the menu (`useLongPress` stops the parent's `contextmenu` while pressed, and gained an `onRelease`). While the clip loads the cover shows a dim speaker inside a spinning accent ring, which pops to full waves once the sound starts (`holdPreview`'s `onReady`). The cover is a listen handle only: it never starts a row drag, `SwipeableRow` skips presses inside `[data-no-swipe]`, and a fired hold blocks touch scrolling so nothing pulls the clip away (the non-passive `touchmove` listener is attached up front, since a browser decides whether a touch can be blocked before the hold fires). Known gap: the preview element is not blessed on the first gesture, so iOS Safari may refuse to play it.
- **Normalization measures real playback (2026-09-28).** It used to take five RMS snapshots 1.5 to 2.7s of wall-clock time after the source was set and lock the whole song to them, so a track restored paused, paused in its first seconds or slow to buffer measured silence and was never normalized, a quiet intro earned the full +6 dB for the loud part, and a resume mid-song measured wherever it landed. Now `scheduleNormMeasurement` samples every 300ms only while the slot is playing, not seeking, buffered and the context running, keeps every block, and re-derives the gain from gated loudness (`services/audio/loudness.ts`: -70 LUFS absolute gate, then -10 LU relative, BS.1770 style without K-weighting), so quiet passages drop out once loud ones arrive. Cuts apply from the 5th block, boosts only after ~10s of playback; cuts ride a 0.5s time constant, rises 2s; sampling freezes at 400 blocks (2 min). A target change re-applies from the stored blocks instead of re-measuring. The mean-based estimate reads a few dB below the old peak-of-snapshots one, so at the same target songs come out slightly louder. Covered by `tests/services/loudness.test.ts`.
- **Drawable crossfade curve (2026-09-07).** The crossfade was a seconds slider over one fixed equal-power ramp, so a quick-out / slow-in transition was unreachable. Settings → Playback → Transitions now carries a graph under the duration slider: the outgoing track falling in neutral white, the incoming one rising in the artwork's accent, and over both a dashed line for the level the pair actually holds (`sqrt(out^2 + in^2)`, which is exactly 1 while neither side is bent, since that is what equal power means). Bend a side and the line leaves unity, tints `--color-warning` past 0.3 dB and the caption names the deviation and where it lands ("-3.1 dB dip at 2.6s"), which is the part no crossfade UI usually shows. **Grab either curve anywhere along its length and it is solved through the pointer**, so it is drawn rather than nudged; a dot at 30% / 70% (never the middle, where the two meet at the default) is the affordance, the 44px touch target and the keyboard handle (`role="slider"`, arrows move the curve the way the eye expects, so the reported value is the level under the dot). Double-click a curve or the Reset link to put it back. **The shape is one warp exponent per direction**, `sin(x^(2^bend) * pi/2)` rising and `cos(...)` falling (`utils/fadeCurve.ts`, shared by the engine and the graph): bend 0 is bit-for-bit the ramp that shipped before, so an existing profile is untouched and `loadSettings`' spread gives an old blob the default for free; the family is monotone at every reachable bend, so no setting can produce a fade that turns back up on itself, and it is invertible in closed form, which is what makes drag-anywhere possible. A non-finite bend (a hand-edited user-data import) is read as 0 rather than reaching `setValueCurveAtTime` as a curve of NaN. Stored as two flat numbers in `velora-audio-settings` (`crossfadeCurveIn`/`crossfadeCurveOut`), so export/import needed no change. The engine keeps the two 0..1 progress shapes cached and rebuilds them only when the bend changes (`ensureFadeShapes`), and **`rampGain` is shared, so the play and pause fades ride the same shape by design**. **Live playhead:** `subscribeCrossfade` fires when a real crossfade starts with how long it lasts, and the graph sweeps a line across with a dot riding each curve for exactly that long, then stops. That is the only moving part, and it is deliberately not idle motion (see the live trap about continuously animating elements); the geometry is memoized so the sweep re-renders nothing it does not have to. **Folded by default:** the row shows a summary strip, the shape in miniature plus the level readout, and opens on click (`grid-template-rows: 0fr` to `1fr`, so nothing is measured and reduce-motion collapses it with every other duration token); the graph's live subscription only exists while it is open, and the folded half is `inert` so its handles stay out of the tab order. Math covered by `tests/utils/fadeCurve.test.ts` (11 assertions: the bend-0 identity against the old sin/cos, endpoints, monotonicity, the round trip, clamping, and the unity property).
- **Output device picker (2026-08-04).** Settings → Audio → Output chooses where sound leaves the machine. Routed with `AudioContext.setSinkId` (`outputDeviceId` in `velora-audio-settings`, `""` = system default), because the mix leaves through the context and not the `<audio>` elements: an element-level `setSinkId` moves nothing here. The row hides itself where the API is missing (Safari, Firefox) via `supportsOutputDeviceSelection()`. A stored id that no longer resolves, device unplugged or its id rotated when device permission lapsed, falls back to the system default and rewrites the setting rather than going quiet. Chromium only exposes device names once microphone access is granted, so `useAudioOutputDevices` reports an unlabelled list as `needsPermission` and a child button opens-then-immediately-stops a mic stream to unlock the names; the list re-enumerates on `devicechange`, and the picker shows the default entry rather than a raw id whenever the stored id isn't in the labelled list.
- **Dropped: Night mode (2026-10-04).** A one-toggle compressor preset plus volume cap for late listening. Cut by decision, never built; don't re-propose. (The strongest "Even out volume" level is named Night mode since 2026-10-05; that is only a compressor curve, no volume cap.)
- **Dropped: Alarm clock + sleep timer (2026-07-23).** Cut by decision, never built; don't re-propose. It was the last open §1 item, so the section is now closed. A wake-to-music alarm only fires if the app is open, awake, and unmuted at the target time, which a browser tab / backgrounded desktop app can't promise, so the core promise ("wake me up") is unreliable by construction; the OS alarm already does this correctly. The sleep-timer half is the only genuinely useful piece and can return on its own later as a small player-menu fade-out-and-pause if wanted, without the alarm scaffolding.
- **Dropped: Casting (Chromecast / AirPlay) (2026-07-22).** Cut by decision, never built; don't re-propose. Reasons: the lift is far larger than the payoff for a self-hosted app, and cross-platform parity is impossible by construction, web Chromecast needs the Google Cast SDK while AirPlay has no public web API (Safari/`<video>`-only), so it could never work the same on every target. It also fights the architecture: a cast receiver moves playback authority off-device, which collides with Velora's server-authoritative controller vs. the client-side one. If ever revived, it belongs in its own capability-gated service beside `audioEngine`, not inside it.
- **Lyrics search via lrclib.net, dropped 2026-07-19.** Out of scope for this repo: it belongs in a plugin, not the frontend. (The old Settings → Playback toggle was local-state-only and did nothing; it and its `settings.playback.lyricsSearch*` locale keys are already removed.) Separate reason to keep it out of the shipped app: lyrics are copyrighted independently of the audio and lrclib is crowdsourced with no licensing chain, so redistribution in a sold product would need legal sign-off.
- **Queue survives a reload in client-side mode** (closed 2026-07-19): was tracked as open in `goals.md` §1 after it had already shipped. `ClientPlaybackController` persists to `localStorage` (`persistResume`/`readStored`/`restoreStored`) and rebuilds on `connect()`: the full queue plus the current track, so auto-advance survives too, not just the one song. Restore goes through the normal resolve path, so a since-deleted track just drops out; a corrupt write is removed rather than retried. Falls back to a track-only write when the full queue would blow the storage quota, and the Velora path awaits the server-queue restore instead (server-authoritative wins). Playback context rides along on the full-queue branch only, see the source-context entry below.
- **Playback source context + nav "playing from here" indicator** (2026-07-18): nothing in the app showed which playlist/album/artist the current queue came from. New `PlaybackContext` (`{ kind: "playlist"|"album"|"artist"|"genre"; id }`) in `playbackTypes.ts`, optional on `QueueRequest` and required-nullable on `PlaybackState` so every construction site has to answer. **Set explicitly by the caller, never derived from `QueueSource`**, sorted detail views queue their visible order as `source: "tracks"` (`playlistView` always, `albumView`/`artistView` when a sort is applied) and would otherwise lose the origin. Both controllers hold it in a private field set by `setQueue` and stamp it onto every snapshot they build (client: `snapshot()`; Velora: `mapSnapshot()` + `predictQueue()`, with `context` destructured out of the wire body next to `startTrack` so it never reaches the backend). Command predictions inherit it for free by spreading `lastState`. Wired at the callsites with a real origin: playlist/album/artist/genre views, `artistAlbumsView`, the home album carousel, and the play/shuffle entries in `playlistMenu`/`mediaMenu` (favorites uses `{ kind: "playlist", id: "favorites" }`, matching its pseudo-playlist route). Sourceless queues (allSongs, search, smartRadio) leave it null. Nav consumes it through a module-level `selectPlayingRowId` selector that projects the context onto nav's own row-id shape (`id` for playlists, `artist:<id>` for pinned artists; album/genre map to ids no row carries), a **primitive** selector, so the nav re-renders on a source change and not on every playback emit. **Indicator design, deliberately not a border or a fill.** Both were tried and rejected: in this system an accent border/fill is the *selected/hovered* grammar (`.trackSelected`, the nav row's own hover), so a playing row read as "the row I just clicked", and the nav has no route-active highlight to disambiguate it. Velora spells playback with motion instead (`.trackActive` spins the cover), so the mark is `NavPlayingMark`: three CSS-animated accent bars plus the word. Unfolded it **replaces the song-count subtitle** (`▮▯▮ Playing`) so the row reports what it's *doing* rather than gaining chrome; folded/top-bottom rows have no text, so the bars sit beside the cover. Never on the artwork (an overlaid badge was tried and rejected too). Bars flatten and the word becomes `nav.paused` when paused, so the row carries play state; reduce-motion keeps a staggered static silhouette. Neutral `--color-white`, **not** the accent, the motion is the signal, and full strength against the `op-80` line it replaces is enough to make the row the loud one. `aria-current` on the row, and the bars carry an `aria-label` in the folded case where there's no visible word. Toggleable via Settings → Display → "Mark the playing playlist" (`navPlayingMark`, default on); off restores the plain song count. **Survives a reload** (same day): the client controller folds `context` into its existing `StoredResume` write, deliberately only on the full-queue branch (the track-only quota fallback and the server-queue path in `initialize()` both leave it null, a queue from another device has no source we can honestly claim), and adds it to the persist-throttle key so a context-only change isn't throttled out. The Velora controller had no local persistence at all, so it gained a small one: `velora-playback-context:<serverUrl>` holds `{ context, queueKey }` where `queueKey` is a `length:firstId:lastId` fingerprint, written from `emit()` (deduped against the last write, so progress ticks don't re-serialize) and reclaimed once in `mapSnapshot`, guarded by `contextSettled` so only the first queue after a reload can adopt it, and only when the fingerprint matches the queue the server actually handed back. **Review pass caught three ordering bugs, all fixed:** (1) `contextSettled` only guarded the *first* snapshot, so a queue replaced from another device kept the old label and then poisoned storage with it, the Velora controller now learns `contextQueueIds` (the id set of the queue it first sees the context with) and retires the context in `reconcileContext` once a snapshot shares *none* of them. Deliberately an overlap test, not `queueKeyOf` equality: shuffle, `addToQueue` and `updateTrack` all change the fingerprint but still overlap, so equality would have dropped the mark on every shuffle. It runs in `emit()` (adoption) rather than `mapSnapshot`, so a stale snapshot `emitSnapshot` discards can't retire a live context. (2) Both controllers assigned `context` *before* the work that can throw (the POST; `resolveSource`), so a failed play left the mark on a queue that never started, Velora restores `priorContext`/`priorContextQueueIds` in its catch, the client controller now assigns after the source resolves (plus at the top of `seedAndBackfill`). (3) The command palette's in-playlist seed queued without a context, so seeding from the palette cleared the mark a row click would have set. **The treatment became a pick (2026-07-28):** `navPlayingStyle` (`cover | bars | spin | accent`) adds three treatments beside the original bars and makes `cover` the new default, the row's own artwork washed behind the button (0.3, 0.5 on hover, 0.18 paused), the cover spinning like a record (paused = `animation-play-state: paused`, `data-reduce-motion` stops it), and the accent fill a playing track row already carries (`.trackActive`, rejected as the *default* above for exactly the reason stated there, fine as an explicit user choice). The animated bars + the "Playing"/"Paused" word run in **every** style (tried the other way, dropping the glyph for the styles that mark the row themselves, and the row lost the thing that actually reads as playback), so a style is a treatment layered around the mark, not a replacement for it. Everything but the wash works folded; a folded row is only the cover thumb, so `cover` falls back to the bars overlay there. The wash reads its url from a `--nav-playing-cover` inline var, and both fills restate themselves on `:hover` so the neutral nav hover fill can't drop them. The picker sits in Appearance → Interface next to the detail-header style (it's a looks choice), while the on/off toggle stays the behavior half in Display → General and hides the picker when off.
- Client-side waveform timeline (desktop) (2026-07-15), the waveform scrubber now works for local-mode and Subsonic tracks, not just Velora. The `waveform` capability (provider-served peaks) stays false on both and the providers still throw `UNSUPPORTED` (safety layer), but on desktop the UI adds a client-decode fallback: `useWaveformAvailable()` (in `useTrackPeaks.ts`) is `capability("waveform") || isElectron()` and gates the `WaveformButton` in `player.tsx` + bigMusic `utilityButtons.tsx` (replacing the old `<Capable feature="waveform">` wrap). When peaks aren't provider-served, `useTrackPeaks` routes to `decodeTrackPeaks` (new `src/utils/clientPeaks.ts`): `musicService.getStreamUrl` → `fetch` → `OfflineAudioContext.decodeAudioData` → `computePeaks` downsamples channel 0 to 500 normalized 0-1 buckets (same shape VeloraProvider.getPeaks returns). Stays opt-in-computed (only when `waveformEnabled` is on, only the current track) and cached three ways: the existing in-memory `resolved`/`inflight` maps, plus a persisted IndexedDB store (`velora-peaks`, keyed `providerType:trackId`, best-effort, read/write failures degrade to recompute) so peaks survive restarts. Fetch/decode failure falls back to the plain scrubber. localProvider/subsonicProvider `getPeaks` untouched (still the throwing safety net).
- Autoplay when queue ends (2026-07-15), on by default (`autoplayWhenQueueEnds` in `useSettings`, Settings → Playback → Behavior). `useAutoplayContinuation` (mounted once in `mainPage`) watches playback state via `usePlaybackSelector`; when the current track becomes the last in the queue while playing with repeat off, it appends a 25-track continuation batch through `playbackService.sendCommand({command:"addToQueue"})`, provider-agnostic, so both controllers get it (client in-memory push, Velora server-side append). Continuation source: `musicService.getSimilarSongs` where `supports("smartRadio")` (Velora now wired to `POST /smart-queue/preview`, side-effect-free similar list; Subsonic `getSimilarSongs2`), random `getTracks(0)` shuffle fallback otherwise (local). Dedups the seed via a ref so it fires once per tail; appending grows the queue and re-arms for the next tail. Excludes ids already queued.

- Crossfade on manual skip toggle (2026-07-14), `crossfadeOnManualSkip` in `velora-audio-settings` (default off: manual next/prev/track-picks hard-cut, natural endings still crossfade; on restores the old always-crossfade behavior). Engine-initiated advances (`advanceInFlight` captured in `reconcile` before reset) count as natural; child toggle under Crossfade in Settings → Playback

- Server-authoritative playback (Velora) and client-side playback (Navidrome) controllers
- Dynamics compressor, Settings → Audio, persisted to `velora-audio-settings`. **Presets (2026-10-05):** the toggle + four sliders became "Even out volume", Off · Light · Medium · Night mode · Advanced; Advanced shows threshold/knee/ratio/attack/release in readable units. Old settings and old export files migrate through `fromLegacyCompressor` (`tests/services/compressor.test.ts`).
- **Previous-button threshold** (2026-07-14), Settings → Playback → Behavior (advanced): `previousRestart` toggle + `previousRestartSeconds` slider (1–10s, default 3) in `useSettings`. Client controller reads it in `retreat()` (replaced the hardcoded 3s constant). Velora controller rewrites the command in `sendCommand` since the backend's own rule is a fixed 3s: past the threshold `previous` becomes `seek 0`; below it (or toggle off) with position > 3s it becomes `playIndex(queueIndex - 1)` so the server can't restart against the setting; at index 0 with repeat-all it becomes `playIndex(queue.length - 1)` because the backend's `retreat()` (verified in `../velora-backend/src/core/playback/playbackController.ts`) never wraps, this matches the client controller's wrap. All callers (player, BigMusic, keybinds, media keys, tray) inherit it via `playbackService`.
- **Seek step setting** (2026-07-14): `seekStepSeconds` in `useSettings` (5/10/30s switcher, advanced, default 10); `useKeybindDispatch`'s seekBackward/seekForward read it live (replaced the `SEEK_STEP_SECONDS` constant).
- **Home search bar.** `SearchBar` (`primitives/searchBar/`) on `homeView.tsx`; debounced `musicService.search()` dropdown (artists/albums/tracks), `genre:`/`bpm:` filters via `src/utils/searchQuery.ts`, Enter → `/search`.
- **`/search` results view.** `SearchView` (`src/screens/views/searchView/`), reads `q` from URL, same filters, renders `MediaCarousel`s + shared `Playlist` list; embeds a `SearchBar` seeded with `initialQuery`.
- **Search includes playlists.** Home dropdown + `SearchView` filter `useLibrary.playlists` client-side by name (`playlistMatchesQuery` in `searchQuery.ts`) since the backend search endpoint returns no playlists.
- **Optimistic shuffle reorder.** `VeloraPlaybackController.predictCommand` now reorders the queue locally on `setShuffle` (current track to front + Fisher-Yates, mirroring the server's `shuffleWithStart`) instead of only flipping the flag, so the sidebar "Up next" updates instantly instead of waiting a round trip. Enable picks a fresh local order (server's random snapshot reconciles invisibly); disable restores the saved pre-shuffle queue (`unshuffledQueue` field) deterministically, falling back to the snapshot when it isn't held (e.g. after reload).
- **Global keyboard shortcuts (P5).** `useGlobalShortcuts` (`src/utils/`), mounted once in `mainPage.tsx`; defaults registry in `keybindActions.ts` (`Space` play/pause, `←`/`→` seek ±10s, `Shift+←`/`Shift+→` prev/next, `↑`/`↓` volume, `M` mute, `S` shuffle, `R` cycle repeat, `L` favorite, `F` toggle BigMusic, `/` focus search), persisted as `useSettings.keybinds`, editable via the Keybind recorder (§6). Bindings are matched via the shared `serializeKeybind()` (`src/utils/keybind.ts`) so the recorder and the listener can't drift; dispatch logic lives in `useKeybindDispatch.ts`, shared with the command palette's action rows (§16). Skips editable targets and the keybind recorder mid-capture.
- **Waveform seek scrubber.** `Timeline` renders a canvas waveform (played/unplayed split, theme-aware accent) when given a `peaks` array, with a `skeletonPulse` placeholder while loading. Peaks are computed lazily server-side and cached: new `peaks` column on `tracks`, `GET /api/v1/songs/:id/peaks` (ffmpeg → mono 8kHz PCM → 1000 normalized buckets in `core/transcoding/waveform.ts`, in-process lock against double-compute). Frontend: `getPeaks` on `IMusicProvider` (Velora; Navidrome throws `UNSUPPORTED`), new `waveform` capability, shared `useTrackPeaks` hook (process-wide cache) used by the player and BigMusic. Toggled via the previously-unused player control button (repurposed the dead `graphicEqEnabled` flag → `waveformEnabled`), gated with `<Capable feature="waveform">`; works in the player and every BigMusic mode (mode Timelines + mobile controls + video) via `ctx.peaks`/`ctx.peaksLoading`.

- **Decomposed icon micro-animations (2026-07-13→15).** SVG-decomposition button primitives replacing the flat Iconify controls across player + BigMusic, each registered in `ICON_ANIMATIONS` (`src/utils/iconAnimations.ts`) + gated on `useIconAnimation(id)` (feeds Appearance → Animated icons cherry-pick; presets none/minimal[=`player` group]/all): `ShuffleButton` (arrows fly out/trail in), `RepeatButton` (dashes+arrowheads roll half a lap per cycle, repeat-one "1" pops), `SkipButton` (`direction` prop, bar bounces), `SidebarButton` (right panel bounces, tints active), `WaveformButton` (5 bars equalizer-dance on / wilt off), `PlayPauseButton` (triangle↔bars path morph), `VolumeButton` (speaker + 2 arcs gated on perceptual volume, strike-through on mute), plus non-decomposed CSS-keyframe nav icons (`home`/`tracks`/`settings` under a new `nav` group, replay per click via a remount key) and `NavPinIcon` (pushpin thunks in on pin via AnimatePresence+Motion, skips first-mount enter). All keep a reduce-motion static fallback. Fix (2026-07-14): Sidebar/skip bounces drive their mounted SVG paths through Motion controls, the prior click-key remount + `initial={false}` suppressed the bounce in packaged prod builds. Remaining candidate (still open in goals.md §1): add-to-playlist/queue `+`→checkmark.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/primitives/{shuffleButton,repeatButton,skipButton,sidebarButton,waveformButton,playPauseButton,volumeButton,favoriteButton}/`, `src/utils/iconAnimations.ts`, `player.tsx` + BigMusic controls, `nav.tsx`

- **Ctrl + scroll is volume, anywhere in the app (2026-08-05).** The wheel only meant volume over the volume control itself; everywhere else the chord was the browser's page zoom, which in a packaged desktop app is a gesture with nothing to offer. `useCtrlWheelVolume()` (`src/utils/volumeWheel.ts`, mounted once in `mainPage.tsx` beside `useGlobalShortcuts`) takes it, gated on the new `ctrlWheelVolume` setting (default on, Integrations → System, next to the unchanged `wheelVolume`). The listener is **non-passive** or `preventDefault` can't stop the zoom, and **capture-phase**, because React delegates `onWheel` from the root: without the capture stop, one notch over the volume slider would run both handlers and move the gain twice. Capture is spelled on the remove too, or the listener outlives the effect. The 0.05-step-in-slider-space nudge that `player.tsx` and `bigMusic.tsx` each carried a copy of is now the one exported `nudgeVolume(deltaY)` all three call. i18n `settings.integrations.ctrlWheelVolume{,Desc}` ×9.
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/volumeWheel.ts`, `src/settings.tsx`, `src/screens/pages/mainPage/mainPage.tsx`, `src/screens/views/settingsView/useSettingsSections.ts`, `player.tsx`, `bigMusic.tsx`, `tests/utils/volumeWheel.test.ts`, all 9 locales

- **First run starts at 20%, except on mobile (2026-08-09).** `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.volume` was `1`, so a fresh profile played its first track at full gain into whatever the system volume happened to be. It is now `FIRST_RUN_VOLUME`: `0.2` on desktop/web, `1` on mobile, where the volume rocker is the real control and a 20% app gain only makes the phone quiet with no obvious way back. First run only, `loadSettings()` merges the stored blob over the defaults, so an existing profile keeps its volume and nothing is written over. Mobile is `isMobilePlatform()`: `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` or `(pointer: coarse)`, the same heuristic `resolveAutoQuality` already used, so mobile web counts too.
  - ↳ files: `src/services/audio/audioEngine.ts`

- **Autoplay continuation stops repeating one artist (2026-09-30).** The Velora smart queue ranked the seed artist first on every signal and took the top N, and each batch was seeded from the last track, so a continuation narrowed onto one artist. `useAutoplayContinuation` now sends the queue in play order (`getSimilarSongs`' `queueIds`); the backend excludes it, counts the artists of its last 10 tracks as already heard, and reranks for variety (see the backend's `smartQueue.ts` `diversify`).
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/useAutoplayContinuation.ts`, `veloraProvider.ts` `getSimilarSongs`, `ImusicProvider.ts`

- **Balance slider (2026-10-01).** For uneven hearing: `AudioSettings.balance` (-1..1, step 0.05 so center is exact) drives a `StereoPannerNode` after `monoRouter`, so a mono mix can still lean toward the better ear, before the analyser + destination. Row sits under Mono output, live through `subscribeSettings`, exported in the `audio` scope. i18n `settings.audio.balance{,Desc,Center,Left,Right}` ×9.
  - ↳ files: `src/services/audio/audioEngine.ts`, `useSettingsSections.ts`, `src/utils/userDataScopes.ts`, `docs/app/settings/audio.md` + `storage.md`

- **Lighter queue start (2026-10-03).** Starting a Velora queue took ~2s: the backend selected every track column, so a 5000-track queue carried each track's ~6 KB waveform `peaks`, and the client then parsed and mapped the queue twice (our own WebSocket echo plus the HTTP response). The backend now leaves `peaks` out of list selects and every track DTO (it has its own `/songs/:id/peaks`), and the controller holds the echoed broadcast raw and only maps it if its revision is still news. A HAR then showed the 11 MB queue downloaded three times per click: progress replies now leave the queue out (and the client no longer maps them), the optimistic one-track queue is marked `queueResolving` so autoplay continuation stops treating it as the queue's end (it refetched the state and posted every queued id), and continuation reads the cached snapshot instead of `getState()`. The backend's WebSocket uses per-message deflate and its Caddy examples `encode zstd gzip`.
  - ↳ files: `veloraPlaybackController.ts` (`heldBroadcast`, `endCommand`, progress, `predictQueue`), `useAutoplayContinuation.ts`, `usePlaybackState.ts` (`getPlaybackSnapshot`), backend `trackColumns.ts`, `trackDto.ts`, `playbackController.ts`, `bootstrap.ts`
- **Snapshots without the queue (2026-10-03).** Every Velora command but progress returned and broadcast the whole queue (up to 5000 tracks, ~11 MB), so a pause shipped and re-mapped it on every device. The backend keeps a `queueRevision`, seeded from boot time so it never repeats across restarts and moved by every change to the queue's contents or order; replies and broadcasts carry the queue only when a command moved it, while `GET /playback/state` and socket open always do. It is opt-in (`?lean=1` on `/playback/commands` and the socket), since older clients read the queue off every snapshot and the backend may deploy first. The controller holds the last queue by its revision (`heldQueue`) and fills queue-less snapshots from it, so the queue array keeps its identity across pauses and skips; one it doesn't hold means a missed change and `/playback/state` is refetched (`resolveSnapshot`, and `adoptBroadcast` sharing one fetch per burst). Plugins and the desktop API read the controller's state, so they still see the full queue.
  - ↳ files: `veloraPlaybackController.ts` (`heldQueue`, `queueFor`, `resolveSnapshot`, `adoptBroadcast`), backend `playbackController.ts` (`touchQueue`, `snapshot`, `broadcast`)
- **Skip silent start (2026-10-05).** Off by default, Playback → Behavior. A song started from the top seeks past 1s or more of near-silence (-40 dB below its peak) found in the waveform peaks, through a `seek` command so both controllers agree; a mid-track restore or a listener who already seeked is left alone. The next track's peaks are prefetched. Shown only where the waveform is (server peaks or desktop decode); the peaks cache moved out of the hook into `utils/trackPeaks.ts` so the engine shares it.
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/trackPeaks.ts` (`leadingSilence`, tested), `audioEngine.ts` (`skipLeadingSilence`), `useSettingsSections.ts`, `userDataScopes.ts`, `docs/app/settings/playback.md` + `storage.md`
- **Radio tuner in the player (2026-10-10).** A playing station left the bar a lone play button. The cover is now the station's plate drawn to an image (`utils/stationArt.ts`, one cached entry, so every BigMusic mode and the cover flight take it unchanged), the subtitle is its host, the seek bar's slot is a tuner dial (`primitives/radioDial/`) with every saved station marked at its hash spot and the needle on the one that's on, and the skips tune along the dial, wrapping (`tuneStation`). Same in BigMusic (shared transport, `BigMusicSeekbar`, bigCover; plugin modes, which get no track, keep the LIVE badge), the mini-player (side swipe and hold tune) and the nav tile and docked tab (the plate). The skips disable with no other station. The station list is shared in `store/radioStations.ts`, loaded by Home and /radio through `loadRadioStations` (request-ordered, so a slow load can't undo a newer list and a logout drops what's in flight) and cleared on logout. Perf: `RadioTuner`/`RadioDial` are memoized on the station, so the bar's per-emit renders and BigMusic's 1s clock tick stop at them (`tests/perf/renderCounts.test.tsx`).
  - ↳ files: `ui/player/radioTuner/RadioTuner.tsx`, `primitives/radioDial/`, `utils/stationArt.ts`, `utils/stationTone.ts`, `utils/playStation.ts`, `store/radioStations.ts`, `ui/bigMusic/bigMusicTransport.tsx`

## 2. Library & Content
- **Card play hint (2026-10-10).** Cards that play pick how they say so (`cardPlayHint`, Library look): bloom (default), pill, ripple, iris, caption or the old still disc. With a mouse nothing shows at rest and one non-looping moment plays on hover without moving the artwork; touch keeps a small mark at rest. A shimmer sweep was prototyped and dropped.
  - ↳ files: `primitives/mediaCard/`, `src/settings.tsx`, `settingsView/useSettingsSections.ts`, `utils/userDataScopes.ts`
- **Playlist grid mode grew up (2026-08-04).** The grid display type was a bare `MediaCard` wall: the playing song was a static outline, tiles had no play affordance, no favorite state, no drag, no sort or size control, and loading showed table-row skeletons. It now speaks the table's language. The playing tile takes the user's `trackPlayingStyle` mark (accent fill / spinning circular cover / blurred artwork wash / accent hairline / equalizer bars over the cover, all paused-aware and reduce-motion guarded), and on top of whichever mark is picked it carries a playhead along the bottom of the artwork, ticking inside its own `TileProgress` leaf so the once-a-second position update re-renders that bar and nothing else in the grid. Tiles also gained the hover play overlay (they play on click, V2 §14.6), a favorite heart (hover-revealed on desktop, a plain state badge on touch, where the tap belongs to the tile and favoriting stays on the long-press menu), the shared `SelectCheckbox` in place of a hand-drawn checkmark, and drag-to-playlist. Tile width follows the same size setting the table uses for row height (`TILE_SIZES`), the view-options menu keeps that size group in grid mode and gains sort field + direction (a grid has no column headers to click), and the skeletons mirror the grid through the shared `GridSkeletons`. Jump-to-current works in grid mode too: `VirtualizedGrid` now reports its measured `{columns, rowHeight, offsetTop}`, so the pill locates a tile by the same arithmetic it uses for a row. `MediaCard` gained four optional passthroughs for this (`overlay`, `style`, `draggable`, `onDragStart`) and stayed dumb; `PlaylistGridCard` is memoized on Playlist's stable callbacks, and its `isPlaying` selector closes over `isActive` so a play/pause toggle re-renders one tile.
  - ↳ files: `ui/playlist/{playlist.tsx,playlist.css,playlistGridCard.tsx}`, `primitives/{mediaCard,virtualizedGrid}`, `utils/playlistFilter.ts`, `tests/utils/playlistFilter.test.ts`
- **The track list's header is a header now (2026-08-04).** `.playlistTracksHeader` was body-size text at op .7 above rows of the same size and family, marking its active sort with weight 600 and a small arrow, with nothing saying the labels were clickable at all until after you'd clicked one; grid mode rendered no cells and left a 43px empty bar whose `min-height` existed only to stop the absolutely-positioned tune button from crashing into the divider; and the sort targets were ~19px tall, four of them across 360px. It's now **one row in two forms, switched in CSS** so it answers the pointer type and not only the width. **The spine** (table, fine pointer) puts the labels on the micro-label role (V2 §4.1, 0.68rem/700/uppercase/0.09em), so the row reads as the table's structure instead of competing with the track titles; each sortable label is a real target whose padding and matching negative margin cancel out, so the text still starts exactly on its column track while the hit area and its `--fill-subtle` hover fill bleed outwards. Sort state is carried by the arrow rather than by colour (the accent was tried and rejected: it's derived from the cover, so at 0.68rem it lands unreadable against a good share of a real library, and the sorted label just comes up to full strength instead), and that arrow is one mask icon (`--vicon-arrow-upward`) painted in `currentColor` and rotated for direction, so a flip animates on `--ease-bounce-soft` rather than swapping two images, and its slot is reserved at opacity 0 so sorting never shifts the label. It ghosts in at .5 on hover, which is what advertises that the labels sort. **The control cluster** (grid mode, `pointer: coarse`, or <768px) drops the labels and puts a sort button in their place on `libraryPageSortBtn`'s exact grammar, so the playlist header and the library toolbar read as one control; it carries the active order's name (44px on touch, where it's sorting's only affordance) and names it in its `aria-label` too, so the button reads the same as it looks. That killed the empty bar, gave touch a real target, and made artist and "back to the served order" reachable in table mode, which the column cycle can't express. Sorting consequently left the view-options menu entirely: `buildSortMenu` is its own builder that the button owns in both modes, so the two controls can't drift, and `buildFilterMenu` is now purely about layout. The tune button stopped being an absolute float in a hand-derived offset and became a flex slot of the same `--playlist-action-col` the rows reserve (identical geometry, both specificity-war overrides deleted), and the detached `<figure className="divider">` became the header's own bottom hairline, ~8px tighter and no longer floating over the first row. Zero new i18n keys: every string it needed already existed in all 9 locales.
  - ↳ files: `ui/playlist/{playlist.tsx,playlist.css}`, `utils/playlistFilter.ts`, `utils/cssIcons.ts`, `tests/utils/playlistFilter.test.ts`
- **Library browse pages reworked (2026-07-24).** The Home "View all" destinations (`/albums`, `/artists`, `/genres`, `/playlists`, `/radio`) were five near-identical files whose whole header card held one word, with no way to find anything but scrolling. They now share one shell, `assets/components/ui/libraryPage/LibraryPage.tsx` (+ `libraryPage.css`), which owns the title/count row, the toolbar, the single scroll container, and the scroll-memory wiring; each page supplies only its body and a sort spec. Toolbar: a live filter, a sort dropdown (field + direction, built by `buildGridSortMenu` in the `buildFilterMenu` shape), and a two-state tile-density toggle. Sort and density persist **per page** in `settings.gridView.views[key]` so "albums by year" can't reorder artists; the filter query stays session-local on purpose (a forgotten filter still hiding the library after a reload is worse than retyping). Filtering is filter-then-sort in one pure `applyGridView`, so Playlists derives both of its sections from the same toolbar state, and the "nothing matches X" + clear-filter state lives in the shell (the only place that knows the filter, not an empty library, emptied the list, so an "add music" empty state can't lie).
  - Sort fields per page: albums name/artist/year/tracks, artists name/albums/tracks, genres name/songs/albums, playlists name/tracks/last-updated/created, radio name. Every page opens on `default`, the provider's served order, which costs nothing.
  - Identity, so the pages stop being interchangeable: `MediaCard` gained `shape="circle"` and artist tiles are round **everywhere** they appear (`/artists`, Home artists, search results, similar artists), album tiles gained the artist line (`Artist · Year`), and coverless genre cards get their own wider text-led column track. `SearchInput` gained `flat` (control fill/hairline instead of a nested `uiContentContainer`), `EmptyState` gained a pre-translated `message` for the interpolated no-matches copy, and `VirtualizedGrid` gained `layoutKey` so a density switch re-measures columns/row height instead of paging against a stale layout.
  - Radio rows were also fixed while in there: `.radioRowMain:active` scaled a full-bleed flex child, which walked its right edge ~10px inward while the trailing icon buttons stayed put, so a press read as the row sliding sideways. Rows now give press feedback with fill (V2 §10 reserves the `:active` scale for buttons and cards). Radio also had no playing state at all: the current station now carries the `.trackActive` grammar (accent fill + accent edge), its glyph swaps to `graphic-eq` with a token-derived breathing pulse while the stream is live, and clicking the station that's already loaded sends `{ command: "toggle" }` instead of re-setting the queue, which would tear down and re-buffer a live stream.
  - Net: `albumsView.css`, `artistsView.css` and `genresView.css` deleted, `playlistsView.css` down to one rule, `radioView.css` down to its list; three copy-pasted `CardSkeletons` + ResizeObserver/scroll blocks replaced by one `GridSkeletons` (square/circle/text) and one measurement path. New `grid.*` i18n family in all 9 locales.
  - ↳ files: `ui/libraryPage/`, `utils/gridView.ts`, `settings.tsx` (`gridView` slice + partialize/merge), the five views, `primitives/{mediaCard,searchInput,emptyState,virtualizedGrid}`
- **Rule-based smart playlists (2026-07-20).** Saved rule sets that re-evaluate against the library instead of holding a fixed track list. Works on every provider: the rules only read fields all three already return, and the sets are device-local (no provider has a write seam for a rule set), so they need no capability gate. Fields are limited to what `Track` actually carries, title/artist/album/genre/format, bpm/duration/rating/energy/danceability/valence, favorite/lossless, and `addedAt` as an age in days; per-field `capability` hides the ones the active provider can't populate (`trackRating`, `extendedTrackStats`). There is deliberately **no `playCount` field**: no provider reports it per track, so that rule needs a backend column before it can exist.
  - Evaluation never slurps the library. `createSmartFetcher` feeds `Playlist`'s `fetchMore` contract by paging `musicService.getTracks(cursor)` and filtering each page, pulling further pages until it has ~25 matches so an all-miss page can't stall the scroll loop; `limit` ends the list early. The editor's live count uses a bounded 500-track scan (`previewSmartMatches`) so typing a rule can't trigger a full-library pass, and says "in the first N" whenever the slice wasn't the whole library.
  - **Server-side resolution (2026-07-20).** That client scan is now only the fallback. On a provider that advertises the new `smartQuery` capability (Velora), the rule set is resolved by the backend via `POST /api/v1/tracks/query`, which returns only the matching tracks plus an exact `total`, so the whole library never crosses the wire: `createSmartFetcher` pages that endpoint directly (no per-page client filter), `previewSmartMatches` reads `total` for an exact count, and `collectSmartTracks` pages it up to `min(limit, 1000)`. The client scan stays for providers without the capability **and** as a runtime fallback: if the endpoint rejects (an older backend 404s, or a provider throws `UNSUPPORTED`) the call falls back to the scan and the missing endpoint is remembered per server URL so it isn't re-hit on every page; a rule-specific 400 falls back for that one call only. Empty/whitespace text rules are stripped before sending (they match everything, which the server also treats as a no-op), and an all-no-op set defers to the client scan so local "matches everything" behavior is preserved. `smartQuery` is added to `ProviderCapabilities` and `IMusicProvider.queryTracks` (Velora `true`; Subsonic/local `false`, throwing `UNSUPPORTED`).
    - Backend (`../velora-backend`, `POST /api/v1/tracks/query`, `authenticate`-gated): `smartRules.ts` whitelists field→column and op→SQL template, binds every value as a bound parameter (never interpolated), and 400s naming the offending field on an unknown/unsupported field (e.g. `rating`, which has no column) or a wrong-typed value. It mirrors the frontend evaluator exactly: a NULL/missing column never matches in either direction, an empty text value is a no-op, `addedAt` compares age in days (timezone-correct interval subtraction), and `favorite` resolves against the requesting user via a left-joined `favorite_songs`. Genre lives in a join table, matched with `IN (subquery)`; `format` is derived from the file-path extension (aliased `m4a`→`aac`), matching the DTO. `TrackRepository.queryTracks/countTracks` reuse `GET /tracks`' joins, DTO mapping, and id-descending cursor so paging is identical; `total` is a `COUNT(*)` over the same WHERE. Covered by `src/__tests__/tracksQuery.test.ts` (text/number/boolean/favorite/genre, match all/any, paging+total, empty rules, and 400 rejections; `format`/`addedAt` are exercised only by the frontend `check:rules` since pg-mem can't run their SQL).
    - ↳ files: `src/services/music/{capabilities.ts,ImusicProvider.ts,providers/{veloraProvider,subsonicProvider,localProvider}.ts}`, `src/utils/smartPlaylistFetch.ts`, `src/screens/views/smartPlaylistView/smartPlaylistView.tsx`; backend `src/routes/v1/library/{tracksQuery,smartRules}.ts`, `src/routes/v1/i_routes.ts`, `src/infrastructure/db/repositories/TrackRepository.ts`
  - Semantics chosen deliberately and covered by the self-check: an empty rule set matches **nothing** (an unfinished playlist shouldn't silently become the whole library), and a rule about a field the track lacks never matches **in either direction**, so `any` can't sweep in everything via a negative operator.
  - Home is the only surface (§13 registry entry `smartPlaylists`, orderable/hideable like the rest), so it also owns management: a leading create card (first, not last, the carousel windows its children), per-card context menu (play/shuffle/next/queue, edit rules, rename, duplicate, save-as-real-playlist behind `createPlaylist`, export, delete), and `/smart/:smartId` for the tracks. Rule edits remount the list via a rules signature so stale matches can't linger.
  - The editor is **draft-based with an explicit Create/Save**, not live-commit: the create card opens an unsaved `newSmartPlaylist()` and nothing reaches the store until the button is pressed, so an abandoned editor leaves no junk behind and an edit can be backed out of. Save is disabled with zero rules (that set matches nothing by design).
  - Cards and the detail header draw an inline `SmartIcon` (the three `auto-awesome` stars split into their own paths) via a new `MediaCard` `coverSlot` prop, since a rule set has no artwork. Each star swells and settles on ancestor hover, staggered so the shimmer travels across the glyph, and pops in on creation. CSS-driven off the `--duration-*` tokens so it follows the animation-speed setting, registered as `smart` in `ICON_ANIMATIONS` (nav group) for the cherry-pick setting, and killed outright under `html[data-reduce-motion]` (§11.3 double guard).
  - Stored in a persisted `useSmartPlaylists` store (`velora-smart-playlists`) and carried in the user-data export/import file; both paths run every rule set through `sanitizeSmartPlaylist`, which drops unknown fields/ops rather than trusting them, and import merges by id instead of overwriting.
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/smartPlaylist.ts` (pure evaluator, type-only imports so `npm run check:rules` can run it via `--experimental-strip-types`), `src/utils/smartPlaylistFetch.ts`, `src/utils/smartPlaylistMenu.ts`, `src/store/smartPlaylists.ts`, `src/assets/components/primitives/smartIcon/`, `src/assets/components/ui/smartPlaylistEditor/`, `src/screens/views/smartPlaylistView/`, `src/screens/views/homeView/components/homeSmartPlaylists/`, `mediaCard.tsx` (`coverSlot`), `iconAnimations.ts`, `homeSections.tsx`, `app.tsx`, `userDataExport.ts`, `scripts/check-smart-rules.mjs`; `smartPlaylist.*`, `settings.iconAnimations.icons.smart` + `settings.userData.importResultSmart` in all 6 locales
- **Smart playlists learn from your listening (2026-10-10).** Closes "Unplayed songs". New rule fields `playCount`, `lastPlayed` (days since, a never-played song counts as infinitely old so "not played in 30 days" keeps the unheard ones) and `skipCount`, plus an order picked before the limit: random (seeded by playlist + local day, so it holds all day and reshuffles at midnight), most played, recently played, longest unplayed. Gated per field and sort on two new capabilities: `playHistory` (Velora server-side, local mode via its `plays` table on the `getTracks` listing) and `skipHistory` (Velora only). Velora reads both from the descriptor's `features.smartPlayHistory`, since an older backend would drop `sort` and page by id. Subsonic and Jellyfin servers keep counts, but Velora reports no plays to them (scrobble dropped, §15), so both stay off and only get the daily random order. Backend: the fields are correlated subqueries over `playback_sessions` with the stats' own play/skip thresholds (`trackPlaySignals` beside `sessionStatsCte`, which now shares one `listenedSecondsSql`), served by a new `(user_id, track_id)` index; a `sort` switches `POST /tracks/query` to offset paging. Client side, a sorted list can't stream, so the scan keeps only the best `cap` rows (limit, at most 1000) while paging the library, bounded at 2x cap in memory; a list that started on the server never falls back to the client halfway, since the two order random differently. A sorted list sends its no-op rules too, so "every song, random" sorts on the server instead of crawling the library.

Deliberately unobtrusive: icon-only until hover/focus expands the label, and visibility is activity-driven, a scroll or a track change pokes it awake and it fades again ~2.5s later unless the pointer rests on it. Same corner, quieter than before: shut it is a dimmed, flat circle holding nothing but the chevron, and hover or keyboard focus opens it into a pill and brings up the accent hairline the playing row carries. The geometry is two constants, `--jump-size` (glyph + padding + border, used for both width and height, which is what makes the closed state a true circle, and re-pointed at 44px under `pointer: coarse`) and `--radius-xl` (clamps to half the box shut, a stadium open, so the radius never animates). Everything else holds still: content is right-aligned and the chip is right-anchored, so the chevron does not move, and the **only** animated property is the artwork-and-title group's own `max-width`, with the chip's width following it. They open as one group rather than two children, so they can't drift apart, and the group is content-sized, so a short title leaves no slack before the chevron; its trailing gap is a margin on the title inside the clip rather than padding on the group, since a border-box width floors at its own padding and would have left the closed group 4px wide, so a closed group is worth exactly zero and the circle stays round. The chip's own padding is derived from `--jump-size` too, which is what keeps the glyph centred in the bigger touch circle. The cover fetch lives in the chip (at 128, the size the rows and the player already ask for, so the cache serves all three from one entry), so the artwork never re-renders the virtualized list, and no strings were added.

Backend already supported `PATCH /playlists/:id { coverDataUrl }` (`../velora-backend/src/routes/v1/library/playlists.ts`), only the frontend plumbing was missing: added `coverDataUrl` to `PlaylistUpdate` (`ImusicProvider.ts`), wired it through in `VeloraProvider.updatePlaylist()` (previously short-circuited to a no-op `getPlaylist()` whenever `name` was absent, cover-only updates never reached the network), and a new `playlistCoverUpload` capability (`true` for Velora, `false` for Navidrome, Subsonic's `updatePlaylist` has no cover param; `NavidromeProvider` throws `UNSUPPORTED` if `coverDataUrl` is passed). The affordance is hidden for the synthetic `"favorites"` and read-only `"all-songs"` pseudo-playlists, which have no backend row to attach a cover to.
- **Animated GIF playlist covers (2026-08-04).** A picked GIF now stays a GIF end to end; before this every path flattened it to frame one. **Needs the matching backend release** (`../velora-backend`, `core/images/thumbnails.ts` + `routes/v1/library/covers.ts`): the animation now comes from the server's thumbnail, so against an older server every cover is a still with nothing to explain why.
  - **Upload.** `downscaleBlob` returns a GIF untouched instead of decoding it with `createImageBitmap` and re-encoding a still WebP (`isGifSource`, mime with a `.gif` name fallback), so `fileToCoverDataUrl` sends the original bytes and re-labels a typeless pick `image/gif` (the skipped re-encode is what used to fix the mime, and `data:application/octet-stream` is refused by the route as "not an image"). Bounded by a `maxBytes` argument: `MAX_COVER_BYTES` 50 MB, the route's own ceiling (67 MB of base64, which is what its 70 MB `bodyLimit` leaves room for), and `MAX_LOCAL_COVER_BYTES` 2 MB for the Favorites cover, which lives in the localStorage settings blob rather than on the server.
  - **Failures say which limit.** `CoverTooLargeError` carries the cap and `utils/coverError.ts` maps it to `playlist.coverTooLarge` (with the size), a 413 to `playlist.coverRejectedTooLarge` (the server or a proxy in front of it capping the body, nginx defaults to 1 MB), everything else to the old generic `playlist.coverUpdateFailed`. One reporter for all four call sites (playlist header, edit dialog, favorites, the store's server-side revert).
  - **Playing only when meant.** `utils/coverAnimation.ts` (`isAnimatedCover` / `coverFrames`) resolves a cover to a `{ still, animated }` pair through `thumbnailUrl(url, size, still?)`, which gained the flag across the provider seam (`ImusicProvider`, `veloraProvider` → `&still=1`, `musicProviderBundle`). Nav rows rest on the still and play under the pointer or on keyboard focus, done in CSS (`content: var(--nav-cover-anim, normal)` on the row's img), so the moving copy isn't fetched until the first hover and no hover state re-renders the nav; `html[data-reduce-motion]` keeps it still. The detail header's banner plays while open and pauses once scrolled to a bar, behind the new `pauseCoverOnCollapse` setting (default on, Appearance, child of the shrink-on-scroll toggle); `useHeaderCollapse` returns `swept` for it, flipped on the same hysteresis as `--sweep` so it costs one render per crossing, not per scroll event.
  - **The banner pauses in place.** An image element has no pause: its only lever is `src`, and swapping that restarts at frame one, so the banner would jump on stop and start over on resume. `primitives/animatedCover/AnimatedCover.tsx` decodes the frames itself (WebCodecs `ImageDecoder` over the blob `useCoverArt` already cached, so no second fetch) and paints them to a `<canvas>` one at a time; pausing is not scheduling the next frame, which leaves the cover exactly where the user was looking and resumes from that same index. The canvas carries the caller's class, so `object-fit: cover` and the variants' blur/scale apply to it unchanged. Falls back to the still/animated `src` swap where `ImageDecoder` is missing (Firefox) or the decode throws, and reduce-motion holds frame zero. The header's **cover tile** pauses with it: that node is built by the view and handed in as a prop, so it can't take the state as a prop, but it renders inside the header's tree, which is what `detailHeader/coverPlayback.ts` (a context) reaches. Views render tiles through `primitives/coverArt/CoverArt.tsx`, which is a plain image until the cover actually animates (playlist, album, artist-songs, artist-favorites; a scanned library really can serve a `folder.gif`). Nav rows keep the CSS swap on purpose: hover-to-play never needed to resume mid-loop, and a decoder per row would be far heavier than one CSS image.
  - **Favorites, the cover with no server.** It's a synthetic playlist with no row to attach artwork to, so its cover has always been a data URL in the persisted settings, which capped it at ~2 MB (localStorage is ~5 MB for the *whole* settings blob) and left it with no still/animated pair to gate anything on. Now split: the still frame stays in `favoritesCoverUrl` (512px WebP via the new `fileToStillDataUrl`, so it still travels with a profile export), and the moving original goes to IndexedDB (`utils/favoritesCoverStore.ts`, db `velora-user`, deliberately not `derivedCache.ts` since that store is wipeable "recomputable" data and a picked cover is not). That gives it the same 50 MB ceiling as any server cover, and `useFavoritesArt()` now returns `animated` (one shared object URL, not one per consumer) so the nav row hovers-to-play and the banner pauses on collapse exactly like every other playlist. Removing the cover clears both halves, and a non-animated pick drops the stored GIF, or it would keep playing under the new cover's still frame.
