- **Import-from-file: nav progress + fast large imports + no lag/memory storm (2026-07-15).** Reworked the playlist file import so large lists (Text/M3U/XSPF) resolve fast, fill the playlist as they go, and stop ballooning memory. Three fixes in `src/utils/playlistImport.ts`: (1) **concurrency**, `resolveRefs()` resolves refs against the library with a bounded pool (`RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY = 6`, `cursor++` hands each ref to one worker) instead of the old serial one-search-at-a-time chain. (2) **batched store writes**, new `useLibrary.addTracksToPlaylist(playlistId, tracks[])` batch action does **one** optimistic `set` per chunk (append all songs + bump `songCount` once) then persists the chunk to the backend with a 6-wide pool, rolling back only the specific track ids that fail; `streamImportInto()` buffers matches and flushes every `FLUSH_CHUNK = 25`. This killed the old per-track `set` storm, importing N tracks used to fire N optimistic sets, each rebuilding the whole `playlists` summary array and re-rendering the **non-virtualized nav**, so 500 tracks meant 500 full nav re-renders of transient garbage that pushed V8's heap high-water up and kept it there (the reported "memory shoots up and stays high"). Now it's N/25 writes. (3) **live fill**, matches stream into the (possibly open) playlist as chunks flush, rather than waiting for the whole list. **Progress shows in the nav like the upload indicator**: new single-slot `src/store/importProgress.ts` (`begin`/`update`/`end`) driven by `streamImportInto` (both entry points), read by `NavImportIndicator` (`src/assets/components/ui/nav/`, mirrors `NavUploadIndicator`'s markup/`navUpload*` classes, folded ring + expanded bar, `--vicon-playlist-add` icon). Both entry points refactored onto the shared core: `importIntoPlaylist(playlistId)` (context menu) and `useImportPlaylist` (new playlist, creates it, streams in, `await`s all backend adds before navigate so the view loads complete, deletes the stray playlist if zero persisted). The earlier per-button progress bar attempt was dropped in favor of the nav indicator. i18n `nav.import.*` in all 6 locales. **High-effort workflow review fixes (2026-07-15):** resolveTrack now swallows a search rejection (a flaky search → no-match, not an aborted import + orphan playlist); `streamImportInto` preserves **file order** (indexed `resolved[]` + contiguous in-order flush pointer instead of resolution-completion order) and serializes chunk persistence via a promise chain so backend concurrency stays bounded to one chunk at a time; `addTracksToPlaylist` returns `{added, failed}` (no longer toasts per chunk) so the caller totals persisted vs failed and toasts **once**, and returns the true persisted count so an all-adds-failed import shows the error (not a false success) and gets cleaned up; the progress store is **generation-guarded** (`begin` returns a token, `update`/`end` no-op on a stale token) so a second concurrent import doesn't hide the first's indicator; `importIntoPlaylist` loads the playlist detail first so dedup can skip tracks already present; dead `name` plumbing removed. Deferred (noted, low value): deletePlaylist-fails-leaves-orphan on a zero-match new import (rare double-edge); NavImportIndicator still duplicates NavUploadIndicator's constants/markup (left to avoid regressing the shipped upload indicator in a fix pass).
- **Clickable artist names, with multi-artist support (2026-06-23).** Every artist name across the app (player bar desktop + mobile mini-player, sidebar Queue/Info/Lyrics, every track row, all 6 BigMusic modes) now links to `/artist/:artistId`. New `TrackArtist {id, name}` + `Track.artists?: TrackArtist[]` (`ImusicProvider.ts`), populated per-provider rather than guessed client-side, because the two backends genuinely differ here: Velora's `tracks.artistId` is a single non-null FK (the scanner joins multi-artist ID3 tags into one combined name, upserted as one `artists` row), so `veloraProvider.mapTrack()` always emits exactly one entry; Navidrome can return a real per-artist OpenSubsonic `artists` array when the server has multi-artist tagging on, so `navidromeProvider.mapTrack()` (`mapTrackArtists()`) uses that when present and falls back to a single `artistId`/`artist` entry otherwise. New shared primitive `ArtistLinks` (`primitives/artistLinks/`) renders no wrapper of its own, drops into any existing `<span>`/`<p>`/`<h2>`/`motion.p` in place of the old `{track.artist}` text, rendering each artist as a real `<button>` (`navigate('/artist/' + id)`, always `stopPropagation()`) joined by ", ", or the plain fallback string when no ids are known. `track.tsx`'s row changed from a single `<button>` to a `<div role="button" tabIndex={0}>` (manual Enter/Space handling) since a real nested button doesn't focus/activate reliably inside another real `<button>`, same div-as-button + stopPropagation pattern already used by `player.tsx`'s mini-player and `continuum.tsx`'s `SideCover`. `veloraPlaybackController.ts` turned out to have its own **separate** `mapTrack()` for server-pushed queue/currentTrack/resume state (parallel to `veloraProvider.ts`'s, not derived from it), missed in the initial pass, which meant the player bar/sidebar/BigMusic/queue (everything sourced from `playbackService` rather than directly from `musicService`) stayed unlinked while playlist/track-list views worked; fixed by mirroring the same one-entry `artists` population there. One known gap: `VeloraProvider.getUserStats()`'s inline `recentlyListened` mapping (feeds Home Overview) has no `artistId` in its `RecentSessionDto` at all, that endpoint's backend DTO would need a field added to support linking; left as a plain-text fallback (graceful, not broken) rather than touching the backend for this pass.

- **Clickable album column (2026-07-17).** The album name in track rows links to `/album/:albumId` like `ArtistLinks` does for artists. New `Track.albumId?` (`ImusicProvider.ts`), mapped from `dto.albumId` in `veloraTrack.ts` and `s.albumId` in `subsonicProvider.mapTrack`, left undefined for local (album ids are `albumKey` but single-track "albums" are filtered by `HAVING COUNT(*)>1`, so a link would 404; plain text is correct there). New shared primitive `AlbumLink` (`primitives/albumLink/`, mirrors `ArtistLinks`): renders the name as a `<button>` navigating on click (`stopPropagation` + BigMusic dismiss) when an id is present, plain text otherwise. `Track` gained a `trackAlbumId` prop and renders the album cell (table + legacy) via `AlbumLink`; threaded from `playlist.tsx` (powers `/tracks`, playlist detail, favorites), `searchBar.tsx` (results dropdown), and `artistAlbumsView.tsx` (discography track lists). The sidebar Info panel's album line was the last plain-text album left and now uses the same primitive (2026-08-06), so the header's artist and album lines behave alike.
- **Favorite column (2026-07-15).** Toggleable trailing heart column in the shared track table (`"favorite"` added to `TrackColumnKey`, last in `TRACK_COLUMNS` so it stays rightmost, default on). Each table-mode row renders a reused `FavoriteButton` wired to `useSession` favorites; the header is a static outline heart; toggled from the `tune` dropdown's Columns group like the other columns. Rows + header reserve a `--playlist-action-col` gutter (+ shared `--padding-xs` insets) so the heart lines up left of the floating tune button. `tune` groups (Display/Size/Columns) now split by dividers.

- **Recent searches (2026-07-19).** `usePaletteRecents` grew `searches` (persisted, most-recent-first, case-insensitive dedupe keeping the newest casing, capped at 8) + `recordSearch`/`removeSearch`/`clearSearches`, same store as the palette's last-command recall, no second mechanism. `/search` records a query only once it settles with at least one result (a typo isn't worth offering back) and shows the full set as a chip card under an empty field: per-chip remove ×, a "Clear" link in the header, click re-runs the query (`SearchBar` is keyed on `rawQuery` there so the field refills, `initialQuery` is seed-only). The `SearchBar` dropdown shows the top 4 as history rows whenever the field is empty (home + topbar get it for free). i18n `search.recent`/`clearRecent`/`removeRecent` in all 6 locales.

- **Undo on playlist removal (2026-07-19).** Removing tracks from a playlist now toasts "Removed N tracks" with an **Undo** button. No command-history stack: the toast's `action` re-adds through the existing optimistic `addTracksToPlaylist`, so undo is just the inverse mutation (server appends, so restored tracks land at the end, playlists have no user-controlled order UI anyway). `useLibrary.removeTrackFromPlaylist(id, trackId)` was replaced by `removeTracksFromPlaylist(id, tracks[])`, one path for the context menu (`[track]`) and `SelectionBar` (which stopped looping single removals), so a bulk remove is one toast instead of N. Partial failure is honest: the optimistic pass and the post-failure correction share one `apply(removed)` helper built off a snapshot of that one playlist (current state elsewhere, so a long remove doesn't revert unrelated edits), so only the tracks that actually failed come back, and that case toasts the failure instead of an undo (toasts are newest-first, so a second toast would surface the error after the success it contradicts). The toast primitive gained `actionLabel`, which renders a `textHyperLink--inline` Button inside the pill (fills the pill's height under `pointer: coarse` for a 44px target, inset focus ring since the pill clips overflow, `stopPropagation` on pointer-down so the pill's drag-to-dismiss doesn't eat the click, and the pill's Enter/Space handler ignores keys bubbling from it); with a label present, tapping the pill body only dismisses, so an undo can't fire twice. Unlabelled `action` toasts (the update prompt) keep tap-to-activate. Delete-track is deliberately not undoable, the file is gone.
  - ↳ files: `src/store/library.ts`, `src/store/toast.ts`, `src/assets/components/primitives/toast/toast.tsx` + `.css`, `src/utils/trackMenu.ts`, `src/assets/components/ui/playlist/selectionBar.tsx`; `contextMenu.track.removedFromPlaylist_one/_other` + `contextMenu.track.undo` in all 6 locales

- **Upload overlay redesign (2026-08-05).** The dialog was one permanent 2px dashed accent rectangle over a list of nested cards, and it answered "what is this file doing" without ever answering "how far along is the batch". Reshaped into two states of one surface. **Header** carries the batch: a live `{{done}} of {{total}} · {{pct}}%` line, a danger-tinted failed count beside it, the pause/resume the store always had but only the nav pill exposed, and its own bottom hairline doubling as the progress rail (scaled, not resized, so a chunk from any of the 3 concurrent uploads doesn't relayout the header). **Dropzone** keeps its full height whether or not a queue is behind it (a collapse-when-busy variant was built and rejected: the card is given the room instead); at rest it's a quiet dashed hairline and only takes the accent while a file is actually over the card, since accent is state and "idle" is not one. **Rows** flattened off `uiContentContainer` (a second 80px-blur surface per row bought no hierarchy inside a card that already had one) onto `--fill-subtle`, each with a tone-coded 28px glyph tile per status so `duplicate` stops reading as a failure, and the row's own background is the progress bar. Fixes along the way: the **whole card accepts a drop**, not just the dashed box, with the backdrop `preventDefault`ing so a near-miss can't navigate the tab away; the queue is its own scroll container so the dropzone stays reachable under a long list; the destination label moved above its field (inline, it put the caret in the middle of the control); the body scrolls rather than clipping when the window is at its 480px minimum height; deprecated `.text-*` utilities swapped for `caption`/`caption-small` + `font-semiBold` subtext; `--radius-lg` and `useSprings().notch` per the §14.4 centered-modal canon; and the modal gained `useBackButtonDismiss` + a focus trap, `onMouseDown` dismissal so a drag-select ending on the backdrop can't discard a typed destination. `useFocusTrap` (`src/utils/useFocusTrap.ts`) extracted from `Dialog` and used by both. Dev panel → Simulate → Upload queue seeds all-states / 60 rows / animated progress / empty. i18n `upload.{dropNow,summaryActive,summaryFinished,summaryFailed}` in all 9 locales.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/uploadOverlay/uploadOverlay.tsx` + `.css`, `src/utils/useFocusTrap.ts` (new), `src/assets/components/primitives/dialog/Dialog.tsx`, `src/assets/components/ui/devTools/DevToolsPanel.tsx`

- **Search bar rebuilt around a cursor (2026-08-06).** The dropdown moved DOM focus onto a row to arrow through it, so reaching a result meant leaving the field, and every keystroke tore the list down to "Searching…" and rebuilt it. It now runs the same model as its sibling the command palette: the input keeps focus and an `activeIndex` cursor walks a single flat row list, hover moves that same cursor (one highlight, never two), the cursor scrolls itself into view, and the field is wired as a real `role="combobox"` with `aria-activedescendant` over a `role="listbox"` (`SearchInput` gained one optional `combobox` prop for it; rows are `role="option"`, `tabIndex -1`, and `preventDefault` their mousedown so the caret never leaves). **Enter's destination is now visible**: an "All results for X" row pinned first with its own `↵` chip, so what the top row does is what the key does, dropped once a query is known to match nothing. Results are **held across keystrokes** and a sticky accent scan line at the panel's top edge says it's still fetching, instead of the list collapsing and jumping. A failed search renders `ErrorState` + retry rather than reading as "no results" (the /search view already made that distinction; the bar didn't). Recents are removable in place (hover ×, always visible on touch, `Delete` on the cursor row) with a Clear link in the section header. All four result kinds render through one row component, so the list reads as one system: tracks lost the full `Track` grid (heavy for a preview, and it forced an invalid `role="button"` inside the listbox) and gained a duration, an equalizer mark on the row that is already playing, and circular artist covers. Panel: the shared `--panel-surface` recipe instead of a hand-rolled `blur(100px) brightness(50%) !important` that overrode reduce-transparency and darkened the light theme, plus a token-driven entrance, `dvh` cap, and `Tab`-out closing it. `.searchPageContainer` dropped its `overflow: hidden` (searchBody owns the page scroll), which was shaving the field's right hairline at fractional widths and clipping the bar's own dropdown. i18n `search.seeAll` in all 9 locales.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/primitives/searchBar/searchBar.tsx` + `.css`, `src/assets/components/primitives/searchInput/searchInput.tsx`, `src/screens/views/searchView/searchView.css`

- **Search page fills itself when empty (2026-09-30).** An empty query showed one card of text chips and nothing else. It now shows three things. **Recent searches** as cards: every result opened from a search (the /search view or the bar's dropdown) is saved as `{ kind, id, title, subtitle, cover }` in `paletteRecents.opened` (12, most recent first, deduped by kind + id) and drawn as a mixed `CarouselSection` row. Subtitles start with the kind ("Song · Artist"), artists are circles, and tracks play in place through `usePlayTrackNow`. Right-click removes one. The typed queries sit under the cards as chips, and one Clear wipes both. **More like X**: `getSimilarSongs` seeded by the last track opened from search, or the one playing when the page opened (held, so playing from the row does not reseed it), gated on `smartRadio`. **Genres**: `HomeGenres` reused, gated on `genreBrowsing`. With nothing to show, a quiet `search.intro` caption. The block stays mounted (`hidden`) under a query, so clearing the field doesn't refetch. `CarouselSection` gained `footer` and skips the carousel when it has no children. `PlaylistCard` gained `onOpen`. Recents are now cleared on logout, because a Subsonic cover url carries the auth token.
  - ↳ files: `src/screens/views/searchView/` (`searchRecents.tsx`, `searchMoreLike.tsx` new), `src/store/paletteRecents.ts`, `src/assets/components/primitives/searchBar/searchBar.tsx`, `src/utils/useLogout.ts`; i18n `search.{removeOpened,moreLike,intro,kind.*}` in all 9 locales

- **Dropped: "Fresh" badges (2026-10-01).** An accent dot on albums added since the last visit. Dropped by choice before any work landed; it would have needed an `addedAt` on `Album` that the Velora backend does not store.

- **List layout for library pages (2026-10-02).** The density toggle on /albums, /artists, /playlists and /radio gained a third option, `list`: one horizontal row per item, cover beside title and subtitle, several columns of rows on wide screens. Comfortable is hidden below `md`, and a stored `comfortable` reads as `list` there (`useLibraryView`), so phones open on the list while desktop keeps comfortable.
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/gridView.ts`, `src/assets/components/ui/libraryPage/` (`LibraryPage.tsx`, `libraryPage.css`), `src/screens/views/radioView/radioView.css`; i18n `grid.list` in all 9 locales

- **Rename a playlist in place (2026-10-05).** Double-click the playlist title (a hold on touch) to edit it in the header; Enter or leaving the field saves, Escape cancels. Same optimistic `renamePlaylist` as the edit modal, offered only on the user's own playlists (not favorites, all-songs or folder-synced ones). `DetailHeader` takes an optional `onRename`, so any detail view can opt in.
  - ↳ files: `primitives/detailHeader/` (`DetailHeader.tsx` `DetailTitle`, `detailHeader.css`), `playlistView.tsx`; i18n `playlist.renameHint`

- **Better empty playlists (2026-10-05).** An empty playlist opens on a filler panel instead of a bare empty state: a library search, recently played (`userStats`) and random suggestions (`randomSongs`), as the track list's own `PlaylistRow` (exported for it: user columns, heart, swipes, menu, preview, click plays) plus a round add button in a `trailing` cell that pops into an accent check (a removal here is quiet: `removeTracksFromPlaylist(..., { quiet })`). Recents re-read on open and after each track change. A live "N added" line, a refresh for suggestions, skeleton rows while loading, search focused on desktop. It stays up while songs are added, until Done.
  - ↳ files: `playlistView/playlistFiller.tsx` + `.css`, `playlistView.tsx` (`fillingId` latch), `ui/playlist/playlist.tsx` (`PlaylistRow`), `primitives/track/track.tsx` (`trailing`); i18n `playlist.fill.*`
- **Lyrics off the Track objects (2026-10-08, `tmp/perf-audit.html` M1).** Velora and local list mappings no longer copy full LRC text onto every Track (queue, favourites, playlist details incl. `all-songs`, plugin copies); `stats.lyrics` is gone from the type. `useTrackLyrics` fetches through `getLyrics` with one shared lookup per track and a 50-entry LRU that also remembers "no lyrics" (a thrown fetch is not remembered; Subsonic/Jellyfin report errors as null, so theirs is); `forgetLyrics` drops one track after a lyrics edit and all on logout. `EditTrackModal` and the desktop API fetch lyrics on demand.

## 3. BigMusic Overlay
- **Overlay chrome is the real topbar (2026-07-19).** The overlay used to mount bare `WindowControls floating`, whose full-width drag strip and caption buttons landed straight on the docked sidebar's tabs. It now re-mounts `<Topbar overlay />` instead, so BigMusic gets the same clock, greeting, now-playing, search and (on Electron) nav arrows + titlebar drag as the rest of the app. The visibility rule moved out of `mainPage.tsx` into an exported `useTopbarVisible()` so both call sites can't drift. The overlay projects the bar's height as `--bm-topbar`, which the close button and the portalled sidebar's header offset by; the dedicated close button is dropped on Electron, where the topbar's back arrow already closes the overlay (web keeps it, it has no arrow).
- **Control-visibility UX (2026-07-15).** Hovering the lyrics-mode controls no longer idle-hides them (`useIdleHide` gained a `hold`), and a hotkey fired while the controls are hidden flashes a center HUD icon (`BigMusicHud` + `actionFeedback` store, pulsed from `useKeybindDispatch` and the desktop global-favorite handler) so the input is visibly confirmed. Cover context menu shipped the same day, see §21.
- 6 modes: Big Cover, Typographic (lyrics), Vinyl, Editorial, Continuum, Polaroid Wall
- `MODE_REGISTRY` pattern for adding new modes
- Idle auto-activate (configurable) + idle cursor auto-hide
- Sidebar-aware layout offsets per mode
- Shared transport controls + video playback across all modes
- **Conditional mode by lyrics** (2026-07-15): opt-in `bigMusicModeByLyrics` in `useSettings` with `bigMusicModeLyrics` (default `lyrics`) / `bigMusicModeNoLyrics` (default `bigCover`); `bigMusic.tsx` resolves `effectiveMode` off `useTrackLyrics(modeByLyrics ? track : null)` (hook stays inert when off, no extra fetch) and feeds it into the built-in/plugin mode resolution. Both pickers reuse `useBigMusicModeOptions()` so plugin modes are selectable and an unavailable pick falls back to bigCover like the single pick. Settings → Appearance → Now Playing: toggle hides the single mode picker and reveals two child pickers; i18n in all 6 locales.
- **Hide sidebar in BigMusic** (2026-09-29): opt-in `bigMusicHideSidebar` closes the docked sidebar when the overlay opens and reopens it on exit, only if it closed it; a `useBigMusic.subscribe` in `store/bigMusic.ts`. Settings → Appearance → Now Playing.
- **Close BigMusic when the queue ends** (2026-09-29): opt-in `bigMusicCloseOnQueueEnd` leaves the overlay when the last track stops with nothing after it (same end state from both controllers: last track kept, stopped, rewound to 0); a playback subscription held only while the overlay is open, in `store/bigMusic.ts`. Settings → Appearance → Now Playing.
- **Mobile-only modes** (2026-09-30): `MODE_REGISTRY` entries carry an optional `platform`; `useBigMusicModeOptions` filters on `useIsMobile`, so every picker, the swipe and the palette follow. Big Cover, Vinyl, Editorial, Continuum and Polaroid Wall are desktop-only; **Pocket** (cover + title on top, transport centered above the timeline) is the mobile default. The shared mobile controls (`BigMusicMobileControls`, used by Pocket and Typographic) are transport, timeline, then one line of shuffle/repeat/favorite + toggles, the toggles folding into a more menu when the line is too narrow. `resolveBigMusicMode` shows an unoffered pick as the form factor's default without rewriting the setting.
- **Mobile mode shell + three modes** (2026-09-30): Pocket's layout is `BigMusicMobileShell` (`bigMusic/bigMusicMobile/`), a grid whose stage box, transport and timeline placement are defaults a mode restates under its own class. Typographic's mobile form moved onto it (lyrics fill down to the transport). New mobile modes **Deck** (playing cover on a stack of the next queue covers, tap one to jump), **Swatch** (paint-chip card of the cover's three colors on a field of its dominant one) and **Nightstand** (quiet now-playing line on top, big clock in the middle). Tapping empty space hides the transport and toggle row while a video plays (always in Nightstand), the timeline dropping into their place and the video dim fading out. The favorite sits beside the title in every mobile mode except Swatch (bottom row, no room on the chips).
- **Mobile lyrics toggle** (2026-09-30): Typographic is desktop-only now. On mobile a lyrics button in the bottom row (only when the track has lyrics, folds into the more menu with the other toggles) swaps any mode's stage for the lyric column (`LyricsBody`, shared with Typographic) under the lifted title line. The choice lives in `useBigMusic.mobileLyrics`, so it survives swiping modes and closing the overlay.
- **Lyrics in every mode, Typographic retired** (2026-10-05): the lyrics toggle works on desktop too, in the transport's utility row of every mode. Desktop swaps the whole mode for `lyricsView/` (Typographic's layout: top bar, lyric column, controls); mobile still swaps only the stage. `useBigMusic.lyrics` is the shared flag and `ctx.lyrics` carries the track's lyrics, fetched once while the overlay is open. New `bigMusicLyricsStyle` (default `typographic`, plus the five sidebar looks through the `Lyrics` primitive, whose sizes are em so BigMusic scales them). Editorial's own lyric overlay went with it so every mode follows the style. Dropped: the Typographic mode (a stored `lyrics` becomes `bigCover`) and the pick-mode-by-lyrics settings (`bigMusicModeByLyrics` and its two pickers), both made pointless by the toggle.

## 4. Backgrounds & Visuals
- **Separate full-screen background (2026-10-06).** Appearance → Background: a "Separate full-screen background" toggle (off by default) and its own style picker. While BigMusic is open the one shared `<Background>` swaps to that style, so there is still one WebGL context; games keep the app style. Tweaks are per style, and Customize shows a labelled block for each style on screen. The per-view idea was cut to app + BigMusic: a settings-view background was dropped as not wanted.
  - ↳ files: `src/settings.tsx`, `screens/pages/mainPage/mainPage.tsx`, `settingsView/useSettingsSections.ts`, `utils/userDataExport.ts` + `userDataScopes.ts`, 4 keys ×9 locales
- 9 WebGL/CSS backgrounds (gradient, aurora, prismaticBurst, iridescence, blobs, lightPillar, silk, pixelBlast, beams)
- **Per-background tweak settings (2026-07-14).** Appearance → "Customize background" (advanced, collapsed behind a Show/Hide button like the animated-icons cherry-pick; the FPS/resolution rows are advanced now too): 1–4 knobs per background (speed everywhere; gradient warp/grain, aurora wave height/blend, prismatic motion style (Orbit/Spin)/intensity/distortion, light pillar rotation/width/glow, silk+beams scale/noise/rotation, pixelBlast shape/size/density, nebula blob count/drift speed/softness blur) + a per-background Reset. Defs registry `src/assets/backgrounds/backgroundTweaks.ts` (defaults = the old hardcoded look), overrides-only persisted in `useSettings.backgroundTweaks`, applied live through each background's existing prop→uniform sync (no remounts; nebula gained blobCount/speed/blur props). Gotchas: settingsBox keys rows by translated label, so a tweak label must not duplicate another row in the same section (duplicate AnimatePresence keys leave ghost rows, hence "Speed"/"Pixel density", not "Animation speed"/"Density"); child-row collapse clips dropdowns, so choice tweaks render as inline switchers; `SettingsSlider` now follows external value changes while not dragging (row reuse across styles + Reset); `resolveTweaks` drops a persisted select value whose option no longer exists. **Pointer-reactive knobs were cut** (follow-pointer, iridescence wobble = pointer displacement only, prismatic "Pointer" motion, pixelBlast click-ripples): the background layer sits behind the app chrome and never receives pointer events, and rewiring the components' listeners to `window` broke pixelBlast rendering, decided not worth the work; don't expose pointer-driven background features without solving that first.
- **"Image / Video" background style (2026-08-07, desktop only).** A picture, GIF or video of the user's own drawn where a shader background would be. Settings → Appearance → Background: the style select gains "Image / Video" (`backgroundOptions()` filters it out where the bridge is absent, and `migrateBackgroundStyle` falls a persisted "media" back to nebula in the web app, so the picker can never sit on a dead value), then a Choose/Replace row showing the file's name + size and a danger Remove row. Fit (fill/fit) / Dim / Blur are ordinary `backgroundTweaks` entries, so they inherit the existing Customize collapse and Reset. **The renderer never holds the file**, which is the whole reason it is desktop-only: a background can be a 300 MB video, so `electron/backgroundMedia.ts` picks it through the native dialog, copies it into `userData/background/media.<ext>` beside a small manifest, and serves it back over `vmedia://background/media`; the renderer gets metadata + a url. Nothing is persisted in the renderer at all (`store/backgroundMedia.ts`, read once from main at boot), so no profile export can carry a filename whose bytes only exist on one machine. Gotchas: the shared `MEDIA_MIME` map answers `.mp4` with **audio**/mp4 (local mode's files are audio) and a `<video>` handed that plays sound over a blank frame, so a background resolves its own content type; mkv is kept out of the dialog because Chromium can't decode it, and accepting it would look like a bug rather than a refusal; the frame is mounted on the settings toggle rather than on `active`, so a hidden tab pauses the video instead of tearing it down and restarting the loop; a video holds on its first frame under reduce-motion (a GIF can't be frozen without re-decoding, so it keeps playing); blur grows the layer by `1 + blur/120` because a blur samples past the edges and would show the page through them; the dim scrim stays `#000` in every theme, like the scrim tokens, since the amount is the user's and no token can express it; the video needs `preload="auto"`, since a video that is never played (reduce-motion, or a window still hidden at mount) stops at HAVE_METADATA, never fires `loadeddata` and leaves the canvas empty. The FPS/resolution rows stay visible for this style, the canvas loop reads both. `mainPage` hands `Background` the plain settings toggle now instead of folding window visibility into it, otherwise a minimize unmounted the video rather than pausing it. Onboarding's background switcher leaves it out on purpose (a file dialog mid-setup would leave the preview blank).
  - ↳ files: `electron/backgroundMedia.ts` (new), `electron/main.ts` (ipc + the `background` host in the vmedia handler), `electron/preload.cts`, `src/utils/platform.ts`, `src/store/backgroundMedia.ts` (new), `src/assets/backgrounds/media/` (new), `background.tsx`, `backgroundTweaks.ts`, `mainPage.tsx`, `settings.tsx`, `useSettingsSections.ts`, `commandPalette.tsx`, `onboardingStage.tsx`, all 9 locales
- Audio-reactive background modulation (`--vis-scale` / `--vis-brightness`)
- **New Year's midnight confetti (2026-07-18).** One-shot burst at each device's local 00:00:00 on Jan 1, mounted once in `app.tsx` (in `updateInfra`, outside `<Routes>`) so it fires in any view. `useConfetti` store (`store/confetti.ts`) exposes `fire()`; `NewYearConfetti` arms a single `setTimeout` to the next Jan 1 (guarded against the ~23-day setTimeout overflow, re-armed on next load) with a `velora-nye-confetti-year` localStorage guard so reloads on Jan 1 don't refire. Bursts from a store subscription (event, not derived state), token-colored pieces, skipped entirely under reduce-motion (JS check + `html[data-reduce-motion]` CSS guard). Also fires on demand via the hidden `confetti`/`party` command-palette verb (`valueCommand.ts` + `commandPalette` value-command item, no help/listing entry).
- Single shared background for the whole app, one WebGL context, lifted above the chrome (`.background_overlay`, z 8999) while BigMusic is open and shown through the transparent overlay, instead of BigMusic mounting a second context. Shader loops pause when offscreen / tab hidden (IntersectionObserver + `visibilitychange`) and reuse cached color buffers (no per-frame `new Color`/`Float32Array`). See `background.tsx` / `mainPage.tsx` / `bigMusic.tsx`.
- **Nebula perf pass (2026-07-14).** Internal render resolution 0.7 → 0.4 default (adaptive range 0.25–0.6), CSS blur fixed at the equivalent constant 70px, per-blob `performance.now()` calls replaced with the rAF timestamp, ~3× less canvas fill work per frame, pixel-identical output. Gotchas: a downscaled-element + `transform: scale(4)` blurred-layer trick (~16× cheaper GPU blur) was tried and reverted, it visibly changed the render on Jenny's setup; keep the blur on the full-size element. A `desynchronized: true` 2d-context hint was also tried and reverted (can push the canvas into a hardware overlay plane that blur/backdrop-filter can't sample).
- **Nebula blur in canvas space (2026-10-07, `tmp/perf-audit.html` G2).** The 70px CSS `filter` + 0.95 `opacity` on the full-viewport canvas are gone: blobs draw into a buffer at the internal resolution and one `drawImage` with `ctx.filter` (blur scaled by the resolution, saturate 1.1) and `globalAlpha` 0.95 puts them on screen. Measured against the old path in Edge at DPR 1/2/3: max 3/255 per channel, mean 0.3, so it is not the reverted `scale(4)` trick above. CSS filter stays as the fallback where `ctx.filter` is missing.
- **WebGL background leak fixes (2026-10-07, from `tmp/perf-audit.html` G1/G6/G11).** PixelBlast never disposed on unmount (an early-return cleanup) and cancelled only its first frame id, so every hide/restore left a live loop and context; it now builds one `dispose()` used by reinit and an unmount-only effect. PixelBlast drops MSAA by default and `powerPreference: high-performance` (LightPillar too). silk/beams/LightPillar share one `webglSupported()` in `backgroundQuality.ts` that frees its probe context and caches only a pass.

- **The nav could hide playlists until a reload (2026-09-13).** `useNavRowWindow` measured its row stride once, on the layout pass the list mounted, and then only re-measured when the *container's* box changed. A stale stride is not cosmetic in a windowed list: the spacers are sized `start * rowSize` while the mounted rows stand at their real height, so the two describe lists of different length, the scroll offset maps to the wrong index, and rows can be scrolled straight past without ever mounting. Nothing in the session recovered it, which is the "a reload sometimes fixes it" half of the report. Two halves to the fix. The observer watches the **sampled row** as well as the container, re-pointed as the window moves (assign before observing, or a synchronous delivery re-enters on the stale sample and recurses). And the stride is read from `offsetTop`/`offsetLeft`, not from a rect: **a rect includes transforms, and `Reorder.Item` animates every list change on one**, so a measure landing mid-animation read a stride that nothing ever re-fired to correct. Offsets round to whole pixels, which the 10-row overscan absorbs.
  **It was still happening, because the hooks outlived the element they were bound to.** Nav returns the mobile tab bar from an early `return` (`isMobile && !buttons`), so below 768px the component itself never unmounts: every hook keeps running while the scroll container under it is destroyed and, on the way back up, rebuilt. `useNavRowWindow` and `useHorizontalWheel` took `RefObject`s and read `.current` inside effects keyed on deps that do not change across that swap, so they stayed bound to the **old detached node** for the rest of the session. Nothing heard the new container scroll, the window stayed parked at the offset the old one ended on, and every row above that offset was unreachable by any amount of scrolling: one trip through mobile width and the playlists were gone until a reload. Both hooks take the **live element** now (a `useState` setter used directly as the callback ref in `nav.tsx`), so React re-runs the effect the moment the node is replaced. The layout pass also reads the scroll offset alongside the box, because a container that was just built always starts at the top and no scroll event ever fires to say so, so it is corrected before the frame is painted rather than one frame into it.
  - ↳ files: `ui/nav/useNavRowWindow.ts` + `tests/components/ui/nav/useNavRowWindow.test.ts` (an element-scoped `ResizeObserver` stub, so a hook watching only the container fails it; a replaced-container case, so a hook holding a ref fails it), `ui/nav/nav.tsx`, `utils/useHorizontalWheel.ts` + `tests/utils/horizontalWheel.test.ts`

One behaviour change fell out of the merge: the keyboard path calls `preventDefault` before the bounds check now, so a row that cannot move no longer changes the volume instead (bare Up/Down are the volume binds and `useGlobalShortcuts` matches on `window` without reading `defaultPrevented`).

The source row dims to `.35` (`.trackDragging`, toggled on the element by the drag util) so the chip reads as that row lifted out, not a copy. Position comes from a document-level `dragover` straight into motion values, so following the cursor never re-renders; the in-flight track + armed flag are a `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot in `trackDrag.ts` (the ghost lives outside the list, and a virtualized source row can unmount mid-drag). Armed is a **counter**, not a boolean: crossing straight from one target into another fires the new target's `dragenter` before the old one's `dragleave`. Release is triple-covered for the same virtualization reason (a `dragend` dispatched at a detached source reaches nothing): the source node, a `document` capture listener, and `releaseTrackDrag()` from the hook's `onDrop`, which must run **after** `readTrack(e)` since it clears the payload. Pointer leaving the window fades the chip out rather than freezing it at the edge. New `lift`/`trail` house springs (`utils/springs.ts`). **There is deliberately no spring on the chip's position, and that is the whole design.** A single spring's stiffness is both how tightly it tracks and how fast it settles, so tight tracking always buys a snappy settle and a fluid settle always buys felt lag; every intermediate tuning of one spring was rejected on feel, from both ends. Instead the position is `pointer + lead`, where `lead` is a saturated share of the gap between the pointer and `trail` (0.35s, bounce 0.3), a slow copy that renders nothing. The chip therefore sits exactly on the cursor at rest, rides *ahead* of it while moving (never behind, so there is nothing to read as lag), and flows back onto it over the trail's much longer settle when the pointer stops, dipping a touch past it first because that spring undershoots on the way back. `MAX_LEAD` is the one knob, and it is the whole effect: at 0 the chip is pinned to the pointer and the trail springs compute nothing. **The chip does not tilt, and that was decided the long way.** Rotation was built and rejected in four forms: linear-off-lag with a hard clamp (snaps, slams into the stop), a spring on the *angle* on top of the position spring (arrives after the motion that caused it, wags on stop), an arctangent lean off sideways movement, and a vertical see-saw in *both* directions. The vertical ones are the instructive failure: a hanging object swings from horizontal acceleration, while vertical acceleration only changes its effective weight, so there is no sideways force for the eye to attribute the turn to and it reads as the card rotating on its own. Weight belongs in where the chip sits, not in how it is turned. **The lean has no spring of its own**, and both wrong answers were tried: driving rotation linearly off the gap with a hard clamp snaps over and slams into the stop, and springing the *angle* on top of a springed position (two cascaded springs) makes the lean arrive after the motion that caused it and wag when you stop. It's geometry instead, `(2·MAX_TILT/π)·atan((gapX − 0.5·gapY) / 160px)` at 6° max: gentle around zero, easing into its limit with no clamp to hit, growing with speed across the whole range. Vertical movement is in there because the pivot is the chip's **top-left corner**, so its mass hangs to the right and an up/down shove torques it through that lever arm (halved, since dragging down a track list is the app's most common motion and shouldn't rock the card). Clockwise is correct for the trailing lean, same corner-pivot geometry. reduce-motion reads the raw pointer value instead of the spring, so no lag, no swing, no entrance. **The one surface in the app with no `backdrop-filter`**, and the reason is worth keeping: a backdrop re-samples whatever it crosses every frame, and crossing Velora's blurred chrome over a WebGL background made the chip visibly laggy. It's solid instead (`linear-gradient(--color-ui, --color-ui)` over `--color-background`, `!important` to beat the per-theme `.uiContentContainer` rules), which also reads as more opaque and more visible. Don't put a moving element on a blurred surface. No new i18n keys, the chip shows track data and is `aria-hidden` (a pointer-only, desktop-only gesture).

Restore is retried whenever `itemCount` grows (capped at 5 attempts), because a virtualized list only has the height to scroll into once its rows exist and a paged list like /tracks needs several pages before a deep offset is reachable; saving is paused until the restore settles, otherwise the clamped scrollTop would overwrite the target mid-restore.   - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/primitives/logoutButton/`, `src/utils/useLogout.ts`, `src/assets/components/ui/nav/nav.{tsx,css}`, `src/screens/views/settingsView/settingsView.tsx`, `src/utils/{cssIcons.ts,useKeybindDispatch.ts}`, `commandPalette.tsx`, all 9 locales
  - **Press and hold skips the confirm (2026-08-09).** A 600ms hold is its own confirmation, so `useConfirmedLogout().requestLogout(skipConfirm)` takes the guarded path only on a click; the hold fills the button with a danger sweep for its whole length and tears it down the moment the pointer lifts or leaves. The window is a fixed constant rather than a `--duration-*` token on purpose: it is an input timing, and a user who set animations to fast did not ask for a shorter hold. The completed hold's `pointerup` still fires a click, which would re-open the very confirm the hold just skipped, hence the one-shot swallow ref. Under reduce-motion the sweep lands flat instead of growing, and a keyboard user keeps the confirm, which is the safe default. i18n `nav.logoutHoldHint` ×9.
- **New Playlist is one control too (2026-08-05).** The logout extraction's twin: create was hand-rolled at three call sites (nav footer, library header, playlists header), each pairing `Button` + `Capable` + `useCreatePlaylist()` on its own, so the folded nav's `"+"` had no accessible name and none of the three had a busy state. It's now `NewPlaylistButton` (`primitives/newPlaylistButton/`) owning the gate, the `aria-label`/`title`, the mark and the pending flag, and `useCreatePlaylist()` returns `{ createPlaylist, pending }` with `pending` covering the create only, never the name prompt: a busy button behind a modal the user is still typing in would be lying about what it's waiting on. The mark stands in for the words and never joins them (Jenny's call, 2026-08-05): the name already says what the button does, so a `"+"` beside it is a second copy of the same word, and the two library headers that used to carry one dropped it. Folded, the mark is the whole button. Busy stays lit rather than greying out (the click did land) and the mark pulses, guarded by `html[data-reduce-motion]`. In the nav, create keeps the accent fill and gains the 1px accent hairline that makes its height equal logout's bordered bar, and the geometry rule the pair shares moved to a `.navNewPlaylistBtn` hook so the shared shape no longer depends on the primitive's own class name. Nav labels also came down to the app's body size (0.9rem) instead of `Button`'s baked-in `size-1`. i18n `nav.creatingPlaylist` ×9.

- **The folded rail, named and sized; the list stops ending on a cut (2026-08-05).** Four gaps the nav's own rows had that its two footer buttons had already fixed. **Names:** `Button` renders its icon with `alt=""` on purpose (a visible label already names the button), and `buildButton` drops the label entirely when folded, so a folded nav was a column of unnamed marks with no tooltip and nothing for a screen reader. Rows now carry `aria-label` when folded and `title` when folded **or** when they're a playlist row, since a playlist name truncates at any nav width. **Touch:** a folded built-in is a lone glyph in a box `.navFoldedButtons` only ever gave `padding-inline`, so it takes the 44px floor under `pointer: coarse`. Growing it on a mouse was built and rejected the same day (Jenny's call, 2026-08-05): the rail's proportions are deliberate, small glyphs over big covers included. **Edges:** the scrolling list cut hard at both ends, so a half-covered row read as the last one. It fades now, the same device `CarouselSection` uses (designsystemV2 §14.5), and scroll-driven with no handler and no re-render: two `@property` lengths animate against `scroll(self)` with `animation-range` over the first and last 20px, so the top fade only exists once you've scrolled and the bottom one retires at the end. A list too short to scroll leaves the timeline inactive and stays at the `0px` initial values, which is exactly why this can't be a static mask; `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())` keeps the plain cut everywhere else, and the horizontal top/bottom strip gets the same rule on the inline axis. **Empty:** a loaded-but-empty list said nothing and read as still loading; it now renders the shared `EmptyState` with the existing `empty.playlists` key (unfolded column only, the rail has no room for words), gated on the store's `loaded` and not just an empty row list: the skeleton branch is `loading && !loaded`, so on the first commit, before the load effect runs, neither flag is set and the message would flash ahead of the fetch. Also deleted the empty `.navContainerFolded {}`. A playlist filter was built alongside this and cut on Jenny's call, no new i18n keys survive.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/nav/nav.{tsx,css}`
- **The name prompt reads like the thing it names (2026-08-05).** The pill that names a playlist wore the confirm's one-line radius while standing three rows tall, and its field was a thin slot that a short title could size down to nothing. `Dialog` now takes an optional `className` (still one shell, no fork) and the prompt uses it to step the radius down a rung to `--radius-lg` (`--radius-md` under 480px), per designsystemV2 §8. The field is the house input at its real metrics: a `<label>` so the whole box is the target, 44px min-height on every pointer, `--padding-sm`/`--padding-md`, a hover fill to match the rest of the control family, and the value typed `font-bold` since it is about to be a title (the placeholder stays 400 so it doesn't read as filled). The form carries `min-width: min(320px, 100%)` so a two-word title can't shrink the pill below a typable width. Input hygiene: `maxLength` at 100 but never below the length handed in, so renaming an over-long imported playlist stays editable rather than delete-only; `autoComplete`/`autoCorrect`/`spellCheck` off and `enterKeyHint="done"`; `max(16px, 1rem)` on coarse pointers, a floor that stops iOS zooming the app on focus without shrinking the field for anyone on a larger text scale. The four `promptForName` callers that opened a blank field now pass the existing `playlist.namePlaceholder`.

## 6. Settings & Personalization
- **Primary button only on floater drags (2026-10-09).** A middle or right press on a settings rail category, the popped settings header or its resize grip no longer pops or picks the panel up; `useDragPosition` guards `e.button`, so `StyleMenu` is covered too.

Replaces About's Clear cache, which never touched covers, and Local Library's second waveform button. Settings and login are never cleared; Electron's HTTP cache is left to Chromium. Also palette rows, no keybinds. **Replaces the planned Accent lock**: applying a snapshot freezes the accent, so a separate `accentLock` state was dropped.

Moving any band, from the curve or the palette's `eq:` command, forks the playing preset into Custom via `setEq`; `customEq` keeps that curve while another preset plays. - **Favorite hotkey chime (2026-09-29).** The OS-level `toggleFavoriteTrack` shortcut (never the in-app keybind, the heart shows that one) plays a short synthesized chime, rising on favorite and falling on unfavorite (`utils/favoriteChime.ts`, its own `AudioContext` so the engine's EQ/volume never color it). `favoriteSound` in Playback → Behavior, desktop only, on by default, with five sounds under `favoriteSoundStyle` (chime, pop, retro, bell, heartbeat; picking one previews it); the player and BigMusic hearts carry the `favorite` style target, so right-click opens the toggle.
- **OLED screen care (2026-09-11).** Two opt-in halves under Appearance → Screen Care, both CSS-only once armed (`utils/useScreenCare.ts`, `index.css`). *Pixel shift* steps the app through a four-point ring of 1-6px once a minute, so no static element stays lit in one place. The transform is on `#root`, not on `body`: a transform is the containing block for every fixed descendant, so shifting `body` would move each overlay portalled to it by the shift a second time, on top of the shift already baked into the rect it was placed from, and a menu would open that far from the cursor for as long as the setting is on. Portals are siblings of `#root`, so a box measured after a step is still placed where it was measured. The one thing that outlives a step is a `position: fixed` plugin frame, and a transform fires neither a resize nor a scroll, so the step announces itself (`RELAYOUT_EVENT`) and `frame/useFramePlacement.ts` re-follows its placeholder. It only exists while armed, for the same containing-block reason, and `shiftPx` is clamped where it is read, since an edited profile reaches that var directly and a large enough one would translate the app off screen along with the settings to undo it. One step a minute is also what keeps it clear of the continuously-animating-surface law (goals.md live traps). The one cost of the `#root` target is that a transform is a stacking context, so while the shift is armed the fixed chrome inside `#root` that sits at `--z-overlay` (the window drag strip, the toast, the drag ghost) paints under a body-portalled menu or sheet instead of over it. That is cheaper than a menu opening a shift away from the cursor, and it only exists for a user who armed the setting. *Idle dim* fades a black `html[data-screen-care]::after` scrim in after 1-10 minutes without input and clears on any move or key; a scrim, never `filter: brightness()`, which as an ancestor filter is a backdrop root and would unfrost every surface in the app while dimmed. Both transitions ride `--duration-verySlow`, so the animation-speed setting and reduce-motion reach them, and the group rides the appearance export scope.
- **Right-click an element to restyle it (2026-09-04).** Settings had grown past the point where finding the row that shapes a thing was easier than living with it, so the thing itself now offers its own rows: right-click the seek bar and its shape/color pickers open at the cursor. Nothing is declared twice, and that is the whole design. A target is one id in three places, `data-style-target="<id>"` on the element, `target: "<id>"` on every registry row that shapes it (`useSettingsSections`), and a name/icon/owning-category line in `utils/styleTargets.ts`; `useStyleRows` then collects every row carrying that id across **all** sections and prunes it with the same dependency rules the settings page uses, which is why a waveform sub-row hidden there is hidden here, why a target whose rows are all gated away (no peaks, no Layout section on mobile) opens nothing at all, and why `nav` can gather rows that live in two different categories. `ui/styleMenu/` renders them as `SettingsBox` in the `compact` form the pop-out panels already had, plus a header naming the target with a jump into its settings category. `tests/utils/styleTargets.test.ts` scans the three spellings against each other, since nothing at runtime fails loudly when one drifts.
  **Two presentations, one body.** An element whose right-click is free gets a floater: one document `contextmenu` listener places it, so an element opts in with an attribute and imports nothing, and it bails on `defaultPrevented`, which is what makes anything owning its own menu win the gesture. The floater is grabbed by its header (`useDragPosition`, the pop-out panels' hook) and, once dragged, stops being a menu and starts being a box: an outside click no longer dismisses what the user parked, so it keeps a close button and Escape. An element that already owns a menu gets the same body as a **submenu flyout** instead, beside the row like "Add to playlist": `DropdownActionEntry` grew a `panel` that opens exactly like `items` does and renders a surface in place of the rows.
  **Which rows that row shows is the element's call, never the menu's**, and getting that wrong is what the first pass shipped. The entry was built by the entity-scoped menu builders, so a playlist offered tile rows whether it was clicked as a tile on the home page or as a row in the nav, where none of them change anything. Both routes now resolve the target from the DOM through one `styleTargetAt`, and the entry is inserted by `useDropdownTrigger.openFromEvent`, above the first destructive row so a menu's last word stays "delete". Only `openFromEvent`, never `openFromElement`: a right-click asks about the thing under the pointer, while a menu opened from a button is a list of actions and a sort or filter menu has no element to restyle. So the menu builders know nothing about any of this, `Track` and `MediaCard` carry an attribute like every other target, and a nav playlist answers with the nav's rows because that is the surface it sits on.
  Three sharp edges. **The background is the space between surfaces, not everything drawn on it**: its element is the whole views area, so a right-click on a playlist header answered with the wallpaper until `outsideSurfaces` made that target skip anything inside a `.uiContentContainer`, and the detail header was given rows of its own. **A text field keeps its native menu**, or the shortcut would cost copy/paste. **The seek bar no longer scrubs on a right-click** (primary button only), which used to move the song out from under the menu that was opening. Tagged today: the seek bar, player, nav, sidebar, topbar, background, the detail header, the full-screen player, song rows and cards. `styleOnRightClick` in Appearance → Interface is on by default and turns off both routes at the one gate. The narrow-pane row reshaping the pop-out panel had scoped to itself moved to `.settingsNarrowPane` in `SettingLine.css`, so both floaters share it.

  **A target that has nothing to say does not claim the gesture.** Every row of `player`, `sidebar` and `topbar` lives in the Layout section, which is not built below `md`, and the waveform rows only exist for a provider that serves peaks: both routes committed before they knew, so a right-click could suppress the native menu and answer with nothing, and a menu entry could fly out empty. `styleTargetAt` now walks outwards past a target that offers nothing here (`desktopOnly` in the target table, checked with the non-hook `isMobileViewport`), and the seek bar drops its attribute when there are no peaks, so it answers with the player instead. The entry also lands above the divider that opens the destructive group rather than inside it, and carries a divider of its own. Two smaller ones with it: the panel is handed its rows instead of rebuilding the registry once per surface while it is open, and `Dropdown`'s outside-click spares `.settingsSelectDropdown`, so a select inside a flyout can be used at all.
- **Right-click the volume for Audio settings (2026-09-29).** New `audio` style target on the volume control (player, BigMusic sliders, video mode). The Audio section is tagged whole through `withTarget` in `useSettingsSections`, so a new Audio row is reachable from the volume without a tag of its own.
- **The waveform, on two axes (2026-09-04).** The seek waveform was one flat accent, so a song's shape carried nothing but its envelope. It now has a **shape** and a **color**, and that split is the point: the shape is the look, the color is a sub-setting of whichever shape is picked. A first pass had five "looks" (classic, spectrum, heat, trail, ribbon) and never shipped, because four of them were the same silhouette in different paint, which is a color choice wearing a look's clothes. Both live in `ui/player/timeline/waveformRenderers.ts` as **two registries**, `WAVEFORM_SHAPES` (`bars`, the original 2px rects at a 3px pitch; `blocks`, 4px stadium-capped bars at a 7px pitch with a 3px floor so a quiet passage still reads chunky instead of collapsing to a hairline; and `ribbon`, one smoothed mirrored body at a 4px pitch) and `WAVEFORM_COLORS` (`solid`, the original single accent; `spectrum`, a horizontal sweep to the app's second accent so how far in you are reads as a hue; `heat`, a vertical ramp cool at the midline and hot at the track's own loudest reach; `trail`, a short sweep anchored at the playhead so the brightest thing on the bar is where you are and it moves with the music). Both are picked in Settings → Appearance → Now Playing under the toggle for the waveform itself, all three only where peaks can be had (the provider's `waveform` capability, or desktop's client-side decode). Every pairing is valid because a shape only builds paths and a color only produces fills, and neither knows the other exists: `drawWave(shape, color, scene)` is the one paint loop in the file, and `bars` + `solid` draws, bar for bar, the waveform that shipped before any of this. Adding a shape or a color is one registry entry plus a string in its union. `blocks` exists because heat used to draw chunkier bars than classic did, and the chunk is **geometry**: letting a color painter carry a step or a bar width would put the look back inside the paint and undo the split, so the weight became its own shape and every color can now be had at either weight. Its rounding is a progressive enhancement, `roundRect` is missing on older Android WebViews and this ships to Capacitor, so the cap falls back to a plain rect and a capless chunky bar is still a chunky bar. Colors never reach a painter as tokens: `.timelineWaveform` carries three channels (`color`, plus `--wave-secondary` / `--wave-hot`, registered with `@property` so the computed value is a resolved color the canvas can read), sampled once per track change and once more when an accent token finishes transitioning, so a theme or a new cover accent moves every combination for free. Two rules hold the cost at or under what the flat default used to pay, and the axis split is what makes them free: `step` is the bar pitch **and** the redraw quantum, so the canvas repaints only when the playhead crosses one bar (never per frame); and every combination pays exactly **two** fills, one `Path2D` of the played run and one of the rest. Color that varies bar to bar is therefore always a gradient, never a `fillStyle` per bar, since assigning `fillStyle` re-parses a color and a wide bar holds ~130 of them. Heat works on both shapes for free because both are drawn from the midline out, so a vertical ramp paints every peak's tip by its own amplitude. The original look, which set one color and flipped `globalAlpha` across ~130 `fillRect` calls, is now two fills like everything else. One trap the ribbon needs: its per-run path samples its far end inclusively (`i <= to`, clamped to the last bucket), or the played body and the unplayed body leave a bar-wide seam at the cut. `tests/utils/waveformRenderers.test.ts` holds all of it over the full shape × color cross product (twelve pairings), failing on any `fillRect`, on a fill/color-parse/gradient budget overrun in any pairing, on the default creating a gradient, on a leaked `globalAlpha`, on `blocks` throwing when `roundRect` is deleted off the engine, and on either key list drifting back toward one merged list of looks.
- **Four more waveform shapes, and an anchor for the colors (2026-09-07).** The shape axis was three silhouettes, two of them teeth and one a body, so the picker still read as one look at three weights. Seven now, and each new one differs in kind rather than in size: **ladder**, the column cut into chips, on a pitch the bar's own height sets so the outermost chip lands flush inside it, so a peak reads as a count of lit segments the way hardware VU does (the middle chip is unconditional, or a quiet passage blinks the column out); **ridge**, the song as terrain, one grounded silhouette with sharp summits standing on the floor instead of mirrored; **trace**, ribbon with the body taken out, two hairlines riding the upper and lower envelope so the song is drawn rather than massed; and **stitch**, one thread laced through it, jumping from the upper envelope to the lower bucket by bucket, so loudness is how wide the lacing swings. Seven shapes x four colors is 28 pairings and every one still pays exactly **two** fills: a shape only builds paths, so a line shape closes both of its bands into the same `Path2D`. Six more were built in the same pass and cut before shipping (steps, zipper, barcode, diamonds, pins, domes): the axis is worth more with a few looks that are unmistakable than with a long picker, so don't re-propose them as a set. **The one thing the split was missing is an anchor.** `heat` ramps vertically and assumed every silhouette grows from the midline, which was true of all three original shapes and is false the moment one stands on the floor. A shape may now declare `anchor` (0.5 by default, 1 for `ridge`) and `drawWave` hands it to the color as a `PaintScene`, so the ramp is built outward from wherever the shape starts and grounded terrain burns at its summits rather than at its floor. Adding a grounded or top-hung shape later stays one registry entry. Everything else held: the pitch is still the redraw quantum, so the wider-pitched shapes repaint less often than the default does, and no color varies bar to bar. `tests/utils/waveformRenderers.test.ts` grew its cross product to 28 pairings on its own, plus a check that every gradient stop stays inside 0-1 and in order, since an anchored ramp is the thing that can push one out (a real canvas throws `IndexSizeError` and the jsdom stub would not). It also holds every shape inside the 18px track at every amplitude, which is what the stub now records line coordinates for: peaks are normalized, so every track has a bar at 1, and a band that straddles its own envelope (trace, stitch) or a chip on a constant pitch (ladder) rides part of itself off the canvas on every song. All three are capped by their own weight instead.
- **Waveform colors reworked to read apart (2026-09-29).** The four colors looked alike because they all leaned on one accent at similar strength. Every palette mode now paints from the background's own three cover colors (new `--color-accent-third` beside `--color-accent-alt`, sampled as `--wave-second`/`--wave-third`), each in a different form: `spectrum` sweeps all three across the song, `heat` is a thermal ramp (third color at the core, accent, white-hot tips), `trail` is a comet (dark body, burning tail), `mono` is plain ink. Two special modes carry fixed colors of their own, `rainbow` (red to violet) and `fire`, with their lightness mirrored when the ink is dark so a light theme deepens them instead of washing them out. Still two fills and at most one gradient per pairing.
- **Pearls waveform shape (2026-09-29).** One bead per bucket sized by amplitude on a hairline thread, at a 14px pitch so the loudest bead fills most of the track and still stops a pixel short of its neighbour instead of turning into a ribbon. A `carved` shape (the bars cut out of a solid strip) was built in the same pass and dropped: don't re-propose it.
- **Progress ring on the cover (2026-09-29).** `player.progressRing` (off by default) replaces the desktop bar's seek bar with an SVG ring around the cover, and the transport moves up beside the favorite button (the grid switches to `max-content` columns, the title truncating first). The ring is a real slider (drag along it, arrow/Page/Home/End keys shared with `Timeline` through `sliderKeyTarget`), sits in a padding band so the artwork still opens BigMusic, and is snapped to the `bars` waveform pitch along its length, so it repaints once per step on the once-a-second tick rather than per frame. Falls back to the bar while the cover is in the nav column.
- **Volume as a popover (2026-09-29).** `player.volumeStyle` switcher: `inline` (default), `popover`, where the desktop bar keeps only the volume button and just the slider opens in a `Dropdown` above it, or `hover`, where the slider is wiped in beside the button on hover, focus or drag (clip-path + opacity, keeps its box so nothing reflows; always shown without hover). `Dropdown` took an optional top-level `panel` (a surface instead of rows, a `Sheet` on mobile), and element anchors carry `flipX`/`flipY` so any button-anchored menu that flips up or left now sits beside its button instead of over it.
- **Player time display (2026-09-29).** `player.timeDisplay` switcher: elapsed / total (default), the time left as a countdown, or hidden. Every now-playing clock reads it (bar, BigMusic inline + split row, fullscreen video) through `formatClock`/`clockEnd` in `formatDuration.ts`; each carries the new `clock` style target, so right-clicking one opens the switcher.
- **Player buttons: pick and auto-hide (2026-09-29).** `player.hiddenControls` (multi-toggle, stores the hidden set so a new button shows by default, normalized by `hiddenPlayerControls` on rehydrate and import) removes any of favorite, previous, next, shuffle, repeat, waveform, sidebar, volume from the desktop bar; play/pause always stays. `player.autoHideControls` fades all of them out until the bar is hovered or holds keyboard focus (`:has(:focus-visible)`), opacity only so the layout never moves, and never on `hover: none`. Play/pause and repeat are sized by class now, not by `nth-child`, so hiding a neighbour can't move the big size.
- **Volume slider looks (2026-09-29).** `player.volumeShape` (`line`, the plain bar, or any waveform shape) + `player.volumeColor` (the waveform colors). `Timeline` owns it for every `kind="volume"` slider (player, BigMusic, video mode): a shaped one feeds a fixed rising ramp to the waveform renderers as its peaks, so there is no second renderer. The slider is its own `volume` style target; the button around it keeps `audio`.
- **Animate waveform on new song (2026-09-29).** `player.waveformBuildIn` (off by default): when a new song's peaks land, the seek waveform's bars spring up left to right with an easeOutBack overshoot, driven from a `buildRef` in `Timeline` so the canvas redraw guard still skips idle frames. Scaled by animation speed, skipped under reduce motion, not replayed for peaks already loaded at mount, never on the volume slider.
- **The poster look, global or per kind (2026-08-28).** Every titled row of tiles (home, search, artist) now draws through a picked look: **row**, the unchanged default (square cover, name under it), or **poster**, where the artwork is cropped to a 2:3 portrait, runs to the tile's own edge, and carries the name on it on a flat `--color-scrim-strong` plate (a label over artwork, which can be any brightness, §5), so nothing sits under the tile and the row reads as a wall of posters. The caption is one box (`MediaCard` gained a `.mediaCardText` wrapper that is `display: contents` everywhere else, so no other look changed a pixel) positioned over the foot of the artwork, which is the card's only in-flow child: the tile is then exactly as tall as the poster and the plate cannot add height or outgrow the rounded corner the way a spanned grid row did. Settings → Appearance carries the global picker plus an opt-in "A look per category" toggle, which reveals one row per `CarouselCategory` (songs, albums, artists, playlists, genres, radio); each has an **Auto** option that stores nothing, so an untouched category keeps following the global pick and switching the override off restores one look everywhere without discarding the picks. Store: `carouselStyle` / `carouselStylePerCategory` / `carouselCategoryStyles`, persisted, grouped under Appearance for export/import, and merged by name on import (a free-form map, like the keymaps, which the generic value merge would otherwise drop); `CarouselSection` takes the category and hands it to `MediaCarousel`, which resolves the look and re-measures its tile step when it changes. A look is a class on the scroller plus the `--carousel-tile` width it sets, so the width the virtualization measures and the width the row draws are one property. Neither look animates on its own, per the repaint measurement in the live traps. Two guards worth keeping: every poster rule is scoped `:not(.mediaCard--circle)`, so a portrait keeps the plain row's square box and caption underneath rather than being restyled and reverted (a round tile has no edge to sit a plate on, and a name over a face reads badly, and a revert that ties on specificity with `mediaCard.css` would be decided by bundle order); and the look reshapes the skeleton with the card, or the load state promises a card the row doesn't draw. Three looks that were built alongside it (a two-row shelf of horizontal cards, a matted gallery frame, a three-row artwork wall) were dropped the same day on the maintainer's call: only the poster departs far enough from the default to be worth a pick. i18n: `settings.ui.carousel*`, `settings.carouselStyle.*`, `settings.carouselCategory.*` ×9.
- **Basic/All settings mode dropped (2026-08-09).** The 2026-07-09 mode switcher (entry below) is gone: the category rail already splits ~150 rows into 18 addressable categories, so hiding a third of each one behind a second filter only made a setting findable by luck. Removed: `useSettings.settingsMode` (type, store field, persisted key, persist-merge entry), the `advanced?` flag on `SettingItem` and `SettingsSection` (30 item sites + the whole Layout section), `pruneSections`' `basic` argument, the rail's switcher, and the per-box "Show N advanced settings" footer hint with its CSS. What stays is the other half of the 07-09 work, **dependency hiding**: `hidden?` still drops a row whose controlling toggle is off, in the one mode there now is. Unrelated and untouched: the theme editor's own basic/all token filter (`customThemes.ts` `advanced`), which gates 20 tokens inside one modal rather than the whole surface. A profile carrying the old `settingsMode` key imports fine, the field is simply ignored. i18n: `settings.mode.showAdvanced*` removed ×9, `settings.mode.{basic,all}` kept for the theme editor.
- **Pop-out settings panels (2026-07-28).** A settings category can be picked up out of the rail and left floating over the app, so an appearance setting can be changed while watching the page it changes instead of walking back into Settings each time. The handle (a pop-out icon, revealed on row hover) both drags and clicks: past a 4px threshold the panel is created under the cursor and follows it out of the rail, a plain click drops it in the resting corner. Panels are draggable by their header, collapse to that header, close, and resize from a corner grip (pointer drag or arrow keys, min 240×120); position/size/collapsed state persist in `store/poppedSettings.ts` (`velora-popped-settings`). **What made it possible is the extraction**: `buildSections` and its ~120 store subscriptions moved out of the 900-line `settingsView.tsx` into `useSettingsSections()` (`settingsView/useSettingsSections.ts`, view down to ~360 lines), so the panel builds the *same* registry and can't drift from the settings page; it also only mounts that hook while something is actually popped. Rows are always the compact form (label + control, no descriptions, 300px): the first cut kept the full rows while on `/settings`, and a panel that reshapes itself as you navigate reads as broken, so the panel is one object everywhere. Only the 7 registry-backed categories are poppable (`POPPABLE_SECTIONS`), the bespoke panels (plugins, admin, about, security, keybinds) are whole components with their own layout. Desktop only: the mobile rail is a drill-in index and a floating draggable panel on a phone is worse than the settings page. Layout details that matter: the panel is **portaled to body** (a fixed element inside the page inherits any transformed/filtered/`contain`ing ancestor as its containing block, the same trap the dialog pill hit), capped at `min(50dvh, …)` until the user drags a size, the header is outside the scroll container so the drag area and buttons never scroll away, and rows inside it come from a **container query on the panel body**, not a breakpoint: the settings row is a two-track grid whose control track is `auto`, which overruns its column in a narrow floater, so under 420px the row wraps and sliders/palettes/selects take their own line (switchers and keybinds too under 340px). Shared with dev tools: the drag-by-header logic became `utils/useDragPosition.ts` (+ `clampToViewport`), and `DevToolsPanel` now uses it instead of its own copy. `SettingsBox` gained `bare` (drop the surface classes when it's already inside one) and `compact`. i18n `settings.popOut.{pickUp,close,collapse,expand,resize}` ×9. **Edge docking (2026-08-04):** a panel dropped within 72px of any screen edge parks against it as a flush 10px tab (`dock: "l"|"r"|"t"|"b"`), keeping its position along that edge and slotting in out of the edge it was dropped on. Hover, focus or tap opens it back out in place, and dragging it lifts it out mid-gesture. Minimized travels with the panel rather than gating the dock, so a tab opens into the header bar or into the whole panel; a pin (set on pointerdown inside, cleared by a pointerdown outside it and outside `.dropdownBackdrop/.sheet/[role=dialog]`) keeps an opened panel from tucking itself away when a select portals its menu outside the box. **One box in every state:** floating, minimized and opened-from-an-edge all use `--popped-w` (300px) and a `--popped-bar` (44px) header, so only the body ever comes and goes and nothing resizes under the pointer; the resting tab is `--dock-thickness` × `--popped-bar`, which is why opening a side tab moves one axis only. The tab is caught from `--dock-hit` (44px) away through an `::after` that grows **inward only** (past the opened box along the edge and the pointer is dropped the moment it opens, which flickers), and that reach needs `overflow: visible` + `contain: layout` on the parked tab since `.uiContentContainer` clips it otherwise. Sizes animate as width/height, never a transform: scaling a backdrop-filter surface tears it (§14.4), and `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` lets the opened panel animate to its content height on Chromium. **`-webkit-app-region: no-drag` on the panel is load-bearing:** Electron's caption drag region is an OS hit-test, so a panel over the topbar is unclickable at any z-index without it, and a side tab additionally clamps its along-edge position below `--topbar-offset`. The armed side is mirrored in a ref because pointermove is a continuous event and React can still be holding its state when the release reads it. i18n `settings.popOut.{dockHint,docked}` ×9.
- **Settings redesign: category rail (2026-07-24).** ~150 rows in 18 stacked blocks became a two-pane surface: a navigation card (search + basic/all switcher + category rail) beside the selected category. The load-bearing change is the **single category model** (`Category = RailItem & { node?, render, find, keys }` in `settingsView.tsx`): the 7 registry sections and the 11 bespoke panels used to be two parallel lists with different gating and ordering, which is why the panels dangled at the bottom; now one ordered array drives the rail, the pane and search, and a section carries a stable `id` so nothing is matched by its translated header. Rail groups (`player | interface | library | account`, `settingsRail/railTypes.ts`) are derived from the entries, so adding a category is one array entry. **Selection lives in the URL hash, not state**: `#<categoryId>` from the rail/nav, `#setting-<anchor>` from the palette, whose owning category is derived from the built registry (no second registration, and a settings link is shareable). This also keeps the effect free of `setState`, which the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` rule now forbids. Search overrides the pane with cross-category results (each keeping its section header) and matching panels; picking a category clears the query. Mobile is the same state projected differently: the rail becomes a full-width drill-in index (logout pinned to its end), the category gets a back button, and Android hardware back pops to the index via `useBackButtonDismiss`. Row anatomy: `settingLineContent` went from `repeat(2, 1fr)` (a toggle stranded half a screen from its label) to `minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,auto)` with a 240px slider column and wrapping controls; the 5 empty `.type*Container` rules are gone. `SettingsBox` header is optional but every call site passes one, so the section title stays inside its `uiContentContainer` (Jenny's call). Untouched by design: every setting's value/behavior, the 8 control primitives, the fuzzy search + English fallback, capability gating, and the 11 panels' internals (re-housed, not rewritten). `nav.tsx`'s About link retargeted `#about-section` → `#about`. i18n `settings.groups.{player,interface,library,account}` + `settings.categories` ×9.
- **Foreign theme import (2026-07-23).** The theme editor's import (file picker + clipboard) now also accepts user-supplied scheme files from other ecosystems: base16/base24 YAML (classic `scheme:` and styling-spec `palette:` layouts, line-based regex, no YAML dep), VS Code theme JSON (JSONC comments/trailing commas stripped string-aware), and Windows Terminal color schemes. New `src/utils/themeImport.ts` (`parseForeignTheme(text, nameHint?)`), tried only after `parseThemesFile` returns null, so Velora's own format and its trust boundary are untouched; converted colors are normalized to opaque hex8 and flow through `createCustomTheme`, missing fields keep editor defaults. Accent = most-chromatic candidate above a gray floor (else spec default); surface drives the `--color-ui`/`--color-transparent-Ui` family and accent-solid derives the 30% translucent accent (mirroring BASIC_MIRRORS); light schemes (declared `type` or background luminance) flip `--icon-brightness`. Filename (minus extension) is the name fallback. Legal basis for a sold app: only files the user picks are parsed, nothing third-party ships bundled, format names used descriptively. No new locale keys.
- **Theme multi-select for mass export/delete (2026-07-23).** Theme editor rail now supports track-style multi-select: ctrl/cmd-click enters select mode, click toggles, shift-click ranges, Esc/back exits first; a "Select" entry in the profile context menu is the touch entry point. A floating bar offers export (one `velora-themes.json` via the existing `downloadThemes` multi-payload) and mass delete (confirm pill, keeps the live-preview invariant when the active profile dies). Reuse pass: `useTrackSelection` generalized to `useItemSelection<T>` (`utils/useItemSelection.ts`), the track selection pill extracted to a generic `primitives/selectionBar/SelectionBar` (count + actions + exit), and the row checkbox to `SelectCheckbox`, with the track list recomposed onto all three. i18n `settings.themeEditor.{select,deleteConfirmMany}` ×9.
