- **Export and import one part at a time (2026-08-09).** Both halves of the user-data file are now picked apart by scope, so "just my appearance settings" is a real answer in both directions. `src/utils/userDataScopes.ts` is the whole model: four content scopes (favorites, playlists, smart playlists, history) plus settings groups that **mirror the settings rail one-for-one** (playback, audio, appearance, layout, display, keybinds, integrations, accessibility) and two with no rail home (library = the per-server pins and nav order, other = the catch-all). Mirroring the rail is what lets the chips borrow `settings.sections.*`, so only six scope labels needed translating. The map is `KEYS_BY_SCOPE` over `settings.tsx`'s `partialize` list, read through `settingsScopeOf`, and **an unmapped key falls into "other" rather than being dropped**, so a setting added next month still exports without touching this file. Legacy spellings the import migrates from (`immersiveDetailHeader`, `disableCoverColorSync`, `globalFavoriteShortcut`) are pinned into the group they belong to, or picking Appearance alone would have stripped the migration that reads them. The settings blob stays **flat in the file** and is split by the same map on both sides, so a v1 file written before scopes existed still imports part by part. **Audio-engine settings now travel at all**, which they never did: `velora-audio-settings` rides beside the store blob as `audioSettings` (file `version: 2`, nothing gates on the number), split across the same Playback/Audio groups the rail shows, and applied through `audioEngine`'s setters, never by writing its localStorage behind the live graph's back. `volume` and `outputDeviceId`/`Label` are deliberately excluded (a live level, and a device that won't exist on the next machine). Every imported audio value is type-, enum- and **range**-checked first, against the ranges the rail itself offers: an unchecked `eqPreset` of `"constructor"` passes an `in` test and leaves the EQ bands undefined (so it is an own-key test), an unbounded eq band lands on a filter whose gain runs to +1541dB, and an unbounded crossfade ends every track before it starts. `NEVER_EXPORTED` is now dropped on the **way out** too, so a file that carries only plugin approvals offers no scope at all; the import-side strip stays for older files. It also covers `onboardingCompleted`, which is this install's first-run flag rather than a preference, so an imported profile can neither replay nor suppress the tour. API: `exportUserData(scopes)`, and the import split into `readUserDataFile(file)` (parse + validate, reports which scopes the file actually holds and how many of each content one) then `importUserData(preview, scopes, onProgress)`. UI is inline in the same section, no modal: an export row that expands a `SettingsMultiToggle` of every scope (all ticked by default, so the plain Export button is unchanged), and an import that reads the file first and offers only what's in it, with counts, before the existing `confirmAction`. **Integrations starts unticked on import** (tray, autostart, media keys, the local API, update channel are about the machine, not the profile); everything else present starts ticked. History is offered on export and never on import, since no provider has a write seam for it. Picker anatomy: fourteen chips in one run is a scan cost, so they sit in two labelled blocks that state the real split (Library goes to your music server, Settings stays on this device), the label drops when a file only holds one of them, and a select-all/none link rides the header's existing divider rather than becoming a third button in the row. A failed import keeps its file and selection standing so it can be retried without picking again; only a run that landed clears them. The revealed import picker takes focus (`role="group"` + `aria-labelledby`), or the step is silent to anyone not watching that corner, and `SettingsMultiToggle` gained `aria-pressed` since its selection is a green border and nothing else (the format-badge picker inherits that). i18n `settings.userData.{scopes.*,chooseParts,hideParts,exportSelection,importSelection,importSelected,importPickAnother,selectAll,selectNone,groupContent,groupSettings}` ×9.
- **Full user-data export/import (2026-07-19).** One versioned JSON file (`kind: "velora-user-data"`, `version: 1`, `exportedAt`) carrying favorites, playlists (name, visibility, track refs), play history, stats, and the persisted `useSettings` blob (custom themes ride inside it). New Settings section `settingsBox/userDataSection/UserDataSection.tsx` (standalone, AboutSection precedent: two buttons + live progress caption + inline result; toasts on failure only per design §14.9; `confirmAction()` before import). Engine is UI-free in `src/utils/userDataExport.ts`; the blob/anchor dance was extracted to a shared `src/utils/downloadFile.ts` and `downloadPlaylist()`/`downloadThemes()` were deduped onto it. Track refs carry title/artist/album/duration, not just ids, so an export re-matches by search on a different server (reuses `playlistImport.ts`'s exported `resolveTrack()`); ids are kept for the same-server `getTrack(id)` fast path. Import treats the file as untrusted: shape/type validation, unknown fields ignored, and restored custom themes go through the new id-preserving `sanitizeStoredThemes()` (same token whitelist + CSS cap as `parseThemesFile`) so raw CSS still only reaches the DOM via the existing `setCustomCss` sanitizer. What's written per capability: settings always (value-only deep-merge that preserves the store's nested setters and never overwrites a function); favorites always (refs resolved in a bounded pool, then `useSession.toggleFavorite` guarded by `isFavorite` so it never un-favorites); playlists only when `musicService.supports("createPlaylist")` (create + addTracks, normal optimistic mutations). Play history and stats are export-only backup, never restored (no provider write seam), and the UI copy says so. `SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY` exported from `settings.tsx` so export reads the persisted blob instead of duplicating `partialize`. i18n `settings.userData.*` in all 6 locales.
- **Dropped: accent contrast floor + always-show row actions (2026-07-19).** The last two open accessibility items, dropped by decision, not deferred. Don't re-propose either. **Accent contrast floor** would have clamped the cover-derived accent to a minimum contrast ratio inside the extraction hook; `disableCoverColorSync` (Appearance) already covers the user who can't read a bad accent, and `highContrast` handles the surface/border half, so the clamp bought a narrow win at the cost of fighting the whole point of the dynamic accent. **Always-show row actions** would have pinned the hover-reveal track-row actions visible; touch already has long-press, and the row is reachable by keyboard, so it was a preference toggle dressed as accessibility. Dropped with them: `forced-colors` (Windows high-contrast mode) stays unhandled, and seek position / volume level still announce nothing to a screen reader beyond their button names. Leftover from the first item: `settings.accessibility.colorBlindMode`/`colorBlindModeDesc` are dead keys in all 6 locales (nothing in `src/` reads them, no `useSettings` entry) and can be deleted whenever the locales are next touched. `docs/goalsDetails/accessibility-settings.md` deleted with this entry.
- **Playback announced to screen readers (2026-07-19).** Track changes and play/pause were entirely silent to a screen reader: the cover and title swapped visually and nothing in the DOM said so, so a blind user heard the music change with no way to learn what was playing. New `primitives/nowPlayingAnnouncer/NowPlayingAnnouncer.tsx`, mounted once by `mainPage` next to the other singletons, subscribes through `usePlaybackSelector` (id/title/artist/isPlaying, `shallowEqual`, so it never re-renders on the 100ms position tick) and speaks "Now playing: title by artist" on a track change, "Paused"/"Resumed" on a state flip without one. It tracks what the user was **last told**, not the last emit, so the restored-but-paused track a reload hydrates is never announced as playing, and the first press of play after a reload says the title instead of a bare "Resumed". **Two alternating `role="status" aria-live="polite"` regions**, not one: a repeated action (pause, resume, pause) produces identical text, and a live region only announces when its content actually changes, so the message alternates between two slots. Hidden with a new `.srOnly` utility in `index.css` (clip-path, not `display:none`, which would hide it from the reader too). Same pass, the transport buttons stopped reading one static name for two states: `PlayPauseButton` names itself `player.play`/`player.pause` by what the click does, `RepeatButton` carries the mode in its name (`player.repeat`/`repeatAll`/`repeatOne`, since `aria-pressed` can't express three states); the mini-player's `label` override was dropped so it inherits the dynamic name. Both buttons also **dropped `aria-pressed`**: a name that changes with the state plus a pressed state reads as the contradictory "Pause, pressed", so the name is the single carrier of state now. The other toggles (favorite, shuffle, sidebar, mute, waveform) keep static names + `aria-pressed`, which is the correct pairing. Dead `player.playPause` key removed from all 6 locales; new `player.{play,pause,repeatOne,repeatAll,nowPlaying,paused,resumed}` ×6. Not covered: seek position and volume changes still announce nothing beyond their button names.
- **Follow system accessibility preferences (2026-07-19).** Reduce-motion, high contrast and interface blur now start from the OS instead of a hardcoded default, and follow it live. New `src/utils/systemPreferences.ts` owns the three media queries (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `prefers-contrast: more`, `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`) plus a `subscribeSystemPreferences` listener; a browser that doesn't know a feature reports no match, which is the right default. **The stored value is now a preference, not a value**: `reduceMotionPref`/`highContrastPref` (`system | on | off`) and `blurIntensityPref` (`system | full | light | off`) are what persists, while `reduceMotion`/`highContrast`/`blurIntensity` stay in the store as *resolved* values that are no longer persisted, so all ~34 consumers, `app.tsx`'s attribute writers, and the plugin BigMusic `ctx.reduceMotion` keep reading the same plain boolean/enum they always did. Only `resolveToggle`/`resolveBlur` know about `"system"`. Resolution happens in the setters, in `merge` (so the first paint is already correct, no post-hydration flash), and in `syncSystemPreferences()`, which one module-level `subscribeSystemPreferences` call drives when the OS flips a preference mid-session. Migration in `merge`: an explicitly persisted `reduceMotion: true`/`highContrast: true` or a non-`full` blur was a real choice and becomes that explicit value; the untouched defaults become `"system"`, which is what lets existing installs pick the OS preference up at all (they all had `false`/`"full"` already written to `velora-settings`, so a first-run-only default would have been dead on arrival). UI: the two Accessibility toggles became `select` rows (matching toastDuration below them) and the Appearance blur switcher gained a leading "Match system" option; the onboarding wizard keeps its 3 explicit blur choices, showing the *resolved* value, so picking one there is a deliberate override. i18n `settings.systemPref.{system,on,off}` ×6. Consequence worth knowing: a user with the OS "reduced transparency"/"transparency effects off" setting now loses surface blur until they pick a blur level explicitly.
- **Toast duration setting (2026-07-19).** WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable): toasts auto-dismissed on fixed 4/5/6s timers with no way to extend, so a slow reader lost the message, and Velora reserves toasts for failures, which is exactly what you don't want to miss. New `useSettings.toastDuration` (`default | long | sticky`, persisted) drives a `DURATION_SCALE` multiplier (1 / 2.5 / 0) applied in `toast.ts` `push()`; `sticky` resolves to `0`, which the store already treats as never-auto-dismiss, so no new mechanism. **Only the per-variant defaults are scaled**, an explicit `options.duration` from a caller (the sticky update prompt) still wins. Read via `useSettings.getState()` at push time rather than a subscription, since the store is called from non-React code. Tap and swipe-up dismiss already work on every toast, so `sticky` is never a trap. One `select` row in Settings → Accessibility; i18n `settings.accessibility.toastDuration{,Desc,Default,Long,Sticky}` ×6.
- **Custom scrollbar (2026-07-19).** Velora's own overlay scrollbar, off by default (`useSettings.customScrollbar`, Appearance → Interface toggle). Native scrollbars stay hidden by the one global rule in `index.css`, nothing is styled or fallen back to. `primitives/customScrollbar/CustomScrollbar.tsx` mounts once next to `ToastViewport` **only while the setting is on**, so it costs nothing off: no scroll container knows about it, and none had to change. Discovery is document-level capture listeners (`scroll` passive + `pointerover`) walking up to the nearest ancestor that actually scrolls (cheap `scrollHeight` check before `getComputedStyle`), falling back to `document.scrollingElement`; two portal thumbs are positioned `fixed` over that element's box in a rAF loop that only runs while visible and stops itself on idle. Both axes, `MIN_THUMB` 28px, drag via pointer capture, accent on hover/drag, 1.2s idle fade (visible while hovering the container so there's something to grab). Overlay by construction, no gutter eating width at 360px. On `pointer: coarse` the thumb is `pointer-events: none` (indicator only): touch scrolls by direct manipulation and a grabbable edge strip would swallow taps, which also sidesteps the 44px-target rule a thin bar can't meet. Reduce-motion is free, the only animation is an opacity transition on `--duration-fast`. i18n `settings.ui.customScrollbar{,Desc}` ×6.
- **Dev tools, dev builds only (2026-07-17, entry point moved 2026-07-26).** A toggle in Settings → About + a floating draggable/collapsible panel (`src/store/devTools.ts`, `src/assets/components/ui/devTools/`). Forces view loading/empty/error states everywhere (seams: `useRetryableLoad` for errors, `useDevListOverride` in grid views + recentlyListened, `CarouselSection` and the `Playlist` component centrally, `usePlaylistDetail` for the detail view, forced error also forces not-loaded since views gate on `failed && !loaded`); forces all 4 nav pills (update per phase, desktop prompt, offline, trial, replaced both old `DEV_FORCE` consts); fires test toasts; overlay openers (confirm pill, name prompt, EditTrackModal with current-or-sample track); design controls (theme cycle, density, text scale, animation speed, reduce-motion, element-outlines overlay, react-scan render highlighting, `react-scan` is a devDependency loaded only from the panel chunk, hit-target-under-44px audit, 8px baseline grid overlay, safe-area inset simulation via the `--safe-*` tokens); route/breakpoint/accent readouts + FPS/heap-memory in an isolated leaf component so the 1s tick doesn't re-render the panel. Minimize collapses to the header bar only; close (X) fully disables dev tools (same as the Settings toggle). Everything is `import.meta.env.DEV`-gated and verified absent from the prod bundle; panel labels are plain English by design (never ships).
  - **No rail entry (2026-07-26).** A whole settings category for one toggle was the wrong weight, so `DevToolsSection` and the `developer` category are gone. The About pane's version chip is now the way in: five taps within 1.2s of each other unlock it (`devTools.unlocked`, persisted, so a reload doesn't cost five more taps) and switch the panel on in the same act, since five taps is intent enough. The chip stays plain text with no fill, hairline or pointer cursor, the only tell is a 1px accent line under it growing on `--about-progress` (`taps / 5`), and it reverts to a `<span>` once spent, so no dead control is left behind. The toggle then lives as an ordinary `SettingLine` under a Developer subheader at the bottom of About (`aboutSection/DeveloperRow.tsx`, a dev-only lazy chunk), revealed with one token-driven entrance killed by `data-reduce-motion`. `useDevUnlocked`/`devUnlock` follow the store's existing prod-inert-hook pattern, so About (which does ship) never touches the store instance; the tap box grows via padding + negative margin, so a coarse pointer gets a real target without moving the identity row. About's two local rows moved onto `SettingLine` too, so the pane has one row grammar. i18n `about.devUnlocked` + `about.devUnlockHint` ×9.
  - **Per-process telemetry (2026-08-07).** The FPS/heap readout only ever sees this renderer, and most of what the app costs now lives elsewhere (GPU process, the palette overlay window, whichever process Chromium put the sandboxed plugin frames in), so the Telemetry section lists CPU % and working set per process straight from `app.getAppMetrics()` over a read-only `appMetrics` bridge call, desktop only. Two holds that matter more than they look: the rAF loop is **refcounted to one** across the badge and the expanded section (a rAF loop does not just observe frames, it asks for one every vsync, and the panel is a blurred surface, so every one of those repaints a backdrop-filter), and both polls stop while the window is hidden, since `getAppMetrics` walks every process and doing that behind a minimized window is the panel costing more than what it measures. The metrics poll additionally only exists while the section is expanded. A copied report falls back to the console when the clipboard is denied.
- **Seek + volume are real sliders (2026-07-19).** The `Timeline` primitive had no a11y surface at all: no role, no `tabIndex`, no key handling. So it wasn't merely silent to a screen reader, it was **inoperable without a pointer**, which also made "announce the seek position" unbuildable, there was no slider to announce. It's now `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin/max/now/valuetext`, focusable, and keyboard-driven (arrows, PageUp/Down, Home/End). One new `kind?: "seek" | "volume"` prop discriminates the two shapes the six call sites use (seconds along a track vs. a 0-1 volume fraction) and drives the label, the spoken value and the step sizes from a single `STEPS` map, so no call site restates them; only the three volume ones pass `kind="volume"`. `aria-valuetext` follows `activeProgress`, not `currentTime`, so a pointer scrub is spoken as it moves rather than only when it lands, and volume reports 0-100 while seek reports "1:23 of 3:45". `duration <= 0` (no track) sets `aria-disabled` + `tabIndex -1` and ignores keys. The key handler calls `preventDefault` **and** `stopPropagation` so the global media keybinds don't act on the same press. Focus ring per designsystemV2 §10.1 (`color-mix` over `--color-accent-solid`, not the frozen purple literal). i18n `player.{seekSlider,seekPosition,volumeSlider,volumePercent}` ×6.
- **Windows forced-colors mode (2026-07-19).** `@media (forced-colors: active)` block in `index.css`. The load-bearing part is that forced-colors **drops `box-shadow` entirely**, and every focus ring in the app is a box-shadow, so high-contrast users had no visible focus indicator anywhere; they're restated as a real `outline: 2px solid Highlight`. Surfaces get `background: Canvas` + a 1px `CanvasText` border with blur off (blur and a 5% hairline are what separate a surface from the page, and both flatten here), `--color-icon` becomes `CanvasText`, and the timeline's fill/thumb/track become `Highlight`/`GrayText` so the slider state survives. Icon `<img>` glyphs are white and forced-colors leaves images alone, so `--icon-brightness` is switched by pairing the query with `prefers-color-scheme` (HC themes still report light/dark), which reuses the existing token instead of adding a mechanism. The waveform canvas needed nothing: it samples the computed `color`, which forced-colors resolves to `CanvasText` on its own. Deliberately **not** remapped: `--color-accent`/`--color-accent-solid` to `Highlight`, that would propagate to every hover fill and selection in the app and risks unreadable Highlight-on-CanvasText pairings across surfaces that can't be verified without a Windows HC machine. **Unverified on-device**, written against the spec.
- Searchable settings UI across 7 sections
- Theme switcher (7 themes)
- Animation speed + reduce-motion (fully wired, collapses durations to 1ms)
- Float mode; layout controls for nav/player/sidebar/topbar
- Cover-color accent sync + default palette editor
- Language selector (6 languages)
- Focus indicators toggle, `focusIndicators` lifted into `useSettings` (persisted); `app.tsx` toggles `data-focus-indicators` on `<html>`; gated global rule in `index.css` forces a bold, high-contrast outline + glow on `:focus` (not just `:focus-visible`, so it stays visible regardless of input method) on every focusable element, overriding the subtler per-component rings.
- **High contrast toggle (2026-07-19).** `highContrast` in `useSettings` (persisted, in the profile export/import merge); `app.tsx` toggles `data-high-contrast` on `<html>` and folds the same flag into the existing `data-reduce-transparency` path (`--surface-blur: 0px` + solid surfaces) rather than adding a second solid-surface mechanism, so anything already keyed on that attribute follows for free. `index.css` gates token overrides on the attribute: `--surface-border`/`--color-border`/`--color-muted` to 45-55% mixes of the theme's own `--color-white`, plus a 2px `.uiContentContainer` border (the 5% hairline is invisible once the blur behind it is gone) and an opacity floor on the `.op-30…90` utilities (0.85, then 1 for 80/90; `.deactive` to 0.65). The token and `.deactive` rules carry `!important`: `html[data-high-contrast]` ties on specificity with `html.<theme>` and themes.css is imported later, so without it every theme that touches those tokens defeated the setting, and `.deactive`'s own `opacity` is `!important` already. That also ranks the overrides above a custom theme's inline `:root` properties, which is intended, an accessibility override outranks a cosmetic theme. `--color-white` is deliberately left alone: every theme already runs text at 16:1+ against its own background, so forcing pure white buys no contrast and would break a light or custom theme with a dark foreground. `op-0/10/20` are deliberately excluded, at that depth they hide an element rather than de-emphasize it. Locale keys already existed in all 6 files. Known limit: the floor reaches the `.op-*` utilities and the tokens, not raw `opacity:` in component CSS (e.g. the 0.38 micro-label).
- Media keys toggle, `mediaKeys` lifted into `useSettings` (persisted, default `true`); `audioEngine.ts` gates Media Session registration behind a `mediaKeysEnabled` flag (`setMediaKeysEnabled()` tears down/sets up action handlers + clears metadata live); `app.tsx` reacts to the setting and calls it.
- **Custom theme/color editor with multi-profile export/import (2026-07-09).** `ThemeEditorModal` (`settingsBox/themeEditor/`, lazy-loaded from a Settings → Appearance button, LicensesModal pattern) + `src/utils/customThemes.ts`. Profiles are token maps (`{ id, name, tokens }`) persisted in `useSettings.customThemes`, applied via the same `:root` `style.setProperty` mechanism as plugin themes; theme key `custom:<id>` (checked before the plugin `:`-key branch in `applyTheme`). Editable tokens: 13 colors as #RRGGBBAA (color input + alpha slider), dark-icons toggle (`--icon-brightness`), 6 radius sliders, hover-scale slider, `--duration-*` deliberately excluded (owned by app.tsx/animationSpeed). Selecting a profile activates it, so edits preview live; profiles appear in the theme switcher + command palette via `useThemeOptions`. Export one/all to JSON (`kind: "velora-themes"`); import validates at the trust boundary (known tokens only, value-shape checks, fresh ids). i18n `settings.themeEditor.*` in all 6 locales. Same pass: removed the eyebrow labels from both this modal and LicensesModal (design choice).
- **Every action, as many shortcuts as you want, and any of them system-wide (2026-08-04).** A command now holds a *list* of chords in two maps, `keybinds` (in-app) and `globalKeybinds` (OS-level), both `Record<command, string[]>` (`Keymap`, `utils/keybindActions.ts`). Two maps rather than one list of `{keys, scope}` objects, so each consumer reads exactly its own and the in-app matcher never filters. A command is either a static action id or `family:target` (`addToPlaylist:<playlistId>`), split on the **first** colon only because a theme key already carries one (`setTheme:custom:42`). Families: add the playing song to / play / open one of your playlists, switch theme, switch the now-playing look; their targets come from live user data (`utils/useKeybindTargets.ts`), and a binding whose target is gone resolves to no label and drops out of the UI instead of pointing nowhere (`isKnownKeybindCommand` also keeps it out of registration). The static registry went 14 → 28: play random, toggle sidebar/topbar, log out and the ten jump-to-view actions, all unbound by default, labelled through the palette's and nav's existing keys via `labelKey` + optional `nameKey` so they needed no new translations. **OS-level shortcuts are now generic:** the renderer pushes the whole bound set through `setGlobalShortcuts([{command, accelerator, focus}])`, `main.ts` holds those accelerators, re-registers the set on every change, `try/catch`es each one (`globalShortcut.register` throws on a chord Electron can't express, and the recorder accepts any key the browser reports) and fires `shortcut:global:fired` with the command id, which runs through the same `useKeybindDispatch` as the keyboard. Commands flagged `focusesWindow` (search, palette, now playing, navigation, open playlist, theme, look) raise the window first: an action that only changes what's on screen does nothing visible when it fires into the tray. The favorite-only path it replaced is gone: `globalFavoriteTrack`, `DESKTOP_GLOBAL_ACTIONS`, `useSettings.globalFavoriteShortcut`, `setFavoriteShortcut`/`onFavoriteShortcut` and the special case in `useDesktopIntegration` (see §11, superseded). Having a global binding *is* the opt-in now, so the toggle had nothing left to say. `normalizeKeymap`/`legacyGlobalKeybinds` (`keybindActions.ts`, shared by the persist merge and user-data import, since the generic value merge would copy an old single chord in as a bare string) carry both old shapes over: `"Ctrl+K"` → `["Ctrl+K"]`, `""` → `[]` (an emptied default stays emptied), and an enabled global favorite becomes `globalKeybinds.toggleFavoriteTrack`. UI: chord chips that re-record in place and carry their own remove, a `+` that only appears with the row (always visible under `pointer: coarse`), a second "System-wide" column on desktop, a Custom group whose `Dropdown` picker drills family → target, and a row-level revert at the far edge so both chord columns start where their header says. The section is a container query, not a breakpoint: under 560px the columns stack and each cell names its own scope. i18n `settings.keybinds.{scopeApp,scopeGlobal,scopeGlobalHint,addCustom,customEmpty,addChord,changeChord,removeChord,groups.*,families.*,actions.goTo}` ×9; `globalSection`/`globalFavorite`/`globalFavoriteDesc`/`edit`/`actions.globalFavoriteTrack` dropped.
  - **Chords stopped being layout-specific (same day).** Serialization read `e.key` alone, so a chord was only as portable as the keyboard it was recorded on. Now every press yields two spellings, the **printed** cap (`e.key`) and the **physical** key (`e.code`), the recorder stores the printed one and the matcher accepts either, printed first (numpad first for numpad keys, which otherwise print the number row's characters and would collide with it). Concretely: a Cyrillic or Greek layout, where the cap can't be typed back, falls through to the physical key instead of silently unbinding everything; **Shift is dropped when it is how the character is made** (`/` is Shift+7 on a German layout, so the shipped `/` default now actually reaches a German user, and `Shift+/` can't be recorded as something a US layout would never produce); dead keys resolve to their position; and comparison is case-insensitive (`chordKey`) because bindings from before this spelled every multi-character key upper-case ("ENTER"). **AltGr is ignored outright** in both the recorder and the matcher (`isAltGraph`): Windows reports it as Ctrl+Alt, so a `Ctrl+Alt+Q` binding would otherwise eat the `@` a German or Nordic layout types. `navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap()` was deliberately not used: it is Chromium-only and async, and the stored chord is already the cap the user pressed. Numpad chords carry through to Electron via `ACCELERATOR_KEYS` (`num1`, `numadd`, …).
  - **The rest of the round (same day).** *Search:* `focusSearch` with no search field on screen navigated to `/`, which redirects to the login route and bounces to the startup view, so the search key moved you somewhere else entirely; it now goes to `/search`, whose `SearchBar` carries the same `globalSearchInput` id as home's. *Cross-scope shadowing:* the two keymaps never conflict with each other, but a system-wide chord is taken before the page sees the key, so a chip whose chord the other scope holds for a **different** command is marked (`--warned`, `--color-warning` hairline) and explains itself in its tooltip, plus a toast at the moment it is bound. Same chord, same command in both scopes is the normal way to make a shortcut work everywhere and says nothing. *OS refusal:* `shortcut:global` became an `invoke` returning the chords `globalShortcut` refused (taken by another app, or unexpressible), kept in `store/shortcutStatus.ts` (not persisted, it is this launch's answer) and shown on the offending chip, instead of a shortcut that silently does nothing. *Discoverability:* command-palette rows now show their own chord as `<kbd>` chips (`PaletteItem.command`, read live from `useSettings.keybinds`, first chord when there are several, hidden under 480px), covering the transport actions, the page jumps, and the theme/now-playing-look switchers. i18n `settings.keybinds.{globalTaken,shadowsApp,shadowedByGlobal}` ×9.
  - **Recording a chord used to run it.** Committing a binding re-renders and blurs the recorder while the key is still travelling to `window`, so the matcher's "a recorder has focus" guard saw `body` and dispatched the action the user had just bound. The recorder's key handler now `stopPropagation()`s (the load-bearing fix, React's root listener sits below `document`, so it can stop the native event before `window` sees it), and the matcher skips **any** focused `.settingsKeybind`, armed or not, because Space and Enter activate a button on the key itself. Both paths covered in `tests/components/settingsKeybind.test.tsx`, which fails on either half being removed.
  - **Favorites is one of the playlists, and the lists follow the nav (2026-08-04).** Play/open-playlist shortcuts take Favorites as a target (not add-to-playlist, that's `toggleFavoriteTrack`); it isn't a backend entity, so playing it reuses `playFavorites` from `playlistMenu.ts` (queues the resolved ids) rather than a `sourceId` the Velora controller would read as NaN, while opening it is the plain `/playlist/favorites` route. Both the target picker and the Custom rows sort playlists through the same `sortByNavOrder` the nav and the add-to-playlist submenu use, so one order everywhere: pinned first, then the dragged order.
- **Keybind recorder UI (2026-06-21).** `KeybindsSection` (`settingsBox/keybindsSection/`), a standalone block below the mapped sections, same precedent as `AdminSection`, not a row in the generic `sections`/`SettingItem` array. Collapsed by default behind a "Customize" row (13 actions would otherwise dominate the settings list); expanding swaps in a full `SettingsBox` with Playback/General subheader groups built from `KEYBIND_ACTIONS`, each row using the existing `settingsKeybind` recorder (now wired to `useSettings.keybinds`/`setKeybind`), plus a "Reset to defaults" row (`resetKeybinds()`, behind the shared `ConfirmDialog`, see §2). Assigning a binding already used by another action clears the other one and toasts a warning, so two actions can never silently collide. `settingsKeybind.tsx` itself got real i18n strings (was hardcoded English), Escape-to-cancel, and renders the binding as `<kbd>` chips (matching the command palette's hint style) instead of a plain string. Hidden entirely on mobile (`useIsMobile()`), recording a chord assumes a physical keyboard. Hidden while the settings search box has a query, since it sits outside the search-filtering logic.
- **Storage usage in nav (2026-07-15).** Opt-in `showStorageUsage` setting (Settings → Display → General, gated on the new `storage` capability so it hides on Subsonic/local) mounts `NavStorageIndicator` in the nav footer: a used/total bar (accent fill, `--color-danger` past 90%, "X used" only when the quota is unlimited i.e. `maxStorage === 0`), collapsing to icon + 32px mini-bar when folded. Reads `getUserStats` `storageUsed`/`maxStorage`, refetching whenever the upload queue drains (storage grew). New `storage` capability (`veloraProvider` true, Subsonic/local false). Shared `src/utils/formatBytes.ts` extracted from uploadOverlay (both consume it). `database` icon added to `cssIcons.ts` for the mask glyph. i18n `nav.storage.{title,used,usedOf}` + `settings.general.{showStorage,showStorageDesc}` in all 6 locales.
- **"Dark icons" reaches every icon path (2026-07-15).** Three root causes behind the custom-theme "Dark icons" toggle not taking (all worked in the built-in light theme, which is why it looked provider-specific): (1) the toggle only sets `--icon-brightness`, which the `.iconImg` `<img>` filter reads but mask glyphs (`background-color`) and inline-SVG (`currentColor`) icons don't, added `--color-icon` (`index.css` `:root`, defaults `var(--color-white)` so the light theme keeps flipping for free), routed nav pin/chevrons/upload icons, the decomposed player buttons (play/pause, shuffle, repeat, skip, waveform, volume, sidebar, favorite), and media-carousel arrows to it, and had `customThemes.ts` flip it (`#000` ↔ `var(--color-white)`) in lockstep with `--icon-brightness`. (2) `button.css` had `.defaultButton img { filter: none }`, whose specificity (`0,0,1,1`) out-ranked the base `.iconImg { filter: var(--icon-brightness) }` (`0,0,1,0`), so **every** button icon (nav home/tracks/settings, etc.) ignored the tint; only `html.light .iconImg` (`0,0,2,1`) punched through, hence "works in white mode, not custom." Removed the redundant reset (all Button icons carry `.iconImg`; non-icon imgs get no filter either way). (3) The topbar is `background: var(--color-pure-black)`, which custom themes can't recolor, so global dark-icons painted its icons/text black on the still-black bar. Pinned `.topbar_container` foreground to the fixed contrast pair `--color-pure-white` (covers text spans + mask icons via `--color-icon`) + kept img icons light via a scoped `--icon-brightness`; `html.light .topbar_container` flips `--icon-brightness` dark (the pure pair swaps on its own). Accent-colored icons (`navPill__icon`, sleep bell) deliberately left on the accent token.
- **Default startup view (2026-07-14).** Persisted `useSettings.startupView` (`home` / `tracks` / `favorites` / `last`, default `home`) + `lastRoute` (default `/home`). `startupPath()` helper (settings.tsx, reads `getState()`) maps the pick to a path (`favorites` → `/playlist/favorites`, the same special-id route the nav Favorites button uses); loginPage's four `navigate("/home")` sites, fresh login, bootstrap, and both already-authed re-entry redirects, now navigate there. "Last visited" reads `lastRoute`, written through from `mainPage` via a `useLocation` effect gated on `startupView === "last"` (no localStorage churn otherwise; detail routes like `/playlist/:id` are restored as-is, views already handle stale/missing content). Deliberately *not* applied on a web reload of a specific view, RequireAuth renders the current URL directly and LoginPage never mounts, so the pick only fires on a true launch from root/`/login` (every Electron launch loads `app://velora` → `/` → `/login`). UI: Settings → Display, new *General* subheader (always visible, not advanced, so it reaches mobile too, Layout is mobile-hidden), a 3-way switcher. i18n `settings.general.{startupView,startupViewDesc,startupHome,startupTracks,startupFavorites,startupLast}` in all 6 locales (reuses existing `subheaders.general`).
- **Appearance, deeper customization: 4 controls (2026-07-14).** All token-driven and *global* (persist across theme switches, not custom-theme tokens), applied on `<html>`/`:root` in `app.tsx` next to `DURATION_SCALES`. **Text scale** (`textScale` small/normal/large/xlarge → root `font-size` %, scales all rem type). **UI density** (`uiDensity` compact/comfortable/spacious → `--ui-density` multiplier; index.css padding/gap tokens rewrapped as `calc(base * var(--ui-density))`). **Interface blur** (`blurIntensity` full/light/off → `--surface-blur`, routed through `.uiContentContainer` + `.uiBackground`; "off" also sets `data-reduce-transparency` on `<html>`, an `!important` rule making surfaces solid+unblurred for readability + GPU savings, mirroring the focus-indicators rule). **Auto day/night** (`autoTheme` toggle + `dayTheme`/`nightTheme` picks): deliberately **not** OS `prefers-color-scheme`, runs off the **local clock** (day 07:00–19:00), `applyActiveTheme()` is the single entry point (setters/rehydrate/scheduled flip), app.tsx schedules one `setTimeout` to the next boundary via `msUntilThemeFlip()` (no polling) and reschedules. Manual `theme` still stands when auto off; the Themes switcher hides while auto is on, day/night pickers show as child rows; an explicit `setTheme` pick (command palette, theme editor) turns auto off so it's never a visual no-op; `removeCustomTheme` clears any of the 3 theme slots referencing a deleted profile. Review pass same day: aurora/chromatic theme `.uiContentContainer` blurs tokenized onto `--surface-blur` (chromatic capped via `min(…, 14px)`) so the "light" level works in every theme; `activeThemeKey()` helper dedupes the auto-slot ternary. New Interface-subheader rows for scale/density/blur; i18n `settings.ui.{textScale,density,blurIntensity,autoTheme,dayTheme,nightTheme}` + `settings.{textScale,density,blurIntensity}.*` in all 6 locales.
- **Settings search, fuzzy + always English-searchable (2026-07-14).** New `src/utils/fuzzyMatch.ts` (`fuzzyScore`/`fuzzyMatches`, subsequence scorer with consecutive-run + word-boundary bonuses, no new dep) replaces the old `.toLowerCase().includes()` filter. `settingsView.tsx`'s inline `sections` array became `buildSections(tf)`, parameterized by the translate function; `filteredSections` builds a second tree via `i18n.getFixedT("en")` only while a query is active and fuzzy-matches against both the active-locale and English label/description (section header, subheader label, setting name, description), zipped by index since both trees share the same structural shape. Extracted `groupSettingItems()` (was inlined in the filter) to build both trees' subheader/item groupings identically.
- **Settings UX regroup, Performance dissolved into Appearance (2026-07-14).** Every control now sits next to what it affects. Appearance gained subheaders: *Theme* (themes, custom themes, + cover-color sync/default colors moved from Performance), *Background* (disable toggle first, then style picker/FPS/resolution moved from Performance, all hidden while disabled, kept non-`child` rows since the collapse wrapper clips select dropdowns), *Interface* (float mode), *Now Playing* (BigMusic mode/auto/widescreen), *Animations* (animation speed moved from Display → Interface, + icon animations). Performance section deleted; Display keeps Track info + Language; wheel volume deliberately stayed in Integrations → System with media keys. Locale half (subheader keys, `sections.performance` removal ×6) had already shipped in the prior commit, this landed the `settingsView.tsx` half, also fixing the raw `settings.sections.performance` key that briefly rendered as the section header.
- **Nav logo right-click/long-press → About (2026-07-12).** Logo click still navigates home; right-click (desktop) or long-press (mobile, native `contextmenu`) opens Settings and scrolls to the About section (`AboutSection` carries `id="about-section"`, `SettingsView` scrolls to it on mount when `location.hash === "#about-section"`). No new surface.
- **Settings Basic/All mode + decluttering (2026-07-09).** Removed the "Settings" title + card wrapper, now a bare full-width search bar (like home) with a Basic/All `SettingsSwitcher` beside it; view split into a fixed header + separately-scrolling `.settingsViewBody`. Persisted `useSettings.settingsMode` ("basic" default). Two hide mechanisms via `advanced?`/`hidden?` flags on `SettingItem` (+ section-level `advanced?`), pruned by `pruneSections()`: **dependency-hidden** items disappear in both modes when their controlling toggle is off (crossfade→duration, loudnessNorm→target, compressor→its 4 params, fadeIn→duration, formatBadges→badgeFormats, topbarVisible→clock/greeting/nowPlaying/search, kept on Electron); **advanced** items + Layout + Keybinds only show in All mode. Orphaned subheaders/empty sections auto-drop. i18n `settings.mode.*` ×6.
- **The licenses modal wears the app's list grammar (2026-08-09).** The row said "selected" 70 times: an accent chip on every line and an accent spine down every open notice, while hover and open shared one neutral fill, so the accent marked nothing and the open row was indistinguishable from the one under the cursor. Now the accent is **state only**, the same split the nav rail settled on: hover is `--fill-subtle-hover`, the open row alone takes the accent hairline, the accent-tinted head and an accent-solid chip, and its notice sits flush under a `--color-border-subtle` hairline instead of a 2px accent border. The head keeps `.defaultButton` for its focus ring but drops the button's resting fade, hover brightness and press scale (doubled selectors, as in `nav.css`), because a full-width row that shrinks 10% under the thumb reads as a glitch; the name carries the row's voice at `op-80 → 1` instead. Container: the column is full-bleed to the card edge and **fades only at the end that still has rows behind it** (`data-lead`/`data-trail` + two `@property` lengths, `mediaCarousel`'s grammar vertically), the search field is `flat` so the app stops stacking a card inside a card, and the intro is the title's subtext rather than a paragraph pulled back up by a negative margin. Also: `useFocusTrap` (Tab used to escape behind the scrim, and nothing was focused on open), the chevron is the real `expand-more-rounded` mask instead of two rotated CSS borders, an opened row scrolls itself into view, the notice is keyboard-scrollable (`tabIndex` + `role="region"`), the empty state is an `<li>` not a `<p>` inside a `<ul>`, `38vh → 38dvh`, and the 480px straggler is on the 479 scale. Narrow: name over badge, so a long SPDX id ("SIL Open Font License 1.1") can't squeeze the package name to nothing.
- **The licenses list is scoped to what actually ships, and no longer carries versions (2026-08-09).** The generator walked *every* non-`dev` entry in `package-lock.json`, so About attributed packages the app does not contain: `@types/*` (declaration-only, nothing of them survives a build), `@capacitor/cli` and its whole subtree (`ansi-regex`, `@xmldom/xmldom`, `slice-ansi`…). That published a free map of the build toolchain and buried the real deps. It now walks the **dependency closure of the shipped roots** (`package.json` `dependencies` minus `@types/*`, plus `electron`, whose runtime electron-builder packages into the installer), with an npm-style `resolve()` over the lockfile paths; `@types/*` are skipped at every depth, and an **optional peer** the app doesn't install is skipped too (that is how `typescript` rode in behind `i18next`). A root missing from the lockfile now exits non-zero rather than silently dropping an attribution. 250-ish entries down to 70. **Versions are gone** from `LicenseEntry`, the generated data and the row: MIT/BSD/ISC/Apache-2.0 all require the notice and the license text, not an exact-version inventory, and `name@1.2.3` was the one part of the modal with real recon value (a pre-built CVE checklist for anyone probing a running install). Hiding the *list* was considered and rejected, it is obscurity (the bundle ships to every browser, and the backend is open source) and Apache-2.0 §4(d) wants the notices in a display the app generates. Same pass: `@capacitor/cli` + `@types/crypto-js` moved to `devDependencies` where they belong, and a manual **Chromium (desktop runtime)** entry was added, since the desktop build embeds it through Electron and nothing attributed it (its full notices ship as `LICENSES.chromium.html` beside the executable).
  - ↳ files: `scripts/generate-licenses.mjs`, `LicensesModal.tsx` + `licensesModal.css` (row is name + license badge), `package.json`
- **Third-party license attribution, About / Licenses screen (2026-07-08)** (app is sold). Full audit: no copyleft anywhere, every bundled dep permissive/commercial-safe. Build-time generator (`scripts/generate-licenses.mjs`, wired into `npm run build` + `npm run gen:licenses`) reads every shipped (non-dev) package from `package-lock.json` + its LICENSE text, plus manual entries for non-npm works (ReactBits, Outfit/Inconsolata fonts, Material Symbols). Emits `src/generated/appInfo.ts` + `src/generated/licenses.ts` (~163 kB, 123 entries). Surfaced via Settings → About (`aboutSection/AboutSection.tsx`) with a lazy-loaded `LicensesModal.tsx` (data chunk only downloads when opened, 0 bytes of license text in the main bundle). i18n `about.*` + `settings.sections.about` ×6.
  - ↳ verify before sale: ReactBits shaders may be modified (MIT covers it).
- **No third-party marks ship any more (2026-08-10).** The login provider tabs carried Navidrome's and Subsonic's logos as bundled PNGs and Jellyfin's as a Simple Icons glyph, three marks the app is sold with and holds no license to. `public/navidrome.png` + `public/subsonic_logo.png` are deleted and the three tabs take neutral Material Symbols (`dns`, `hub`, `library-music`); `simple-icons--jellyfin.svg` stops being fetched the moment the `iconify:simple-icons:jellyfin` literal is gone, since `fetch-icons.mjs` greps the source for its download list. Only Velora's own logo is left. The brand **names** stay as text: nominative use is what lets a user find the tab for their server, and it is the logo, not the word, that is the mark being used. Outfit is self-hosted since 2026-07-19 (`public/fonts/outfit-variable.woff2` + `OFL.txt`, the OFL obligation the generator's notice covers); Inconsolata is never shipped or served, `--font-mono` only names it, so the entry says so rather than claiming a CDN (corrected 2026-08-10). Regenerate after dep changes: `npm run gen:licenses`.
- **Cover shape (2026-09-30).** Appearance → Interface (and a song row's right-click) picks how library covers are cut: rounded, square, circle. One token, `--cover-radius`, set from `data-cover-shape` on `<html>`, read by each cover site with its own radius as fallback; the now-playing cover is left out because it flies into BigMusic. Detail in `docs/app/settings/appearance.md`.
  - ↳ files: `src/index.css`, `src/app.tsx`, `useSettingsSections.ts`
  - **Dropped: duotone cover color (2026-09-30).** Built alongside and removed by decision before shipping; don't re-propose.
- **Middle-click to play next (2026-10-01).** Display → General toggle `middleClickPlayNext` (on): a middle click on a song row or song card sends `addNext`. `utils/middleClick.ts` owns the press on those elements: native autoscroll is suppressed there (it starts on the press, so a plain click would also leave it stuck on) and a middle drag is emulated as a velocity scroll of the nearest scroller per axis (`utils/scrollable.ts`, shared with `CustomScrollbar`).
  - ↳ files: `utils/middleClick.ts`, `primitives/track/track.tsx` (`playNextOnMiddleClick`), `primitives/mediaCard/mediaCard.tsx` (`playNextId`)
- **Lyrics on seek hover (2026-10-01).** Appearance toggle `player.seekLyricPreview` (off): hovering the seek bar shows the time and the synced lyric line at that point in one pill, so the chorus can be found before clicking. `useSeekLyrics` fetches only while the setting is on; the pill's anchor slides with the cursor so it never leaves the track.
  - ↳ files: `utils/useSeekLyrics.ts`, `ui/player/timeline/timeline.tsx` (`lyrics` prop), `bigMusic/modes/useLrc.ts` (`lineAt`)
- **Paste to search (2026-10-01).** Display → General toggle `pasteToSearch` (on): a paste outside a text field opens `/search?q=` with the clipboard text, "Artist - Title" separators turned into spaces. Listens for `paste`, not a Ctrl+V keydown, so it needs no clipboard permission. Local mode's track search now matches every word across title/artist/album instead of the whole string per column.
  - ↳ files: `utils/usePasteToSearch.ts`, `electron/localLibrary.ts` (`search`)
- **Changelog (2026-10-03).** One `docs/changelog/<version>.json` per user-facing release, starting at 0.49.49, typed and validated by `utils/changelog.ts`, checked by `npm run check:changelog`. Settings → About → What's new shows it newest first, windowed by `useMeasuredWindow` (variable-height rows); the About viewers share the `AboutModal` shell.
  - ↳ files: `utils/changelog.ts`, `scripts/check-changelog.mjs`, `aboutSection/ChangelogModal.tsx`, `aboutSection/AboutModal.tsx`
- **Custom tooltips (2026-10-05).** Appearance → Interface toggle `customTooltips` (on): one auto-attaching layer draws every `title=` as a pill, facing away from its chrome region's screen edge, also on keyboard focus, never on touch, skipping text already shown in full. Unfolded nav playlist rows dropped their title (it repeated the name).
  - ↳ files: `primitives/tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`, `utils/tooltipPlacement.ts`
- **Settings re-sort and full search (2026-10-06).** Appearance and Display are split into General, Player Bar, Full-screen Player, Theme & Color, Background, Interface and Library Look under a new App / Player / Look & feel rail; each subheader group is its own titled card, and on desktop the pane is one continuous scroll through every category with the rail highlighting where you are (`settingsRail/scrollSpy.ts`). Search matches names only (no descriptions), covers every row including dependency-hidden and Customize-gated ones (greyed under the row that unlocks them, `dependsOn` where that is not the row above), and always brings a sub-setting's parent along. Old `#appearance` / `#display` links and saved pop-out panels map through `RETIRED_SECTIONS`; export scopes mirror the new rail. Platform gates moved from `hidden` to `only()` so search never offers a row the device lacks.
  - ↳ files: `settingsView/settingsSearch.ts`, `settingsRail/scrollSpy.ts`, `useSettingsSections.ts`, `settingsView.tsx`, `settingsRail/railTypes.ts`, `utils/userDataScopes.ts`, `utils/styleTargets.ts`, `store/poppedSettings.ts`, `tests/screens/settingsSearch.test.ts`

- **Style menu gear jumps to the setting** (2026-10-08): the gear opens `/settings#style-<target>`, which picks the section holding that element's first visible row and scrolls to it without the flash (`data-target-row` on `SettingLine`). `mobileSection` on style targets retired.
- **Settings perf (2026-10-08).** The wide-layout settings pane (web and app) mounts only the categories within a screen of the viewport (`SettingsCategory`, window in `useSettingsSpy`, unmount past two screens); anchor/style jumps pin their category. A settings write re-renders only its own row: `SettingsRegistry` publishes each build to a per-mount store, `App`'s settings effects live in a null-rendering `SettingsEffects`. Settings persist trails a burst by 250ms (`utils/debouncedStorage.ts`, flushed on `pagehide`/hide/read). Open follow-up in `goals.md` §6.
  - ↳ files: `settingsView/SettingsCategory.tsx`, `settingsView/settingsRegistry.tsx`, `settingsView/settingsRegistryStore.ts`, `utils/debouncedStorage.ts`, `tests/perf/settingsRenders.test.tsx`

## 7. Notifications
- **Toast system.** `useToast` (`src/store/toast.ts`, not persisted, FIFO-ish swap queue) + `ToastViewport` (`primitives/toast/`), mounted once at the app root in `app.tsx` (outside `<Routes>`, live on every route, not just authenticated ones). Imperative API: `toast.success/error/info/warning(message, { duration? })`.
- **Design: dynamic-island-style notch**, not a corner stack. Fixed top-center, offset below the topbar via a `--topbar-offset` var (set by `mainPage.tsx`, defaults to `0px` on routes without one) + `env(safe-area-inset-top)`. Fully hidden when idle (nothing rendered until a toast fires).
- **Swap-with-badge queue.** A new toast immediately becomes the visible one; anything still showing waits its turn and is counted in a `+N` badge, not a strict FIFO display order.
- **Morph animation.** The pill is a single persistent `motion.div` (`layout` prop, spring transition) so swapping toasts resizes the pill in place instead of replaying a full enter/exit; only the inner content (icon/text/badge) crossfades quickly. Respects `reduceMotion` (collapses to instant).
- **Variant color = icon only**, neutral `uiContentContainer` surface otherwise, icon is a CSS `mask-image` (not the `color=` query param) so it tracks the live token (`--color-success/danger/warning`, `--color-accent-solid`), including theme switches and the dynamic cover-art accent.
- Dismiss: tap or swipe-up (`drag="y"` with a velocity/offset threshold); auto-dismiss timer owned by the store, paused for queued (non-active) toasts.
- Proven via temporary test buttons on `/dev` (`devPage.tsx`), kept there for future tuning.
- **Real call sites wired (2026-06-21).** Optimistic-revert failures now toast: `useSession.toggleFavorite` and `useLibrary.addTrackToPlaylist`/`removeTrackFromPlaylist` toast directly from their store catch blocks (after reverting) since each is called from several fire-and-forget sites (player, bigMusic, trackMenu, playlistView), centralizing in the store avoids repeating the check at every caller. Stores import `i18n` directly (same pattern as `utils/trackMenu.ts` etc.) since they're outside React. `useCreatePlaylist`'s failure path (only one call site, already has `t()` via the hook) toasts at the call site instead. `deletePlaylist` already toasted at its one call site (`playlistMenu.ts`) from before this pass, left as-is, not duplicated. New keys: `contextMenu.track.favoriteUpdateFailed`/`addToPlaylistFailed`/`removeFromPlaylistFailed`, `playlist.createFailed` (all 6 locales).

## 8. Stats & Analytics
- Home Overview: monthly + all-time playtime/track-count stats
- The `/stats` route/view was removed 2026-06-21 (it rendered nothing). Rebuilt from scratch 2026-07-24, see below.
- **Closed 2026-07-19**: the listening milestones/badges idea (Night Owl, Completionist, 1000 tracks played) was dropped. Not a bad idea, just not one we want; don't re-propose it.
- **`/stats` listening report (2026-07-24).** `/api/v1/stats/listening` already returned months, top tracks/artists/albums, devices, streaks, best day, completion/skip counts and library totals; `getUserStats` reduced all of it to four numbers. New `getListeningStats(months)` on `IMusicProvider` maps the whole payload (`ListeningStats` and friends in `ImusicProvider.ts`), gated on a new `listeningStats` capability (Velora only; Subsonic/Jellyfin/local throw UNSUPPORTED, local because its SQLite keeps play counts, not per-session rows). `StatsView` reads how much → when → what → how → what you own: hero band (all-time listened, active days, current/longest streak, best day, unique tracks/artists), a monthly bar chart whose header readout follows hover/focus/tap instead of a floating tooltip, a tabbed Most-listened ranking (songs play, artists/albums navigate) whose rows encode share as a scaled fill behind the row, a habits card (finished/partial/skipped split bar, completion rate, average + longest play, per-device breakdown) and a library facts card. Range switcher 3/6/12/24 months refetches; the whole route redirects to `/home` without the capability. Reached from Overview's Stats "View all", Top Artists' "View all" (`/stats?top=artists` deep-links the tab) and the command palette. Local components: `ActivityChart`, `RankList` (reused for the three rankings and the device list), `SplitBar`.

## 9. Theming & Localization
- 7 themes via token-override classes (chromatic, default, oled, graphite, abyss, glazedCeramic, sakura)
- 9 languages (en, de, fr, es, it, ja, pt, zh, ko), full key parity (~1211 base keys each)
- **Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, Korean locales (2026-07-22).** Full translations of all base keys; zh/ko collapse `_one`/`_other` plurals to `_other` (ja convention), pt splits `selection.selected` like es. Registered in `i18n.ts` (`LANGUAGE_OPTIONS`) + `LanguageSwitcher`. Russian was started and dropped by choice mid-generation; re-add later if wanted.
- No known gaps.
- **Custom color wheel picker (2026-07-19).** New `primitives/colorPicker/` replaces every `<input type="color">`: anchored popover with a hue ring around a saturation/brightness square, hex readout, keyboard sliders, live-drag emit. Used by the theme editor swatches and Settings → default cover colors (which now debounce store writes via the extracted `utils/useDebouncedCommit.ts`). `HexField` moved into the primitive and is shared. **Eyedropper in the wheel (2026-07-29):** the footer gained a screen-sample button, so every wheel (theme editor swatches + default cover colors) can pick a color off the page, not just the theme editor's own per-row button. `hasEyeDropper`/`pickScreenColor` extracted to `utils/eyeDropper.ts` (Chromium-only, button hidden elsewhere); the popover hides itself while sampling and reports it through the optional `onPickingChange`, which is how the theme editor modal keeps getting out of the way.
- **Color sync modes (2026-07-29).** The old inverted `disableCoverColorSync` toggle became `colorSync` (on by default) plus a `colorSyncSource` switcher with two modes: `cover` (the playing track, the default and the old behavior) and `header` (the playlist/album/artist header on screen). `DetailHeader`/`ArtistHero` publish their artwork through `store/headerCover.ts` while mounted, `mainPage` reads it and falls back to the playing cover where there is no header (home, settings) or the header's art is a glyph. Legacy persisted values migrate in `merge` (and on user-data import); `useCoverColors` now takes an already-resolved `blob:` URL straight through, so the artist hero's image isn't cached twice.
- **Chromatic by default, and a dark theme for a lit panel (2026-09-10).** `chromatic` is the out-of-the-box `theme` and heads `THEME_OPTIONS`, so a fresh install opens on the accent-tinted look the cover art drives. **Brushed Titanium was deleted** (block, option row and 9 locale labels), **`dark` was renamed `oled`** since pure black is a pick for a panel that switches pixels off, not the generic dark, and a new **`graphite`** takes that job: neutral #17181b page, panels lifted to rgba(35,37,41,.88) with white-mix hairlines, no accent override so the cover keeps coloring it, and `.op-50` nudged to 0.62 for the contrast the lift costs. `RETIRED_THEMES` carries all three moves (`dark`→`oled`, `brushedTitanium`/`neo`→`graphite`) on rehydrate and on user-data import; `nightTheme` and the custom-theme-removal fallbacks follow the renames.
- **Built-in theme swap (2026-07-20).** light/aurora/sunrise/neo retired, replaced by four designed themes ported from the theme profiles in `../proof/themes`: **Abyss** (deep-sea teal, no blur, bioluminescent glow), **Glazed Ceramic** (light, specular glaze sheen), **Sakura** (light blossom pink), **Brushed Titanium** (satin grey, tight radii, brushed grain). Ported as real `html.<key>` blocks (tokens + scoped flourishes), so themes may now also set radius/hover-scale/fill/hairline tokens. Retired keys migrate on rehydrate and on user-data import (`RETIRED_THEMES`/`migrateTheme` in `settings.tsx`: light→sakura, aurora→abyss, sunrise→glazedCeramic, neo→brushedTitanium); `dayTheme` default is sakura; `LIGHT_THEMES` replaces the `theme === "light"` check in `useNativeStatusBar`; the dead `html.light .topbar_container` / `.iconImg` rules are gone. Active player toggles (`.controlsActive`) are a `sepia+hue-rotate` chain that only tints white icons, so on/off was indistinguishable on the black icons of the two light themes: fixed inside `themes.css` for sakura/glazedCeramic only (accent color + accent chip, `:has` on the SVG buttons), the global rule and the other themes are untouched.
- **Theme rework (2026-07-09).** dark → pure-black OLED, cold steel-blue accent (`#4aa3ff`); aurora → deep indigo-navy with a violet↔teal glow (`#a855f7`/`#2dd4bf`, tinted `.uiContentContainer`); neo → matrix/CRT terminal: pitch black + acid-green phosphor foreground (`--color-white: #dcffe6`) + green neutrals, acid-green/cyan neon accent (`#7cff4d`/`#22d3ee`), pitch-black cards with lit-edge highlight + neon bloom `box-shadow` + theme-scoped green `::selection` (no longer shares sunrise's coral). Fixed malformed `--color-ui: rgba(8,8,8)` in dark. Theme-picker swatches updated (`settings.tsx` `THEME_OPTIONS`). `themes.css` + `settings.tsx`; default/light/sunrise/chromatic untouched.
- **Custom day/night switch times (2026-09-30).** Auto day/night swaps at the user's `dayStart`/`nightStart` (two 15-minute sliders under the toggle, shown in the topbar clock's 12h/24h form) instead of fixed 07:00/19:00. Night may wrap past midnight either way; a bad stored or imported value falls back via `validStart`.
- **Accent strength (2026-10-05).** Appearance slider (`accentStrength`, 10 to 60 %, default 30) sets the alpha of the translucent `--color-accent` fill that `mainPage.tsx` writes; `--color-accent-solid` stays opaque so focus rings and progress keep their contrast. Validated by `validAccentStrength` on rehydrate and import, since it lands in a CSS value.
- **Smart themes (2026-10-09).** A toggle at the top of the theme editor turns a custom theme into a smart one: six rules (color source, tone, harmony, saturation, panels, corners) and a seed are stored on the profile, every rule change regenerates its colors and radii (`utils/smartTheme.ts`), and Shuffle rolls a new seed behind the accent shimmer. Text is forced to pass the editor's AA check, a hue taken from the theme's own accent never drifts, and rules survive export/import through `sanitizeSmartRules`. Smart profiles carry the SmartIcon in the rail.

## 10. Auth & Session
- Login (provider tabs, server URL, credentials, error/loading states)
- Session restore on reload (cookie-based for Velora, password-persisted for Navidrome)
- Logout (full teardown of audio/playback/music/session/library state)
- Intro/loading splash screen, covers the cold-load session-restore gap and the login → `/home` transition. Logo over the user's configured background, indeterminate progress bar, fades via `--duration-slow`. A `useSplash` store survives the `LoginPage` ↔ `RequireAuth`/`MainPage` route boundary.
  - ↳ files: `src/store/splash.ts`, `src/assets/components/primitives/splashScreen/SplashScreen.tsx`, `src/app.tsx`
- TOTP / two-factor login (2026-06-26), server signals `TOTP_REQUIRED`/`INVALID_TOTP_CODE`; frontend appends a 6-digit authenticator-code field on the second step and passes `totpCode` to the connect call.
- First-admin bootstrap (2026-06-26), `GET /api/v1/auth/bootstrap` (added to backend) returns `{ needsBootstrap }`. Login page probes the URL (600ms debounce) and switches to "Server Setup" mode: confirm-password field, accent badge, "Create Admin Account" button. `POST /bootstrap` creates the admin + sets cookies; frontend then runs the normal connect/navigate path. Utils: `checkBootstrap`/`performBootstrap` in `veloraProvider.ts`.

## 11. Platform Expansion

**Local-mode expansion**, rebuilt incrementally after the combined pass was reverted 2026-07-15, then closed 2026-07-19 by dropping the remaining backlog (below). The detail file `docs/goalsDetails/local-mode-expansion.md` is deleted; its content is in git history.
- **Dropped: web (OPFS) `IPlatformAdapter` impl (2026-07-22).** Cut by decision, never built; don't re-propose. A browser local mode (OPFS for audio bytes + IndexedDB index + service-worker media serving + `music-metadata` import) was scoped and is buildable with zero new deps, but it's a large, self-contained platform whose audience (people running the closed web app with no server at all) is thin, and it duplicates the Electron local mode that already covers the offline case. Only the `vmedia://` hardcode in `localProvider.ts` would need generalizing (adapter owns the stream/cover URL scheme) if it's ever revived; Capacitor's adapter is still open and would want the same refactor. Local mode on web stays unavailable (`getPlatformAdapter()` returns null in the browser, so the login tab doesn't appear).
- **Dropped: local-mode Smart Radio + delete-track (2026-07-19).** Cut from the local-mode expansion by decision, never built; don't re-propose. Smart Radio would have flipped the `smartRadio` capability with an offline `getSimilarSongs` (genre/artist/bpm/year scoring via `json_each`); delete-track would have flipped `deleteTrack` + `isAdmin: true` on the synthetic local user (delete = `rmSync` + row DELETE + `pruneOrphanCovers`). The consuming UI is capability-gated and stays hidden in local mode with both caps off, so nothing else changes.
- **Dropped: songKey storage persistence + Reset button (2026-07-19).** The plan to key local favorites/playlists/plays by a stable songKey (normalized `artist|title|album`) so they survive a folder switch, plus a Reset-storage button. A combined implementation broke local-mode loading and was reverted 2026-07-15; dropped rather than rebuilt. Consequence accepted: local user data stays keyed by track-row id and does not carry across music folders (each folder's per-hash DB keeps its own). If ever revived, the migration gotchas (transactional table rebuilds, delimiter in the key formula, override re-parse orphaning favorites, duplicate handling) are in git history of `docs/goalsDetails/local-mode-expansion.md`.
- **User-choosable music folder (2026-07-19).** One library per folder (goals.md §11): the chosen folder lives in `desktop-prefs.json` under `localMusicDir` (readable before any DB opens, so it can't sit in the library meta table), extracted with `readPrefs`/`writePrefs` into a new `electron/prefs.ts`. `musicDir()` follows it; the DB + covers dir are scoped per folder by a `sha256(normalizedPath).slice(0,16)` hash (`local-library-<hash>.db` / `covers-<hash>/`), the default `<OS Music>/Velora` keeping the legacy unsuffixed paths so existing data is untouched; path normalized + lowercased on win32. `chooseFolder()` (dialog, rejects a folder inside userData, no-op on the active folder, drops the prefs key when the default is re-picked) resets the module singletons and reopens the new library; new `local:chooseFolder` IPC + adapter method. Missing-folder guard: `getDb()` no longer creates a custom folder, `scan()` bails without touching rows if the folder is gone (an empty scan would FK-cascade away favorites/playlists/history), `importFile()` recreates it on explicit import, and `status()` gained `folderExists`. Settings → Local Library got a "Change folder" button that clears playback first (per-folder ids collide) then rescans, plus an unavailable-folder warning line.
- **Genre browsing (2026-07-17).** `getGenres`/`getSongsByGenre` over `json_each(t.genres)` (songCount `COUNT(DISTINCT t.id)`; albumCount only over `HAVING COUNT(*)>1` albumKeys; songs-by-genre uses `EXISTS` so a duplicated tag can't double the row); full seam adapter→preload→provider + `genreBrowsing` flipped. **Redesign:** genres moved off the nav tab into a home carousel section (`HomeGenres`, gated on `genreBrowsing`) with "View all" → `/genres`; extracted a shared `GenreCard` primitive (V2 §10 card grammar) used by both the home section and the full view.
- **Play history + stats (2026-07-18).** `plays` table (trackId FK cascade + playedAt, indexed); `LocalPlayRecorder` observes every `ClientPlaybackController.commit()` (progress ticks included), one play per listen, a listen starts on id change OR position reset to <2s from >5s (covers repeat-one/end-of-queue/manual restart), counts at ≥30s or ≥85%, restored resume state never credits. Gated `supports("localLibrary")`, fire-and-forget `recordPlay`. `getUserStats` (playtime = plays × duration, monthly = calendar month like Velora, recentlyListened 50, topArtists 20) + `getMostPlayedAlbums` (albumPlays CTE over `ALBUM_COLS`), full seam adapter→preload→provider; `userStats` + `mostPlayedAlbums` flipped, storage fields 0 (cap stays off).
- **Home empty-library prompt (2026-07-18).** Not local-only: `HomeEmptyState` replaces *all* home sections whenever `albumsLoaded && artistsLoaded` and both counts are 0 (every section would hide itself and leave a blank page). CTA opens the upload/import overlay when `canAddMusic`, else a plain caption (`empty.libraryReadOnly`). `homeView` loads albums+artists itself (cached loaders) so the check holds even when those sections are hidden. Shipped with the app-wide empty-state pass (§13).
- **Desktop API v2 reads + command verbs (2026-07-17).** Search round-trip generalized to ONE `api-data:*` channel serving `GET /v1/{queue,playlists,library,similar}` (Bearer + no-CORS, per-kind sanitizers, `library` paged via `cursor`/`limit`, `similar` gated on the new `similarSupported` snapshot flag = smartRadio cap). Verbs `addToQueue`/`playNext`(→`addNext`)/`favorite`(current track, optional bool) added to `parseCommand` + `check-desktop-api.mjs` + the `useDesktopIntegration` command switch. Discovery caps advertise all four reads + verbs.
- **Desktop API v3: relative control, entity playback, artwork, a positional feed (2026-08-09).** Purely additive over v2, so the wallpaper and the import companion keep working untouched: every v2 route, field, header and default is unchanged, the new SSE frame is a *named* `progress` event (invisible to a v2 `EventSource.onmessage`) and a WS ack only fires for a client that sent a `requestId`. Control gained `volume`/`seek` deltas (exactly one of absolute or relative, both or neither is `INVALID_COMMAND`), `mute` (derived from the engine volume, so the app's own mute button and a client agree; the restore level is runtime-only), `playTrack`/`playPlaylist` (mirroring the app's own `setQueue` grammar, context hints included) and `playIndex`. Reads gained `GET /v1/playlist?id=` and `GET /v1/track/cover?id=`, the latter deliberately Bearer + no-CORS rather than an extension of the open `/v1/cover`, because artwork for an arbitrary id is a library read like `/v1/search`; its cache is bounded by entries, bytes, a provider stamp (ids are only unique per provider) and a 60s TTL (nothing observes a re-cover). `GET /v1/search` took `type=album|artist|all` while `type=track` stayed byte-identical. Position is now interpolated in main from a receive stamp and pushed from the engine clock, not the controller's 5s-stale `currentTime`, with a 1s `progress` frame on SSE and WS while something is playing and someone is listening. Discovery advertises the new caps plus a top-level `commands` array served from a single `SUPPORTED_COMMANDS` in `apiValidation.js`. Protocol doc rewritten as v3 (`../plans/desktop-api-protocol.md`), which also fixed two stale v2 claims: the v2 reads and verbs were never documented, and import `429 BUSY` is strict single-flight, not "more than 3 in flight".

**Desktop mini player window (2026-09-05).** A small frameless always-on-top now-playing window, `app://velora/#mini`, built on the palette overlay's split: the app renderer stays the brain and publishes a snapshot (`src/utils/miniPlayer.ts`, mounted in `mainPage`), the window draws it and reports the button that was pressed, so every control still mutates the one queue, engine and session that exist. It gets its own narrow preload (`electron/preloadMini.cts`, nine calls over eight channels) rather than the app's: no local library, no plugin files, no vmedia key, and no cover url either, since a Subsonic one carries credentials in its query string, so artwork travels as keyed data-url bytes like the palette's. Transport runs through the existing keybind dispatcher, so favorite, skip and play/pause behave exactly as the keys do; seek is a `seek` command with a validated 0..1 ratio; the wheel over the window is volume, with a readout that leaves. The look travels whole (theme class, the inline `:root` tokens, the `data-*` a11y attributes) and is republished off a `MutationObserver` on `:root`, debounced, because the accent is derived from the cover *after* the track change and no store update announces it; dragging a chrome resize handle rewrites `--nav-width` on every pointer move, which is what the debounce is for.
- **The controls are the app's own primitives**, `FavoriteButton` / `SkipButton` / `PlayPauseButton` / `Button`, animations included, rather than lookalikes: a second set of transport buttons is how a window starts reading as something built next to the app instead of part of it. They bring i18n and the settings store into the document (they translate their own labels and read the animation settings), which is the price, and the window then translates all of its own strings, so the snapshot carries a `language` rather than a label table. What still never gets in is a second session, audio engine or playback connection. Two consequences to keep: the settings store is switched to a no-op storage right after it hydrates (`miniEntry.tsx`), because it subscribes to the OS preferences at module scope and one of those firing would persist this window's stale snapshot over the app's newer settings; and i18n is imported first in that entry because it top-level awaits the detected language, which resolves from the same `velora-language` key the app writes. Two knock-ons of that freeze, both accepted: a settings change made after the window opened reaches its CSS (the snapshot carries the tokens and the `data-*` attributes) but not the JS-driven icon animations, which read the store; and a custom theme's advanced raw CSS body is file-backed on desktop, so this document restores the profile's tokens (through the snapshot) but not that body. Widening the preload to fix either would give the window the app's bridge back, which is the whole thing being avoided.
- **Costs nothing while closed**, unlike the overlay, which keeps a hidden renderer so its chord opens instantly. Nothing exists until the first toggle, closing calls `close()` so the process actually ends, and the host subscribes to playback only between `mini:open` and `mini:close`. The trade is a few hundred ms on first open, which is right for a window you leave up rather than flash.
- **One markup, two shapes**, decided by a container query on the window's own aspect ratio: a bar (cover square, title over artist, transport, the playhead left to the seek line along the bottom because that row is tight) while it is wide, and past 8/5 a poster where the artwork becomes the window, the meta line has room for the playhead counter, and the controls sit on a band that blurs it. The window is resizable, so the shape is the setting; bounds and the pin live in `desktop-prefs.json`. **It is dragged in JS, not by a `-webkit-app-region` region**, which hands its mouse events to the OS: the window moved, but the wheel never reached the volume and `:hover` never fired, so the chrome holding the pin stayed invisible, and a region covering the window edge eats the resize border too. No coordinate crosses the bridge: the renderer says only that the pointer moved and main places the window from `getCursorScreenPoint()`, because a renderer's `screenX` is its own display's CSS pixels and stops meaning the same thing halfway across a monitor with another scale factor. The size travels with every placement (one `setBounds`, all four numbers rounded), so a DPI change mid-drag has nothing left to rescale. Every channel the window itself can send runs through `onMiniIpc`, which does the sender check and logs rather than letting a bad argument reach the main process as an uncaught exception.
- **Pinned by default** at the `floating` level, not the palette's `screen-saver`: a window that stays up must not sit permanently over a fullscreen game. The pin drops it back into the stack, and main owns the property, handing the initial value over as a launch argument the way the media key is. It is the one piece of chrome that never hides, because whether the window floats has to be readable at a glance: floating paints the glyph in the accent, upright and at full opacity, off it is a dim tilted pin. The chrome row follows the theme's own icon brightness in bar shape, where it sits on the page background and a light theme wants black glyphs, and takes the clock's scrim chip in poster shape, where it is on artwork. Expand and close still reveal on hover, keeping their space so the pin cannot shift under the pointer.
- **It keeps the size the user gave it.** Windows rescales a window when it crosses to a display with another scale factor, and on a frameless one that correction compounds: a few trips between a 100% and a 150% monitor and it has doubled. `bindMiniSizeStability` remembers the intended bounds and re-asserts them for any resize outside a real drag-resize (`will-resize`/`resized` bracket that; nothing else in the app resizes this window). Win32 only, which is where the behaviour lives.
- **In the taskbar**, unlike the palette overlay, which flashes up for a second: this is a window you alt-tab back to and minimize like any other, and its entry names the track. Both windows sit under one Velora icon because `app.setAppUserModelId` now names the app explicitly (Windows groups taskbar buttons by that id, and left alone it is derived from the running exe, which is electron.exe in dev).
- The surface is painted from `--color-background` + the `--surface-border` pair rather than composing `.uiContentContainer`, which lives in `mainPage.css`, a file this document deliberately never loads; the tokens are in `index.css`, so themes, density, text scale, reduce-motion and reduce-transparency all still reach it, and the accent re-tints the seek fill with the cover. The top-left carries the wall clock whenever the topbar's own is on (same `clock12h` format, ticked on the minute), since the taskbar clock is exactly what a fullscreen game hides; play is the middle of a three-part transport row, so the two skips stay equidistant from it however many buttons the sides carry. (The palette overlay does compose that class and therefore gets nothing from it, which is why its own `--surface-paint` override is dead code there; left alone.)
