- Entry points: a `toggleMiniPlayer` keybind command (desktop-only, in-app or system-wide), a command palette row, a pop-out button in the player's right cluster, and a tray item, which is routed through the renderer rather than main's toggle so a mini player can't be opened from the login screen with nothing to draw into it. `clock()` is spelled locally rather than pulled from `formatDuration`, which formats spoken durations through i18n; this is a clock face. Artwork is one slot, not a cache: the window holds only the cover it is drawing and the host resends whenever that key changes, so a window left up all day cannot accumulate a data url per track. Logging out with it open blanks it rather than leaving the last user's track on screen.
- ↳ files: `src/mini/`, `src/utils/miniPlayer.ts`, `electron/preloadMini.cts`, `electron/main.ts`, `electron/prefs.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/utils/keybindActions.ts`, `src/utils/useKeybindDispatch.ts`

**Desktop shell via Electron, v1 (2026-07-07).** `electron/main.ts` (ESM) + `electron/preload.cts` (sandboxed CJS), compiled by `tsc -p electron` into `dist-electron/`. Frameless `BrowserWindow`; prod serves `dist/` over a privileged `app://velora` protocol with SPA fallback (`file://` would break BrowserRouter and give cookies no stable origin), dev loads the vite server via `electron . --dev-url http://localhost:5500`. Hardened defaults: `contextIsolation` + `sandbox` on, `nodeIntegration` off, external links open in the OS browser, navigation locked to the app origin, F12 toggles devtools (no menu bar in a frameless window). The preload bridge exposes only `minimize/toggleMaximize/close` as `window.veloraDesktop`, no fs/node surface crosses it, per the §11 IPC rule. Frontend side: `src/utils/platform.ts` (`isElectron()` + bridge types), `html.electron` root class for CSS gating, PWA updater disabled in the shell, topbar-as-titlebar + `WindowControls` (see §5). Scripts: `build:electron`, `desktop` (dev), `desktop:prod`. Packaging (electron-builder installers) deliberately deferred, see §11 Planned.
- ↳ files: `electron/`, `src/utils/platform.ts`, `package.json` (`main` field + scripts), `eslint.config.js`, `.gitignore`

**Desktop tray mini-player + global media keys + NSIS packaging (2026-07-10).**
- **Tray / close-to-tray**: closing the window hides it (playback keeps running); only the tray's Quit (or an OS-initiated quit via `before-quit`) exits. Tray menu: current track line (disabled), Play/Pause, Next, Previous, Show, Quit; tooltip mirrors the track. Click/double-click the tray icon shows the window. `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` added so a second launch focuses the existing window instead of spawning one (essential once the app lives in the tray).
- **Global media keys**: `globalShortcut.register` for `MediaPlayPause`/`MediaNextTrack`/`MediaPreviousTrack`/`MediaStop` on ready, `unregisterAll` on `will-quit`; works while unfocused or hidden in the tray. (Complements the §1 Media Session API item, which covers browser/mobile lock-screen surfaces.)
- **Media keys hold on, rather than only while playing (2026-09-07).** They were registered on the `isPlaying` push alone, so a launch and every reload (both land paused) came up with the keys unclaimed and the play key dead on the one press that would have fixed it. `syncMediaKeys()` now decides from three things: playing, a track loaded at all (`nowPlaying.title || artist`, which survives a reload since main keeps the last push), or the window focused, and only a Velora with nothing to play and nothing in front lets go. `globalShortcut` is greedy and first-come, so a key another app already holds simply fails: `heldMediaKeys` tracks what actually registered and a 10s ticker runs only while something is missing, taking each key as soon as its holder releases it. `powerMonitor`'s `resume`/`unlock-screen` re-take them outright, since a sleep can drop a registration on the OS side while Electron still believes it holds one. Second half of the same bug: a key pressed while the renderer is still booting had nobody listening, so `sendCommand` parks one command (8s TTL) and replays it on the first `playback:nowPlaying` push after a **new main-frame document** loads, which is the signal that `useDesktopIntegration`'s listener is live again (a plugin iframe navigating is not a reload, and neither is a same-document route change: nothing is pushed after one, so treating it as a reload would strand the parked command). Trade-off taken deliberately: a paused Velora now keeps the keys from whatever else is playing, which the old gate avoided; Windows SMTC would share them instead and is still the real fix.
- **Bridge**: preload gains `onPlaybackCommand` (main → renderer transport commands) and `setNowPlaying` (renderer → main display-only `{title, artist, isPlaying}` plus translated tray labels, i18n stays in the renderer; main holds English fallbacks until the first push). Still no fs/node surface. Renderer side is one hook, `useDesktopIntegration` (`src/utils/`), mounted in `mainPage.tsx`: commands dispatch through `playbackService.sendCommand(...)`, state mirrors off `playbackService.subscribe` (deduped, and since subscribe re-emits current state, a language change refreshes the labels). No-op on web/Capacitor; both bridge methods are optional in the type so an older packaged preload can't break the renderer.
- **BigMusic titlebar fix**: BigMusic (`--z-bigmusic`) covers the topbar, which on Electron is the titlebar, leaving no reachable caption buttons or drag region while the overlay is open. The overlay now renders `<WindowControls floating />` (the login page's fixed top-right variant + drag strip) when `isElectron()`; BigMusic's own close button sits top-left so they don't collide.
- **Packaging**: `electron-builder` (dev dep) + `electron-builder.yml`: appId `de.uplift-beyond.velora`, NSIS target (assisted installer, choosable dir), icon `build/icon.png` (copy of pwa-512), `files` limited to `dist/` + `dist-electron/` with `!node_modules/**` (renderer is fully bundled; main has no runtime npm deps, keeps the package lean). `npm run desktop:dist` builds to `release/` (gitignored). `electronDist: node_modules/electron/dist` copies the locally installed electron instead of download+extract, the extract's dir rename gets EPERM-blocked in this environment (likely Defender on the Downloads path). Window/tray icons now resolve via `assetPath()` (dist/ first, public/ fallback) so they exist inside the packaged asar.
- ↳ files: `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.cts`, `src/utils/platform.ts`, `src/utils/useDesktopIntegration.ts`, `mainPage.tsx`, `bigMusic.tsx`, `electron-builder.yml`, `build/icon.png`, `package.json` (`desktop:dist`, description/author), all 6 locales (`desktop.tray.*`; reuses `player.playPause`/`player.next`)

**`electron-builder` 22 → 26: dropped 2026-08-09, it was never open.** The roadmap carried a "(Next)" bump citing three `npm audit` highs (NSIS installer arbitrary-code-exec, AppImage search path, `builder-util-runtime` credential leak). The dep has been `^26.15.3` since `910f9e3` (2026-07-10), the same commit that added NSIS packaging above, so every installer ever built came off 26 and the NSIS/publish config it wanted re-verified is the config that shipped. `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. The item was written against a stale audit; there is nothing to bump and nothing to re-verify.

Mobile shell via Capacitor, Android (2026-06-21). The `android/` project itself (deps, `capacitor.config.ts`, gitignored native folder) was scaffolded in an earlier pass alongside the §18 mobile-responsive retrofit; this pass added the actual native integration:
- **Hardware back button**: `useNativeBackButton` (`src/utils/`) listens for `@capacitor/app`'s `backButton` event. `canGoBack: true` calls `window.history.back()`, which feeds the same popstate path `useBackButtonDismiss` and react-router already consume, so it closes an open overlay/sheet or does router back-nav for free, no Android-specific branching needed in either of those. `canGoBack: false` (root of history) requires a second press within 2s, shows a `toast.info(t("app.pressBackToExit"))` and arms a timer, before calling `App.exitApp()`, so a stray press doesn't kill the app outright.
- **Status bar / safe-area**: `useNativeStatusBar` (`src/utils/`) calls `StatusBar.setOverlaysWebView({ overlay: true })` once on mount, which is what makes the `--safe-top`/etc. `env(safe-area-inset-*)` tokens (already built in §18) report real values on Android, without overlay mode the WebView never draws under the system bars, so the insets stay 0. Icon style (`StatusBar.setStyle`) reacts to `useSettings().theme`, `Style.Light` (dark icons) for the `light` theme, `Style.Dark` (light icons) for every other theme, since all of them have a dark base surface.
- **Splash handoff**: `capacitor.config.ts` sets `SplashScreen.launchAutoHide: false` so the native launch splash stays up until JS explicitly hides it; `app.tsx` calls `SplashScreen.hide()` in a plain `useEffect`. Because `RequireAuth`'s `useLayoutEffect` (which shows the JS `SplashHost`) runs before any `useEffect` in the same commit, the JS splash is already painted by the time the native one hides, no white-flash gap between the two.
- Added `@capacitor/app`, `@capacitor/status-bar`, `@capacitor/splash-screen`; `npm run build:android` (build + `cap sync android`) and `npm run cap:android` (open Android Studio) scripts.
- **App icon / splash branding**: replaced Capacitor's default placeholder mark (the generated `android/` project's stock icon/splash, never touched since `cap add android`) with the real Velora logo. Added `@capacitor/assets` (dev dependency) + `assets/logo.png` (copy of `public/veloraLogo.png`); `npx @capacitor/assets generate --android --iconBackgroundColor '#080808' --splashBackgroundColor '#080808'` (also `*Dark` variants, same value) regenerated all adaptive-icon layers, legacy/round icons, and portrait/landscape/light/dark splash variants from it. Used `--color-background`'s actual value (`#080808`) rather than inventing a new brand color, since no "icon background purple" token exists anywhere in the design system.
- iOS deliberately not scaffolded yet (no Mac/Xcode to build/test one), see §11 Planned. The bootstrap code itself is platform-agnostic (`Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` gates correctly); only the back-button hook is inherently Android-only (iOS has no hardware back button).
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/useNativeBackButton.ts`, `src/utils/useNativeStatusBar.ts`, `src/app.tsx`, `capacitor.config.ts`, `package.json`, `assets/logo.png`, all 6 `src/locales/*/translation.json` (`app.pressBackToExit`)

On a new build it fires a sticky `toast.info(t("app.updateAvailable"))` whose tap action runs `updateServiceWorker(true)`. Added an optional `action?: () => void` to the toast store/viewport (tap runs it instead of dismissing, reusable). Icons (`pwa-192/512/512-maskable/apple-touch-icon`) generated from `public/veloraLogo.png` (4000² source) via a one-off sharp script (sharp not added to deps). `theme_color`/`background_color` = `#080808` (the `--color-background` value).

**Desktop window bounds persistence (2026-07-12).** Electron stores normal window `x/y/width/height` + maximized state in `userData/desktop-prefs.json`, restores on launch, clamps the saved rectangle back into the matched work area when too little is visible after a display change. Maximized restore is deferred while start-minimized is active (launch at login stays hidden in the tray). Bounds not saved while minimized/fullscreen/maximized.

**Windows taskbar thumbnail toolbar (2026-07-12).** Prev / play-pause / next on the taskbar preview (`win.setThumbarButtons`, win32 only). Reuses the tray's transport commands (`sendCommand`) + `nowPlaying`, no renderer wiring, play/pause icon + tooltips swap with state (`updateThumbar()` called on toggle since the icon depends on `isPlaying`).

**Global favorite shortcut, desktop (2026-07-13; superseded 2026-08-04 by the per-command global keymap, §6).** The favorite keybind was already customizable in-app (`toggleFavoriteTrack`, default `L`); added a desktop-only OS-level variant `globalFavoriteTrack` (default `Ctrl+L`, in `DESKTOP_GLOBAL_ACTIONS`, skipped by the in-app matcher) that fires when Velora is unfocused. Opt-in via `useSettings.globalFavoriteShortcut` (default off, a `globalShortcut` is greedy) in a desktop-only "Global (desktop)" group in Settings → Keybinds. Renderer pushes the accelerator via `setFavoriteShortcut`; `main.ts` registers via `globalShortcut` (modifier-less bindings refused) and fires `shortcut:favorite:fired` back; `useDesktopIntegration` toggles the current track's favorite. Cleaned up by `will-quit` `unregisterAll`. i18n `settings.keybinds.globalSection`/`globalFavorite`/`globalFavoriteDesc`/`actions.globalFavoriteTrack` ×6.

**Desktop tray toggles + wheel-volume (2026-07-12, extends the 2026-07-10 tray item).** Settings → Integrations desktop toggles: close-to-tray `useSettings.closeToTray` (default on) → `window:closeToTray`; launch-on-startup `openAtLogin` → `app:openAtLogin` (`setLoginItemSettings`); start-minimized `startMinimized` → `app:startMinimized` (persisted to `userData/desktop-prefs.json`, read at `ready-to-show`). Real quit paths confirm when a local library scan or Electron update download is running; hide-to-tray stays silent. Plus cross-platform `wheelVolume` (default on), scroll over the player's volume control nudges volume in slider space.

**Desktop fullscreen (F11) handling (2026-07-10).** Main pushes `window:fullscreen` over IPC (`enter/leave-full-screen`, re-sent on `did-finish-load`); `useDesktopFullscreen()` hides the topbar/titlebar (`mainPage.tsx`) and every `WindowControls` instance while fullscreen, F11 toggles back. `window:toggleMaximize` exits fullscreen defensively. Fixed the caption close button hovering grey instead of `--color-danger` (specificity). And fixed the caption buttons being dead since shell v1: `onClick={bridge.minimize}` passed the contextBridge function directly, so React's SyntheticEvent hit the bridge's argument serialization and threw "object could not be cloned", handlers now wrapped (`onClick={() => bridge.minimize()}`); never pass a bridged function directly as an event handler.

**Desktop auto-update (2026-07-10).** electron-updater over a generic (static) feed (`publish` in `electron-builder.yml` → `https://uplift-beyond.de/velora/desktop`): checks hourly + on launch (packaged only), downloads in the background (blockmap deltas), then surfaces through the same `useAppUpdate` store as the web SW so the nav pill prompts; click = silent `quitAndInstall` + relaunch, ignored = installs on next real quit. Main is now esbuild-bundled (`scripts/build-electron.mjs`, ESM + createRequire banner) since the package ships no node_modules; preload stays tsc. IPC: `update:ready` (re-sent on `did-finish-load`) / `update:install`; renderer in `useDesktopIntegration`. Publishing = upload `latest.yml` + `Velora-Setup-x.y.z.exe` + `.blockmap` from `release/` to the feed URL after `npm run desktop:dist`. Unsigned is fine (no `publisherName`); set `publisherName` if ever code-signed. Automated server-side: `n8n/deploy-electron.sh` builds the Windows installer on Linux and copies the three feed files to `/var/www/html/uplift/velora/desktop`, plus a stable `Velora-Setup.exe` (`DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL`). Gotcha: the local EPERM workaround `electronDist` moved out of `electron-builder.yml` into the `desktop:dist` script (`-c.electronDist=...`), on the yml it would make the server package Linux electron into the Windows installer. Settings → About "Check for updates" runs a real manual check (`update:check` → `checkForUpdates()`, toasts found/ready/up-to-date; `about.updateFound`/`about.updateReady` ×6).
  - ↳ background download now a setting (2026-07-12): `useSettings.desktopBackgroundUpdate` (default off) → Settings → Integrations → Updates, `isElectron()`-gated → main `autoUpdater.autoDownload` via `update:setBackgroundDownload`. Off: main skips the download and pushes `update:available`; the nav pill shows a "download" phase (`useAppUpdate.phase`) that calls `update:download`, flips to passive `downloading`, then normal `ready`/install on `update-downloaded`. Flipping it on with an update waiting downloads immediately. Renderer wiring in `useDesktopIntegration`.
  - ↳ web auto-update now a setting (2026-07-12): `useSettings.webAutoUpdate` (default off) → Settings → Integrations → Updates, `isBrowser()`-gated. On: `PWAUpdater` silently reloads (`updateServiceWorker(true)`), no pill. Off: existing nav pill. i18n `settings.integrations.webAutoUpdate*` + `settings.subheaders.updates` ×6.
  - ↳ fixed (2026-07-12): the manual "Check for updates" toast always said "downloading in the background" even with background download off; `AboutSection.tsx` now reads `desktopBackgroundUpdate` and picks `about.updateFound` (bg on) vs new `about.updateFoundManual` (bg off) ×6.

**Discord Rich Presence (2026-07-11).** Desktop only. Hand-rolled Discord IPC client in main (`electron/discordPresence.ts`, `node:net`, no npm dep, official `discord-rpc` is deprecated) driven off the `playback:nowPlaying` push (extended with position/duration). Shows "Listening to Velora" + title/artist + a live progress bar (dropped when paused); static `velora` logo asset (cover art isn't feasible, auth-bound/`vmedia://` URLs aren't public). Public app id `1525545639025574088` (no secret/token sent). Opt-in via `useSettings.discordRichPresence` (default off) → Settings → Integrations, `isElectron()`-gated; renderer pushes the enable flag + a seek-guard refresh via `setDiscordEnabled`/`setNowPlaying`. Reconnects when Discord starts/restarts; main throttles + clears on quit. i18n `settings.integrations.discordRichPresence*` ×6. Hardened: authenticated-shell cleanup disables/clears presence; every activity frame observes Discord's five-per-20s limit; title/artist trimmed, clamped to 128 chars, omitted when < 2 chars.
  - ↳ still open: a `velora` art asset must be uploaded in the Discord dev portal (Rich Presence → Art Assets) for the logo to render; presence works without it, just no image.

**Desktop loopback now-playing API (2026-07-12).** Exposes the current track for any provider on a `127.0.0.1:9863` HTTP server (`electron/localApi.ts`) so other local apps consume it without touching the backend or auth. Endpoints (all CORS `*`, loopback only): `GET /now-playing` (JSON), `GET /events` (SSE), `GET /cover` (bytes), `POST /command` (play/pause/toggle/next/previous/stop/seek → forwarded to the renderer on `playback:command`). Snapshot: `{ provider, isPlaying, positionSeconds, durationSeconds, volume, favorited, shuffle, repeat, queueIndex, queueLength, track:{id,title,artist,album}|null, coverUrl, colors, lyrics, updatedAt }`. Renderer side `useLocalApi()` (in `useDesktopIntegration.ts`, mounted from `mainPage.tsx`): subscribes to `playbackService` + `audioEngine` volume + `useSession` favorites + provider type, dedups with the tray seek-guard, resolves lyrics (embedded `track.stats.lyrics` or `musicService.getLyrics`), fetches cover bytes on track change, derives the cover palette via `coverColorsFromBlob` (extracted from `useCoverColors`, hex, index 0 = accent), hands all to main (main re-serves the cover on `/cover`; auth-bound `vmedia://` cover URLs never leave the renderer). Toggle: `useSettings.localApi` (default off), Settings → Integrations, `isElectron()`-gated; server stops + clears on logout and quit. ⚠️ Responses carry `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`, without it Chromium's Private Network Access blocks any public/`file://` origin (the live Wallpaper Engine wallpaper) from reaching a loopback server. **velora-wallpaper** (`../other/velora-wallpaper`) rewired onto this (EventSource `/events`, cover `/cover`, palette + lyrics from the snapshot); its old backend login/WebSocket/ticket flow deleted, so it now depends on the desktop app running. i18n `settings.integrations.localApi*` ×6.

**Local mode (desktop v1) + platform adapter (2026-07-11).** Scope: core only (scan/browse/play/search/favorites/playlists/resume; in-app import added 2026-07-12; no local history/stats, `userStats` off like Navidrome); library folder is the fixed app-managed `<OS Music>/Velora`, auto-created.
- **Main process owns everything** (`electron/localLibrary.ts`): `node:sqlite` DB at `userData/local-library.db` (tracks/playlists/playlist_tracks/favorites/meta; albums/artists are `GROUP BY` views), `music-metadata` tag scan (upsert by path, mtime+size skip, deletes vanished files), album covers extracted to `userData/covers/<albumKey>.jpg`. Zero native deps: Electron 43's Node 24.17 has `node:sqlite` built in; `music-metadata` is esbuild-inlined into `dist-electron/main.js` (kept in `dependencies` only so `gen:licenses` emits its MIT notice; web `dist/` unaffected).
- **In-app import** (2026-07-12): local mode reuses Home's Upload button + overlay with native file/folder pickers. Selected audio copied into the managed folder without overwriting; folder imports preserve the root dir, structure, and common folder-cover images; excludes the managed library subtree; queues a fresh scan after any active scan. Rescans + refreshes immediately.
- **Metadata editing** (2026-07-13): local tracks use the shared Edit Info context-menu modal for title/artist/album/cover. Text corrections persist in a SQLite override layer so rescans can't erase them; custom JPEG/PNG/WebP covers are main-process validated, capped at 10 MB, stored under cache-safe per-track keys. Album/artist/playlist/favorites caches refresh after saving; mounted track lists patch the edited row without resetting scroll.
- **Title cleanup** (2026-07-12): scans match backend rules for embedded/filename-inferred artist prefixes + parenthesized/bracketed suffixes, including already-indexed tracks. **Missing albums** (2026-07-12): tracks without an embedded album show `-` (matches the backend's null-album behavior). **Metadata refresh retry** (2026-07-12): a failed file keeps the migration pending so the next scan retries it.
- **`vmedia://` protocol** (`main.ts`, registered in dev too): `vmedia://track/<id>` streams audio, `vmedia://cover/<key>` serves covers. ⚠️ Range requests served manually (`createReadStream` + 206/`Content-Range`): `net.fetch(pathToFileURL)` inside `protocol.handle` ignores the Range header and returns full-body 200s, so Chromium treated the source as unseekable, every timeline seek snapped to 0:00. Every response carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and the engine attaches `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`, without that pairing the Web Audio graph outputs silence (same trap as Navidrome CORS). ⚠️ The scheme must be registered with `corsEnabled: true`, else Chromium blocks every cross-origin request before it reaches the handler (no audio, no covers).
- **Narrow IPC** (`local:*` invokes + `local:scanProgress` push) exposed as `veloraDesktop.local` in `preload.cts`; the bridge implements `IPlatformAdapter` 1:1 (`src/services/platform/IPlatformAdapter.ts`; `getPlatformAdapter()` in `electronPlatformAdapter.ts`, future Capacitor/web impls slot in there). No raw fs/SQL crosses the bridge.

Bearer-token auth: 32-byte base64url token generated from Settings → Integrations, safeStorage(DPAPI)-encrypted at `<userData>/import-token.bin`, constant-time compare, copy-to-clipboard in main so plaintext never reaches the renderer (unavailable without safeStorage). Recording: new `src/services/playback/localPlayRecorder.ts`, observed from `ClientPlaybackController.commit()` on every committed state (incl. the ~5s progress ticks). One listen = one play: a listen starts when the current track id changes or its position drops to <2s from >5s (covers repeat-one, end-of-queue replay, manual restart, not just id transitions), and counts once past 30s or 85% of duration (short tracks); first sight mid-track (restored resume) marks itself already-counted so a reload never credits a phantom play. - **Custom-theme CSS moved out of localStorage on desktop (2026-07-26).** A theme profile's raw CSS body used to ride the persisted settings blob, which the whole settings object shares with the ~5 MB origin quota, so the cap had to stay small (20k, raised to 200k the same day) or one big theme could push the blob past the quota and silently lose every setting. On desktop the body is now a file, `userData/themes/<id>.css` (`electron/themeCss.ts`, a three-handler `theme-css:list|write|delete` surface), and the cap there is 2 MB. The renderer half is `src/utils/themeCssStore.ts`: `cssLimit()` answers per platform (read at call time, never cached) and is what `sanitizeThemeCss`, the editor's `maxLength`, and both import trust boundaries consume. The store shape is unchanged, `css` is still the in-memory field everything reads; `settings.tsx` only strips it in `partialize` when the bridge exists, fills the bodies back in once at boot (then re-applies the active theme, so a file-backed body lands a tick after the tokens), and mirrors `customThemes` to disk from **one** subscription so every write path (editor, import, delete, user-data restore) is covered without knowing where the CSS lives. Existing profiles migrate for free: a body only in the store is written out on that first mirror pass, and the next persist drops it from localStorage. The id is the trust boundary since it becomes a filename, main refuses anything but `[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}` and `sanitizeStoredThemes` re-mints an imported id that couldn't be one. Web is unchanged (no bridge, 200k, body stays in the blob), and an older packaged preload without the bridge degrades to exactly that.
  - ↳ files: `electron/themeCss.ts` (new), `electron/{main.ts,preload.cts}`, `src/utils/{themeCssStore.ts (new),cssPolicy.js,sanitizeCss.ts,customThemes.ts,platform.ts}`, `src/settings.tsx`, `ThemeCssEditor.tsx`, `scripts/check-theme-css.mjs`, `tests/utils/themeCssStore.test.ts` (new)

Design: a proportional by-format disk meter (one flex segment per format, accent-ramp tints via `color-mix(accent-solid → color-ui)`, monochrome so it tracks the cover accent instead of a hardcoded palette) with a matched-swatch legend; segments grow-in on load. Same block surfaces the recomputable waveform cache with a red destructive **Clear cache** (`SettingsButton variant="danger"` + `confirmAction({variant:"destructive"})`, disabled when empty). The IndexedDB peaks store (`velora-peaks`, shared by local + Subsonic-on-desktop) was extracted out of `clientPeaks.ts` into a reusable `utils/derivedCache.ts` (`cacheGet`/`cachePut`/`derivedCacheStats`/`clearDerivedCache`), one clearable seam for future derived data too. i18n `settings.localLibrary.storage.*` ×6.

- **Tauri desktop shell built to Phase 0, then dropped (2026-08-06).** A second shell beside `electron/`, same React app out of the same `dist/`. Dropped by decision, not by failure: the Electron shell already ships and works, so a second desktop surface is not worth carrying. It reached a runnable app (frameless window, a `velora://` protocol with SPA fallback and the missing-`.html` 404 that stops `plugin-frame.html` ever being answered with the app shell, window controls, drag regions, single instance, an ACL-gated per-launch media key, an http(s)-only opener), with `cargo test` green on the traversal refusals and the whole TS suite passing. The renderer half stands on its own: `isElectron()` split into `isDesktopShell()` (the 28 sites that meant "is there a desktop shell") and `isElectron()` (only the `html.electron` toggle, since `-webkit-app-region` is Electron-only). Everything is on the **`tauri-shell` branch** at `830dd67`, with the design, the full parity map and phases 1 to 6 in `docs/goalsDetails/tauri-shell.md` on that branch. Do not re-propose without a reason Electron cannot cover: the known costs are a second packaging pipeline that **cannot** cross-build from the Linux deploy box (no wine path, Tauri links native Windows code through MSVC), a new backend CORS origin (`http://velora.localhost`), and a second signed update feed (`latest.json`, not `latest.yml`).

- **Android native media session (2026-09-30).** Our own Capacitor plugin, no third-party package: `VeloraMediaPlugin.java` bridges to `MediaPlaybackService.java`, a `mediaPlayback` foreground service with a `MediaSessionCompat` + `MediaStyle` notification (lock screen, shade, headset/Bluetooth keys, Android 13+ scrubber). Buttons: favorite, previous, play/pause, next; radio hides skip/seek, and the heart for anything unfavoritable. Foreground plus a partial wake lock while playing, detached (swipeable) while paused, gone on swipe-from-recents or when the page dies. Artwork is fetched natively (http(s) only, capped at 8MB and 512px) with the WebView's cookies, redirects followed by hand so cookies only ever go to the artwork's own host. JS side: `services/platform/nativeMedia.ts` (null off Android) and `utils/useNativeMediaSession.ts`, fed by the engine's public position/rate/playhead seams with drift-deduped bridge calls; `audioEngine.handleMediaAction` is now the one transport both the browser MediaSession and the native one use (`tests/services/mediaActions.test.ts`). Gated on `mediaKeys`. `android/` is versioned since the same day. **Unverified on-device**; the status-bar glyph is a stock music note until a monochrome Velora mark exists. Same day: the app label is `Velora` (was the template's `velora-music`), the 3-button nav bar drops its contrast scrim (`MainActivity`), and both bars' icons follow the app theme through `SystemBars.setStyle` (`useNativeStatusBar.ts`).
- **Local-mode playlist covers, and stale media keys after a restart (2026-10-04).** Local playlists take a custom cover like Velora's (`playlistCoverUpload` on for `LocalProvider`): `local:setPlaylistCover` writes it under a fresh `playlist-<id>-<ts>` key in the covers dir (new URL each time, so no cached image survives), stored in a new `playlists.coverKey` column, preferred over the first song's art by `LOCAL_PLAYLIST_SUMMARIES_QUERY` and `toPlaylist`, kept by `pruneOrphanCovers`, removed with the playlist. Also: every `vmedia://` URL carries a per-launch key, so anything persisted from an earlier launch (the client controller's resume queue, `velora-session` stats, the jar, palette recents) 403'd, which left a restored queue unplayable after every restart; `reviveMediaUrl` (`services/platform/mediaUrl.ts`) swaps in the current key on read. The OS media controls now get local covers as a blob URL, since `MediaMetadata` refuses custom schemes.
- **Cover cache on disk (2026-10-05).** Desktop keeps cover thumbnails in `userData/cover-cache` (`electron/coverCache.ts`, one file per sha256 of the key, narrow `coverCache` preload bridge). `useBlobUrl` checks disk before the network and stores what it fetched; full-size covers stay memory-only. Least recently used goes first past the user's cap (Settings → Integrations → Cover Cache: an on/off toggle, on by default, where off clears it; a 100 MB to 5 GB slider, default 500 MB; a usage meter with Clear that previews what a lowered cap will trim); atime is last use, mtime is when stored, so there is no index file. Entries older than 30 days are refetched and kept as the offline fallback. Keys drop auth params per provider (`coverCacheKey`: Subsonic `t/s/p/v/c/f`, Jellyfin `api_key`), so no secret lands on disk. Logout keeps the cache by decision (maybe a setting later). Plain LRU, no protected tier: nav and player covers are touched every launch.

## 12. Bugs / Inconsistencies (resolved)
- **The 2026-09-28 review's UX gaps closed (2026-10-04).** U2: a server queue that wins the restore keeps this device's repeat and shuffle, the server stores neither. U3: the home section drag handle moves its section with ArrowUp/ArrowDown and keeps focus. U4: nav rows (playlists, pinned artists/albums) get "Move to top / bottom" in their menu, inside their pin group, since a drag can't reach past the frozen row window; edge auto-scroll was judged not worth it. U5 was already fixed in `9a5b20e4`. U6: the Spotlight starts paused under reduce-motion, the button still resumes it. `docs/goalsDetails/review-2026-09-28.md` deleted.
  - ↳ files: `clientPlaybackController.ts`, `homeView.tsx`, `ui/nav/nav.tsx`, `utils/navPlaylistOrder.ts`, `homeSpotlight.tsx`
- **Five stale tests on `main` (2026-09-30).** Test drift, not app bugs. `buildGrid.test.ts` still called `buildMobileGrid` with two args after the floating mini player added a third: the cases now pass it, a floating case was added, and the seam invariant knows a docked player and tab bar share no line while a floating player shares none at all. `smartPlaylistView.test.tsx` mocked `playlistFilter` wholesale, so the new `buildOptionsMenu` was missing; the mock is partial now.
- **Opening or closing BigMusic rebooted a framed plugin sidebar tab (2026-09-01).** `Sidebar` returned `createPortal(content, overlayEl)` while BigMusic was up and bare `content` otherwise, and React reconciles a portal fiber against a host-element fiber by tag, so the two never matched: the whole panel subtree unmounted on every cover press, `PluginFrame`'s cleanup ran, `host.destroy()` fired, and the plugin lost its boot, its handshake and all its state (in-realm 1.x tabs re-rendered from scratch for the same reason). The premise the four frame containers rest on, that the frame survives the portal, held for the `<iframe>` and never for the React wrapper that owns it. The panel is now **always** portalled into one host element created once and moved by hand between the grid slot and the overlay: the returned element type never changes, so nothing remounts, and moving a DOM node is not something React reconciles. Three things the shape depends on. The host is attached from the slot's **ref callback**, not from the layout effect, because refs land before the portalled subtree's own layout effects and a frame placed against a detached node would measure nothing. Host and slot are both `display: contents`, so `.sidebar_container` stays the grid item that `grid-area: sidebar` and `.sidebar_container > .uiContentContainer` are written against. And the re-attach test is `host.isConnected`, not `host.parentElement`: crossing the mobile breakpoint drops the whole desktop tree while leaving the host parented to a slot that is no longer in the document, which lost the sidebar outright until the next BigMusic toggle (the layout effect skips mobile for the same reason, or an empty host is left in the overlay). Checks: `tests/components/sidebarPortal.test.tsx`, node identity plus mount count across a BigMusic round trip, and the panel still connected across a mobile one. Both counted on a mount effect rather than a render, since a re-render is harmless here, and the breakpoint mock is an external store because `Sidebar` is `memo()`d and a bare rerender bails out.
  - ↳ files: `ui/sidebar/sidebar.tsx`, `tests/components/sidebarPortal.test.tsx`
- **"Play next" / "Add to queue" reported dead, not reproducible in the frontend (closed 2026-08-31).** Reported 2026-08-12: every entry point sent the command and the queue never moved. Both paths re-read and both are correct: `ClientPlaybackController` splices at `queueIndex + 1` and pushes at the end, keeping `unshuffledQueue` in step, and every sender (`trackMenu`, `playlistMenu`, `mediaMenu`, `smartPlaylistMenu`, the selection bar, the swipe action) posts a well-formed command. On `VeloraPlaybackController` the predictor returns `null` for both **by design**, so the queue only moves once the server pushes its snapshot back, which is exactly what a backend that stopped applying them looks like from the UI. Nothing in the frontend was ever changed and it works now, so the fault was server-side, most likely the same server-queue handling that `f848d49` (a deleted track staying gone from the server queue) landed in. If it returns on a Velora server while Navidrome/local stays fine, it is a backend bug, not this repo.
- **Deleting the playing track put it back seconds later (2026-08-31).** `useLibrary.deleteTrack` sends `removeTrack` after the DELETE, and `VeloraPlaybackController` applied it as a **local** queue edit on the premise that the server had nothing left to remove. It does: the server's queue holds resolved track objects, not ids, so the row outlives the deleted row in the DB, and nothing consumes the backend's `library.song.removed` event. Every command answers with the full server snapshot, so the next thing that bumped the server's revision (a play/pause, another device's broadcast, or a socket reconnect, which resets the client's revision guard) put the deleted track back in the queue and pointed the player at a file that no longer exists. The `progress` tick is the one snapshot that does *not* do it: the server returns it without bumping the revision, so `emitSnapshot` drops it. `removeTrack` is now rewritten into the `removeAt` the server already implements (ids resolved to positions against `lastState.queue`), so it goes through the normal predict-post-adopt path, the removal survives the next snapshot, and other devices get it on the broadcast. A track that is not in the queue still posts nothing.
- **The app asked api.iconify.design for icons at runtime (2026-08-10).** `resolveIconSrc` bundled the icons `scripts/fetch-icons.mjs` could grep for and fell back to the CDN for everything else: any name built at runtime, every plugin-declared icon, and **every colored icon** (the color was a query param, so the palette's red heart and its per-theme swatch went out on each render). That is a visitor's IP handed to a third party to draw a glyph, which an EU-hosted install cannot do, and it was invisible in dev because the missing icon still appeared. Now there is **no runtime fallback at all**: the resolver answers a bundled url or a blank `data:` SVG, plus a dev-console warning naming the id. Four things had to move with it. (1) A color is no longer a different file: `Icon` paints it through the same white glyph with `mask-image` (`.iconMask`), which is the mask pattern the toast and dialog icons already used, and the palette overlay does the same over the url it is sent. (2) Iconify stays a **build-time** dependency and `src/generated/icons/` stays gitignored (deliberate, weighed against committing the set 2026-08-10): the network call moves to the build machine instead of disappearing, and the guarantee is enforced rather than stored, `npm run build` passes `--strict` so a referenced icon that can't be fetched fails the build instead of shipping blank. 24 icons no name in `src/` mentions were pruned. (3) A plugin names its icon at runtime and so can never be pre-fetched: `hostPluginIcon` holds a declared name to what the app ships and falls back to the generic `extension` mark (a nav row or a player control is often nothing but its glyph, and a hole reads as broken), applied at the two seams every host renderer already goes through, `pluginRegistry`'s selectors (nav, BigMusic modes, commands and context-menu items alike) and the chrome descriptor parser. A plugin's own frame still gets `null` from `icon.read`, since substituting a puzzle piece inside a plugin's UI would be the host lying. Settings → Plugins falls back to the monogram. (4) `Button` stopped putting `.iconImg` on a non-icon `img`: that class is the glyph tint and it blows artwork out to white, which is why `nav.css` had a `[src*="iconify.design"]` exclusion, a selector that silently inverted the moment icons became same-origin. Cover art is keyed on the glyph class now, not on a url. Licenses text and the SDK's `Icon` doc restated: icons come from Iconify at build time, nothing at runtime. **The grep is the weak point, and review found its one live victim:** the login button spelled its glyph as `` `iconify:${cond ? "shield-person" : …}` ``, so the fetcher (which looks for `iconify:<name>`) never saw either arm and the primary button on the login screen would have drawn blank. The literals are whole now (`"iconify:shield-person"`), which is the shape any runtime-picked icon has to take. `hostPluginIcon`'s own `extension` mark is guarded the same way, by naming it where the fetcher can read it plus a check that it is bundled.
  - ↳ files: `utils/iconify.ts`, `primitives/icon/Icon.tsx`, `primitives/button/Button.tsx`, `src/index.css`, `ui/nav/nav.css`, `ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx`, `overlay/PaletteOverlay.tsx`, `utils/paletteOverlay.ts`, `services/plugins/pluginIcon.ts` + `pluginRegistry.ts` + `chrome/descriptors.ts` + `frame/bridgeMethods.ts`, `settingsView/.../PluginRow.tsx`, `scripts/fetch-icons.mjs`, `.gitignore`, `docs/designsystemV2.md` §9
- **A framed plugin sidebar tab showed nothing on mobile (2026-08-10).** The desktop half of this was fixed 2026-08-06 by giving `sidebarTabs` its own frame container at `--z-bigmusic + 2`; on mobile the sidebar is not a docked panel at all but a `Sheet` at `--z-modal` (9200), so the frame at 9002 sat behind the sheet's scrim and blurred panel exactly as it had sat behind the BigMusic overlay. Raising the `sidebar` layer was not available: it has to stay under `--z-modal` so a dialog or a toast opened over a plugin tab keeps winning. **The layer is now picked from the mount rather than from the surface**, which is what the surface alone could never say: `sidebarTabs` is two different mounts in two different z bands. `FrameHostOptions` takes an optional `layer`, `PluginFrame` takes it as a prop (and reboots the frame if it changes, since a container swap *is* the reparent that reloads the document), and `PluginTabView` reads `useIsMobile()` and asks for the new fourth container, `sheet` at `calc(var(--z-modal) + 1)`. Deliberately the only container above `--z-modal` and only one step above it: the confirm/prompt pills and the toast are at `--z-overlay`, so a plugin surface can never cover the answer to a question the host asked. Safe to decide once because the mobile/desktop swap returns a different element type from `Sidebar` and remounts the whole subtree anyway. **Second half, same bug:** a `Sheet` springs its panel up from `y: 100%`, and a transform moves a box without resizing it or scrolling anything, so none of `useFramePlacement`'s listeners fire and a frame placed on the first pass would keep the rect the placeholder had while it was still off the bottom of the screen. The hook now follows the box for a bounded 600ms after each (re)sync, re-placing only when the rect actually changed, which also covers the desktop sidebar's slide-in and the gap between the layout effect and the frame host being created (that used to wait for a `status` change to come back around). In-realm (1.x) tabs were never affected either time, they are ordinary React children. **Third half, and the one neither z nor timing would have reached:** the placeholder was zero pixels tall in the sheet, so `place()` read it as unplaced and parked the frame whatever band it was in. `.pluginFrame` is sized `height: 100%` and has no content of its own, and the docked panel is the only chain that gives that a definite height (`.sidebar_content` is a flex column, `.sidebarViewContainer` a `flex: 1` item); `.sheetContent` is a plain block, so the percentage resolved to `auto` and collapsed. The built-in tabs never showed it because their content sizes them. Fixed with one mobile-scoped height on the placeholder rather than by restructuring the sheet, which would have changed how queue/lyrics/info size there. Checks: three cases in `tests/services/plugins/frame/frameHost.test.ts` (surface default, mount override, and every container in its own band); the collapse is layout, so nothing in jsdom can hold it.
  - ↳ files: `services/plugins/frame/frameHost.ts`, `frame/PluginFrame.tsx`, `frame/useFramePlacement.ts`, `ui/sidebar/sidebar.tsx`, `ui/sidebar/sidebar.css`
- **Every modal animated in unfrosted, and the surface layer that caused it is reverted (2026-08-09).** The logout confirm faded in flat and snapped to frosted at the end; so did licenses, the theme editor, the smart-playlist and edit-track/playlist modals, the station modal and (for one day) the command palette. Cause: **an element's own `opacity`/`filter` is applied after its own `backdrop-filter`, but an ancestor's is not** (an ancestor is a *backdrop root*). Moving the fill and blur to `.uiContentContainer::before` the day before therefore turned every fading card into a backdrop root for its own blur, where before the fade and the frost had coexisted fine. Rather than rewrite each modal to spring on transform only and fade `::before` + its children (the shape `commandPalette.css` had already been patched into), the layer itself went back onto the element: `--surface-paint` / `--surface-filter` stay, so every theme, floater and accessibility override reads unchanged, and the 11-selector scroll-container opt-out group is gone with it. **The split was never load-bearing.** Measured the day it landed (RTX 3080, 240Hz): idle with the background running and ~14 blurred surfaces was **2%** with or without it, and the 20% case was one 40px cover animating at the *display's* refresh rate rather than the background's 30fps. Stepping the spins is what took that to 2%; the split only halved a number that stepping zeroed, and `spin` is no longer the default anyway. What re-breaks: nothing measured, and nothing in the fixes from that day, since they are all `--surface-filter: none` token overrides (nav pills, `overviewInner`, `trackDragGhost`) that read the same either way, including the nav pills' entrance flicker, which cannot recur with no filter to sample. Reworked instead: the palette's transform-only entrance is back to a plain fade, `.playlistJumpPill` takes its rest dim on the box and declares `background: var(--surface-paint)` so `.buttonSecondary`'s fill cannot win, the docked popped-settings tab transitions its accent on the panel, and glazedCeramic's search-field sheen is scoped to the `--flat` form so it cannot overwrite the surface paint.
  - ↳ files: `screens/pages/mainPage/mainPage.css`, `src/index.css`, `assets/css/themes.css`, `ui/commandPalette/` (css + tsx), `ui/playlist/playlist.css`, `ui/poppedSettings/poppedSettings.css`, `ui/nav/nav.css` (comment), `settingsView/settingsBox/settingsBox.css`, `docs/designsystemV2.md` §6.1
- **The context menu had square corners and a 12px inset in the built app, but not in dev (2026-08-09).** `.dropdownPanel` declares its own `border-radius` and `padding` at plain single-class specificity, and each ties exactly with `.uiContentContainer`s (`--float-radius`, 0 outside float mode, and `--padding-default`), so the winner was whichever rule the stylesheet emitted last: dev injects each component CSS file as its module executes, the build splits and concatenates chunks in another order, and there the surface won both. Not a new regression so much as a coin flip that had been landing the other way, and it took the panel corners *and* pushed every menu row 12px off the edge the hover fill is supposed to reach. Fixed the way the four floaters that already hit this are (`notFoundPage`, `languageSwitcher`, `selectionBar`, `onboarding`): `!important` on both properties, which is what `.dropdownPanel`s own `overflow` line already did, for the same reason, one line above the radius. Applied across the floating family in one pass rather than only the reported one, since they all sat on the same tie: the dropdown panel (and its submenu, same class), `.settingsSelectDropdown`, `.searchBarResults`, `.sheetPanel` and `.devToolsPanel`. The sheet three safe-area `padding-*` longhands needed it too, or its own `!important` shorthand would have outranked them and eaten the inset. Verified in the built CSS, not just in source. Not done, and the better shape if this recurs: drop `padding`/`border-radius` on the base rule to `:where(.uiContentContainer)` so a component class wins on specificity instead of on file order, which would also cover the ~35 view cards sitting on the same tie today and winning it by luck. Left out here because `mainPage.css` was being rewritten in another session at the time.
- **The rest of the performance-audit backlog dropped (2026-08-09, on request, don't re-propose it).** The 2026-08-08 GPU/CPU/memory audit shipped its GPU and MEM batches (29 of 45 findings, see the entries below and §4/§12 elsewhere); the remaining CPU batch and NET-1 were dropped as not worth chasing, and `docs/reportfindings/` was deleted with them. The full report with file:line evidence is in git history before this date if it's ever wanted back.
- **Playing animations repainted the surfaces around them (2026-08-07).** Four infinite playback-driven animations sat inside blurred `uiContentContainer` surfaces, so for as long as music played (most of a session) every frame re-rasterized a `backdrop-filter`. The three worth keeping got `will-change: transform` so the compositor gives them their own layer (track row spin, playlist grid card spin, `PlayingBars`), dropped back to `auto` when paused or under reduce-motion so an idle app isn't holding layers. The fourth was removed: the nav's now-playing mark ran bars inside the nav's blurred panel for the whole session and is now a static play/pause `Icon`. The word beside it still carries the state; folded rows have no room for the word, so there it rides the glyph's `alt`.
- **The palette overlay kept a ~100MB renderer alive with the setting off (2026-08-07).** `createOverlayWindow()` ran unconditionally in `whenReady`, and turning "Palette over other apps" off only stopped the renderer marking its global chord `overlay: true`, so the window stayed, hidden, forever; hiding a window frees nothing. It is now created and destroyed by `syncOverlayWindow()` off the shortcut registration itself: a registered chord carrying `overlay` is the only thing that can ever show it, so that is exactly when the process exists (pre-warmed, so the chord still opens it instantly). Teardown is on a 1s timer because `useGlobalShortcuts` sends `[]` then the new set on every change (effect cleanup, then effect), and that blank moment is not the user turning it off. `openPaletteOverlay` still creates lazily as the safety net.
- **Keybinds were dead while focus was inside a plugin screen (2026-08-06).** A plugin surface is a sandboxed cross-origin iframe, so a keydown in it is a keydown in another origin's document and the host's `window` listener never saw it: play/pause, volume, next, the palette, every chord the user bound silently did nothing from the moment they clicked into a plugin page or a plugin BigMusic mode. The forwarding lives in the **frame document's bootstrap** (`public/plugin-frame.html`), not in the SDK runtime the goals pointer guessed at: `plugin-sdk/runtime/` is bundled *into each plugin*, so a listener there would only reach plugins rebuilt against a newer SDK, while the bootstrap is host-owned and already in every frame ever mounted. It posts the fields a chord is made of (`key`, `code`, the four modifiers, `altGraph`) plus an `editable` flag as a versioned `key` guest message (`KeyMessage` in `frameProtocol.ts`), on a capture listener so plugin code cannot swallow the press first, skipping IME composition. `frameHost` forwards it onto a tiny bus (`frame/frameKeys.ts`) only when the frame is **placed**, is `document.activeElement` and the window itself still has focus; between them those three guards say "the user pressed this, in here, now", the focus half *is* the keybind-recorder guard (a chord being recorded in Settings has focus there), and `hasFocus` is what closes the alt-tab case, since `activeElement` goes on naming the iframe after the user has moved to another app. `useGlobalShortcuts` runs both sources through one `match()`, so a forwarded key is held to the same AltGr and don't-hijack-typing rules as a local one (`editable` is reported by the frame rather than acted on there, because that rule belongs in one place). Nothing is `preventDefault()`ed: the press already happened in a document the host cannot reach into. Residual, and deliberate: the frame realm runs plugin code, so a focused plugin can forge a press and reach the user's own keymap; the guards are about *where the user is* rather than about what was sent, which is the most a boundary with no key access can assert. Editing the bootstrap moves its CSP hash, so `public/plugin-frame.html`'s `<meta>` was regenerated (`npm run check:csp` prints the new one). Checks: five cases in `tests/services/plugins/frame/frameHost.test.ts` (placed + focused, unfocused, unplaced, unfocused window, malformed), six in `tests/utils/useGlobalShortcuts.test.ts`, and a third protocol-version mirror over the bootstrap in `protocolMirror.test.ts`.
- **The sidebar lost its plugin tabs and its resize handle the moment BigMusic opened (2026-08-06).** One cause behind both: the docked panel is portalled into the overlay while BigMusic is up, and two things it depends on stayed behind in the page. (1) **A framed plugin tab painted behind the overlay.** `frameHost` picked a container from the surface alone, so a `sidebarTabs` frame sat on `page` at `--z-card + 1` while its placeholder had moved above `--z-bigmusic`: the panel was there, the plugin's content was under 9000 units of overlay, and being un-hittable rather than merely hidden it took no click either. The frame cannot follow the portal (moving an `<iframe>` reloads its document), so the layer is decided once instead: a third container, `sidebar` at `--z-bigmusic + 2`, above a plugin BigMusic mode drawing underneath the panel and still under `--z-modal`, with dropdowns portalling above `--z-overlay` as before. In-realm (1.x) tabs were never affected, they are ordinary React children. (2) **The resize handle was disabled there on purpose** (`showResize = sidebarVisible && !bigMusicActive`), because it wrote the live width onto `.mainApp_container` via `closest()` and the overlay is a *sibling* of the grid, so a portalled handle would have found nothing to write to and the overlay panel read a committed `${sidebarWidth}px` anyway. `--nav-width`/`--sidebar-width` now live on the document root (the `--topbar-offset` pattern, set from `mainPage` in an effect and removed on unmount) instead of inline on the grid, `ResizeHandle` writes and reads them there, and the grid is still looked up (by id, since `closest` can't reach it) only to freeze its column transition mid-drag. The overlay panel's width and BigMusic's `--bm-sidebar-left/right` both consume `var(--sidebar-width)`, so a drag moves the panel and re-insets the mode in the same frame without a re-render. Don't put those two vars back on the grid element: an inline value on the element beats the inherited one and the drag would stop reaching the columns.
- **Deleting the open playlist left the user on its dead route (2026-08-06).** `PlaylistView` has no not-found path, so after confirming a delete the view sat on a failed detail fetch (`ErrorState` + Retry for a playlist that no longer exists). `buildPlaylistMenuEntries`' delete handler now checks whether the current path is that playlist's and sends the user to `/home` through the `navigateTo` seam (which also dismisses BigMusic, so the navigation isn't hidden behind the overlay). Only on success, a failed delete reverts and toasts as before. The menu builder is the single delete call site, so the check lives there rather than in the view.
- **The two leftover mobile-weight items dropped (2026-08-04, on request, not measured against, so don't re-propose them).** What the 2026-08-04 mobile audit found and did not fix, recorded here so the evidence isn't lost. (1) **An animated WebGL background under ~44 `backdrop-filter` surfaces**: defaults are `backgroundEnabled: true` at 30fps/half-res with blur `full` (20px), and a moving background behind a backdrop-filter forces a full-screen re-blur every frame, which pegs a phone GPU and starves the main thread. Would have wanted a measurement first and then likely a mobile default (background off, or blur down) rather than a code change; the knobs are `src/settings.tsx` (`backgroundEnabled`/`backgroundResolution`/`resolveBlur`) and `src/assets/backgrounds/backgroundQuality.ts`. (2) **Eager bundle + unpaged list payloads**: one 1.16 MB `index` chunk + a 660 KB vendor chunk + 244 KB CSS, all parsed before first paint (only the WebGL backgrounds and two modals split out today), and `getAlbums`/`getArtists`/`getFavorites` take no cursor while `getTracks(cursor, limit)` does, so the grids are virtualized but the JSON is the whole library. Would have been route-level `lazy()` + `manualChunks` in `vite.config.ts` and matching cursors in `ImusicProvider.ts` + both providers + `src/store/library.ts`.
- **The web app was unusable on a phone: songs buffered forever and lists crawled (2026-08-04).** Same bundle as desktop, a different workload. Two causes, both fixed; the remaining two are open under §12 in `goals.md`. (1) **Streams were lossless by default.** `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.audioQuality` was `"lossless"` and `buildStreamUrl` returns the base URL untouched for it, so every play downloaded the *original* file, 25-40 MB for a FLAC, while the backend's opus transcoding (`/songs/:id/stream?format=opus&quality=…`) sat unused unless someone changed the setting. New `"auto"` quality, now the default and first in the picker (`settings.quality.auto` + a reworked `qualityDesc` in all 9 locales): `resolveAutoQuality()` reads `navigator.connection` (saveData or 2g → low, 3g → medium) and otherwise splits on `pointer: coarse`, phone/tablet → opus 320, desktop → the original. Resolved per track load, not at boot, so changing network takes effect on the next song. A desktop-side variant that also downgraded when the *server* was remote was built and then dropped on request; desktop always gets the original under auto. Because the old default is already persisted on every existing install, a one-time migration (`velora-audio-settings-version`, its own key so the version never leaks into `getSettings()` or the export file) moves a stored `"lossless"` to `"auto"` once. A lossless pick made after that is a real choice and is left alone. (2) **Every cover was downloaded full-size and re-encoded on the main thread.** The backend served cover files as-is (embedded art is routinely 1400-3000px, hundreds of KB to MB) and `useBlobUrl` fetched each one in JS then ran `downscaleBlob`, a full-resolution decode plus a WebP re-encode, per cover, six at a time, for a 48px row; the 12 MB thumb cache meant scrolling a long list redid it. Backend (`velora-backend`, **needs a deploy**): `/covers/:filename`, `/artistImg/:filename` and `/albumCovers/:filename` take `?size=128|256|512`, served from a new `core/images/thumbnails.ts` (ffmpeg → libwebp, `cache/thumbnails/<dir>/<size>/`, never upscaled, per-destination in-flight map so a cold cache doesn't spawn one ffmpeg per row, tmp+rename so no reader sees a half-written file, source-mtime comparison so a replaced cover can't serve the stale thumb). Anything it can't produce returns null and the route serves the original, so an ffmpeg without libwebp degrades to today's behavior rather than to a broken image; an unrecognised size does the same, which is what keeps a newer client safe against an older server. Frontend: new optional `IMusicProvider.thumbnailUrl(url, size)` (Velora rounds up to its three sizes, Subsonic passes `size` straight through since `getCoverArt` takes any), surfaced as `providerBundle.getThumbnailUrl`; `useBlobUrl` fetches that URL and skips `downscaleBlob` entirely when it comes back changed. Measured on a real 469 KB PNG cover: 2.8 KB at 256px, ~168x less over the wire and no decode/encode at all. Checks: `tests/services/coverThumbnails.test.ts` (auto-quality table, size rounding), two cases in `tests/utils/useBlobUrl.test.ts` (server-sized vs local-downscale paths), `src/__tests__/coverThumbnails.test.ts` backend-side (traversal refusal, missing source, size allowlist, real encode + shared in-flight + mtime refresh). The backend test targets `getThumbnail` directly rather than the route: the route tests in `localImages.test.ts` already 401 in this environment, unrelated to this change.
- **Spamming play/pause/shuffle/repeat made the controls flip-flop on Velora (2026-07-29).** Velora-only, the client controller (Navidrome/local) has no round trip and was never affected. Every command response is a snapshot of the server *as of that command*, and `emitSnapshot` adopted each one in arrival order: click pause then play quickly and the first response, landing after the second click, reasserted "paused" until the second response undid it again. The `pendingTrackId` guard only covered commands that change track, so play/pause/shuffle/repeat had nothing holding the line. `VeloraPlaybackController` now stamps each user command with a `commandSeq`; a response whose seq is no longer the newest returns the optimistic state instead of emitting, so the last click wins and the client stays the truth while anything is in flight. WS broadcasts are held, not adopted, for the same window (`commandsInFlight`), since a broadcast racing our own command describes a state the user has already moved past; the last command out replays the newest held one through `emitSnapshot`, so the revision guard drops it when the responses already moved past it and nothing is lost if the command that would have carried it throws (held state is cleared on reconnect, where the revision counter resets). `progress` is exempt from both counters: it's telemetry, not intent, and its reply is already inert (the backend doesn't bump `revision` for it, so the revision guard drops it). State still converges on the server, only the *newest* command's snapshot is adopted, and it carries everything, including changes made from another device.
- **Clicking shuffle or repeat rewound the audio a few seconds and made it stall (2026-07-29).** Neither command touches the position, but both controllers reported one that was up to 5 seconds old, and the engine "corrected" the gap by seeking (`SEEK_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` is 3), which restarts the stream buffer, hence the momentary silence. The engine only reports its real position on the 5s `progress` tick, so a cached `currentTime` is stale for most of that window, which is why it only bit when the click landed more than 3s after a tick. Velora path: `predictCommand` already extrapolated for play/pause/toggle/seek (`estimatedPosition`) but the `setShuffle`/`setRepeat` branches spread `...s` unchanged, so the optimistic state carried the stale value; they now carry the extrapolated position, and the server snapshot that follows ~100ms later agrees with it (the backend settles its own position at the top of every command, so it was never the one lying). Client path (Navidrome/local): `commit()` restarts the position clock (`updatedAtMs = Date.now()`) while `positionSeconds` still held the last tick's value, throwing away the elapsed time for *any* command that doesn't set a position; `settlePosition()` now restarts the clock too, which makes it idempotent, and `sendCommand` calls it once up front instead of per-case in play/pause. There the rewind was permanent, not corrected by a snapshot.
- **The hero detail headers never reached their bar on a phone (2026-07-29).** With `collapseDetailHeader` on, the immersive/banner/split headers shrank part-way and then bounced back open on mobile. The body reserved the whole filter-search gutter (`--detail-search-w`, `clamp(120px, 40%, 180px)`) as `--collapse` ran to 1, on top of a 78px cover tile: on a 360px phone that left the desc column too narrow for the touch-sized controls, they wrapped onto a second row, and the taller content overrode the bar's `min-height`. Two changes in `detailHeader.css`, mobile only: the body now reserves just the closed 44px glyph in both states and `--detail-search-w` is the wider open width, so the field opens *over* the type on a solid fill (what the split variant already did, its duplicate rules folded into the shared `.detailHeaderHero` ones); and the cover gives up much more on the way down (96 to 56px, 80 to 56px below 479px) and rides centered in the bar, which hands the controls exactly the width they need to stay on one row. Desktop geometry untouched.
- **A playlist's first song never reached the nav cover, and an uploaded cover could disappear on reload (2026-07-26).** Two separate faults in the same flow. (1) The nav read `p.coverUrl ?? COVER_PLACEHOLDER` off the summary, and providers only derive "first song's art" server-side on the *next* list fetch, so adding the first song to a new playlist left the nav on the placeholder until a reload (cards and the detail header already derived it client-side). The derivation is now one shared rule, `derivePlaylistCover(playlist, detail)` in `src/utils/playlistCover.ts`, used by both `PlaylistCard` and `nav.tsx` off the `details` already in the store. This does **not** reinstate the 2026-07-19 removal above: nothing fetches a detail to warm a cover, the nav just reads one when it happens to be loaded, which is exactly the case a fresh add creates. It also self-corrects when the covering song is removed, unlike writing a derived cover into the summary would. (2) A picked cover was sent as a raw `FileReader` data URL, so a normal phone photo became a multi-MB base64 PATCH body: slow enough to still be in flight when the page was reloaded (optimistic cover shown, nothing stored) and big enough for a proxy to reject. `fileToCoverDataUrl` (`src/utils/imageScale.ts`) now downscales to 1024px WebP first, tens of KB, and both call sites (`playlistView`, `EditPlaylistModal`) use it instead of their own duplicated reader. `useBlobUrl`'s private `downscaleBlob` moved into that util so there is one implementation. `updatePlaylistCover` also stopped falling back to the local data URL when the server answered without a cover (`updated.coverUrl ?? coverDataUrl`), which made a non-persisting write look like a success until the next reload; it now reverts and toasts. Backend (`velora-backend`, needs a deploy): playlist covers are written to `playlist-<id>-<rand>.<ext>` instead of a fixed `playlist-<id>.<ext>`, with the previous file unlinked, because `/api/v1/covers/*` is served `max-age=604800` and a replacement cover on the same filename would have kept showing the cached old image; the size-limit message said 4 MB while the check was 15 MB. New `src/__tests__/playlistCover.test.ts` covers upload, persistence and replacement (it deliberately skips the list endpoint: the cover-fallback COALESCE with a correlated subquery is valid Postgres but the in-memory test db can't plan it).
- **Waveform/playhead trailed the music by ~1s (2026-07-24).** In `live` mode the timeline set fill/thumb/waveform to the just-arrived whole-second tick (`Math.floor`ed) and glided *toward* it over a 1s CSS/JS transition, so the playhead only reached a position as the audio was already a second past it (worse right after a fractional-second seek). Fixed by driving the live seek timeline imperatively from the ground-truth audio position: `Timeline` gained `getPosition?: () => number | null` + `isPlaying?`; when `live` and a getter is present (and not dragging), a ref-based rAF paints fill width / thumb left / waveform boundary every frame from `audioEngine.getPositionSeconds()` (a `useLayoutEffect` re-anchors on each render for the paused/seek/track-change case), matching the codebase's "canvas draws via refs, no re-render" pattern. New `.syncing` class drops the width/left glide so the per-frame writes aren't smeared. A `seekHintRef` holds the target after a seek until the audio element converges (or 2s), so server-mode (Velora) seeks don't bounce the thumb back on release. Wired at the two live call sites: `PlayerTimeline` (player.tsx) and `BigMusicSeekbar` (bigMusicTransport.tsx, used by every BigMusic mode). Volume timelines and the non-`live` video-mode timeline are untouched. Files: `timeline.tsx`, `timeline.css`, `player.tsx`, `bigMusicTransport.tsx`.
- **Button icon double-announced to screen readers; EditTrackModal showed stale fields on re-open (2026-07-24).** Two fixes from the new test suite's `docs/fails.md`. (1) `Button` set the icon `alt` to the string label, so an icon+text button announced its name twice ("PlayPlay"); the icon is now always decorative (`alt=""`), the visible text or `aria-label` naming the button. (2) `EditTrackModal` reloaded its field state only on a false->true `open` transition, so a second `promptEditTrack` while the modal was already open swapped the store track (cover followed) but left title/artist/album/lyrics on the previous track; it now reloads whenever the active track id changes. Both pinned tests flipped to the correct assertion. `docs/fails.md` deleted with the fix: the remaining entries were all low/quirk/nit/doc (e.g. reversed `bpm:` range, sub-1MB storage rounding, `localProvider upload:true` vs a stale doc line) and were dropped as not worth tracking; the two that mattered are these.
- **Local scan moved off the Electron main thread (2026-07-19).** A big first scan used to freeze tray/window-controls/`vmedia://`/IPC because the whole pipeline (recursive `readdirSync`, per-file `statSync` + `music-metadata` parse + sync cover `writeFileSync` + sync `node:sqlite` inserts) ran in the main process. Split the scan/index engine out of `localLibrary.ts` into an Electron-free `electron/localScanEngine.ts` (parameterized by an explicit `ScanCtx = { db, musicDir, coversDir, coverKeys }` instead of the module singletons, since a `worker_thread` has no Electron `app`): `runScan`, `indexFile`, `applyTrackOverride`, cover extraction/prune, `inferArtistFromFilename`, `extractLyrics`, and the `AUDIO_EXTENSIONS`/`METADATA_VERSION` constants moved there. New `electron/localScanWorker.ts` opens its own `DatabaseSync` on the same WAL db, loads `coverKeys` from disk, runs the engine, and streams `{type:'progress'|'done'|'error'}` messages. `scan()` in `localLibrary.ts` is now a thin driver: it keeps the `scanning` flag + `scanCompletion` bookkeeping, bootstraps the folder/schema via `getDb()`, spawns the worker (`new URL('./localScanWorker.js', import.meta.url)`, paths passed via `workerData` since the worker can't read prefs/`app`), relays progress to the renderer unchanged, then `reloadCoverKeys()` from the covers dir (the worker wrote them on its own connection, so main's in-memory set is stale). Two-writer safety: `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` on both connections so a `recordPlay`/`addFavorite`/`updateTrack` on main during a scan retries instead of throwing `SQLITE_BUSY` (WAL allows one writer + concurrent readers). Worker crash/error resolves the scan promise with a zero-result fallback + a final `done:true` so the UI never hangs (guarded by a `settled` flag against `done`+`exit` double-fire). Main still uses the engine directly for the fast single-file paths (`importFile`, `updateTrack`). Build: `scripts/build-electron.mjs` bundles the worker as a second esbuild entry; `electron/tsconfig.json` includes it for type-checking; `dist-electron/**` already ships it. Not runtime-verified on-device (no Electron here); folds into the §11 packaged-build verification pass.
- **Nav playlist list virtualized (2026-07-19)** (open since the reverted 2026-07-02 attempt, which left no git trace, so this was designed from the stated failure modes). New `useNavRowWindow.ts` hook co-located in `nav/`: fixed-stride windowing over the existing `.navPlaylistContainer` scroll element (which is the `Reorder.Group` itself), passive scroll listener + ResizeObserver, row height and viewport measured live (48px fallback) so density/text-scale/fold/drag-resize self-correct; the always-rendered favorites row doubles as the height sample. 10-row overscan each side against fast-scroll blanking. Gated to the left/right vertical layouts and off during skeleton/error, so the top/bottom horizontal strip and loading states render exactly as before; folded nav stays virtualized. The likely "didn't feel right" killer is handled head-on: rows unmounting mid-drag would kill the motion `Reorder` gesture, so `NavReorderRow` reports drag state and the hook freezes the window while a drag is in flight, resyncing on release; `.navRowSpacer` divs (`flex-shrink: 0`) keep scroll geometry byte-identical so scroll feel/momentum are native. Context menus, drop targets, playing mark, and `handleReorder` work unchanged on mounted rows. Same pass: playlist labels ellipsize to one row (`.truncate` + the `min-width: 0` chain in nav.css), which also protects the uniform-row-height assumption. Dev seed tool for eyeballing it: DevToolsPanel (Settings → Developer) "Nav playlists" row, Seed 100 injects `dev-playlist-1..100` with varied-length names client-side into `useLibrary` via direct `setState` (deliberately bypasses optimistic mutations, fake local data, zero backend calls, idempotent), Clear filters them out by id prefix; placed there instead of `/dev` because that route mounts no nav. Known tradeoffs (same as `VirtualizedGrid`): keyboard focus is lost if the focused row scrolls out of the window, and the pin animation only plays when both old and new positions are in-window.
- Nav playlist-detail cover warming dropped (2026-07-19). The backend now serves a derived cover in the playlist list endpoints: `COALESCE(playlists.cover_url, first track by position with cover art)` in `PlaylistRepository.listWithCounts` (shared by the user/folder list queries), plus a first-track cover for the virtual All Songs playlist (`TrackRepository.firstCoverArt`, id asc to match its track order). Frontend: nav's proactive `loadPlaylist` warming effect and the `details`-based icon fallback deleted (`nav.tsx`), so cover-less playlists no longer trigger a full detail fetch each (pinned All Songs used to fetch the entire library). `SubsonicProvider.mapPlaylist` now maps the playlist `coverArt` the API already returns; `LocalProvider` already served one.
- Format badges never rendered in playlists, and the stacked one overflowed the row (2026-07-19). `Track` has two render paths and the badge was gated on `!props.columns`, so table mode, which every playlist uses, showed none at all; its Format column separately returned a bare `trackFormat.toUpperCase()` string with no badge chrome. The badge now renders under the artist in **both** modes, skipped only when the user enabled the dedicated Format column (avoids showing it twice) or on 48px compact rows (no room for a third line). Two new `FormatBadge` props: `always` (used by the Format column, `display.formatBadges` defaults to **false** and `badgeFormats` is a whitelist, so without the bypass an opt-in column would render blank for most users; `showBitrate` still shapes the label and `-` stays the no-format fallback) and `stacked` (0.6rem/line-height 1, so the third line fits the fixed 62px row). Deliberately named `stacked`, not `compact`: it renders on default/large rows and is dropped on `rowSize: "compact"`, so the row-size word would have read backwards. Known limit: `ROW_HEIGHTS` is fixed px while text is rem, so at textScale large/xlarge the three-line stack clips against `.track`'s `overflow: hidden`; only reachable with the badge setting on, and the mismatch predates this change.
- Dragging a track the queue already holds re-added it, so a row dragged out of the Queue panel and back onto it silently duplicated (2026-07-19). `useTrackDropTarget` gained an optional `canDrop(track)` predicate, checked in dragenter/dragover/dragleave off the module-level `draggedTrack` (dragover can only read `types`, never the payload) and re-checked on drop. Refusing = not calling `preventDefault` in dragover, which is exactly what makes the browser show "can't drop here". QueueView passes `(track) => !queue?.some(q => q.id === track.id)`, which covers self-drop and any duplicate from elsewhere in one rule. A drag from another window has no module state, so it stays allowed at hover and is caught by the drop-time check. Other targets (nav playlists, Favorites) pass no predicate and are unchanged.
- External-import API uploads only flashed in the nav (2026-07-17). The nav upload pill (`NavUploadIndicator`) shows while an item is `queued`/`uploading`, but an external import into local mode finishes in well under a second, so the pill appeared and vanished before it could be seen (the import itself worked). Not caused by the Desktop API v2 change, that only touched `importApi.ts`/`preload.cts`/`useExternalImport.ts` and left the `beginExternal`→pill path untouched. Fix: the pill now holds on-screen for `LINGER_MS` (1600ms) after the last item finishes, but only on a real active→idle transition (armed via the adjust-on-render pattern, not a synchronous effect setState, so mount/navigation don't flash it), showing a "done" state (`nav.upload.done` in all 6 locales, pause control hidden). Regular multi-file uploads are unaffected (they stay active throughout).
- New uploads/imports didn't appear in `/tracks` or home Recently Added until a manual reload (2026-07-17). Both hold their tracks in component-local state (Playlist's paged `loadedSongs`, RecentlyAdded's fetch), so `refreshLocalLibrary()` (albums/artists/playlists/favorites only) never reached them. Added a session `newTracks` buffer to `useLibrary` (`noteTrackAdded`, deduped newest-first; cleared on logout, and a deleted id is dropped from it). The exported `noteUploadedTrack(result)` helper fetches a genuinely-new track (`inserted`/`imported` + trackId) via `musicService.getTrack` and pushes it, called from `uploadQueue`'s success `.then` and `useExternalImport`. Consumers prepend it deduped without remounting: `Playlist` gained a `prependTracks` prop (fetchMore lists only, skipped under forced-empty dev state), TracksView passes `newTracks`, RecentlyAdded merges + caps at its limit. Existing keyed rows stay mounted; only the new row/card is added.
- Deleting the currently-playing track kept playing it and left it in the queue (2026-07-17). Added a `removeTrack` playback command (`playbackTypes.ts`); `useLibrary.deleteTrack` fires it after a successful backend delete. `ClientPlaybackController` (local/Navidrome) edits its own queue (`removeFromQueue`): removing the current track advances to what was next (or stops, wrapping on repeat-all, if it was last), removing others just shifts `queueIndex`. The Velora backend has no such command, so `VeloraPlaybackController` applies the same edit locally on its cached snapshot (`applyRemoveTrack` + `emit`, no round trip, the track is already gone server-side) so the engine switches off the deleted track; the next real command's snapshot reconciles.
- Velora playback not instant on a cold transcode cache (2026-07-15). Backend fix in `stream.ts`: a fresh `<audio>` load sends `Range: bytes=0-`, which used to hit the blocking `transcodeToFile` branch (awaited the whole encode before any bytes). Added `rangeStartsAtZero()` and gated the blocking branch on `range && !rangeStartsAtZero(range)`, so `bytes=0-` falls through to the existing tee branch (streams ffmpeg stdout to the client while writing the cache in parallel), instant like Navidrome. Only a real seek into uncached content (start > 0, or suffix `bytes=-N`) still transcodes-to-disk first. Non-blocker to verify on-device: iOS Safari can be finicky about a `200` + `Accept-Ranges: none` reply to `bytes=0-`.
