- Queue lost on app start in client mode (local/Navidrome) (2026-07-14). `ClientPlaybackController` now persists the full queue (+ index, shuffle, repeat) in its localStorage resume write, not just the single resume track, and seeds it back in the constructor so auto-advance works after reload; the throttle key includes queue/index/shuffle/repeat so structural changes write immediately, and a quota-overflow write falls back to the single-track resume (prior behavior) and skips the oversized queue until it changes. Velora mode unaffected (queue comes from the backend).
- Scroll-over-volume did nothing in BigMusic (2026-07-14). Added `onVolumeWheel` to `BigMusicContext` (mirrors `player.tsx`'s handler: gated on `wheelVolume`, reads live gain, steps in slider space) and wired `onWheel` on the three volume wrappers (`bigMusicVolume`/`bmCardVolume`/`bmVideoVolume`).
- Multi-selected track rows filled with a solid accent background instead of a border (2026-07-15). `.trackSelected` (`src/assets/components/primitives/track/track.css`) set `background-color: var(--color-accent)`. Switched to a 1px `var(--color-accent-solid)` border (`.track` now has a `border: 1px solid transparent` base + `border-color` in the transition, `box-sizing: border-box` already in place so no layout shift); background stays the normal row surface. `.trackActive` (currently-playing row) deliberately kept its background fill, Jenny confirmed only the multi-select highlight should change.
- Switching a song in the tracks view was slow on Subsonic/Navidrome (client mode) (2026-07-14). Clicking a track starts a `source: "allSongs"` queue, and Subsonic has no all-songs endpoint, so `ClientPlaybackController.resolveSource` crawled the entire library page by page (`search3`, 500/page, sequential `await`) before the first note could play, a big library meant dozens of blocking round-trips. Velora was unaffected (server resolves `allSongs` in one command). Fixed by seeding the clicked track as a one-track queue and starting playback immediately (`seedAndBackfill`), then crawling the full library in the background (`backfillAllSongs`) and splicing it in around the still-playing track, same `currentTrack.id` at the reindexed position, so the audio engine's `active.trackId !== track.id` guard never reloads; `settlePosition()` before the re-commit preserves elapsed time so the drift-seek guard doesn't snap back to 0:00. Bails if the user moved on (queue no longer the lone seed), keeps the seed playing if the library drifted and no longer lists it, and honors shuffle. All four `allSongs` callers pass `startTrack`, so every real path hits the fast route. File: `src/services/playback/controllers/clientPlaybackController.ts`.
- Remaining 2026-07-13 perf audit interval findings closed (2026-07-14; what's left of idle GPU is the animated WebGL bg + backdrop blur, tracked under the "Later" perf follow-up): topbar clock ticks minute-aligned via a self-rescheduling timeout (recovers alignment after system sleep/timer throttling) and not at all when clock+greeting are both hidden; `PWAUpdater` sw.js poll backed off 15s → 5 min; `Lyrics.tsx` active-line tracking replaced the 60fps rAF poll with a timeout that sleeps until the next line's timestamp (clamped 50ms–1s so seeks/pauses are still caught within a second); timeline waveform skips the canvas redraw unless the played-bar count (`Math.round(activeProgress * bars)`, exactly the bars drawn as played) crossed a bar or peaks/canvas size changed (`lastDrawnRef`); a color re-sample forces the next draw via `played = -1`.
- Loopback cover export used the wrong credential mode (2026-07-14). `useDesktopIntegration.ts`'s desktop loopback cover fetch hardcoded `credentials: "include"`, unlike the app's normal cover path (`useBlobUrl.ts`) which asks `providerBundle.getCoverArtCredentials()` (`include` only for Velora, `omit` for Navidrome/local). Forced credentials could make CORS reject Navidrome/`vmedia://` cover requests, leaving loopback consumers without cover bytes + palette colors. Fixed by reusing `providerBundle.getCoverArtCredentials()`.
- Iconify-over-network tech debt cleared (2026-07-13). Every UI glyph used to `<img src>` / mask off `api.iconify.design` at runtime (a third-party CDN dependency + per-icon round-trips, broken offline). Now: `scripts/fetch-icons.mjs` greps `iconify:`/`material-symbols:` literals out of `src/`, downloads each SVG (white-baked, `?color=white`) into the gitignored `src/generated/icons/`, and runs on `predev`/`build`. New `Icon` primitive (`src/assets/components/primitives/icon/Icon.tsx`) + `resolveIconSrc()`/`normalizeIconId()` (`src/utils/iconify.ts`) resolve **local-first** via `import.meta.glob` (Vite inlines the ~109 tiny SVGs as same-origin data URIs); `Button.imgProps` routes through `Icon`. Only plugin-supplied names or a non-white/dynamic `color` hit the CDN fallback. CSS masks/backgrounds (nav.css, settingsView.css) can't call the resolver, so their 8 icons are mirrored as `:root --vicon-*` vars from `src/utils/cssIcons.ts` (imported in `main.tsx`). Migrated all central renderers off hardcoded CDN URLs: Button, dropdown, commandPalette, toast, confirmDialog, searchInput, windowControls, languageSwitcher, uploadOverlay, topbar, NavPill, login/activation pages. Convention going forward: static icon literals carry the `iconify:` prefix so the fetch script can discover them. (Known: the palette's `=== "one"` comparison yields a harmless `material-symbols:one` fetch warning, skipped in `fetch-icons.mjs`. The toggle-topbar icon's nonexistent `dock-to-top` name was fixed 2026-07-15 → `top-panel-open`.)
- Switching providers without a page reload muted playback entirely (found + resolved 2026-07-11, surfaced by local-mode testing): `audioEngine.attach()`'s `initGraph` early-returns once `ctx` exists, so the two `<audio>` slots kept the `crossOrigin` from the *first* attach of the page's lifetime, logout→login to a different provider (local/Navidrome ↔ Velora) then streamed with the wrong CORS mode: stale `anonymous` dropped the cookies Velora streams need (401 → no audio, timer stuck 0:00), stale `use-credentials` CORS-blocked anonymous media into Web Audio silence. Fixed in `attach()` by re-applying the requested `crossOrigin` to both slot elements on every attach (elements must be reused, `createMediaElementSource` is once-per-element, and the property takes effect on next load). File: `src/services/audio/audioEngine.ts`.
- Nav playlist cover fell back to the generic "folder" icon for cover-less playlists until the playlist was opened once (2026-07-09). `resolveIcon` in `nav.tsx` derives a cover from `details[p.id]?.songs`, but `details` is only warm after visiting `PlaylistView`. Fixed with a small effect in `nav.tsx` that proactively `loadPlaylist(p.id)`s any user/pinned-velora playlist lacking a `coverUrl` and not yet cached, reuses the existing `loadPlaylist` seam (dedupes against cached details, swallows errors), so nav covers resolve up front.
- Folder playlist search not working, two root causes fixed (2026-06-27): (1) command palette's `playlistResults` only searched user playlists (`useLibrary.playlists`), not velora/folder playlists, fixed by loading `veloraPlaylists` in the palette and merging both lists in the search; (2) the virtualized `Playlist` component didn't reset scroll position when the `songs` prop changed, so after scrolling down in a long playlist and typing a search query, the filtered results at indices 0–N were off-screen above the scroll position and invisible, fixed by a `useEffect` in `Playlist` that resets `scrollTop` to 0 whenever `staticSongs` changes. Files: `src/assets/components/ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx`, `src/assets/components/ui/playlist/playlist.tsx`.
- Home `Overview`'s swallowed Navidrome `UNSUPPORTED` error (permanent dash/skeleton placeholders), fixed via capability gating, see §14.
- Volume up/down arrow keys stepped raw gain linearly instead of the slider's perceptual curve, so each press moved a different visible amount on the volume bar depending on current level. Fixed (2026-06-20) by stepping in slider space via the shared `volumeToSlider`/`sliderToVolume` (`src/utils/volumeCurve.ts`) in `useKeybindDispatch.ts`, matching how dragging the bar already worked. Also deduped `bigMusic.tsx`'s identical local copy of the curve to import the shared util instead.
- BigMusic Lyrics/Editorial modes had insufficient top safe-area padding on mobile (notch overlap), `bigCover`/`vinyl`/`continuum`/`polaroidWall` already did `max(<clamp>, var(--safe-top))` on their top padding; `lyrics.css`'s `.bmLyricsTopBar` and `editorial.css`'s main padding didn't. Brought both in line (2026-06-21).
- Player could grow/overflow with a long title: desktop `.playerControls_content` used `grid-template-columns: .5fr 1fr .5fr` with no `minmax(0, ...)`, so a long title's column expanded past its share and pushed the favorite button behind the timeline. Fixed via `minmax(0, ...)` tracks + `.playerTrackDesc` dropping its `width: fit-content` for default flex sizing + `min-width: 0` (lets it shrink/ellipsis instead of forcing growth) + `flex-shrink: 0` on the cover image and favorite button; also hardened `.playerControls_container` (the outer grid item, shared by the mobile single-column shell) with `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden` against the same class of overflow. (2026-06-21)
- Enabling shuffle lagged the audio ~1s and made the queue visibly re-shuffle twice. Two causes (fixed 2026-06-25, `veloraPlaybackController.ts`): (1) `sendCommand`'s snapshot adoption (unlike `setQueue`) didn't preserve the live audio position, so the `setShuffle` snapshot's stale server position seeked the audio backward, the "lag"; (2) the optimistic prediction reordered the queue with its own random order, then the server's snapshot brought a *different* random order (`shuffleWithStart`, backend), so "Up next" visibly shuffled twice. Fix: extracted `preserveLivePosition()` (carry the tracked position forward on a same-track snapshot) and reused it in both `setQueue` and `sendCommand`; stopped optimistically reordering on shuffle-enable (just flip the flag + save `unshuffledQueue` for deterministic disable, leave order to the snapshot, removed the now-dead `shuffleFrom`). Added a transient `queueResolving` flag (`PlaybackState`) set on the optimistic enable and cleared by the snapshot; `QueueView` shows `skeletonPulse` loaders for "Up next" while it's set instead of the stale order. Review follow-ups (2026-06-25): `setQueue` now drops `unshuffledQueue` when a new queue starts (else disabling shuffle could restore a stale queue from the previous source, with a mismatched index); `QueueView` sizes the resolving loaders to the reshuffle window (`min(queue.length-1, 15)`) instead of a flat 6 so a tiny/empty queue doesn't flash a full block; and `Sidebar` keeps the active view mounted through its slide-out (`mounted` state cleared on `transitionend`) so the panel no longer animates away empty, while still unmounting when fully hidden to avoid background lyrics/cover fetches.
- Velora playback would occasionally "loop" backward mid-track on laggy clients, and got worse with two devices open on one account (each fighting over the shared position). Root cause was backend, not audio: `applyPlaybackCommand`'s `"progress"` case (`../velora-backend/src/core/playback/playbackController.ts`) blindly overwrote the shared `positionSeconds` with whatever any client reported. Under main-thread lag (delays when a pending fetch's `.then()` runs) or two devices each reporting their own position, requests can be *processed* out of send order; since `revision` increments in processing order, a stale/earlier position could land with a *higher* revision and slip past the frontend's revision guard, snapping the live audio backward. Fixed (2026-06-25) with a small monotonic guard: a `"progress"` report that would move the position backward by more than 2s while playing is ignored as stale; real rewinds (`"seek"`) are untouched. Devices intentionally stay on one shared, loosely-synced session (by design, the user wants the same song audible on multiple devices/rooms at once), so the fix is this guard alone, not per-device session isolation. Regression test added to `playbackControl.test.ts`.
- 2026-07-02 audit (was `fableReview.md`, now removed; all findings resolved): Navidrome `addNext`/`addToQueue` update `unshuffledQueue`; timeline seek thumb/preview clear on off-track drag release; login stale bootstrap probe stale-guarded; `android/**` added to ESLint ignores; Escape over BigMusic+palette closes only the palette; waveform re-samples on `:root` accent `transitionend`; `useBlobUrl` no longer caches non-ok responses; `addTrackToPlaylist` songCount duplicate-drift fixed; Navidrome `getArtist` N+1 fixed (metadata-only + memoized `albumCache` lazy fetch); Navidrome `getResume` `JSON.parse` guarded; shared `src/services/music/veloraTrack.ts` extracted (#18). Low/polish (2026-07-02): upload dropzone drag highlight uses an enter/leave depth counter (no strobe); accent tokens (`--color-accent`/`-solid`) cleared on `MainPage` unmount so they don't leak onto login after logout; track menu "Add to playlist" submenu shows a disabled "Loading playlists…" placeholder when opened before playlists load; dead `nav.analytics`/`login.goToMain` i18n keys removed from de/es/fr/it/ja; stale mobile-sidebar comment in `buildGrid.ts` corrected. Also from that session, previously unrecorded: BigMusic stops reserving sidebar width on mobile (`!isMobile` guard on the `--bm-sidebar-*` offset) and `sidebarVisible` now defaults to `false` (fresh installs only, persisted users keep their value); the waveform's unplayed bars now sample the accent token instead of `--color-white` (confirmed intended 2026-07-05; dark cover accents were then hard to see, so the bar color is now `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent-solid) 70%, var(--color-white))` on `.timelineWaveform`, sampled by the canvas via computed `color`; tune the 70% ratio there). Follow-up review 2026-07-05 on this batch: duplicate add-to-playlist now skips the request entirely (Subsonic would append a real duplicate the UI hid); discography lazy-expand collapses the row on fetch failure instead of leaving a stuck skeleton (tap again to retry); palette Escape moved from the input's keydown to a window capture listener so it closes regardless of focus and still shields BigMusic's Esc listener. Nav playlist-list virtualization (#13) and iOS long-press context-menu gap (#19) left open (see `goals.md` §5/§11).

- Pinned nav not scoped to the connected server (resolved 2026-07-07): pinned playlists/artists lived in one global `pinnedPlaylists`/`pinnedArtists` array in `useSettings`, so a pin from one backend leaked onto another where that id may not exist. Now keyed per normalized server url: `pinnedPlaylistsByServer`/`pinnedArtistsByServer` maps are the persisted source of truth; flat `pinnedPlaylists`/`pinnedArtists` stay as a reactive mirror of the active server so consumers (`nav.tsx`, `playlistMenu.ts`, `mediaMenu.ts`) are unchanged. `setActiveServer(providerBundle.getServerUrl())` populates the mirror on connect/resume (called at the 3 `useProvider.sync()` sites: `sessionRestore.ts`, `loginPage.tsx` login + bootstrap). Pre-scoping flat pins are carried over in `merge` and adopted onto the first server seen (one-time migration, no data loss). Files: `src/settings.tsx`, `src/services/sessionRestore.ts`, `src/screens/pages/loginPage/loginPage.tsx`.
- Settings sliders didn't work with touch (resolved 2026-07-09): `SettingsSlider` (also the plugin SDK's `Slider`) was mouse-event-only (`onMouseDown` + window `mousemove`/`mouseup`); switched to pointer events (`onPointerDown` + window `pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel`, matching `timeline.tsx`) and added `touch-action: none` on the track. Files: `settingsSlider.tsx`/`.css`.
- BigMusic z-index hole (found 2026-07-06, resolved 2026-07-06): `.bigMusicOverlay` hardcoded `z-index: 9000` above the whole `--z-*` scale, so toast, `ConfirmDialog`, `NamePromptModal`, `EditTrackModal`, and desktop `Dropdown` menus (all at `z-overlay` 999 / `z-modal` 50) rendered behind BigMusic while open; the command palette dodged it with a `z-index: 9999 !important` hack. Fixed by restructuring the token scale in `index.css`: new `--z-bigmusic: 9000` (consumed by `bigMusic.css`; `.background_overlay` is `calc(var(--z-bigmusic) - 1)`) with `--z-modal`/`--z-tooltip`/`--z-overlay` lifted above it to 9200/9300/9500, semantics: BigMusic covers page chrome and in-page popovers (`--z-dropdown` and below), while every sheet/dialog/menu/toast layer beats it by default. The interim escape hatch (`ABOVE_BIG_MUSIC_Z`, `Sheet`/`Dropdown` `zIndex` props + submenu threading, QueueView/sidebar conditionals) and the palette's `!important` hack were all removed as redundant. Safe because `--z-tooltip` had no consumers and nothing occupied 100–999 between the layers; the desktop docked sidebar is unaffected (it portals *into* the overlay element). `docs/designsystemV2.md` §2.6 documents the new scale.
- Local-mode seek + reload, two fixes (2026-07-11): (1) timeline seeks always snapped back to 0:00, the `vmedia://` handler relied on `net.fetch(file://)` honoring the forwarded Range header, which it doesn't inside `protocol.handle`; now serves ranges manually (see §11). (2) client-mode playback (local/Navidrome) didn't survive a reload: the resume plumbing (`getResume`/`saveResume`) existed but nothing called it, `ClientPlaybackController` now persists its resume on every `commit()` (cleared on stop) and seeds the last track, paused at its stored position, in the constructor. Velora mode was never affected (server restores the queue). Follow-up: position-only writes are throttled (`RESUME_PERSIST_THROTTLE_MS` 15s); track/play-state transitions still persist immediately.
- Nav local-mode playlist covers showed the folder icon instead of the first song's art (2026-07-11). `nav.tsx`'s `buildButton` only treated `http`/`/`-prefixed icons as image URLs, so local `vmedia://cover/<albumKey>` covers were mangled into `iconify:vmedia://…`. Now detects any `://` scheme (`nav.tsx:184`).
- Pause visual renderer work while Electron is hidden in the tray (2026-07-13). Electron visibility IPC unmounts the shared background, stops audio-reactive DOM writes (since removed, see next), and gates the player + BigMusic position tickers. The shared background lifecycle also unmounts every implementation when the page is hidden or offscreen. Files: `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.cts`, `useDesktopIntegration.ts`, `mainPage.tsx`, `src/assets/backgrounds/`, `player.tsx`, `bigMusic.tsx`.
- Perf audit fixes (2026-07-13): audio-reactive visuals removed entirely (the hook, `createBrightnessReader`, the vis analyser, the `--vis-*` root vars, the `equalizerEnabled` setting + its player/BigMusic toggle buttons, and every background's per-frame brightness read, backgrounds no longer touch the CSSOM per frame); player bar 100ms position tick moved into leaf components (`PlayerClock`/`PlayerTimeline`/`MiniProgress` in `player.tsx`) so the bar no longer re-renders 10×/s while playing; reverb `ConvolverNode` now only connected while `reverbWet > 0` (`audioEngine.ts` `applySettings`) instead of convolving at wet 0 forever.
- Background shader resolution/fps (2026-07-13). Two Settings → Performance selects (dependency-hidden while the background is disabled): frame-rate cap `backgroundFps` ("30" default / "60") and internal render resolution `backgroundResolution` ("half" default / "full" = dpr capped at 2 / "quarter"). Shared `getBackgroundQuality()` (`src/assets/backgrounds/backgroundQuality.ts`) read once per mount by every implementation; `background.tsx` keys the active one on both settings (no per-frame reads, no GL rebuilds). Resolution routes through each renderer's dpr (OGL `Renderer({ dpr })`, three.js `setPixelRatio`); fps via a shared `createFrameThrottle()`. Exceptions: pixelBlast keeps 1× resolution (fps cap still applies); blobs keeps its adaptive canvas scaling + own throttle. Also clamped `nav.css` `blur(999px)` → `blur(60px)` (both pills). Review fix: player position hooks share optimistic seek broadcasts (`positionSetters` in `player.tsx`) so the clock/mini progress track a paused seek instantly.
- Add-to-playlist by keybind said nothing (2026-08-06). The menu path confirms itself (the menu closes over the row you clicked), but a hotkey or a palette row leaves no trace, so the add was silent while a duplicate and a failure both toasted. `addTrackToPlaylist` now returns `"added" | "duplicate" | "failed"` and `useKeybindDispatch` toasts `contextMenu.track.addedToPlaylist` with the playlist name on `"added"` only, so the confirmation lives on the callers with no inline feedback and the menu stays quiet (designsystemV2 §14.9). Files: `store/library.ts`, `utils/useKeybindDispatch.ts`, 9 locales.

- Split detail header stopped collapsing, and sat at the cover's own size, whenever the artwork moved (2026-09-07). The split variant takes its panel out of flow so only the (collapsing) header height sizes it, but the rule named `img` alone, and an animated cover is drawn into a `canvas` (`AnimatedCover`). A canvas has an intrinsic size, so in flow it was the one thing in that box with a height of its own and the header sized to it, ~512px, with `--collapse` still running and nothing to show for it. Favorites is where it showed, since a device-stored GIF is the cover that animates most, but any `.gif` cover hit it. `detailHeader.css` absolutizes `> canvas` beside `> img`.
- Favorites cover rows lived on the wrong element (2026-09-07). The three `favoritesCover` settings were tagged `target: "card"`, so right-clicking any album or artist tile offered to restyle Favorites, while the one surface the pick actually paints, the favorites detail header, answered with the header rows alone. New `favoritesArt` style target (`utils/styleTargets.ts` + a `styleTarget.favoritesArt` label in the nine locales, worded like the setting it opens), declared on the header's cover box through `DetailHeader`'s new `coverTarget` prop and passed only for favorites. Nested inside `detailHeader`, so the picture answers for the picture and the card around it still answers for the header. The favorites tile in the playlists grid is not tagged: it goes on answering with the card rows.
- Turning the local API off left the import API running (2026-09-30, review B4). The import toggle is a child row hidden while `localApi` is off, but `useExternalImport` enabled the endpoint from `externalImport` alone and main keeps the loopback server up while either route group is on, so "import on, then local API off" still accepted token-gated uploads behind a Settings page that showed everything off. The effective flag is now `localApi && externalImport`, the token rows gate on `localApi` alone, the token availability probe no longer rejects unhandled, and a failed generate/regenerate toasts `settings.integrations.apiTokenGenerateFailed`. Files: `utils/useExternalImport.ts`, `settingsView/useSettingsSections.ts`, 9 locales, `docs/app/settings/integrations.md`.
- Review 2026-09-28 playback batch (2026-10-02): B1 Velora playback opened one WebSocket per early subscriber and never closed the extras (`openSocket` now joins an in-flight ticket fetch and bails if torn down or disposed meanwhile); B2 repeat-one with crossfade cut the song's last seconds (the early crossfade exit skips when the next track is the same one, `ended` loops it); U1 Next under repeat-one restarted instead of skipping (new `advance` command is the engine's end-of-track move, `next` is the user's skip and wraps under repeat-one, the Velora controller rewrites them to the server's `next` / `playIndex`); B3 audio settings rows went stale after an import or a pop-out (`utils/useAudioSettings.ts`, one `useSyncExternalStore` over the engine, replaces ~20 mirrored states); B5 autoplay passes the `tracks` hint; B6 its random fallback uses `randomTrackPool` instead of the 100 newest; B7 a pause mid-fetch retries on resume; B8 `insertAt` after Stop keeps the index at -1 and the all-songs backfill checks it. Files: `veloraPlaybackController.ts`, `clientPlaybackController.ts`, `playbackTypes.ts`, `audioEngine.ts`, `useSettingsSections.ts`, `useAutoplayContinuation.ts`.
- Accent colour pulled the full-resolution cover on every track change (2026-10-07, `tmp/perf-audit.html` M3). `useCoverColors` now asks `useBlobUrl` for the 128px thumb (the player bar's own cache entry), and the desktop local API hands main a 512px copy via `resolveCoverUrl` and samples its palette from that, instead of fetching the original a second time.
- Song change hitched with colour sync on (2026-10-07). The sync lived in `MainPage`, so every cover/palette update re-rendered the whole shell, popped settings registry included; it is now `AccentSync` in `mainPage.tsx` and BigMusic reads `useLivePalette`. A parked docked settings tab's body is `content-visibility: hidden`, so its rows skip the restyle on each frame of the `:root` accent fade.

## 13. Home Page Expansion
Planned 2026-06-17. Foundations and all four sections are done. User-customizable home (reorder / show-hide sections, 2026-07-17; plus in-place drag-to-reorder on the home view itself, 2026-07-18, hover a section title, it slides right revealing a drag handle, dragging persists the same `homeSectionOrder`; touch path stays Settings → Home) and the empty-library prompt (2026-07-18, §11) followed. Velora-only, hidden in Navidrome mode via the capability model. (The "Made for you" smart-mix idea lives on as the Audio-DNA smart mixes item in `goals.md` §2.)

- **Scroll memory (2026-10-12).** Home keeps its scroll position across navigation (back button included) through `useScrollMemory`, retried on the body's content height while its sections load (`HomeScrollMemory` in `homeView.tsx`).

- **State-coverage follow-ups (2026-07-18).** `Overview` was the worst offender, a failed `getUserStats` was swallowed into `console.error` while the skeleton condition (`recentlyListened === null`) never cleared, so the card pulsed forever with `—` numbers. It now reports success/failure through `useRetryableLoad` (refresh button reuses the same `retry`), renders `ErrorState` in place of its content, shows `EmptyState` for a no-history user, honors the dev loading/empty/error states, and drops its byte-for-byte fork of the shared `TrackSkeleton`. Numbers fall back to `—` only while loading, so a no-history user still sees a real library size. Nav's playlist list gained an error path (silently blank before) with a compact `ErrorState` + retry, folded down to a labelled retry icon where there's no room, plus the dev loading/error states. `SystemTab`'s "unreachable" state gained a retry instead of being a dead end until you reopened Settings. (`LibraryTab` was audited and left alone, it already surfaces scan failures inline with a tone.)
- **App-wide empty states (2026-07-18).** New `EmptyState` primitive (twin of `ErrorState`: centered `caption op-50` + optional CTA, V2 §13) wired into every surface that could load successfully and return nothing, the shared `Playlist` track list (`emptyMessageKey`, covers /tracks, playlist/album/genre/artist songs), albums, artists, genres (migrated off its bespoke span), playlists (both sections; "Your playlists" carries a `+ New playlist` CTA), recently listened, discography, and `CarouselSection`. i18n under `empty.*` in all 6 locales. The dev-tools "empty" view state now reaches all of them: grid views via `useDevListOverride`, the track list and carousels via `useDevViewState`, and home via `HomeEmptyState`. Home is the one deliberate single-empty surface, one state replaces all sections rather than each carousel showing its own.

- **Carousel redesign (2026-08-04),** superseding the header-nav pass above. The row was cut dead at the section card's inner padding, so the only thing saying it continued was a pair of 28px arrows in the far corner, and at an edge they didn't disappear, they went `.deactive` (grayscale + `not-allowed`), which reads broken rather than "you're at the start". **The row now runs full bleed** (negative inline margin, the padding restored inside the scroller and mirrored into `scroll-padding-inline` so the first tile still lines up under the title) and **fades at its own edge** through a `mask-image` whose two lengths are `@property`-registered, so the fade animates instead of popping the instant a scroll starts, and only the side with content behind it fades: the fade is a readout of where the row is, not a permanent vignette. **The arrows became paddles floating over that faded band**, mounted only for a direction the row can still travel (no disabled state to explain), revealed on hover of the row, absent entirely under `pointer: coarse`/`hover: none` where the swipe is the affordance and a paddle would just sit on the artwork. They page by **whole tiles** (`floor(clientWidth / itemStep) * itemStep`) rather than by 0.8 of the viewport, so a page can't park a sliver of a card against the edge, and the page is `behavior: "auto"` under reduce-motion. Spacers opt out of snapping (`scroll-snap-align: none`), which the old row could snap onto. **Section header:** the title carries a chevron and opens the full view itself (plain `<button>` styled locally, the same call `.playlistSortable` makes, with the padding/negative-margin trick so its hover fill bleeds without moving the text), and the named "View all" stays alongside it. That let `onNav`/`CarouselNavButtons` and the absolutely-positioned action cluster go. The line under the header stays the shared `.divider` utility: a local hairline was tried and reverted, because a section card that draws its own line does not match the ones every other card draws. Home's drag hot zone narrowed to the handle's own gutter, since it used to cover 40% of the title row and would now swallow the title's click. Skeletons gained the subtitle bar they were missing. `textHyperLink`'s hover moved off `--color-accent`: both the accent and the background shader derive from the same cover, so the hover state was landing on its own colour. Zero new i18n keys.

Now ranked rows (rank as type, 40px cover, name + listened time) with a thin accent bar sized by listened time against #1, so the gap between places shows. Two columns of five on desktop (column flow, one list under a 560px container), top five on mobile.
- **Spotlight (2026-08-10).** Home opens on a stage instead of a row of cards: one pick at a time out of a five-pick reel, each held ten seconds. A pick is a song or an artist, and its **reason** is the card's kicker (`Rediscover` / `New in your library` / `On repeat lately` / `From your artists`), so the section says why it is showing you this. The reel is drawn once per visit and cached **in module state for five minutes** (`spotlightReel.ts`, keyed by user id so a logout can't hand it to the next account, and never persisted): stepping off home and back resumes the same five picks *and* the pick that was on screen, a genuinely new visit draws new ones. Composition: copy on the left over the card's own surface, artwork bleeding off the right edge and dissolving into it through a `mask-image` (the carousel's fade grammar turned sideways), and a flat wash mixed from that pick's own cover colour via `useCoverColors` (respecting `colorSync`/`coverColorDefaults`), so an advance is felt as a change of light before it's read. Nothing sits on a scrim, so the text keeps the surface's contrast; the kicker is tinted from the cover's hue rather than dimmed to gray. Indicator is five segments over the copy column: filled = shown, accent = current, empty = upcoming; each is a button that jumps, hover/focus pauses the count where it stands (and resumes there), and an explicit pause toggle sits at the end of the row for the keyboard and for WCAG 2.2.2. Reel sourcing is provider-agnostic and costs one request: `getRandomSongs` where the provider has it, and for Velora (which does not) a page from a **random offset** derived from `stats.totalTracks`, so it is a window into the whole library rather than the newest page; artists come from `stats.topArtists` then the library list, both preferring entries that have artwork, and the two kinds are interleaved so the reel never runs three songs before its first artist. No new capability: with nothing to show it renders `null` like every other home section. Registered as the first entry in `BUILTIN_HOME_SECTIONS`, so it is reorderable and hideable through the existing Settings → Home control; `orderKeys` changed with it, a key the saved order never saw now slots in behind its **default neighbour** instead of appending at the bottom, so a section meant to open home still opens it for someone who reordered before it existed.
  - **No countdown bar, and no backdrop-filter on the card. Both are measurements.** The indicator first shipped as a per-segment bar counting the ten seconds down, and it took this card from **1.5% to 20% GPU** (2026-08-10): the 2026-08-08 law again, a line advancing at the panel's refresh rate, except this is the widest surface in the app, so every frame resampled a full-width backdrop. Three fixes were tried in order and the first two were kept as well, since they are right on their own: **stepping** the bar (`steps()`, the cover-spin answer), then **dropping the card's blur**, `.homeSpotlight` restates `--surface-paint: var(--color-ui)` / `--surface-filter: none` and kills `backdrop-filter` outright, all `!important` the way `data-reduce-transparency` does, since a per-theme surface override outranks a component class; that is free here because the card is already almost entirely artwork and flat wash, and the play glyph over the artwork lost its own blur with it. Neither was enough on the measured machine, so **the moving line went**. Position is now marked by state rather than by motion: filled = shown, accent + `scaleY(2)` = current, empty = upcoming, one transition per advance and nothing per frame. What that costs is the "how long is it up" half of the ask; the pause control and the jump-to-segment buttons stay, and the rotation is still ten seconds on a JS timer that hover, focus and the pause button all hold. **Don't re-add a continuously animating element to this card** without measuring it on a high-refresh panel first.
  - **The Overview card was deleted, and its contents were rehoused** (2026-08-10). It was a titled card holding three nested cards: two recently-listened rows, monthly activity, and all-time stats. The numbers became **the reel's opening page**, in the stage's own language rather than a grid of tiles: kicker "This month", the month's listening time as the display line, then one row of three plain figures (tracks played, all-time listening, songs in library) where a media pick puts its meta line, the cover of the last thing you played on the art side, and "View stats" (`<Capable feature="listeningStats">`) where the play controls sit. It holds **15s** rather than 10 (`SPOTLIGHT_OVERVIEW_MS`), since four numbers take longer to read than a title. The pick carries **no data at all**: both the numbers and the artwork are read live at render, because a reel lives five minutes and a readout that old is simply wrong. The artwork is **the cover of whatever is playing**, falling back to the newest entry in `stats.recentlyListened` when nothing is. It was first written as a build-time snapshot of that stats entry and that was the bug: `stats` is only refetched at login, so in a long-lived tab the page showed a cover the user had moved past hours earlier. A provider with no user stats never builds the page and the reel stays five media picks.
  - **Recently listened became its own section** at the foot of home (`homeRecentlyListened/`), a `CarouselSection` of `MediaCard`s over the same `useSession.stats.recentlyListened` (no extra fetch), "View all" → `/recently-listened`, gated on `userStats`. Overview's refresh button came with it, but now writes back through a new `useSession.refreshStats()` instead of into a component's own state, so refreshing also updates Top Artists and the Spotlight's opening page. That is a fix, not a port: the old button refreshed two rows and left every other stats surface stale.
  - **Reordering.** The card has no title in the drag handle's gutter (its copy is centred, clear of that corner), so nothing revealed the handle on hover the way a section title does. Hovering the card reveals it instead (`.homeSection:has(> .homeSpotlight):hover`), grab zone unchanged, so it drags exactly like the titled sections.
  - Art goes through `useCoverArt` at 640px (the longest edge the stage can draw) rather than straight into an `<img src>`: the raw url skips the provider's thumbnail endpoint, so the poster was downloading and decoding the full-resolution original five times per reel. The next pick's copy is warmed during the current one's ten seconds, and the palette samples that same sized copy instead of pulling the cover again.
  - **Swipe to step** (2026-10-03): on a phone a sideways swipe on the card moves the reel (left next, right previous, wrapping), on the row swipe's `SWIPE_COMMIT`/`SWIPE_VELOCITY` thresholds with a tap haptic. It is a motion `onPanEnd`, not a drag, so the card never moves and nothing changes under reduce-motion; `touch-action: pan-y` hands vertical scrolling back to the page.
  - ↳ files: `src/screens/views/homeView/components/{homeSpotlight/*,homeRecentlyListened/*}`, deleted `components/overview/*`, `homeView/{homeSections.tsx,homeView.css}`, `src/store/session.ts` (`refreshStats`), `tests/screens/views/homeView/homeSections.test.tsx`, all 9 `src/locales/*/translation.json` (`main.spotlight.*`; the stats labels stay on their existing `main.overview.*` keys, which `/recently-listened` and the keybind list also read)

A section being dragged keeps its surface. The Spotlight's wash runs edge to edge as a band. Fewer blurred surfaces as a side effect.

## 14. Provider Parity
- **Genre browsing on Velora (2026-10-04).** `genreBrowsing` was the last browse surface Velora lacked, now on, so the Home genres row, `/genres`, `/genre/:name`, the Library tab and the search page's genres show up with no UI change. Backend: `GET /api/v1/genres` (`TrackRepository.listGenres`) merges tags case-insensitively under their most common spelling, matching the smart-rule genre match, which is why "Rock" and "rock" are one card. A genre's songs reuse `POST /tracks/query` with a `genre is <name>` rule, so `getSongsByGenre`'s cursor is a track id on Velora (opaque, like every cursor). Clicking a row queues the whole genre server-side through a new `"genre"` queue source resolved by the same rule and order, and the controller passes a genre's `sourceId` through as a string instead of `Number()`ing it. Track genres only; `artist_genres` is left out on purpose.
- **Reverse audit, closed 2026-07-19.** Confirms nothing in the app assumes Subsonic-only capabilities Velora lacks. Last run 2026-07-17 and clean: all 7 Subsonic-true / Velora-false caps gate through the capability model (never provider identity), nothing reads `playlistVisibility` or `playlist.isPublic`, and every `getProviderType`/`useProviderType` branch is infra (cache key, API report, section placement) rather than a feature gate. Kept as a **trigger, not a standing task**: re-run it when the §15 playlist visibility toggle is built. Evidence sheet stays at `docs/goalsDetails/provider-parity-audit.md`.
- **Re-run 2026-07-19 after the §15 visibility toggle landed, still clean**, and the capability-key follow-up is closed with it. All 7 Subsonic-true caps still gate through the model (the new toggle correctly uses `musicService.supports("playlistVisibility")`, being non-component code), only 3 `getProviderType` reads remain and all are infra: peaks cache key, desktop API report, and settings section *ordering* (`settingsView.tsx:100` hoists Local Library in local mode; `PluginsSection includeLocal` is the same switch). The two keys the old bullet asked for both exist: `storage` is consumed by `NavStorageIndicator`, and `extendedTrackStats` is declared by every provider but deliberately **not** wired into `InfoView`, which keeps its per-field `!= null` check because that also hides rows for a Velora track with no analysis yet, which a capability gate alone would not. The key stays as the seam for §2 audio-DNA mixes. Same pass fixed three leftover en dashes in `capabilities.ts` / `ImusicProvider.ts` comments. Evidence: `docs/goalsDetails/provider-parity-audit.md`.
- Provider-aware UI audit (audited 2026-06-17, closed 2026-06-19), every Velora-only surface now hides in Navidrome mode at the component level via `getProviderType()`/`useCapability()` (P6) instead of catching `UNSUPPORTED`. Playback already had full parity. Closed gaps:
  - Home `Overview` + `RecentlyListenedView`, wrapped in `<Capable feature="userStats">` / `useCapability("userStats")`, fixing the §12 dash/skeleton bug.
  - **Lyrics**, new `IMusicProvider.getLyrics(trackId)`: Velora reads embedded `stats.lyrics`; Navidrome lazily fetches Subsonic's `getLyricsBySongId` and converts it to the same LRC-line format. Shared `src/utils/useTrackLyrics.ts` hook (gated on the now-`true`-for-both `lyrics` capability) feeds the sidebar Lyrics tab + BigMusic Typographic/Editorial.
    - ↳ files: `ImusicProvider.ts`, `providers/{velora,navidrome}Provider.ts`, `utils/useTrackLyrics.ts`, `primitives/Lyrics/Lyrics.tsx`, `bigMusic/modes/{lyrics,editorial}/*.tsx`
  - `getPlaylists("velora")`: already gated via the `veloraPlaylists` capability in `homePlaylist.tsx`/`playlistsView.tsx`.
  - Still open at archive time (carried into `goals.md` §14): extended track stats (`energy`/`danceability`/`valence`/`moodTags`, undefined on Navidrome) and storage stats (Velora-only), gate future UI on `extendedTrackStats` / a new capability key respectively. `/stats` view (§8) is unbuilt, gate on landing. (§13 Top Artists landed 2026-06-21, gated on `userStats`.)
- Standard pattern, `useProviderType()` (`src/store/provider.ts`) over P6.
- **Subsonic generalization (2026-07-14)**: `NavidromeProvider` was never Navidrome-specific (plain Subsonic/OpenSubsonic client), so it's now the generic `SubsonicProvider` (`src/services/music/providers/subsonicProvider.ts`), one class for the whole family, Navidrome, Airsonic (+Advanced), gonic, Ampache (Subsonic backend), Supysonic, Astiga, and any other token-auth Subsonic server; never fork it per server. OpenSubsonic extras (structured lyrics, multi-artist tags) already degrade gracefully on servers that lack them (`getLyrics` catches → `null`).
  - Backward compat: `ProviderType`/`PlaybackConnectionConfig` `"navidrome"` → `"subsonic"`; `readPersistedConnection()` migrates a persisted `velora-connection` of type `"navidrome"` (and the older plaintext-password shape) to the new shape on read and rewrites storage, so existing Navidrome sessions restore untouched. The playback resume scope keeps its historical `navidrome:` storage prefix on purpose (opaque namespace; changing it would drop everyone's resume state). `velora-session` never held the provider type, so no migration there.
  - Login redesign: tabs are now Velora / Navidrome / Subsonic / This device, tab `id` (UI identity) is split from `providerType` (connection type), so Navidrome keeps its own button (biggest server, clearer for people who don't know Subsonic) while sharing the one provider with the generic Subsonic tab, whose hint names Airsonic/gonic/Ampache/Supysonic/Astiga (`login.subsonicHint`, all 6 locales). Local mode relabeled "This device" (`login.localMode`) with an `iconify:computer` tab icon; tab row wraps 2x2; vinyl showcase removed and the card centered (`grid-template-columns: min(440px, 100%)`).
  - Rejected from the family: **Funkwhale**, exposes a Subsonic API but only accepts plaintext `p=` auth (no token/salt), which would force storing the password at rest; parked in `goals.md` §14 with Plex/Kodi.
  - ↳ files: `providers/subsonicProvider.ts` (renamed), `musicProviderBundle.ts`, `sessionRestore.ts`, `playbackControllerBundle.ts`, `loginPage.tsx` (+ `.css`), all 6 locales, `CLAUDE.md`/`README.md` provider tables
- **Jellyfin provider (2026-07-22).** New `JellyfinProvider` (`src/services/music/providers/jellyfinProvider.ts`), one Emby-compatible class for the whole family (auth sent under both Jellyfin's `Authorization` and Emby's `X-Emby-Authorization` header names; only the Jellyfin login tab ships for now, Emby stays untested). Client-side playback (`ClientPlaybackController`, like the Subsonic family), own `jellyfin:` resume scope. Auth: `POST /Users/AuthenticateByName` issues a long-lived `AccessToken`; only `{token, userId}` + a once-generated stable `DeviceId` (`velora-jellyfin-device-id`) are persisted, never the password. The bundle reads the token off the instance post-connect (`getAuth()`), since it isn't known until login. Media auth rides in the URL (`api_key=` on `/Audio/{id}/universal` and `/Items/{id}/Images/Primary`) because `<audio>`/`<img>` can't send a header (engine uses `crossOrigin="anonymous"`, covers `credentials: "omit"`); `universal` direct-plays common containers and transcodes the rest to progressive mp3 (no HLS/MSE in the audio engine). Caps true: `createPlaylist`, `lyrics` (`/Audio/{id}/Lyrics`, ticks→LRC), `genreBrowsing`, `recentlyAddedAlbums`, `mostPlayedAlbums`, `favoriteMedia` (one `FavoriteItems/{id}` endpoint for track/album/artist), `smartRadio` (`/Items/{id}/InstantMix`), `newestFirstTracks` (DateCreated desc). Off for v1: `trackRating` (Jellyfin's 0-10 axis ≠ the 1-5 UI), `playlistVisibility`, `playQueueSync`. Playlist removal is keyed by per-entry `PlaylistItemId`, looked up before the `DELETE`. `login.jellyfinHint` ×6.
  - ↳ files: `providers/jellyfinProvider.ts` (new), `musicProviderBundle.ts`, `playbackControllerBundle.ts`, `sessionRestore.ts`, `loginPage.tsx`, all 6 locales
- **Playlist song count on every provider (2026-08-10).** `Playlist.songCount` was only ever set by Velora and local mode, so on Subsonic/Jellyfin the count was `undefined` and every surface that reads it silently rendered nothing: the playlist card and nav row lost their "N songs" subtitle, search results lost it too, and `PlaylistCard`'s first-song cover fallback never ran (it gates on `songCount`). Both mappers now fill it from the field the server already sends, `songCount` on the Subsonic playlist element and `ChildCount` on the Jellyfin item (already requested in `FIELDS`), falling back to the mapped `songs.length` on the detail path.
  - ↳ files: `providers/subsonicProvider.ts` (`mapPlaylist`), `providers/jellyfinProvider.ts` (`mapPlaylist`)
- **Dropped: separate Emby login tab (2026-07-22).** The Jellyfin provider is already one Emby-compatible class (sends both `Authorization` and `X-Emby-Authorization` on every request, `jellyfinProvider.ts:184`) and the login hint already reads "Also works with Emby" in all 6 locales, so an Emby server logs in through the Jellyfin tab today. A second tab would only fork one API family into two labels, exactly what the "one class per API family, labels only per server" rule forbids. Discoverability is covered by the hint. Don't re-propose.
- **Dropped: Kodi + Funkwhale providers (2026-07-22).** Speculative-provider backlog closed; don't re-propose without a real user asking. Current coverage (Velora + the whole Subsonic family + Jellyfin/Emby + local) already spans every self-hosted music server people actually run, so both were long-tail with real downsides. **Kodi** (JSON-RPC) is a video-first media center almost nobody runs headless as a music streaming server, and its API is an awkward fit for this client. **Funkwhale** exposes a Subsonic API but only accepts plaintext `p=` auth (no token/salt), so supporting it would force storing the user's password at rest, the exact regression this codebase refuses everywhere else (why it was already rejected from the Subsonic family). The `IMusicProvider` + capability seam is unchanged; adding a wanted provider later is still additive.
- **Plex provider, dropped 2026-07-22.** Not worth the surface area: Plex is a video-first product whose music users already have Plexamp (polished, hard to beat), and its cloud-account/paywall direction alienates exactly the self-hosted/privacy audience Velora targets, who are already on Navidrome/Jellyfin (both supported). Auth is a plex.tv **token flow** routed through Plex's cloud, at odds with the other providers and more fragile. Revisit only if a real user asks; until then don't re-propose. Kodi/Funkwhale stay parked in `goals.md` §14.

## 15. Navidrome-only capabilities

- **Multiple music folders (2026-07-23).** New `musicFolders` capability (Subsonic only) + `IMusicProvider.getMusicFolders()` / `setMusicFolder(id | null)` (new `MusicFolder` type). `SubsonicProvider` holds the scope in its config and a `withFolder()` helper appends `musicFolderId` to every library *listing*: `getTracks`/`search` (search3), the three `getAlbumList2` methods, `getArtists`, `getRandomSongs`, `getSongsByGenre`, and both `getStarred2` reads; id-addressed detail calls stay unscoped, `getGenres` has no folder param in the spec. Selection persists in the `velora-connection` entry (optional `musicFolderId`, fresh login resets to all folders) and `resume()` feeds it back into the provider config; UI routes through `providerBundle.setMusicFolder()` / `getMusicFolderId()` exposed on `musicService` as bundle methods (persistence is why it doesn't proxy straight to the provider). UI: standalone `MusicFoldersSection` in Settings behind `<Capable feature="musicFolders">`, reusing `SettingLine type="select"` ("All folders" + one entry per folder); hides itself when the server reports fewer than two folders, and on change refetches via the existing `refreshLocalLibrary()` helper (generic despite the name). i18n `settings.musicFolders.*` ×9.
- **Artist bio + images (2026-07-23).** `SubsonicProvider.getArtist` fetches `getArtistInfo2` in parallel: `Artist.bio` (HTML/entities stripped provider-side), a last.fm artist image used only when the artist has no cover (the generic `2a96cbd8...` star placeholder is filtered), and `Artist.similarArtists` (new `SimilarArtist` type, id-less/"-1" entries dropped, capped at 20). Plain-Subsonic servers degrade to the bare artist (catch-and-null, same stance as lyrics). New `artistInfo` capability (Subsonic only); the artist view's "Similar artists" `CarouselSection` is `<Capable>`-gated and hides quietly when absent, while the bio lights up through the view's existing presence-driven render. Jellyfin has a similar-artists API but stays false, flipping it later is one line + a mapper. i18n `artist.similarArtists` ×9. Caveat: the header image goes through `useBlobUrl` (a fetch), so a CORS-blocking last.fm CDN image falls back to the empty-avatar state; similar-artist cards use a plain `<img>` and are immune.
- **Internet radio stations (2026-07-23).** Full CRUD on the Subsonic endpoints (`getInternetRadioStations` + create/update/delete; request param `homepageUrl` vs response `homePageUrl`, update always sends it so clearing works) behind the new `internetRadio` capability. `/radio` view (§15 scaffold: skeletons, `ErrorState`, `EmptyState` + add CTA, `embedded` prop), entry points: a capability-gated home section (`homeRadio`, registered in `BUILTIN_HOME_SECTIONS`, hidden at zero stations, View All to `/radio`) + the mobile Library tab (deliberately no nav button), add/edit via a §14.4 centered modal, delete via `confirmAction`; optimistic list mutations with revert + `toast.error`, refetch after create/update for authoritative ids; list capped at 500. Playback: synthetic track (`radio:<id>` via `src/services/music/radioTrack.ts`, duration 0, streamUrl = station URL) fed through the normal `setQueue({tracks})` path, so engine/player/media-session work unmodified; the id prefix keys three special cases (no transcode params in `audioEngine.swapTo`, radio queues skipped from Subsonic `savePlayQueue`, `clampPosition` treats duration 0 as unbounded) plus a fourth: `useTrackPeaks` never fetches/decodes peaks for radio ids (endless stream, the waveform scrubber otherwise loads forever), falling back to the plain timeline bar. **Local mode also supports it** (capability true): stations persist device-locally in localStorage (`velora-local-radio-stations`, `crypto.randomUUID()` ids), `LocalProvider.getStreamUrl` resolves `radio:` ids. **Velora supports it too** (backend `0c99e25` / v0.4.0: per-user `/api/v1/radio-stations` CRUD + `radio:<id>` resolution in the server-authoritative queue via `resolveTracksByIds`); `VeloraProvider` calls it through `apiFetch`, `VeloraPlaybackController.wireTrackId()` keeps radio ids as strings on the wire (everything else stays numeric) and skips listening sessions for them, and `TrackDto.streamUrl` lets server queue snapshots map radio entries to playable tracks. Jellyfin stays false + UNSUPPORTED. i18n `nav.radio` + `radio.*` ×9. Known limitation: stations whose servers send no CORS headers stay silent (the engine's Web Audio graph needs `crossOrigin`), not fixable without bypassing the shared effects graph.
- **Random songs (2026-07-23).** New `randomSongs` capability + `IMusicProvider.getRandomSongs(count = 100)`: Subsonic `getRandomSongs?size=N`, Jellyfin `/Items?SortBy=Random`, local mode via a full adapter crawl + partial Fisher-Yates sample (cheap, on-device SQLite), Velora UNSUPPORTED (no backend endpoint; add one there if this should light up). New `"random"` `QueueSource` resolved in `ClientPlaybackController` (client-only, like `genre`); surfaced as a capability-gated "Play Random Songs" command-palette action (icon `casino`). i18n `commandPalette.actions.playRandom` ×9.
- **Subsonic play tracking / scrobble, dropped 2026-07-19.** Was flagged as the highest-impact parity gap (Subsonic writes no plays, so stats and the ListenBrainz plugin stay dead in Subsonic mode); decided not to build it. Don't re-propose without a new decision; the note that the local-mode `LocalPlayRecorder` seam could feed it goes dormant with it.
- **Playlist visibility toggle (2026-07-19).** Subsonic's `public` flag is server-side visibility: a public playlist is listed in every other user's `getPlaylists` on that server (with an `owner` attribute), playable by them, editable only by its owner. Not a share link, nothing anonymous. `SubsonicProvider` already read it (`mapPlaylist` → `isPublic`) and already sent it on `updatePlaylist`, so this was the UI half plus a store action. New `useLibrary.setPlaylistVisibility()` follows the `renamePlaylist` optimistic shape (patch the nav summary **and** any loaded detail, revert the pair on failure, `toast.error`). The menu entry is spread into `buildPlaylistMenuEntries` behind `musicService.supports("playlistVisibility")`, so it appears in the nav, playlists view, playlist header, home carousel and command palette from one edit, and never renders on Velora or local. Same pass, closed the matching gap in `SubsonicProvider.createPlaylist()`, which took no `isPublic` despite `IMusicProvider` offering it; it now forwards the flag **only when the caller passes one**, leaving the server's own default for new playlists intact rather than guessing. i18n `contextMenu.playlist.{makePublic,makePrivate}` + `playlist.visibilityFailed` ×6. **Watch out:** Velora's `isPublic` is an unrelated field meaning "this is a Velora-curated playlist" (`veloraProvider.mapPlaylist` sets it from `dto.source === "velora"`), which is why `VeloraProvider.updatePlaylist` throws `UNSUPPORTED` on it and the capability is false there. Don't unify the two.

## 16. Command Palette
**Closed 2026-07-19**, the two deferred verbs were dropped, not deferred again: `speed:1.25` (conflicts with `SPECIAL_MODE_RATE`, which owns `playbackRate` for slowed/nightcore) and `queue:clear` (would need a `clear` in the `PlaybackCommand` union, touching the controller protocol + both controllers). Don't re-add either without a deliberate design decision.

Implemented 2026-06-19, global `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` overlay, centered modal (PowerToys-Run-style), single always-focused input with virtual keyboard selection (Up/Down/Enter/Esc), mouse hover syncs the same selection.
- **Toggle is now a remappable keybind (2026-06-21).** `serializeKeybind()` (`src/utils/keybind.ts`) collapses `ctrlKey`/`metaKey` into a single `"Ctrl"` token, so a binding recorded on one platform (Cmd on Mac, Ctrl elsewhere) matches the other; added `toggleCommandPalette` (default `Ctrl+K`) to `KEYBIND_ACTIONS`/`useKeybindDispatch.ts`, removed the old hardcoded chord check from `useGlobalShortcuts.ts`. The "fires even while typing" behavior generalized rather than special-cased: any binding held with Ctrl/Cmd bypasses the editable-target guard (chords aren't printable text), plain keys still don't.
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/keybind.ts`, `src/utils/keybindActions.ts`, `src/utils/useGlobalShortcuts.ts`, `src/utils/useKeybindDispatch.ts`, `src/screens/views/settingsView/settingsBox/keybindsSection/KeybindsSection.tsx`
- Shared dispatcher, the keybind action `switch` was extracted from `useGlobalShortcuts.ts` into `src/utils/useKeybindDispatch.ts` so the palette's playback-action rows and the keyboard listener never drift apart.
- Sections: **Pages** (Home/Tracks/Favorites/Playlists/Albums/Artists/Recently Listened/Settings, + Stats gated on `userStats`) and **Actions** (play/pause, prev/next, shuffle, repeat, favorite, open Now Playing, via `useKeybindDispatch`) always show, filtered by query text; **Playlists/Artists/Albums/Tracks** search results (via `musicService.search()` + `parseSearchQuery`, same `genre:`/`bpm:` filters as the Home search bar) and an **"In `<playlist>`"** section (when the route is `/playlist/:id`) only show once there's a query.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx` (+ `.css`), mounted in `mainPage.tsx`
  - ↳ seam: `musicService`/`playbackService` only; capability-gated via `useCapability`, never provider identity
- Scoped out of v1: "open playlist settings" (no target UI exists yet, see §2); a full-screen mobile sheet form was considered and dropped, the centered modal reads fine on mobile as-is (see §18's command-palette entry point note).
- New shared utilities pulled out along the way: `trackMatchesText()` (searchQuery.ts) and `usePlaylistDetail()` (utils/), also used to de-duplicate `playlistView.tsx`'s own playlist-resolution/filter logic.
- **Expanded 2026-06-20**: Actions section grew to cover most of the always-on controls: toggle sidebar/topbar, volume up/down, toggle mute, seek ±10s, and log out (all via `useKeybindDispatch`/`useSettings`, logout via new shared `useLogout()` hook also now used by `nav.tsx`, replacing its inlined teardown).
- Added search-gated **switcher actions**, "Switch to `<mode>` mode" / "`<theme>` theme" / "`<language>`" for every BigMusic mode, theme, and language. Only appear once the user types a query (would otherwise bury the always-on actions above in ~19 extra rows); typing matches against the rendered title same as other rows.
  - ↳ files: shared option lists now live next to their owning state, `THEME_OPTIONS` (`src/settings.tsx`) and `LANGUAGE_OPTIONS` (`src/i18n.ts`), and are consumed by both `settingsView.tsx` (refactored off inline option arrays) and `commandPalette.tsx`, so adding a theme/language only means updating one list.
- **BigMusic visibility fix** that motivated the switcher actions: picking a page/playlist/artist/album from the palette now closes BigMusic first (`goTo()` helper calls `useBigMusic.setActive(false)` before `navigate()`) since the overlay sits above routed views and previously hid the destination; conversely, picking a BigMusic-mode switcher action opens BigMusic (`setActive(true)`) so the new mode is actually visible.
- **Inline value commands (2026-06-20)**: typing `vol:<0-100>` or `seek:<seconds>`/`seek:<m:ss>` (e.g. `vol:20`, `seek:1:30`) is parsed as a single command (`set volume to 20%` / `seek to 1:30`) that renders as its own pinned **Command** section at the top of the list, auto-selected, so Enter runs it immediately; library search is skipped entirely while a value command matches (no pointless network call). `seek:` is disabled with no current track, and clamps to the track's duration.
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/valueCommand.ts` (new, `parseValueCommand()`, kept separate from `searchQuery.ts`'s `genre:`/`bpm:` result filters since this runs one action instead of filtering); `commandPalette.tsx` (`valueCommandItem` + pinned `command` section)
  - ↳ seam: `audioEngine.setVolume()` for `vol:`; `playbackService.sendCommand({ command: "seek", seconds })` for `seek:`
- **"Upload Music" page entry (2026-06-21).** Added to the **Pages** section (it's a real route, `/upload`, see §2), gated `canUpload ? [...] : []` same as the other conditional rows; `run` just navigates via the shared `goTo()` helper.
- **Mobile entry point (2026-06-21).** No way to open the palette on mobile at all (`Ctrl`/`Cmd`+K is keyboard-only), fixed via a long-press on the mobile tab bar's Search tab (`MobileTabBar.tsx`) calling `useCommandPalette.toggle()`. See §18.
- **Background switcher command (2026-07-09).** Added a search-gated "Switch to `<background>` background" row per background style, mirroring the theme/language switchers. Extracted the 9-item list into a shared `BACKGROUND_OPTIONS` (`src/settings.tsx`, next to `THEME_OPTIONS`) consumed by both `settingsView.tsx` (replacing its inline option array) and `commandPalette.tsx`. i18n `commandPalette.actions.switchBackground` in all 6 locales. Seam: `useSettings.setBackgroundStyle`, no new store logic.
- **B: Action panel on the highlighted row (2026-07-15).** `Tab` or `→` (from the end of the query) on a track / playlist / album / artist result opens a per-row sub-action panel; `Shift+Tab`, `←` (from the start), `Esc`, or a `›` chevron (mouse) back out. The panel is built lazily from the row's own context menu, the old `flattenPlaylistMenu` was generalized to `flattenMenu(entries, { keepOpen, idPrefix, prefix })` and now also flattens `buildTrackMenuEntries` / `buildAlbumMenuEntries` / `buildArtistMenuEntries` (plus a "Play" row using `playFromPalette`'s addNext+jump, and a "Go to artist" nav row where an artist id exists). Sub-actions carry `keepOpen`: playback/library/toggle rows run without dismissing the palette (chaining) and rebuild the panel via the retained `builder()` so favorite/rating/pin labels reflect the just-toggled state (activeIndex clamped on rebuild); nav rows and modal-opening rows (`MODAL_ENTRY_IDS`: edit-info/delete/new-playlist) omit it and close, the palette is `z-overlay` and would otherwise occlude a `z-modal` dialog and swallow its Escape. State: `subPanel` (`{title, builder, items}`) cleared on open-edge and on query change; Escape capture listener backs out one level before closing; Tab traps focus in the input while a panel is open. Keyboard-first; the `›` chevron is the pointer equivalent and stays visible with a 44px tap target on touch (`@media (hover: none)`). i18n `commandPalette.subActions.goToArtist` + `hints.actions`/`hints.back` in all 6 locales.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx` (+ `.css`); reuses `src/utils/trackMenu.ts` / `playlistMenu.ts` / `mediaMenu.ts`
- **A: Fuzzy match + frecency ranking (2026-07-15).** Fuzzy matching landed first, pages/actions/switchers + playlist-management sections filter via `fuzzyMatches` (the subsequence scorer shared with Settings search, `src/utils/fuzzyMatch.ts`) instead of `.includes()`, so "tgltp" → Toggle Topbar, "exm3u" → Manage X: Export: M3U. Frecency ranking then floats a user's most-used commands to the top: new persisted `usePaletteFrecency` store (`src/store/paletteFrecency.ts`, localStorage `velora-palette-frecency`, exposes `clear()`) records each activation with a `{count, lastUsed}` entry; `frecencyScore = count × 0.5^(age / 14d)` (frequency discounted by recency) drives a stable `sortByFrecency` applied to the **pages / actions / playlist-manage** sections only, search-result sections keep their relevance/library order. Untouched palette looks identical (all scores 0 → original order preserved). Recorded on both `activate` and `activateSub` (feeds §16 C+D recents later); entries capped (prune to top 200 once past 300) so localStorage stays lean. Deliberately not wired into logout (device-preference-like, same as `useSettings`/`useLicense`).
  - ↳ files: `src/store/paletteFrecency.ts` (new), `src/assets/components/ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx`
- **C+D: Scope prefixes + recents/history (2026-07-15).** Leading-char scope prefixes restrict which sections render: `>` commands (actions + switchers + Manage), `@` tracks (search tracks + in-playlist), `#` library (playlists/albums/artists), `?` help. Pure `parsePaletteScope(query) → {scope, text}` helper strips the prefix and feeds the remainder into the existing `parseSearchQuery`/`parseValueCommand`/`fuzzyMatches` flow; the `sections` useMemo gates each section off `scope` (unscoped keeps prior behavior). Under `>` the theme/language/mode/background switchers (previously query-gated) are always reachable, e.g. `>theme aurora`; backend search is skipped in commands/help scope (`wantsSearch`). **Empty-query recents:** _removed 2026-07-19_, the "Recent" section (recently played tracks + recently visited pages), its `getUserStats` fetch, the `usePaletteRecents.routes`/`recordRoute` half and the `mainPage.tsx` route recording, and the `commandPalette.sections.recent` key are all gone; the palette's empty state is pages/actions again. `pageDefs` (path-carrying) stays. **`?` cheatsheet:** static rows for the four prefixes + `vol:`/`seek:`/`sleep:` value commands + a switchers hint + a keyboard-hint row; prefix/value rows drill in by filling the input (`keepOpen`, so activating doesn't dismiss). **Last-command recall:** `activate` records the query that ran a real command into `usePaletteRecents.lastCommand`; `ArrowUp` on an empty input recalls it. `activate` gained a `keepOpen` check (generalized from `activateSub`) so help drill-in rows chain without closing. `usePaletteRecents` (`src/store/paletteRecents.ts`, localStorage `velora-palette-recents`, exposes `clear()`) records routes app-wide from `mainPage.tsx`'s existing location effect (alongside `lastRoute`). i18n `commandPalette.sections.recent`/`.help` + `commandPalette.help.*` in all 6 locales.
  - ↳ files: `src/store/paletteRecents.ts` (new), `src/assets/components/ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx`, `src/screens/pages/mainPage/mainPage.tsx`
- **E: Command DSL expansion, three new verbs (2026-07-15).** Grew the `vol:`/`seek:`/`sleep:` mini-language in `src/utils/valueCommand.ts` (additive union members + parse branches, still returns `null` for unrecognized so search falls through): **`rate:N`** (0–5, `rate:0` clears) sets the current track's star rating via the `useRating` store, disabled when there's no current track or `trackRating` is unsupported (Subsonic-only); **`eq:BAND±N`** (`eq:bass+3`, `eq:treble-2`, `eq:mid+1`; aliases bass/low→low, mid/mids→mid, treble/high/highs→high) reads the current band off `audioEngine.getSettings().eq`, applies `current+delta` clamped to ±12 dB, and writes only that band via `audioEngine.setEq(Partial)`; **jump-to-setting**, a bare recognized setting name (`crossfade`, `eq`/`equalizer`, `theme`, `language`/`lang`, `quality`, `normalization`/`normalize`) renders a pinned command row that navigates to `/settings#setting-<anchor>`. The anchor mechanism: `SettingLine`'s `Base` type gained an optional `anchor` rendered as `id="setting-<anchor>"` on the row; six `buildSections` controls carry one (theme anchored on the always-visible auto-theme toggle since the switcher hides under auto-theme); `settingsView`'s existing `#about-section` scroll effect was generalized to scroll to any hashed id on `location.hash` change (reacts within /settings without a remount, `behavior` respects `data-reduce-motion`). Help cheatsheet (`?`) gained rate/eq/jump rows. i18n `commandPalette.actions.ratingSet`/`ratingClear`/`eqAdjust`/`jumpToSetting` + `commandPalette.eqBands.*` + `commandPalette.settingAnchors.*` + `commandPalette.help.rate`/`eq`/`jumpSetting` in all 6 locales. **Deferred:** `speed:` (playbackRate is owned by `SPECIAL_MODE_RATE` slowed/nightcore modes, a free-rate verb needs a design decision) and `queue:clear` (no `clear` command in the `PlaybackCommand` union, touches the controller protocol + both controllers).
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/valueCommand.ts`, `src/assets/components/ui/commandPalette/commandPalette.tsx`, `src/screens/views/settingsView/settingsView.tsx`, `src/screens/views/settingsView/settingsBox/SettingLine/SettingLine.tsx`
  - ↳ seam: `useRating`/`useCapability("trackRating")` for `rate:`; `audioEngine.setEq` for `eq:`; hash + `id` anchor for jump-to-setting

- **Play-from-palette must not wipe the queue (2026-07-14).** `playFromPalette(trackId, seedQueue)` helper: with a current track it `addNext([id])` then `playIndex` on the returned state's `queueIndex + 1` (reads the index off the awaited command result, correct after the controller inserts, no stale closure); an empty queue falls back to the caller's `setQueue` seed. Wired into `trackResults` + `inPlaylistResults`.
- **"Open playlist settings" command (2026-07-14).** No separate playlist-settings panel exists, so a playlist's settings surface is its context menu; the palette flattens `buildPlaylistMenuEntries`/`buildFavoritesMenuEntries` into a "Manage {name}" section shown while viewing a playlist (rename, pin, export/import, delete, play/shuffle/next), searchable + query-filtered like the pages/actions sections.
- **Actions outrank pages while typing (2026-08-04).** Section order is now query-dependent: with a query it's Actions → Pages → Manage, empty it stays Pages → Manage → Actions. Typing a word is asking for a verb, so "play" reaches play/pause before the Playlists page or a playlist named the same, and the top row is what Enter runs. Applies to the desktop overlay for free, it draws the order it's handed.
- **Desktop overlay window (2026-08-04).** A global `toggleCommandPalette` chord no longer raises Velora: while the app isn't the focused window, main opens the palette as its own always-on-top window on the display the cursor is on, over a game or whatever else is in front. Dismisses on Escape, on blur (clicking back into the game) and on activating a row, and a row only pulls the app forward when it needs it, navigation, a dialog, or a command whose own `focusesWindow` says so; play/volume/favorite stay headless. Settings → Integrations → "Palette over other apps" (`paletteOverlay`, default on) opts out, and the flag rides the existing `setGlobalShortcuts` spec (`overlay`) rather than a second IPC, so it can't race registration.
  - **The split that makes it work:** the palette keeps running in the main window and publishes a serialized snapshot (rows, section titles, pre-translated labels, theme class + `:root`'s inline style + `data-*` attributes so the overlay inherits the live accent, density, text scale and durations); the overlay sends back a row id and the main window runs the real closure. A second renderer booting the app would carry its own session, i18n, audio engine and, under `ClientPlaybackController`, its own queue, and nearly every palette action mutates main-window state. Covers travel as data urls keyed by an opaque id (a Subsonic cover url carries credentials), sent once per key rather than in every snapshot; `resolveCoverUrl` was added to `useBlobUrl.ts` as the non-hook half of the existing cache.
  - The overlay owns only its input text and its cursor, so typing and arrowing never round-trip; `cursorKey` tells it when the list is a new list rather than the same one rebuilt.
  - **Now-playing strip along the bottom**, cover + title/artist + prev/play/next + favorite (favorite carries the accent chip while it's on, the momentary three never do), since skipping or hearting the current track is the most common reason to open this over a game and it shouldn't need a search. Its own `transport` message runs through the palette's `dispatch` and deliberately doesn't dismiss, so the palette you just opened survives a skip. The accepted set is closed to those four commands, never an arbitrary command string. Shuffle and repeat were built and then cut back out, so the strip stays a glance rather than a second player.
  - Blur is the OS window material (acrylic on Windows, vibrancy on macOS), because a CSS `backdrop-filter` samples only its own document and would blur nothing over a game. Elsewhere the window is transparent and the card's own tint carries the contrast (`html.paletteOverlayBlurred`).
  - ↳ files: `src/utils/paletteOverlay.ts` (new host + protocol), `src/overlay/` (new: entry, view, bridge, css), `src/main.tsx` + `src/appBoot.tsx` (hash branch), `electron/main.ts` (`createOverlayWindow`/`openPaletteOverlay`/relay), `electron/preloadOverlay.cts` (new narrow bridge), `commandPalette.tsx` (`remote` mode + `focusesApp` tags), `store/commandPalette.ts`, `useGlobalShortcuts.ts`, `settings.tsx`
  - ↳ tests: `tests/utils/paletteOverlay.test.ts` (message normalization, row lookup, the focus decision, mode follow)
  - Known limit: draws over borderless-fullscreen games (what most use), never over exclusive fullscreen, no window can. A custom theme's raw CSS doesn't travel; the overlay falls back to the built-in tokens.
