2026-06-20: the 4 local-only no-ops (Default View, Disable Visualization, Discord Rich Presence, Large Text) were removed rather than wired, see §4/§6.

2026-06-21: the Keybind recorder (14 actions + reset) sits outside this table, same as Admin, it's a standalone `KeybindsSection` block below the mapped sections, not a row in `sections`. All 14 wired; collapsed by default and hidden on mobile (see §6/§18).

2026-08-04: The animated-icons cherry-pick is a preview grid instead of 13 toggle rows. Expanding it renders one tile per icon that mounts the **real** component (`SettingLine/settingsTypes/iconAnimationPicker/`, a new `iconAnimations` SettingItem type that is a full-width block rather than a label/control row), so a tile shows the thing it is about to turn on, and clicking it both flips the setting and plays the animation. Three replay shapes, because the icons have three kinds of trigger: the click-driven ones (favorite, shuffle, sidebar, waveform, repeat, skip, play/pause, volume) are replayed by clicking the rendered button through a ref, deferred out of the effect because dispatching a discrete event while React is flushing the commit throws inside the reconciler; the nav glyphs animate off a one-shot CSS class, so they remount on the tick; the nav pin's animation *is* its enter/exit, so the preview lifts it out and lets it thunk back, on a gap that scales with the animation-speed setting and is skipped under reduce-motion (nothing to replay when the pin is static). The stage inside a tile is `inert`, which keeps the real button out of the tab order and out of the tile's accessible name while still letting the programmatic replay reach it, and it stops its own click from bubbling back into the tile handler (that would toggle the setting again, forever). The tile is the control: `role="switch"` + `aria-checked`, Enter/Space. Groups come from `ICON_ANIMATIONS[].group` through a `Record<IconAnimationGroup, string>`, so adding a group is a compile error here rather than a group of icons silently missing from the picker, and the preset switcher moved into the block's head. `SettingLine`'s `description` is optional as of this (the block labels itself). i18n `settings.iconAnimations.groups.{player,nav}` ×9, `customize`/`customizeDesc`/`showButton` reworded, `iconDesc` dropped.

2026-08-04: Appearance copy pass, 35 strings rewritten in all 9 locales. The one inverted toggle in the app ("Disable background", on = no background) is now "Animated background" and reads positively (key renamed `performance.disableBackground` → `.background`). Jargon out of the descriptions (renderer, internal render resolution, UI float states, full-bleed, welcome flow); Float is "Floating panels" with Floating / Edge to edge. The five look-alike indicator rows moved under their own **Indicators** subheader as `Sidebar: …` / `Song list: …`, so the favorites-cover and first-run-tour rows now close out Interface.

## 18. Mobile Support

**Foundations (MF1/MF2/MF3), 2026-06-20.** The shared groundwork that unblocked every
per-surface mobile retrofit below. Scope was deliberately the three foundation items only;
Nav/Player kept their desktop internals at this point (separate tickets, done further below).
- **MF1, breakpoint hook + Sheet primitive.** `src/utils/useBreakpoint.ts`: `useMediaQuery` (generic), `useIsMobile` (single source of truth for `< md` = 768px), `useBreakpoint` (`xs`–`xl` tier), `BREAKPOINTS` const mirroring docs/designsystemV2.md §12.2. New `primitives/sheet/Sheet.tsx` + `sheet.css`, presentational bottom sheet (`{open, onClose, children, className?}`), portals to `document.body`, `.uiContentContainer` panel (top-rounded, drag-handle, internal scroll, `max-height:85dvh`), `z-modal`. Slide via `motion` drag-to-dismiss; backdrop-click + Escape close; reduce-motion collapses to instant (gated on `useSettings.reduceMotion`, same pattern as `toast.tsx`).
- **MF2, mobile shell branch.** `buildGrid.ts` gains `buildMobileGrid(topbarVisible)`, single column `[topbar?] / views 1fr / player auto / nav calc(60px + safe-bottom)`, ignoring nav/player/sidebar position prefs (mobile overrides arrangement, not prefs). `mainPage.tsx` picks it via `useIsMobile()`; sidebar becomes a `Sheet` (driven by `sidebar.sidebarVisible`) except while BigMusic is open (`!bigMusicActive` guard, Sidebar self-portals into the overlay there, same as desktop). `mainApp_container--mobile` zeroes float gap/padding for a full-bleed shell + applies `--safe-top/left/right`. Desktop path untouched (provably pixel-identical). Side effect: the Sidebar per-surface ticket is resolved.
- **MF3, viewport + safe-area tokens.** `index.html` viewport now `viewport-fit=cover`. `index.css :root` adds `--safe-top/bottom/left/right` (= `env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)`); existing raw `env()` call sites (toast, splashScreen, dropdown, commandPalette ×3) migrated onto the tokens (behavior-neutral). `100vh`/`100dvh` audit: already clean (full-page containers all `100dvh/100dvw`; remaining raw `vh/vw` are proportional sizing inside `clamp()`/`min()`, not jank risks).
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean (only pre-existing warnings, none in new files).

**Per-surface mobile sweep, 2026-06-20.** Built on the foundations above.
- **Nav → bottom tab bar** (`nav.tsx` + `nav/MobileTabBar.tsx`): Home/Search/Tracks/Library/Settings, `useLocation` active state, ≥44px, safe-bottom.
- **New Library screen** (`screens/views/libraryView/` + `/library` route): `Tabs` (Playlists/Albums/Artists) reusing the existing grid views via a new `embedded` prop that hides their own header; Library header owns the title + "+ New playlist". Logout moved to a mobile-only Settings row (`useLogout`). Reuses `main.playlist/albums/artists` strings (no new tab keys).
- **Player → mini-player** (`player.tsx`): compact cover/title/play-pause/next + progress line; tap/swipe-up → BigMusic (shared `layoutId`); volume/EQ/toggles dropped on mobile. New `player.*` aria keys ×6 locales.
- **BigMusic gestures** (`bigMusic.tsx` + modes): swipe-down dismiss, swipe-between-modes (wrap), coarse-pointer ≥44px, mode safe-area insets, idle cursor-hide off on touch.
- **BigMusic per-mode reflow** (`modes/*/**.css`, additive `@media (max-width: 767px)`): bigCover drops its 340px min-width (was overflowing 360px) → fluid card; vinyl stacks disc over a centered info panel with reduced padding; editorial collapses its 42/58 two-column spread to a cover band + text panel (border-top instead of border-left, downward vignette, smaller title); continuum grows the centre cover + tightens spread; polaroidWall shrinks hero/snapshots; lyrics widens the text column (74vw so the ~1.22× active-line scale doesn't clip against the stage's overflow:hidden) + tightens gutters. Desktop ≥768px unchanged.
- **BigMusic mobile controls + gesture fixes** (follow-up, 2026-06-20):
  - **Swipe-to-dismiss reliability** (`bigMusic.tsx`): the close/step-mode *decision* now comes from the raw pointer delta on pointer-up (motion drag stays only as the visual finger-follow), instead of relying on motion's `onDragEnd` firing, which is why swipe-down often did nothing. Thresholds eased to 90px down / 80px side. Timeline (`.timelineContainer`, mouse-only, no touch scrub) added to the gesture opt-out so a horizontal drag on it doesn't switch modes; the synced lyric column removed from opt-out (it doesn't scroll, so a swipe there should dismiss).
  - **Shared mobile control stack** (`bigMusicTransport.tsx` `BigMusicMobileControls` + `bigMusic.css`): core transport (prev / big play / next) above the timeline, secondary (shuffle / repeat / favorite) below, native-player layout. Every mode swaps it in on `useIsMobile()` (desktop trio untouched in the `else`). Volume slider and the utility cluster (graphic-eq/eq/sidebar/video) are dropped on mobile (`UtilityButtons` returns null on mobile, matching the mini-player). bigCover hides its duplicate info-row favorite on mobile.
  - **Controls no longer idle-hide on mobile** (`lyrics.tsx`): `useIdleHide` gated to `!isMobile` (only the lyrics mode auto-hid its footer).
  - **`touch-action: none` on the overlay** (`bigMusic.css`, 2026-06-20): the real reason swipe-down still did nothing, with the default `touch-action: auto` the browser claimed a vertical drag as a scroll and fired `pointercancel` (not `pointerup`), so the raw-pointer-delta commit above never ran. Scrollable plain-lyrics columns re-enable `touch-action: pan-y` (`lyrics.css`/`editorial.css`); `.bmCntStage` already owned `touch-action: none`.
- **Views reflow**: `@media` mobile rules across the routed views + `SettingLine` (label-over-control); carousels/`tracksView`/`statsView` already fine.
- **Dropdown → Sheet** (`dropdown.tsx`): mobile menus use the shared `Sheet` with stack-based submenus; desktop path untouched.
- **Global touch polish**: `.buttonIcon` ≥44px on `(pointer: coarse)`, `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent`.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings).

**Mobile review fixes, 2026-06-21.** Three bugs from a recall code-review of the mobile sweep:
- **Sidebar sheet auto-opened + couldn't reopen** (`settings.tsx`, `mainPage.tsx`, `player.tsx`, `sidebar.tsx`): the sheet was driven by the persisted desktop `sidebarVisible` (default `true`), so it force-opened on every mobile launch and, once dismissed, no mobile control could set it back. Added an ephemeral, non-persisted `sidebar.mobileSidebarOpen` flag (default closed) to drive the sheet; a new Queue button in the mini-player opens it; `Sidebar` gained an `embedded` prop that disables the docked slide-out class (which would otherwise hide the content inside the sheet). Desktop `sidebarVisible` (docked grid) untouched.
- **Timeline had no touch scrub** (`timeline.tsx`, `timeline.css`): it was mouse-only (`onMouseDown` + document `mousemove/up`), so drag-to-seek didn't work by touch, the only seek control in BigMusic on mobile. Converted to pointer events (`onPointerDown` + document `pointermove/up/cancel`) and added `touch-action: none` to `.timelineContainer`.
- **Mini-player swipe-up could be stolen by the browser** (`player.css`): `.miniPlayer` had `touch-action: pan-y` while being a `motion` `drag="y"` target; switched to `touch-action: none` (matches the BigMusic overlay) so the swipe-up-to-expand commits.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean on touched files.

**Login page 360px audit, 2026-06-21.** Fixed three real mobile bugs under the existing `@media (max-width: 900px)` block in `loginPage.tsx`/`.css`: (1) `.login_container` was `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden` with no way to scroll, so once the on-screen keyboard covered the form there was no path to the submit button, switched to `min-height: 100dvh` + `overflow-y: auto` on mobile. (2) input font-size was `.95rem` (~15px), under the 16px floor that stops iOS Safari from zooming the page on focus, bumped to `1rem`. (3) `.loginPasswordToggle`/`.loginProvider` tap targets were well under 44px, grown via `@media (pointer: coarse)` (glyph unchanged), matching the `.buttonIcon` pattern. Also added missing `--safe-*` inset padding to `.login_container`/`.loginTopBar` and mobile-appropriate `inputMode`/`autoCapitalize`/`autoCorrect`/`spellCheck` on the server-URL and username fields. Verified via `tsc`/`eslint` clean; **not** visually verified in a real browser viewport, worth a manual pass on a real device before considering this fully closed.

**Mobile player-controls rebalance, 2026-06-21.** The mini-player and BigMusic's mobile control stack had drifted: the mini-player carried Skip-Next + a Queue button, while BigMusic's `UtilityButtons` (graphic-eq/equalizer/sidebar/video) returned `null` on mobile entirely, desktop's `playerControls` button set wasn't actually reachable on mobile at all. Rebalanced: (1) `UtilityButtons` no longer early-returns on mobile; its sidebar button now reads `isMobile` to show a Queue icon calling a new `ctx.onOpenQueue` (opens the mobile sheet via `useSettings().sidebar.setMobileSidebarOpen`) instead of the desktop-only `onToggleSidebar`/`sidebarVisible` dock toggle. (2) `BigMusicMobileControls` (`bigMusicTransport.tsx`) renders `<UtilityButtons>` in a new `.bmMobileUtility` row (own `flex-wrap` + tighter gap than `.bmMobileSecondary`, since up to 4 icons no longer fit the 40px-gap row sized for 3). (3) `player.tsx`'s mini-player swaps Skip-Next for the Favorite/heart toggle (matches the desktop bar) and drops the Queue button now that it lives in BigMusic, skip-to-next is reachable only via BigMusic going forward, by design. Considered swapping the centered desktop modal for a full-screen sheet on mobile; decided against it after seeing it live, the centered modal reads fine on mobile as-is. See §16.

**Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts hidden on mobile, 2026-06-21.** `KeybindsSection` returns `null` on `useIsMobile()`, recording a chord assumes a physical keyboard, which mobile doesn't have. See §6.

- **BigMusic's mobile Queue button was dead-wired, and the panel it pointed at had no way to close.** It called a new `ctx.onOpenQueue` → `setMobileSidebarOpen(true)`, but that flag's only consumer (the `<Sheet>` in `mainPage.tsx`) is unmounted specifically while BigMusic is active, and this button only ever renders inside BigMusic. Dropped the now-fully-unused `sidebar.mobileSidebarOpen`/`setMobileSidebarOpen` from `useSettings` and the `embedded` prop from `Sidebar`.

**Mobile sidebar (Queue/Lyrics/Info) as a Sheet, 2026-07-06.** Real mobile presentation for the panel removed above. `Sidebar` now branches on `useIsMobile()`: mobile renders the shared tab header + view content inside a `Sheet` (dedupe'd desktop/mobile tabs into a `SidebarTabs` helper); desktop keeps its docked-panel/BigMusic-portal logic unchanged. Entry point is the sidebar icon in BigMusic's `UtilityButtons` (the only place it was ever reachable on mobile), on mobile it toggles a new ephemeral `mobileSidebarOpen` flag on `useBigMusic` (not persisted, same reasoning as `active`/`overlayEl`) instead of the desktop `sidebarVisible` setting. `mainPage.tsx` now mounts `<Sidebar/>` unconditionally (its mobile branch portals via `Sheet` regardless of grid placement).

Gave `Sheet` an opt-in `zIndex` prop (`store/bigMusic.ts` exports `ABOVE_BIG_MUSIC_Z = 9500`), used only by this sheet, so every other `Sheet` consumer (dropdowns, upload overlay) is unaffected. Threaded the same escape hatch through `Dropdown` (both its mobile-Sheet and desktop-portal paths) and wired `QueueView`'s track context menu to use it whenever `bigMusicActive`, otherwise long-pressing a queued track inside the new sheet (or right-clicking one in the desktop-docked panel while BigMusic is open, a pre-existing but previously-unnoticed instance of the same bug) would itself render invisibly beneath the sheet/overlay. The broader issue (every other `z-overlay`/`z-modal` consumer, toast, `ConfirmDialog`, command palette, etc., also renders behind BigMusic) is unpatched; tracked as a new bug in §12.

- Verified: `tsc -b && vite build` clean; `eslint` 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings, none in touched files).

**Track-row swipe actions + pull-to-refresh (2026-07-15).** The two remaining `docs/mobile-improvements.md` code items (#3/#4), both mobile-only (`useIsMobile()`); desktop and reduce-motion render the rows untouched.
- **Swipe actions:** new `primitives/swipeableRow/SwipeableRow.tsx` (+ `.css`), a `motion` `drag="x"` wrapper (`dragDirectionLock` + `touch-action: pan-y` so it never fights vertical scroll) that reveals an accent action layer arming via `useTransform` on the drag offset (input ranges kept monotonically increasing, so the right side maps `[-COMMIT,0]`). Swipe right adds to queue (`playbackService.sendCommand({command:"addToQueue"})`), swipe left toggles favorite (`useSession.toggleFavorite`); commit on distance (72px) or velocity (500px/s), `navigator.vibrate?.(10)` on commit, `dragSnapToOrigin` back. Off in select mode, on desktop, and under reduce-motion (returns `<>{children}</>`, so no motion mounts and the same actions stay reachable via long-press). Wraps `Track` in `playlist.tsx` list mode only (grid cards unchanged), covering TracksView, PlaylistView, and search. Reuses the existing `contextMenu.track.*` labels (no new action strings). Long-press context menu and tap-to-play still fire (motion only suppresses the click after an actual drag); row height is unchanged so the manual virtualizer math is untouched.
- **Pull-to-refresh:** new `utils/usePullToRefresh.ts` hook + `primitives/pullToRefresh/PullIndicator.tsx` (+ `.css`). Non-passive touch listeners on the scroll container arm only at `scrollTop<=0` and after winning the vertical axis (`preventDefault` while pulling), damped travel (0.5x, cap 120px), 64px threshold, min 600ms spinner. Wired into `playlist.tsx`'s `.playlistTracksContainer` (now `position: relative` to anchor the descending indicator): fetchMore lists reset to the first page (`loadMore` now returns its promise); static lists take an optional `onRefresh` prop (PlaylistView passes a forced `loadPlaylist(id, true)` / `loadFavorites(true)`, since an unforced reload short-circuits on the cached playlist). Spinner honors reduce-motion (no spin). New `pullToRefresh.refreshing` aria key ×6 locales.
- Scope: core track lists only (Queue / RecentlyListened / Home deferred; the primitive and hook are reusable when wanted). Verified `tsc -b` + `eslint` clean on touched files (`playlist.tsx` keeps its one pre-existing `exhaustive-deps` warning).

**Mobile tab bar rework, 2026-09-12.** The bar shipped in the 2026-06-20 sweep as five icon
buttons and had not been touched since, so it was the one piece of chrome outside the app's own
vocabulary. Eight changes, in `nav/MobileTabBar.tsx` (rewritten), the new `nav/MobileNavStatus.tsx`,
`nav.css`, `button.css`, `Button.tsx`, `buildGrid.ts`, `utils/haptics.ts` (new) and
`utils/iconAnimations.ts`:
- **A tab now speaks for its whole neighbourhood.** Active state matched only the five tab paths,
  so opening a playlist, an album, an artist or the stats page left every tab dark, which reads as
  "you are nowhere". `OWNED` maps each tab to the routes it owns (both `/playlist` and `/playlists`:
  the second is not under the first) and `tabForPath` resolves the lit one.
- **The active mark is the one the desktop rows wear.** It was opacity plus an accent text colour;
  it is now a mark driven by `navActiveStyle` (`accent` / `ring` / `none`, with `cover` falling back
  to the accent the way a folded desktop row does), travelling between tabs as a single element via
  `layoutId` on the `notch` spring, so a tap is answered by a move and not by two crossfades. The
  glyph and label stay neutral at full opacity: accent-on-accent dropped under the contrast floor on
  the lighter themes.
- **The bar declares `data-style-target="nav"`**, so long-press-to-restyle reaches it. It was the one
  chrome region excluded, even though `nav` is explicitly not `desktopOnly` in `styleTargets.ts`.
- **The status line (`MobileNavStatus`).** An upload, an import, a sleep timer and a lost connection
  report themselves in the desktop nav footer, which the phone does not render, so none of the four
  had anywhere to appear (only a waiting update did, through `useMobileUpdateToast`). One line above
  the tabs, present only while there is something to say, showing the most urgent: a transient job
  outranks a standing one, which outranks the ambient network state. Upload taps through to the
  queue overlay, the sleep timer taps to cancel. Progress is a hairline that moves only when the job
  reports, never per frame. The mobile grid's nav row became `auto` (the bar owns its own minimum
  height) so the line can grow it.
- **Re-tap leads back, then scrolls to top.** A tap on a lit tab returns to the tab's own view when
  the route is one it merely owns (a playlist under Library), and scrolls to top once you are on it.
  The box is found the way the overlay scrollbar finds one (whichever is actually scrolled) rather
  than by threading a ref through every view.
- **Long-press rows per tab**, through the existing Dropdown, which is already a Sheet on mobile:
  Home to Recently Listened and Stats, Tracks to Favorites and Upload, Library straight to its
  sub-grids, Settings to Appearance / Audio / About. Search keeps the command palette it already
  opened. `openFromEvent` folds the restyle panel into the same menu, so the bar's new style target
  is reachable from the press that opens the rows.
- **A `navTab` Button variant** replaced eight `!important` overrides of `buttonIcon`, and a haptic
  tick (`utils/haptics.ts`, shared with `SwipeableRow`) plus the nav glyph animations now fire on
  tap; `search` and `library` joined `ICON_ANIMATIONS` so all five tabs animate rather than three.
- **Three real bugs at phone width:** the label was `nowrap` with no truncation, so "Einstellungen",
  "Configurações" and "Bibliothèque" collided at 360px (now a `clamp()` size with ellipsis as the
  safety net); only `--safe-bottom` was applied, so a notched phone in landscape clipped the outer
  tabs (`--safe-left/right` now too); and a landscape phone kept the full 60px bar, which now drops
  its labels and gives ~10px back while keeping the 44px targets.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (0 errors) and `npm run build` clean.

**Mobile review batch, 2026-09-13.** Five items out of a read-through of the whole mobile shell. The
review's other findings stayed open, see `goals.md` §18.
- **The queue is one gesture from the mini-player** (`ui/player/player.tsx`, `player.css`). It was
  four steps: mini-player, BigMusic, utility row, sheet, for one of the three actions a phone user
  reaches for most, because `mobileSidebarOpen` had exactly one control anywhere in the app
  (`utilityButtons.tsx`). A left swipe on the mini-player now opens the same sheet directly; the
  sheet never needed BigMusic, `Sidebar`'s mobile branch renders it off that flag alone and
  `mainPage` mounts `Sidebar` unconditionally. The whole mobile branch moved into its own
  `MiniPlayer` component so the desktop bar never creates the drag motion value, the gesture is
  two-axis with `dragDirectionLock` and elastic only on the two directions that do something, and an
  accent layer arms behind the card on the way out. That layer is literally the row swipe's:
  `SwipeableRow` now exports `SwipeActionLayer` (taking `icon`/`label` rather than a whole
  `SwipeAction`, since a layer never commits anything) plus `SWIPE_COMMIT` / `SWIPE_VELOCITY`, so
  the two gestures share one arming curve, one threshold pair and one stylesheet instead of the three
  copies the first pass wrote. Left elastic is the row's `0.7` for the same reason: the commit tests
  the raw offset while the layer tracks the elastic-damped `x`, so a lower value leaves the affordance
  visibly half-armed at the moment it fires. **`PanInfo` reports offset and velocity on both axes even while the lock only moves one**,
  so a diagonal flick satisfied both thresholds and opened BigMusic and the sheet at once: the axis
  is picked by offset dominance before either threshold is tested. BigMusic's utility row stays the
  visible-button equivalent, so the swipe is an accelerator and not a hidden-only affordance.
- **A list row carries its own overflow button on touch** (`primitives/track/track.tsx` + `.css`,
  `ui/playlist/playlist.{tsx,css}`, `contextMenu.trackActions` ×9 locales). Swipe covered queue and
  favorite; everything else (add to playlist, go to album, edit, delete) sat behind the native
  long-press `contextmenu` that iOS never reliably delivers, which designsystemV2 §14.6 forbids. New
  opt-in `menuButton` prop on `Track`, rendered only under `(pointer: coarse)` and only when the row
  has an `onContextMenu`, calling that same handler so there is one menu and the restyle row still
  rides along. **The grid template is untouched on purpose:** `.track` already reserves a trailing
  gutter (`--playlist-action-col`, there so the favorite column lines up under the header heart), the
  button is absolutely positioned into it, and the gutter widens to 44px under coarse only, where the
  column spine is `display: none` anyway. Both halves matter: the header row shares the row's
  template, and the row height is load bearing for the virtualizer's `startIndex`/`topPad` math.
  **Removed 2026-09-30 at Jenny's call**: the `⋮` cluttered mobile rows; long-press + swipe remain the touch paths, don't re-add it.
- **Touch inputs stopped zooming iOS Safari** (9 CSS files). Safari zooms the viewport whenever a
  focused input computes under 16px, and ten real text-entry selectors were under it, including the
  main search field (`.searchInputField__input`, .95rem), every settings input (`--text-control`,
  0.875rem) and the command palette (1.05rem, which the 90% text-scale setting drops to ~15.1px).
  Each gets `font-size: max(16px, <its own value>)` inside `@media (pointer: coarse)`, so desktop is
  byte-identical and a user who scales text *up* still gets the larger size; a flat `16px` would have
  fought the setting. The tokens themselves were left alone, they have non-input consumers. The name
  prompt (`namePromptModal.css`) already carried exactly this pattern; the login and activation pages
  carried a weaker one, a bare `1rem` gated on `(max-width: 767px)`, which the 90% text-scale setting
  drops to 14.4px, so both are on the real floor now. `.adminInput` is shared with the security
  section's password/TOTP fields, so its rule is unscoped rather than `.adminSection .adminInput`.
  Still open, flagged not fixed:
  `.hexFieldInput` and `.themeEditorNameInput` use `all: unset` with no font-size rule of their own,
  so there is nothing to point an override at without guessing the cascade.
- **The animated background starts cheap on a phone** (`utils/platform.ts`, `settings.tsx`). A phone
  got the same 30fps half-resolution shader as a 240Hz desktop, under the same blurred surface stack
  that goals.md's live traps measure as this app's dominant GPU cost. New `LOW_POWER_DEVICE` read
  once at module scope (`(pointer: coarse)`, or `hardwareConcurrency <= 4` guarded against a `0`
  reading; no user-agent sniffing) picks `15` / `quarter` as the **first-run default only**. No merge
  change was needed and that is the point: `merge(p, current)` already reads
  `p.backgroundFps ?? current.backgroundFps` with `current` being the fresh initializer, so a stored
  choice always wins and only a profile that never had the key picks the device tier up.
- **Fullscreen video controls stopped vanishing for good on touch**
  (`bigMusic/bigMusicVideo/bigMusicVideo.tsx`, `bigMusic/useIdleHide.ts`). In fullscreen the controls
  hid after 3s and the only thing that brought them back was `onMouseMove`, which never fires on a
  phone, so they were gone until the video was. Both timer-arming sites are now gated on
  `useIsMobile()`, plus an effect that unhides if a hide was scheduled just before the breakpoint was
  crossed. `useIdleHide` had the mirror bug: `if (!enabled) return` left a `hidden: true` stuck
  forever when the flag flipped mid-hide, so it resets now. Lyrics already passed `!isMobile`, and
  editorial's hide is a manual button whose reveal button survives it, so both were left alone.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint src` 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings), `npm run build`
  clean including `check:csp`. `vitest` has 5 failures that pre-date this work, proven by re-running
  them on a stashed tree; tracked in `goals.md` §18.

**The five tests failing since `19dd18f`, resolved 2026-09-13.** Decided per case, and in four of
the five the behaviour was the deliberate half.
- `buildGrid.test.ts` ×2 still expected the mobile nav row's old `calc(60px + var(--safe-bottom))`.
  `19dd18f` made it `auto` on purpose, so `MobileNavStatus` can grow the bar by a line and the 60px
  floor lives in `nav.css` where text scale and density can push past it. Expectations updated.
- `MobileTabBar.test.tsx` asserted Home lit at exactly `/home` and dark on a sub-route, which is
  what `OWNED` deliberately replaced: a tab speaks for a neighbourhood, and the bar going dark on a
  playlist reads as "you are nowhere". Rewritten to the real contract, Home lit across
  `/home` + `/recently-listened` + `/stats`, Library lit on `/playlist/123`, and a new case pinning
  the other half: a route no tab owns (`/dev`) leaves every tab dark.
- The icon pair (`descriptors.test.ts`, `pluginRegistry.test.ts`) was **not** a stale expectation and
  not a behaviour change: both were right, and `hostPluginIcon` is correct. They failed because they
  named `mdi:ghost` as "a name the app doesn't ship", and `src/generated/icons/` is gitignored build
  output that `scripts/fetch-icons.mjs` only ever adds to. `mdi:ghost` was referenced from `src/`
  once, so the file is still on disk for anyone who built then, `lookupIconSrc` resolves it, and the
  fallback correctly declines to fire. 21 such orphans are sitting there now. Both tests moved to a
  name no set has and assert `lookupIconSrc(UNSHIPPED)` is undefined first, so the premise fails
  loudly instead of the fallback looking broken. Not pruned in `fetch-icons.mjs` on purpose: a
  runtime-built name is a sanctioned hand-add (docs/designsystemV2.md §9), and a prune would delete
  it on the next build.
- Verified: `vitest` 194 files / 2296 passing (4 expected-fail), `eslint` 0 errors (6 pre-existing
  warnings), `npm run build` clean including `check:csp`.

- **Android tab bar sat behind the system nav buttons (2026-09-30).** `.uiContentContainer`'s padding loads after `nav.css` at equal specificity, so in the built app it replaced `.navTabBarContent`'s `var(--safe-bottom)` bottom padding with 12px: the bar grew by the inset (60 + 48px) while its buttons sat in the 48px behind Android's 3-button nav. Scoped the rule under `.navTabBar`. Measured on-device over DevTools (S23+, Android 16, WebView 153): Capacitor's insets were correct all along.

- **Hold play/pause in the mini-player to skip (2026-09-30).** The mini-player had no Next, so skipping meant opening BigMusic. A 500ms hold on its play button now sends `next` with a haptic tick (not on live streams); the release click is swallowed so it doesn't also toggle, and a 10px move cancels it so the card swipes still win. A white ring fills over the progress ring while held, then fades out once it skips. `utils/useLongPress.ts`, reusable for any button with a click, tested in `tests/utils/useLongPress.test.tsx`.

- **Three more small gestures (2026-09-30).** Double tap a BigMusic cover to favorite (mobile only since the same day; desktop keeps an instant single-click close): it only ever adds, like a like, and a big heart pops where the finger was at a random upright tilt (`HeartBurst` in `BigMusicHud.tsx`). Covers whose single tap closes the overlay wait out the 300ms double-tap window first (`utils/useDoubleTap.ts`, tested). A right swipe on the mini-player is Previous, mirroring the left swipe to the queue. Right-click or long-press any now-playing favorite (bar, mini-player, BigMusic) for an add-to-playlist menu (`buildAddTrackToPlaylistEntries` in `trackMenu.ts`).

- **Dock the mini-player into the tab bar (2026-10-02).** Swipe the mini-player down and it leaves its row; its cover, wearing the desktop bar's `CoverRing` (display-only when it has no `onSeek`), takes the Tracks tab's place with the song as its label. Tapping that tab brings the player back. Persisted as `player.mobileDocked`, read through `useMiniPlayerDock` (ignored with nothing loaded) so the player, the tab bar and `buildMobileGrid` (no player row while docked) never disagree.
- **Trial and storage on mobile (2026-10-02).** The desktop nav footer is the only place either showed, and the phone renders a tab bar instead, so a mobile user never saw when their trial ends. Both pills (`NavTrialBadge`, `NavStorageIndicator`, the latter still behind `showStorageUsage` + capability `storage`) now render unfolded at the top of the mobile Settings index. The dev-tools pill toggles also reach the mobile status line now, sharing `DEV_PILL_SAMPLES` with the desktop pills.
- **Plugins on mobile (2026-10-02).** Three plugin surfaces had no phone form. Plugin pages: a trailing "Plugins" tab on the Library view (drill-in rows, the mobile Settings index grammar, so nothing sits between a tab and its toolbar) and a "Plugins" group in the Library tab's long-press menu (both from `selectNavEntries`), and the Library tab owns `/p` so the bar stays lit on a plugin page. Nav widgets: mounted for good in `MobileNavStatus` and shown as a strip above the tabs, ranked below offline and above the trial notice; a tap hides one until its label changes. Player controls: in the BigMusic mobile row after the utility toggles. That row's fold moved from a fixed 310px container query to a measured one (44px per target), since the plugin count decides how much room it needs; folded, the toggles and plugin controls share the more menu. Both mobile sites run their frames through `useChromeSources` (one headless frame per entry, descriptors in declared order, 1.x plugins left out), tested in `tests/services/plugins/chrome/useChromeSources.test.tsx`. The mini-player still skips player controls.
- **Landscape phones and touch tablets (2026-10-02).** `useIsMobile` was width-only, so an 852x393 phone drew the desktop shell. Mobile is now `MOBILE_QUERY` (narrow, or coarse and at most 480px tall), repeated verbatim in every CSS phone query and held there by `tests/utils/shellQueries.test.ts`. A landscape phone gets the tab bar as a glyph rail down the left (`buildMobileGrid`'s `landscape`, `.mainApp_container--landscape` in `nav.css`) and BigMusic's mobile shell goes two-column with even padding and the close button top-right. A touch tablet in the 768 to 1023 band keeps the desktop grid, but the sidebar slides over the views (`buildGrid`'s `sidebarOverlay`, `sidebar.css`) instead of squeezing them to ~218px; a mouse keeps the docked column.
- **Flip to pause (2026-10-03).** Playback setting, off by default, phone only (`useIsPhone`: the mobile shell on a coarse pointer, so a narrowed desktop window never sees it). `useFlipToPause` reads `deviceorientation`: face down held 700ms pauses, face up resumes only what it paused. Runs only while the app is visible, since the WebView stops sensor events in the background; a native `SensorManager` version in `MediaPlaybackService` would lift that. Pose check in `tests/utils/flipToPause.test.ts`.
- **Better haptics (2026-10-03).** Every buzz went through `navigator.vibrate`, which the Android WebView ignores without a `VIBRATE` permission (the manifest has none), and which is a raw motor pulse besides. `VeloraHapticsPlugin` drives the motor instead, as media vibrations so Android's touch vibration switch doesn't mute them (the system's tuned tick and click on 29+); `navigator.vibrate` stays the fallback outside the app. New: ticks every 5% while scrubbing the seek bar, cover ring and volume (a tap at mute and full), per step on settings sliders (capped at 24) and per speed preset, and a held play button rumbles up to its skip (`hapticSwell`: a grainy rumble swelling from a whisper to full strength, starting 150ms in so a plain tap stays silent, then 30ms of silence and the `HIT`, a full-strength br with a decaying tail). Shaped buzzes drive the motor through the plugin's `waveform` (strength per 20ms slice, or closing-in on/off pulses on motors without strength control), which is why the manifest now carries `VIBRATE`. Ticks closer than 35ms are dropped. All behind Accessibility → Haptic feedback, off by default (it is the only gate, so turning it on is the opt-in), shown only where the device can vibrate. `createDetents` in `utils/haptics.ts`, tested in `tests/utils/haptics.test.ts`.
- **Pick which haptics play (2026-10-03).** Under the Haptic feedback toggle, a tile picker like the animated icons: every feel is a `HapticId` in the `HAPTICS` registry (`utils/haptics.ts`) and every call names one (`haptic(kind, id)`, `createDetents(count, id)`), so the check stays inside `haptics.ts`. `disabledHaptics` is a disabled-list, so a feel shipped later starts on; turning a tile on plays its `preview`. Presets Essential (the basics group: seek bar, sliders, taps, hold to skip) and All. Dev tools gained a "Phone settings" chip that shows the phone-only rows (flip to pause, haptics, the mobile speed button and floating player) on any screen.
- **Four more haptic feels (2026-10-03).** Two new picker groups, off under Essential: in `moments`, favorite (a soft "ba-dum" on favoriting from the heart button or BigMusic's cover double tap, one faint tick on unfavoriting or double tapping a song already liked) and shuffle (a dice rattle with gaps rolled once per press by `diceWave`, then a landing hit, only when shuffle turns on); in `feedback`, errors (a double buzz from `toast.ts`, error toasts only) and games (`hapticGame`: a rising pattern for a correct guess or a solved puzzle, a flat low buzz per wrong guess; skips, giving up and Unheard stay silent). Each shape keeps its strengths and timings as named constants at its top in `utils/haptics.ts`; the heart plays on the click, not the `active` flip, so the BigMusic HUD replay stays silent.
- **Lyrics on the lock screen (2026-10-03).** Settings → Integrations, under Media key support, off by default, Android shell only. The synced line being sung replaces the artist in the existing media session (lock screen, notification, Android 13+ media controls), back to the artist between lines and on tracks without synced lyrics. JS only: `useNativeMediaSession` arms one timer per line from the playhead, so the bridge is only called when the line changes.
- **Settings sorted by platform (2026-10-03).** Every row was checked against what it does on a phone, a touch tablet and a desktop, and is now shown only where it does something, through three gates picked by what the row needs (`docs/app/settings/README.md`, Gating): `useIsMobile` for chrome the mobile shell lacks (float, nav marks, Big Cover's widescreen, hide sidebar, seek step), `useIsPhone` for keyboard rows and the output device (paste to search, focus indicators, so a narrowed desktop window keeps them), and the new `useIsTouch` (`hover: none`) for mouse rows (hover styles, auto-hide controls, seek-hover lyrics, middle-click, both wheel rows). Layout stays on mobile with only Sidebar tabs, since the mobile Sheet reads them. Rows that work on touch but named a mouse or keyboard swap to a touch key (`...Touch` / `...Mobile`): long-press to restyle, cover pause in the background, dim on touch, auto full-screen, hold to preview without the right-click line, storage in Settings, lock screen controls, the magnified mini player, and the tour's palette step ("Tap Search", `mobileBodyKey`). Animate waveform on new song now defaults on. Phones and tablets have no app volume any more (`HARDWARE_VOLUME` in `audioEngine.ts`): the gain is pinned at 1, a stored lower value included, and every volume slider and mute button (player bar, BigMusic, Big Cover, video player, guess game, Unheard) plus the volume look rows are gone there; the rocker is the volume.
- **Dropped: a back affordance for chrome-less mobile (2026-10-02).** Flagged by the 2026-09-13 review because `navigate(-1)` lives only in the topbar; checked by Jenny on device, back navigation already works, so nothing to build.
- **Plugin pages under the tablet sidebar (2026-10-04).** The slide-over sidebar sits in the app grid, a stacking context at `--z-card`, so routed plugin frames (`page` layer, `--z-card + 1`) drew over it. While it is up, `sidebar.tsx` cuts its untransformed box out of the whole `page` layer with `clipFrameLayer` (`frameHost.ts`), a `clip-path` on the container, so no frame is resized and the plugin keeps its layout. The panel also took its resize handle, slide and overlay side from `sidebarPosition`, while a left/right nav puts it opposite the nav; both now read `sidebarOnRight` from `buildGrid.ts`.
- **Pull to refresh on Home and Recently Listened (2026-10-04).** Both reuse `usePullToRefresh` + `PullIndicator`. Home keeps one `.homeBody` for the empty and the filled state so the listener never loses its element, remounts the sections so each refetches, and forces the cached halves (albums, artists, stats, folder playlists if loaded). Recently Listened hands `Playlist` its loader as `onRefresh`, with a request counter so a slow 15s poll can't overwrite a newer pull. Queue left out by choice.
- **Sidebar sheet snap points (2026-10-05).** The mobile sidebar `Sheet` rests at half (where it opens) and full (`SHEET_SNAPS` in `sidebar.tsx`, `snapPoints`/`initialSnap` on `Sheet`, opt-in so menus keep their content height). A drag now starts anywhere on the panel: down over a list that is at its top drags the sheet (and closes it past half), up expands it until full, then the list scrolls. Built on pointer events plus a non-passive `touchmove` that cancels the scroll once the sheet owns the gesture, since motion's drag lost every press that landed on a scroll container. The tabs sit in the new `header` slot, pinned above the scrolling content. Settle rules in `sheetSnap.ts`, tested in `tests/components/primitives/sheetSnap.test.ts`.

## 19. Plugin System

- **A plugin settings panel is drawn by the host's settings box, 2026-08-06.** It already used
  `SettingLine` per row, but laid the rows out itself, so it was missing everything the box adds
  around them: the rules between rows, the title, and the indent a dependent row gets. Five plugin
  rows next to five host rows read as two different surfaces. Now `PluginSettingsPanel` maps the
  descriptor to `SettingRow[]` and hands the whole thing to `SettingsBox` (`bare`, the card is
  `PluginsSection`'s), so the panel cannot drift from a host panel when that changes. The two rows a
  panel needs that the registry had no type for moved into it rather than staying beside it:
  `SettingRow` = `SettingItem` + `note` + `link`, kept out of `SettingItem` so the settings search
  still sees a leaf as label + description. Also `child` now survives `parsePanelRows` (the
  downloader had been declaring it on its SponsorBlock sub-toggles and having it parsed away), and a
  leading plain `text` row becomes the section description, where a host section puts its own. SDK
  2.2.0.
- **The host policy is `script-src 'self'`, 2026-08-04.** The last of the flag-day cleanup, and it
  closed the two items as one, because they were one: `'unsafe-inline'` was there for the import map
  and `blob:` for `pluginLoader`'s in-realm `import()`, and once `HOST_SDK_VERSIONS` went to a single
  entry neither had a consumer left in a production build. So the built document ships no import map
  and no `plugin-runtime` entries at all (`vite.config.ts` emits the map only under `ctx.server`, and
  the seven shims stopped being build entries), and the dev server gets `HOST_CSP_DEV` by rewriting
  the meta, never by adding a second one, since two policies intersect. The planned alternative was to hash the import map, which would have forced the
  meta out of `index.html` into a build-time injection ordered before vite's head-prepend; not
  shipping the script is strictly stronger than naming its hash and has no ordering to get wrong.
  It is containment, not hardening: `pluginLoader` refuses a 2.x bundle in this realm, but that is a
  guard in code, and now the browser refuses *any* bundle here, so a wiring bug fails closed. Also
  deletes the second copy of the SDK the app was shipping for a map nothing could use.
  **Android was measured rather than argued.** Capacitor's `JSInjector` inserts its whole native
  bridge as an inline `<script>` immediately after `<head>`, before this meta, and a meta policy does
  not govern what the parser already ran: a Blink probe confirmed the pre-meta script runs and a
  post-meta one is refused. That makes the policy load-bearing on **not** being first in `<head>`,
  the opposite of what "put the CSP first" reads like it does. `check-csp.mjs` now also asserts the
  shipped document has zero inline `<script>` (the `--dist` pass is the one that can see a vite
  plugin injecting one) and that `HOST_CSP` never names either source again. Full record:
  `docs/plugin/frame-delivery.md` §4.6.

- **An approval covers the permission list, 2026-08-03.** The revision consent bound to was the
  bundle alone (`sri:<hash>` / `ver:<version>` on the server, `<mtime>-<size>` locally), and
  `plugin.json` is a different file from `ui.mjs`: a plugin approved with a narrow `ui.permissions`
  could widen it without changing a byte the hash covered, so no new approval row appeared and
  `compileMethods` handed the next frame the wider table. That is the exact thing sandbox-design §3
  forbids. The revision is now `perm:<sorted set>|<bundle identity>`, computed **once per source**
  from the same parsed set the approval row lists, stored as `PluginRuntimeInfo.revision`, and read
  from there by both settings lists: the old shape had the UI spell the revision a second time,
  which is the drift that would put the two halves back out of step. The permission half goes first
  because a permission cannot contain `|` while a manifest version is an arbitrary string, so a
  chosen version can never spell a different permission set; the set goes in verbatim rather than
  digested, because `network:<host>` takes arbitrary hostnames and a short digest of an
  attacker-chosen list is a collision search. Sorted, so re-ordering a manifest is not a
  re-approval. `ui.externalHosts` binds too, having been folded into the set since the port: it was
  the one grant that never appeared on the approval row at all. Two consequences, both wanted: every
  existing approval is invalidated (a one-time re-approve), and the "narrowing leaves a live frame
  on the old grant table" case is gone, since narrowing now unapproves and unmounts the surface. No
  backend or electron change was needed, which the goals item had assumed: the descriptor already
  carries `ui.permissions`, and computing the revision client-side is what makes it bind to what was
  actually shown. The local bundle key deliberately did **not** move: it is a cache identity, and
  folding permissions in would remount a live frame over a manifest edit that changed no code.

- **Server plugins have icons, 2026-08-03.** `manifestSchema` is a `z.object`, so it stripped the
  undeclared `icon` key before the descriptor ever saw it and every server plugin drew a monogram
  while desktop ones had had artwork since the port. The field is declared and projected (top level,
  beside `name`/`version`, since an icon is identity rather than part of the UI surface, and the row
  exists before any bundle is approved) with `DESCRIPTOR_CACHE_VERSION` bumped so Redis stops
  serving the old body. The `image` form gets `GET /api/plugins/:name/assets/*`, registered in the
  `protected_` scope beside `pluginUiRoute`: the path is request input, so it passes the same
  grammar the frontend's parser applies (relative only, no `..`, no scheme or drive letter) and then
  `resolveInside`, which is what actually stops a symlink pointing out of the folder. Images only,
  512 KB cap, type looked up rather than sniffed, and `nosniff` + `default-src 'none'; sandbox` on
  the response, because an svg served off the app origin is a scriptable document one navigation
  away. Cookie auth covers it, so a plain `<img src>` works the way covers already do. The three
  shipped plugins with a UI (`ghost-catalog`, `listenbrainz-scrobbler`, `recommendations`) declare
  an `iconify` name, so the capability is visible rather than merely available.

- **A rebuilt plugin bundle no longer needs a backend restart, 2026-08-03.** `loader.ts` hashed
  `ui.mjs` once at boot while `plugins.ts` read it from disk per request, so new bytes met a stale
  `sri` and the host refused them: correct (it cannot tell a rebuild from a swap) and, in an
  authoring loop, an afternoon of "the fix did not apply". The registry entry now carries a
  `bundleStamp` (mtime+size) and `refreshBundleHashes()` re-reads only the bundles whose bytes
  moved. It is called from `getDescriptor()` **before** the Redis read, and invalidates the cache
  when something changed: the descriptor is the only reader whose value the client verifies against,
  and it owns the cache a change has to invalidate, so putting it anywhere else would leave a stale
  body nothing would clear. A bundle that becomes unreadable drops its hash rather than keeping one
  for bytes nothing can produce, which the frontend already renders as a plugin that says why.

- **SDK 2.1.0: a plugin can copy, and its cards are the host's cards again, 2026-08-03.** Both are
  the same lesson from the port, found in `ghost-catalog`: a frame is not a smaller browser, it is a
  cross-origin document with nothing delegated to it, so a capability that reads as ordinary
  in-page code is simply absent there. `navigator.clipboard.writeText` was the case, and doubly so:
  no `clipboard-write` crosses to an opaque origin, and a `chrome` surface's frame is 1x1 and
  offscreen, so it can never hold focus either. Its "copy list" button therefore failed every time
  and toasted its own failure. `ui.clipboard.writeText()` is now a bridge call the host performs,
  ungated for the reason `toast` is (it writes, never reads, so the worst it does is replace what
  the user copied) and capped at 100k. There is no `readText` and there will not be one.
  The second half is `Surface`: it was drawn from `--color-ui` because `--surface-bg` /
  `--surface-border` were on the do-not-pipe list, which was over-broad. Only the *blur* cannot
  cross (a backdrop filter samples the frame's own backdrop); the two colours are exactly what every
  theme sets to restyle `.uiContentContainer`, and they must be variables rather than a class rule
  precisely so custom themes can reach them. Piping them makes a plugin card follow every theme,
  present and future, for free. Also fixed with them: a `rows` block was being handed to
  `CarouselSection`'s carousel, which force-sizes every child to 140-170px, so a plugin's row list
  rendered as one squeezed column that scrolled sideways (`stacked` renders the same titled card
  with a stacked body).

- **The sandbox is mandatory, 2026-08-03.** `HOST_SDK_VERSIONS` is one entry. Until it was, the
  isolation this whole phase built was **opt-in by the plugin**: a 1.x bundle resolves react and the
  SDK through the document import map and therefore executes in the host realm, so declaring
  `ui.sdk: "^1"` was a supported way to run with the session cookie, the full DOM and
  `window.veloraDesktop`, and an author who wanted that simply declared it. The only thing in the
  way was the approval row, which is consent rather than containment and does not even say the two
  cases differ. That broke the design's own premise (`sandbox-design.md` §8: it has to hold without
  anyone reading the plugin) and §3's "a permission the user was not shown is not granted", which
  cannot bind a plugin that never asks.
  Now a `^1` manifest fails `sdkSupported`, lands on `incompatible`, and `isRenderable` refuses it,
  so it never mounts and its bytes are never fetched or executed. One line, and only that cheap
  because the ports below landed first, which is exactly the order the plan chose. Two things worth
  keeping straight: the in-realm loader path **stays**, because `devSource` declares no range and is
  the authoring loop's only mount (compiled out of production, so not a way back in), and the doc
  framing that called this "a deletion rather than a cutover" was corrected in place, since reading
  it as cleanup is what let it sit open.

- **All eight first-party plugins run behind the frame boundary, 2026-08-02.** Phase 4 step 6, the
  exit criterion for the whole sandbox phase. `lyrics-plus`, `karaoke`, `bigmusic-pack`,
  `concert-dates`, `release-radar`, `listenbrainz-scrobbler`, `recommendations` and `ghost-catalog`
  all declare `ui.sdk: "^2.0.0"` and carry their own React and SDK runtime; every built `ui.mjs`
  imports nothing, which is the property a frame forces (no import map, no way to fetch one) and the
  one each check script now asserts. `obs-now-playing-overlay` is not ported: it runs in OBS.
  Four things the port found that reading the plan would not have:
  - **`process.env.NODE_ENV` is not substituted in a vite lib build**, so bundling React shipped its
    development copy *and* left live `process` reads, which are a `ReferenceError` in a frame. One
    `define` fixes both and takes a bundle from ~830KB to ~285KB. Now in `docs/plugin-authoring.md`,
    because a plugin without it does not run at all and says nothing useful about why.
  - **The app's utility classes do not exist inside a frame.** A frame ships the SDK's base CSS and
    the kit's own rules, so every `op-50`, `caption-small`, `truncate` and `divider` in a ported
    surface styled nothing, silently. The plugins now carry a small shared token-built stylesheet.
  - **Cover art from a plugin's own API cannot render**, because `img-src data: blob:` admits no
    provider path and there is no way to mint a media handle from a plugin's own response.
    `recommendations` and `ghost-catalog` fell back to the no-artwork tiles they already had.
    **Closed 2026-08-03** by `usePluginCoverUrl(path)` (SDK 2.1.0): a `media.cover` bridge method
    behind `library.read` that takes the cover path the plugin's backend returned and answers with
    bytes. The containment is that the host does not *resolve* the path, it re-derives it: only a
    filename matching the cover grammar survives, the address is rebuilt around it and has to equal
    the one asked for, and the response is refused unless it really is an image. Without that pair a
    plugin could name `/api/v1/users/me` and be handed a credentialed read as "art". It reuses the
    existing handle cache and byte budget, so a plugin cover costs what a host one does.
    `ghost-catalog` keeps its no-artwork cards: its releases are MusicBrainz ones, so there is no
    Velora cover to name in the first place.
  - **A frame has no outbound link.** No `allow-popups`, and the host policy is `frame-src 'self'`,
    so `target="_blank"`, `window.open` and self-navigation are all refused. The only outbound link
    left is a settings panel's host-rendered `link` row, which is why `concert-dates` lost its
    per-event ticket buttons rather than shipping dead ones. Open item, see `goals.md` §19.
  - Two host defects the ports exposed and closed: every section row rendered as a `<button>` even
    where the plugin attached no handler (a function cannot cross a clone, so the SDK now leaves an
    `actionable` marker where it captured one), and a `cards` block's "View all" dispatched a
    suffixed key the SDK never registered, so it answered "No handler" on every press.

- **The five `chrome` points render descriptors, 2026-08-02.** The half of step 6 that is host work.
  A `box` point gets a frame in a rect and paints; these five cannot, because they live inside host
  layout a frame would break (a settings list, a drag-reorderable home grid, the player transport
  row, the nav footer). So the plugin describes and the host draws.
  - **The frame is still real, it just never paints.** A chrome surface is the same sandboxed frame
    with the same bridge, grants, token piping and crash handling, never `place()`d, so it stays at
    the offscreen rect every frame starts in. That matters because a chrome surface still runs plugin
    React with state, effects and timers, which every shipped panel needs (ghost-catalog polls a sync
    job, both settings panels read storage during render). Inventing a headless runtime instead would
    have been a second implementation of all of it.
  - **A descriptor names a host component; it does not describe a layout.** No box model, no style,
    no class, no nesting. Six of the eight panel row types *are* `SettingItem`s and render through
    `SettingLine` unchanged, a card is a `MediaCard`, a section is a `CarouselSection`, a nav widget
    is the extracted `NavStatusPill`. So a plugin panel is a host panel by construction rather than
    by its author copying the design, and a plugin cannot express a surface that does not already
    look like Velora. `text` and `link` are the only two drawn here, because Settings has no row for
    either and every shipped panel needs both.
  - **Only the data crosses; the closures stay.** `usePluginDescriptor` walks the shape once, sends
    the fields and keeps the handlers keyed by the id beside them, so a press invokes that id and the
    original closure runs in the plugin's realm with its own state still in scope. Handlers are
    refreshed on every render even when the data is byte-identical, or a button would act on values
    the user can no longer see.
  - **Parsing is the trust boundary**, in the shape `parseUiContributes` uses on a manifest: a bad
    row drops itself rather than taking the surface down, a repeated id is dropped (an id is how a
    callback is addressed, so a duplicate is ambiguous rather than redundant), a field the table does
    not name never reaches a renderer, a cover is only ever a media handle and never a URL, and a
    `link` href must be absolute http(s), since an in-app destination is `usePluginNavigate`'s job
    and every other scheme is a sink.
  - **`NavStatusPill` extracted from `NavStorageIndicator`.** The storage figure was already this
    component in all but generality, and the one plugin that ever used `navWidgets` had hand-rolled a
    130-line copy of it in inline styles. Both compose it now; the storage readout keeps its own
    `--vicon` mask glyph through a modifier class, and a plugin names an icon instead.

- **A plugin frame can load the app's font and its icons, 2026-08-02.** The last step 6 blocker, and
  a policy consequence rather than a bug: the frame policy named no `font-src`, which falls back to
  `default-src 'none'`, and `'none'` refuses a `data:` face exactly as it refuses an origin. So every
  plugin surface rendered in system sans, with no glyphs at all, since `img-src data: blob:` admits
  neither the app's same-origin SVGs nor the CDN.
  - `font-src data:` is the whole widening, and it is **measured, not reasoned**: two new probe rows
    on all three engines say the app's real woff2 loads from `data:` and that a network face is still
    refused, and `font` became a seventh witness channel so the directive cannot quietly open an
    egress path. The bytes probed are the real font file, because a synthetic face that fails to
    *parse* rejects exactly like one the policy refused.
  - The woff2 crosses on `init`, **not in the token snapshot**, which is the obvious home and the
    wrong one: the snapshot is re-pushed on every accent change and the accent is derived from the
    cover, so a 32KB face would cross once per track for the life of the session.
  - Icons are resolved on demand instead of piped: 181 are bundled locally and the rest are CDN, so
    shipping the set would cross far more than any surface draws. `icon.read` answers with SVG text
    the frame turns into its own `data:` URL, and the name is held to the same grammar a manifest
    icon passes, which admits no slash, dot or scheme and so cannot steer either lookup.

- **Six of the seven step 6 blockers, 2026-08-02.** Everything the port needed except the frame's
  font and icons, which stays open in `docs/goalsDetails/plugin-system.md` because widening a
  shipped policy wants a probe row first.
  - **`bigMusicModes` is a box surface.** The blocker was that `PluginBigMusicContext` is eleven
    callbacks plus two host-realm scalars and `postMessage` structured-clones, so the object cannot
    cross at all. It now crosses in halves: the data goes as props, and `plugin-sdk/runtime/`
    `bigmusic.js` rebuilds the callbacks and `getPosition()` on arrival, so a mode's signature is
    identical in both realms and only its manifest's major decides where it runs. The callbacks are
    two allowlisted methods rather than eleven (`bigmusic.control` behind `playback.control`,
    `bigmusic.chrome` for close/fold, which the in-realm ctx also hands over ungated), and both
    dispatch by action name into the host's **own** ctx closures: `onShuffle` toggles and
    `onCycleRepeat` cycles, neither of which is expressible as a playback command without the frame
    re-deriving state the host already holds, and a second copy of that is a second thing to drift.
    Two scalars are retired rather than ported: `position` was a host-realm sample and
    `getPosition()` interpolates the pushed anchor, so it is right *between* pushes rather than only
    at the instant it was taken; `coverBlobUrl` was a host-origin blob url an opaque origin cannot
    resolve, and `cover` is the handle for the same art.
  - **`BridgeMethod.surface` scopes a method to one extension point.** A grant says what a plugin
    may do; this says where. Without it a routed page holding `playback.control` could close the
    overlay another plugin's mode was drawing. `activeBigMusicContext` is the second half of the
    same question, checking that the calling plugin is the one on screen, and a call that misses is
    silent rather than thrown: a click landing as the overlay closes is a race, not a refusal, and
    these are wired straight to onClick.
  - **The frame container had to split in two.** A container is a stacking context and its children
    cannot escape it, so the single one at `--z-card + 1` would have painted every BigMusic mode
    behind the overlay it belongs to. `page` and `bigmusic` bands now, the second still under
    `--z-modal` so a dialog or toast opened over a plugin mode stays on top.
  - **`useCapability()` answers over the bridge**, from one `capabilities` array on `init`. It is
    the only ungated handshake field, and deliberately: a capability names what the *server* can do,
    never what the user has, which makes it the same class as the piped design tokens rather than
    the same class as `serverUrl`. Sent once, because a provider only swaps across a login or a
    logout and both tear every frame down.
  - **`queueCovers`**, one media handle per queue row, index-for-index. A filmstrip is the one
    surface the single `cover` handle cannot serve, and resolving `track.coverArt` is not open to a
    frame at all under `img-src data: blob:`. Left a parallel array rather than folded into
    `PluginTrack` so a playlist of several thousand songs does not mint a handle per row it never
    draws.
  - **`ghost-catalog` and `recommendations` now declare `library.read`**, which `playTrackById`
    needs alongside `playback.control` because it reads the track before queueing it.
  - **The five plugin check scripts assert the shipped manifests again.** They still expected
    `ui.externalHosts`, which folded into `permissions` as `network:` grants in step 4; each now
    asserts the legacy array is *absent*, so the fold cannot silently come undone.
  - **`timestamped-lyrics`' dead UI is gone.** It declared `ui: { frontendBundle: "ui.js" }`, a key
    nothing has served since the React plugin system landed, so the panel was already unloadable;
    the 202-line IIFE behind it read `localStorage.v_user` and fetched with `credentials: "include"`,
    which is the shape the sandbox exists to end. Dropped rather than ported, and the legacy field
    went out of the backend zod schema with its last declarer, so a new plugin cannot declare one.

- **Plugin storage is file-backed on desktop, 2026-08-01.** Every `storage.set` used to land in
  the renderer's origin bucket next to `velora-session`, `velora-audio-settings` and the theme
  profiles, so one plugin caching a payload could evict the app's own state, and the 128 KB
  per-key cap only existed because of that shared quota. Same move custom-theme CSS made
  2026-07-26: `electron/pluginStorage.ts` plus a `plugin-storage:*` bridge (`list`/`write`/
  `delete`) keep one JSON file per plugin namespace in `userData/plugin-storage`, read once at
  boot into the in-memory map `src/services/plugins/pluginStorage.ts` owns. The map is what keeps
  the SDK's `PluginStorage` synchronous over an async file store, and it is the seam Phase 4
  step 5 will call from the frame's RPC bridge instead of adding a second implementation:
  `createPluginStorage` in `sdk/internal.ts` is now pure per-plugin namespacing with no backing
  knowledge at all.
  **Storage keys never become paths.** A key is an arbitrary plugin-controlled string, so the
  keys live *inside* the JSON and the only path input is the namespace id, which the host derives
  as base64url of the already percent-encoded prefix. Main revalidates `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,240}$`
  anyway and refuses rather than escapes, the same refuse-don't-escape rule `THEME_ID` uses.
  Prefix parsing is `key.split(":", 4)`, which holds because every segment is encoded, so a key
  containing `:` cannot widen its own namespace.
  Cap is read at call time like `cssLimit()`: 128 KB on web, 1 MB on desktop, where a file is not
  a shared quota. Namespace writes coalesce on a microtask so a burst of sets is one file write,
  and main refuses an oversized namespace rather than truncating (truncated JSON would lose the
  whole namespace). `clearPluginStorage` sweeps both backings, so no caller knows which is live.

- **Plugin storage is per account, and survives logout, 2026-08-01.** Shipped in the same batch,
  on top of the file backing above. The namespace was `velora-plugin:<host>:<plugin>:`, per server
  and plugin but not per user, so `useLogout` wiped *all* plugin storage on the way out purely to
  stop the next account on the machine reading the previous user's data. The cost was that no
  plugin could keep anything across a logout: cached lyrics, per-plugin preferences and cached API
  responses all died every time, even logging straight back into the same account.
  The namespace now carries the account, `velora-plugin:<encHost>:<encAccount>:<encPlugin>:`, and
  logout no longer wipes. Uninstall, revoke and a plugin's own `storage.clear()` still do, and
  `clearPluginStorage` lost its no-argument default on purpose: an uncalled default that wipes
  every account's plugin data is a foot-gun, and "wipe everything" was only ever the logout sweep.
  **The account segment is not the `userID` alone.** Subsonic and Jellyfin identify a user by name
  and hardcode `userID: 0`, so the segment would have been the constant `0` and every account on
  one server would have shared a namespace, turning the removed wipe into a straight cross-account
  leak on those providers. Only a safe positive integer is trusted verbatim; otherwise `userName`
  is folded into a digits-only FNV-1a hash with a leading `0`, which no canonical id stringifies
  to. The no-session fallback is the constant `no-account`, hyphenated so a numeric id can never
  encode into it.
  **The prefix is derived per call, not captured.** `createPluginStorage` closes over the deriving
  function, so a live storage object follows the current account rather than the one it was built
  under. Capturing would in fact be safe today (logout hard-replaces the document whenever plugin
  code has run, and `PluginBootstrap` only mounts under `RequireAuth`), but that is an invariant of
  `pluginLoader`/`useLogout`, not of the storage code, and a future account-switch or 401-reauth
  flow inside one document would break it in silence.
  **Pre-account values are deleted at boot, not migrated.** Their contract was already "wiped on
  logout", so losing them costs a cache, while folding them into whichever account logs in first
  would hand that account the previous user's data, the exact leak the segment closes. Only the
  third segment separates the two shapes, and `encodeURIComponent` escapes `:`, so no live
  four-segment key can be misread as legacy (a port, punycode host or IPv6 literal all encode
  clear of it). Known and inert: a legacy key whose plugin name was literally all digits or
  `no-account` is not swept, and no current prefix can address it.
  **What this does not buy.** On a shared machine the values now sit on disk after logout instead
  of being deleted. Another account cannot address them through the SDK, but the desktop bridge is
  not tenancy-scoped, so `veloraDesktop.pluginStorage.list()` still hands a hostile plugin every
  namespace, other accounts' included. That is the pre-sandbox caveat the frame boundary closes,
  and the threat model says so rather than implying a guarantee. Uninstall is also per account now
  (see the open follow-up).
  15 checks in `tests/services/plugins/pluginStorage.test.ts`, plus cross-account separation in
  `hostilePlugin.test.ts` and a regression guard in `useLogout.test.ts` asserting the wipe never
  comes back.

- **Plugins can ship their own icon, 2026-08-01.** The manifest had no identity field at all, so
  every row in Settings to Plugins was two initials on a state-tinted tile. Optional `icon` at the
  manifest root now carries `{ image?, iconify? }`, parsed by one shared module
  (`src/services/plugins/pluginIcon.ts`) that both sources call and `electron/localPlugins.ts`
  mirrors, warn-and-drop per half like `parseUiContributes`. Image wins, iconify is the
  `onError` fallback, monogram is the fallback after that, all inside the same tile so the list's
  left edge stays straight and the tone colouring still reads.
  **Both forms are grammars, never URLs.** `iconify` reuses the existing `sanitizePluginIcon`
  class that `nav`/`commands` icons already pass, which excludes `/` and `.` so no scheme,
  `data:`, `javascript:` or protocol-relative value can match. `image` is a relative path with no
  leading `/`, no `..`, no backslash, no `:` (so no scheme and no drive letter) and a renderable
  extension, capped at 200 chars. Local plugins inline it as a `data:` URL on the existing
  `plugins:list` DTO, resolved through the hardened `pluginFile()` with a new realpath re-check on
  the file itself so a symlinked directory segment cannot escape, and capped at 128 KB. Server
  plugins point at the same auth-gated `/api/plugins/<name>/…` scope `bundleUrl` already uses.
  **Backend half not shipped:** the descriptor's zod schema drops the unknown field, so server
  plugins get no icon until `../velora-backend` passes `icon` through (and adds an assets route
  for the image form). Degrades cleanly through the fallback chain meanwhile.

- **BigMusic player controls in the SDK, 2026-08-01.** A mode owns the whole overlay and the host
  renders no shared control bar, so every built-in mode places `BigMusicTransport` /
  `BigMusicSeekbar` / `BigMusicMobileControls` itself, but the SDK kit shipped none of them: a
  plugin mode had no way to pause, skip or seek short of hand-rolling buttons off `ctx`, and could
  not reach the animated `PlayPauseButton`/`SkipButton` primitives, so it looked close and never
  right. `@velora/plugin-sdk/ui` now exports `Controls`, `Seekbar`, `Clock`, `Transport`,
  `Extras`, `MobileControls` (SDK 1.6.0).
  **They take no `ctx`, which is the whole bridge.** The plugin ctx is a sanitized subset, so
  re-deriving `windowVisible` / `isLive` / `peaks` / `onVolumeWheel` would have forked
  `bigMusic.tsx`'s wiring. Instead a host-internal React context (`bigMusicHostContext.ts`,
  outside the import map and never re-exported from `sdk/ui.tsx`) publishes the real host
  `BigMusicContext` with `track` nulled and `queue` emptied, so no `streamUrl` sits anywhere in a
  plugin's subtree, not even on a fiber. Nothing is synthesized. The utility cluster (waveform /
  queue / video) never renders for plugins, via a `utility?: boolean` default-`true` prop on the
  two host components rather than a fork, so all six built-in modes are byte-identical in
  behavior; `ctx.onToggleSidebar` stays available, so nothing was taken away either. The host
  leaves keep their own 1 Hz tick off the coarse position and the wrappers are memoized, so the
  plugin's 100 ms tick does not re-render them.

- **Raw-fragment audit, and the taste profile it uncovered, 2026-07-26.** Backend-only
  (`../velora-backend`), the two follow-ups Phase 3.5 left behind.
  **The audit now walks arguments, not a method list.** `pluginDb.ts` only ever checked the first
  argument of the `TABLE_ARG` methods, and only when it was a drizzle `Table`; the regex tripwire
  only ran on `execute()`. But a raw `sql` fragment names its own tables, so
  `.where(sql\`... from users ...\`)` reached past both and the postgres role was its only check
  (nothing at all when role provisioning had fallen back to the shared pool). Every wrapped method
  now audits anything in its arguments that `is(value, SQL)`, descending two levels into object
  literals and arrays so a projection and `onConflictDoUpdate({ set: { x: sql\`\` } })` are covered;
  the accessor's own `select`/`selectDistinct` audit too, since a projection never reaches the
  proxy. Walking the arguments is what keeps it from drifting against drizzle's method list.
  **Four things only the real code showed.** (1) The `is(value, SQL)` gate is load-bearing:
  `auditExecute` has a `typeof query === "string"` branch, and plugins pass raw LRC lyrics and
  MusicBrainz JSON into `.set()`/`.values()`, so a song title containing "from the" would have been
  constant warn-spam and an occasional hard throw. Argument data is also why the walk cannot lead
  with `is()` at all: drizzle's `is()` reads the value's prototype constructor, so it throws
  outright on a null-prototype object, which is exactly what fastify parses a query string into and
  hands the plugin through `ctx.http`. (2) Only object literals and arrays are descended, never a
  Table or Column, which would drag the whole schema through the walk.
  (3) `SQL.Aliased` cannot be read by `sqlToQuery`, so the fragment inside it is what gets audited.
  (4) A `(?!\s*\()` lookahead to skip `from unnest(...)` is the wrong tool: the name capture
  backtracks a character at a time until the lookahead passes, so `unnest(` read as a table named
  "unnes" and `into upsert_probe (id)` as "upsert_prob". It has to be an optional trailing group,
  and it only means "not a table" after `from`/`join`, since after `into` a paren is a column list.
  A lookahead is the wrong tool for `only`/`lateral` too, for the opposite reason: they sit between
  the keyword and the table, so skipping them killed the whole match and `from only users` named no
  table at all. They are consumed as a prefix; only `set` stays a lookahead, since `do update set`
  has no table after it.
  Fragments are also where `EXTRACT(epoch FROM se.occurred_at)` lives, which reads as a table named
  `occurred_at`; that run and `IS DISTINCT FROM` / `TRIM(... FROM ...)` / `SUBSTRING(x FROM y)` are
  blanked before matching. Checked against all six shipped plugins: 29 fragments, all silent, no
  manifest needs a new `db:` permission. Three are newly reached (album-images' `MIN_TRACKS_FILTER`
  at two call sites, and recommendations' upsert `set` at two keys, which is what needs depth 2).
  **The taste profile had never been derived.** `deriveTasteProfile`'s seed CTE, three identical
  copies, ordered by `MAX(se.occurred_at)` with no `GROUP BY` *and* selected `DISTINCT` with an
  order key outside the select list. Postgres rejects it either way (42P10 first, 42803 behind it),
  so `POST /taste/derive` 500'd and the every-25-plays auto-derive swallowed it in a `.catch`. It
  read as bland recommendations rather than a crash, which is why it survived. The dedupe moved
  outside an ordered subquery and the three copies became one `seedCte(userId)`, so the seed now
  matches `TasteProfileRepository.derive()`: newest 500 rows then dedupe, not 500 distinct tracks.
  (The normalisation still differs from the repository's, and did before; only the seed was wrong.)
  Verified: both `tsc` projects clean, plugin tests 109/109, full backend suite 236 passed / 5
  failed, and those 5 are the known pre-existing set (library artwork ×2, localImages, playlists
  ×2), none of it plugin code. Worth knowing before reading a suite result: **back-to-back runs
  inflate the failure count**, because the auth rate limiter is Redis-persisted and carries its
  429s across runs, so a second run in quick succession reported 35 failures where a rested one
  reports 5. Compare like for like, or rest in between. Then verified against a live postgres 16:
  the old CTE fails with **42P10** `for SELECT DISTINCT, ORDER BY expressions must appear in select
  list`, and with the `DISTINCT` removed the second defect surfaces as **42803** `column
  "se.track_id" must appear in the GROUP BY clause`, exactly as predicted; all three rewritten
  queries run, directly and through `createPluginDb` with recommendations' declared grants, with no
  audit warning. End to end on the running backend: `/taste` is 401 unauthenticated, `POST
  /taste/derive` is **200** where it used to 500, and against seeded genre/mood/bpm data it returns
  `hasTaste: true` with real affinities and writes them to `user_taste_profile` (seed removed and
  the profile re-derived afterwards). All six plugins load clean on boot with no undeclared-table
  warnings, which is the audit's own live check. Left open in
  `docs/goalsDetails/plugin-system.md`: the rediscover collection ranks by one expression and sorts
  by another, found in passing.
- **Per-plugin postgres role, 2026-07-26.** Backend-only (`../velora-backend`), the other half of
  Phase 3's "no path to `users`". Phase 3 enforced `db:<table>` on the typed drizzle builder and
  could only *tripwire* `execute()`, because raw SQL is text: 21 of the plugins' 69 db calls, ten of
  them DDL. So the enforcement moved into the database. Each plugin now connects as
  `velora_plugin_<name>` on its own pool (`core/plugin-system/pluginRole.ts`), which makes
  `$client`, `sql.raw` and DDL all fail the same way a declared-table violation does.
  **Grants follow the manifest, ownership follows who wrote the table.** Declared *host* tables get
  `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, REFERENCES` plus `USAGE, SELECT` on the sequences behind their
  serial columns (without which every INSERT fails). Declared tables the host schema does not define
  are the plugin's own, and a grant cannot carry `ALTER TABLE` or `CREATE INDEX`, which
  listenbrainz-scrobbler runs six of on every boot: those are handed over with
  `ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO` instead. Fresh installs never reach that path (the plugin creates and
  therefore owns the table in `onLoad`); it exists for the upgrade, where the table is already there
  and the app owns it. Host vs plugin is read off the drizzle schema files rather than a hand-kept
  list, because getting it wrong in the plugin direction would hand a plugin ownership of `tracks`.
  `GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public` stays, since two plugins create their own tables and PG15
  dropped the implicit `PUBLIC` grant. The four credential tables are revoked last, after every
  grant, so no earlier statement can re-open them.
  **Rejected: `SET ROLE` on the shared pool.** A session can always `RESET ROLE` back to the role it
  authenticated as, so one line of plugin-controlled SQL undoes it. Separate login roles on separate
  pools is the only version that holds. Passwords are HMAC-derived from `JWT_SECRET` rather than
