  random, so a second app instance booting against the same database does not `ALTER ROLE` the
  first one's pool out from under it.
  **`VELORA_PLUGIN_DB_ROLES=auto|require|off`.** `auto` falls back to the shared connection with a
  loud error when the database user cannot create roles (managed postgres without `CREATEROLE`, or
  a `pg_hba` that rejects the new role), and the startup plugin list marks those `(shared db)` so
  the degrade is visible rather than buried. `require` refuses to load a plugin it could not
  isolate; `off` is the one-env-var rollback to in-process enforcement only. Connection budget: pool
  `max` 3 per plugin, role `CONNECTION LIMIT` 5.
  **Audited before shipping, not after.** Every table, join, CTE, FK and DDL statement across all
  six plugins was checked against its manifest: no plugin touches an undeclared table, so no
  manifest needed editing. Two things that look fatal and are not, recorded so nobody "fixes" them:
  recommendations INSERTs into six tables with FKs into `users`, which works because postgres runs
  the referential-integrity check as the *referenced* table's owner, so the inserting role needs no
  privilege on `users`; and ghost-catalog's `ON DELETE CASCADE` works in the other direction for the
  same reason. Tests: `src/__tests__/pluginRole.test.ts` covers the statement planner, which is the
  part that is testable without a live postgres (pg-mem has no roles, so provisioning is skipped
  whenever the test database is injected).
  **The one bug a unit test could not have caught.** On the first boot against a real database every
  plugin fell back to the shared pool: drizzle expands an interpolated JS array into a placeholder
  *list*, so `= any(${tables})` came out as `any(($1, ... $9))`, which postgres reads as a row
  constructor and rejects with 42809. It lived in the catalog lookups, not the plan, so the planner
  tests were blind to it. Both lookups go through an `anyOf()` that binds the list as one `text[]`
  via `sql.param`, and a test now asserts the generated SQL. Verified end to end against postgres 16:
  six roles created, grant counts matching every manifest, `has_table_privilege` reporting no plugin
  role can read any credential table (that check covers ownership, membership and `PUBLIC` alike),
  and both DDL plugins running their `ALTER TABLE`/`CREATE INDEX` as themselves during `onLoad`.
  **A `GRANT` can succeed and do nothing**, which is the second thing only a real database showed.
  Issued by a user with `CREATEROLE` but without ownership of the object, postgres answers
  `WARNING: no privileges were granted` and then `GRANT`, exit 0. The statement loop read that as
  success and the pool's `select 1` still passed (`PUBLIC` holds `CONNECT` and `USAGE`), so a
  plausible deployment would have produced roles with no grants and logged nothing anywhere. There is
  now an `auditRole()` post-condition on what postgres reports back: a reachable credential table
  throws, a missing grant logs an error naming it. `CREATEROLE` alone was never sufficient, the app
  user has to own what it grants on, and the docs say so now.
  **Proven residual risk, accepted:** the role holds `CREATE ON SCHEMA public` (two plugins create
  their own tables), so a SQL injection confined to a plugin's own connection can define
  `public.upper(varchar)` and have the app role resolve to it, CVE-2018-1058 style. Demonstrated
  live. Accepted because a backend plugin can `import { db }` regardless, which is strictly more
  power; a schema per plugin is the fix if plugins ever move out of process.
- **Sandbox Phase 3, backend containment, 2026-07-25.** Backend-only (`../velora-backend`), no
  frontend change. `onLoad(ctx)` used to receive the encapsulated `FastifyInstance`, the drizzle
  client and the shared ioredis client, and `manifest.permissions` had six populated declarations
  and **zero readers**. The context is now built from those declarations, in
  `core/plugin-system/{permissions,pluginHttp,pluginDb,context}.ts`.
  **`ctx.http` was the sharp end.** Not through anything exotic: `http.server` is the raw Node
  server for the whole app (swap its `request` listener and every login body is readable),
  `http.inject`/`http.routing` dispatch into the root router, the prototype chain reaches the root
  instance while it is still un-started so `addHook`/`register` are permitted on it, and the hooks
  sit under a plain symbol a plugin can look up and empty, deleting its own `authenticate` gate.
  It is replaced by a facade over `get/post/put/patch/delete` whose only route option is
  `{ adminOnly }`, and whose handler receives `{ id, user: {id, role}, body, params, query }`
  instead of a `FastifyRequest`, because that request carries the caller's `Authorization` header
  and `velora_access_token` cookie: every plugin route was being handed a live credential of
  whoever called it. Reply narrows to `status()` and `send()`. The four plugins that imported
  `adminOnly` from `core/auth/middleware` now pass `{ adminOnly: true }`.
  **`ctx.db`** keeps the seven query methods and hides `$client` (the live `pg.Pool`, one line from
  the password hashes), `session`, `dialect`, `query` and `_`, on the client, on every builder the
  chain returns, and on the transaction object. Table access on the typed path (`from`, `insert`,
  `update`, `delete`, every join) is checked against the manifest's `db:<table>` grants and throws
  naming the permission to add; the four credential tables are undeclarable, not merely undeclared.
  `execute()` stays open because raw SQL is 21 of the plugins' 69 db calls (including the DDL two of
  them use for their own tables), with a tripwire that throws on a credential table in the SQL text
  and warns once on an undeclared one; CTE names are excluded so a plugin's analytics queries do not
  read as undeclared tables.
  **Everything else follows the same rule.** `ctx.cache` needs `cache` and namespaces every key
  under `plugin:<name>:`, which broke exactly one legitimate use (timestamped-lyrics deleting the
  host's `track:meta:<id>` after writing lyrics), so that became `ctx.library.invalidateTrack(id)`,
  gated on `db:tracks`. `ctx.events` is subscribe-only (a plugin could forge `playback.completed`)
  and gated per domain. `ctx.auth.registerLoginSecondFactorVerifier` needs
  `auth:loginSecondFactor`: any plugin could previously put itself on every login. `ctx.paths` was
  dead code handing out absolute roots (all three filesystem plugins rebuilt them from a direct
  `config/i_config` import instead) and is now `pluginDir` plus `resolve(<grant name>)`, so a grant
  names a root and there is no path to traverse. `entry` and `ui.entry` are resolve-then-verify
  against the plugin folder, realpath included. All six manifests were rewritten to declare what
  they actually touch (they were wrong in both directions: listenbrainz-scrobbler declared no `db:`
  at all while reading four core tables, recommendations declared three permission *groups* that are
  not table names).
  **Honest about what it is not.** A backend plugin is an ESM module imported into the host process,
  so it can `import { db }` and skip the context. This makes the declared surface the real one and
  enforces it on the path plugin code takes; containing a hostile module needs a process boundary,
  which the plan already rejected because it breaks `ctx.http`/`db`/`events` for all six at once.
  The plan's "scoped db accessor (no path to `users`)" is met on the typed path and tripwired on the
  raw one; genuinely scoping raw SQL needs a per-plugin postgres role, recorded as the follow-up.
  New: `tsconfig.plugins.json` + `npm run typecheck:plugins`, because `plugins/` was outside the
  main tsconfig and nothing type-checked it against the context it is handed, which is how a
  breaking context change could have shipped. Tests: `src/__tests__/pluginPermissions.test.ts` and
  `pluginCapabilities.test.ts` (60), including static checks that every shipped plugin declares the
  roots, event domains and capabilities its source names. Also fixed a pre-existing bug the new
  typecheck surfaced: `isTimestampedLyrics` is a `value is string` predicate that also tests a
  regex, so its false branch narrowed `track.lyrics` to `null` and the untimestamped-lyrics branch
  under it was typed as unreachable while being reachable at runtime.
- **Sandbox Phase 2, 2026-07-25.** The extension point registry as a single source of truth. The
  contribution list had been hand-maintained in **five** places (the frontend types, the Electron
  validator, the backend zod schema, `plugin-sdk/index.d.ts`, and the host mount sites) and had
  drifted three ways: `navWidgets` was missing from the backend schema entirely (it only survived
  because the schema is a `looseObject`), `lyricsSources` was declared by a plugin that nothing
  implemented, and the client had **no validation at all**, `serverSource` cast the descriptor
  straight into the registry. One table in `services/plugins/extensionPoints.ts` now generates the
  runtime parser, the TS contribution types (mapped types over an `as const` literal, so
  `PluginNavContribution` and friends are aliases rather than copies), and the backend zod schema;
  `electron/pluginPoints.ts` and `core/plugin-system/extensionPoints.ts` mirror it because those two
  builds cannot import from `src/`, and `tests/services/plugins/extensionPoints.test.ts` imports all
  three plus the SDK typings and fails on drift. A tiny field vocabulary
  (`id | text | text? | path | flag? | tokens`) is what makes one row express all three artifacts.
  **The security half is the client parse.** A descriptor is the one manifest no validator on the
  machine ever saw, and it could name anything: ids are now a grammar (they become the persisted
  `<plugin>:<id>` keys behind `useSettings.theme` and `bigMusicMode`), route paths must stay inside
  `/p/<plugin>/` (the URL parser normalises `..`, so `route: "../../login"` rendered a plugin nav
  row that opened a host page), titles reject control characters, entries are capped per point, and
  fields the table does not name are stripped instead of carried. Unknown *points* warn and drop
  rather than rejecting the plugin, so an older host meets a newer plugin without losing it;
  `externalHosts` now parses through the same host grammar as `network:<host>` instead of reaching
  `hostMatches` as whatever the server sent. **`navWidgets` kept** (maintainer decision, overruling
  a draft that deleted it once its only consumer was retired): a plugin needs some way to speak
  while the user is looking elsewhere. **`lyricsSources` implemented** rather than left declared and
  dead, which also proved the `service` kind: no component and therefore no hooks, so the host calls
  an exported resolver with a host-built `{ fetchExternal, storage }` context (`createFetchExternal`
  / `createPluginStorage` factored out of the hooks, storage lazy so a source that never touches it
  is not recorded as using it). `useTrackLyrics` gained it as a third tier after embedded and
  provider lyrics, which is what makes it useful on Navidrome-without-OpenSubsonic and in local
  mode; first non-empty wins, a source that throws or takes longer than 8s is skipped. Host SDK
  **1.4.0 → 1.5.0**.
- **Sandbox Phase 1, 2026-07-25.** The permission model as one artifact across both repos.
  Declaration, display and audit only: nothing enforces a grant yet, that arrives with the frame in
  Phase 4, which is exactly why the vocabulary has to exist first. `ui.permissions` is deliberately
  **separate from the existing `manifest.permissions`** (backend resources, populated by all seven
  plugins, honored by nobody until Phase 3): two boundaries, two vocabularies, and nesting the new
  one under `ui` meant no migration of the seven live manifests. The list lives in
  `services/plugins/permissions.ts` with two mirrors of it, the backend
  (`core/plugin-system/uiPermissions.ts`) and the Electron validator
  (`electron/localPlugins.ts`, which cannot import from `src/`);
  `tests/services/plugins/permissions.test.ts` reads both off disk and fails on drift, skipping the
  backend when the sibling repo is absent so a single-repo checkout still passes. The two sides validate in **opposite directions on purpose**:
  the client warn-and-drops an unknown string (an older host meeting a newer plugin must not lose
  the whole plugin over one key), while the backend and the Electron validator reject it, since both
  load manifests off their own disk where an unknown value is an authoring bug that should be loud.
  **Display:** the approval row now spells out what it is granting *before* the toggle is flipped,
  via an optional `details`/`detailsLabel` on the shared `SettingItem` rather than a forked plugin
  row, so `network:<host>` reads as the host and bare `network:*` reads as the open internet.
  **Audit:** `pluginAudit.ts` records observed capability use per plugin and warns once per
  (plugin, permission) pair on anything undeclared; once per pair matters because these are React
  render paths, so a naive warn fires every scroll frame. It never throws and degrades to a silent
  no-op outside a `PluginSurface`, because several SDK hooks are reachable from host code too.
  `playback`'s transport calls stay unattributable (module singleton, no React context) and that gap
  is recorded as an `it.fails` rather than papered over with a global current-plugin tracker; the
  frame closes it for free since every RPC is attributed by construction. **Two holes closed on the
  way:** a server advertising a bundle with no `sri` had its bytes fetched and executed with no
  integrity check at all (the check was `if (info.sri)`), now refused before the credentialed fetch
  and surfaced on the row as an error instead of a toggle that fails on click; and `devSource`'s
  body moved inside the build-time `import.meta.env.DEV` constant, so a path whose URL comes out of
  attacker-writable `localStorage` is absent from a production bundle rather than merely inert.
- **Sandbox Phase 0.5, 2026-07-25.** The cheap revocation and metadata fixes that had to land before
  the frame boundary, because they close more real exposure than the frame does and none of them
  needs it. **Revocation:** clearing the registry unregisters contributions but cannot unload a
  module, so a plugin that had run kept its timers, listeners and any patched global across logout
  (an SPA `navigate("/login")`) and would observe the next login; the same held for the disable
  toggle, which had no way to stop running code. `pluginLoader` now records that a bundle was
  evaluated (`hasPluginCodeRun`, set *before* the import since a throwing module may already have run
  side effects, and keyed per plugin so a bundle that threw in `setup` cannot dodge the toggle) and
  both paths replace the document instead. Uninstall is *not* one of them: dropping the approval
  when a folder disappears or a server stops advertising can't reload (a server would then own a
  reload trigger), so that plugin keeps running until the next launch. Logout awaits the server-side
  logout first, which is why `providerBundle.disconnect()` became `async` (it used to fire `logout()`
  and drop the promise, so a reload would have aborted it and left the session alive). **Metadata
  beacons:** a manifest is rendered before any plugin code runs, so `icon` (passed to `<img src>`
  when it contains `://` or a leading `/`) and theme token values (`--vicon-*` are consumed by
  `mask-image`) were an off-app request carrying the user's IP with nothing executing. Both are
  sanitized in the registry selectors, one choke point for nav/commands/BigMusic/themes rather than
  per render site, with a CSS-function **allowlist** so a future fetching function is refused without
  anyone remembering to add it. **Tenancy:** plugin storage keys encode both halves (unencoded, a
  plugin named `a:b` writing `x` and a plugin named `a` writing `b:x` are the same entry), the
  prefix builder is shared with the host, the namespace is deleted when a plugin stops being
  advertised or its folder disappears, and everything under `velora-plugin:` is wiped on logout (it
  is keyed per server, not per user, so the next account inherited it). **Credentials:**
  `VeloraProvider` scrubs `config.password`/`totpCode` once the session cookie exists; profile import
  drops `approvedLocalPlugins` and `disabledPlugins` as well as `approvedServerPlugins`, so a file
  can neither approve plugin code nor lift a disable off an already approved one (`deepMergeValues`
  copies every key present in the live store, so dropping is what excludes, not omitting from an
  allowlist).
  **`vmedia://`** answered any caller in the renderer with sequential integer ids and `ACAO *`, so
  anything able to make a request could enumerate the library; it now requires a per-launch key that
  main passes through `additionalArguments` to the preload, which subframes never get
  (`nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: false` is now explicit and commented as load-bearing). Backend:
  `verifyLoginSecondFactors` received the `FastifyRequest` and the raw login body (every user's
  plaintext password) plus the full repository row (`passwordHash`) behind a type that named only
  three fields; the input is now built by hand from `{id, username, isAdmin}` plus `ip`/`userAgent`.
  Fixture: `tests/services/plugins/hostilePlugin.test.ts` states each guarantee from the attacker's
  side, with the not-yet-true ones as `it.fails` so a phase exit is a test flipping, not a note.

**PH3 complete: 2026-07-07** (Management UI). Settings → Plugins box in `PluginsSection.tsx`
lists every registered plugin (name · version) with a status line and an enable/disable
toggle; incompatible plugins show *"Incompatible (needs SDK x.y)"* (`sdkRange`) instead of
vanishing; errors show their message. Enabled-state persists flat (not per-server, decided
2026-07-07) as `useSettings.disabledPlugins: string[]` + `setPluginDisabled()`, which also
flips the new `PluginRuntimeInfo.enabled` flag via `usePluginRegistry.setEnabled()`. Sources
(`serverSource`/`devSource`) compute `enabled` from `disabledPlugins` at registration;
`isRenderable` (now exported) gained `&& p.enabled`, so all surfaces, nav, routes
(`PluginPage` now guards on it too), settings panels, artist/home sections, BigMusic modes,
sidebar tabs, player controls, commands, themes, hide reactively, and the existing
dangling-pick fallback handles an active plugin theme/mode being disabled. Disabled plugins
never lazy-load (no surface mounts). i18n: `settings.sections.plugins` +
`plugins.status.*` in all 6 locales.

**PH1 complete: 2026-07-06** (Core runtime + UI authoring SDK + backend redesign, per the
architecture in `docs/plugin-system-design.md`). Acceptance plugin was **ghost-catalog**
(not led-sync, which no longer exists in the backend); a new **`artistSections`** extension
surface was added to v1 for it (decided with the maintainer). Authoring guide:
`docs/plugin-authoring.md`.

- **Shared-React import map**: `src/pluginRuntime/` shims (react, react-dom, jsx-runtime,
  jsx-dev-runtime, sdk, sdk-ui, sdk-theme) built as extra rollup inputs with stable un-hashed
  names under `assets/plugin-runtime/`; a vite plugin injects the `<script type="importmap">`
  (dev paths in serve, built paths in build). Rollup shares chunks across entries, so plugins
  get the host's single React instance without externalizing the host build. Two hard-won
  gotchas: `build.rollupOptions.preserveEntrySignatures: 'exports-only'` is required (Vite
  strips entry exports by default, shims silently became empty modules), and `export *` from
  the CJS react package drops all named exports through the interop: the shims list React's
  public API explicitly (plain `.js` so tsc skips the `export =` @types conflict).
- **Runtime core** (`src/services/plugins/`): `pluginRegistry` (zustand; manifest
  contributions register pre-execution, ids namespaced `<plugin>:<id>`, `resetSource()` +
  `clear()` on logout via both `useLogout` and the `PluginBootstrap` route unmount);
  `pluginLoader` (fetch with credentials → `crypto.subtle` SHA-384 SRI verify → blob-URL
  `import()`, keyed by bundle URL so upgrades re-load and failures retry after re-register);
  `sources/serverSource` (auth-gated descriptor, Velora-provider-only, semver-gates `ui.sdk`
  → `incompatible` status, merges manifest `locales` into i18next under `plugin:<name>`);
  dev-only `sources/devSource` (`localStorage["velora-plugin-dev-url"]`, SRI skipped,
  contributes read from the definition); `PluginSurface` (per-mount error boundary +
  Suspense + `PluginMetaContext`); `serverFetch` (cookie fetch with the same
  401 → refresh → retry-once behavior as `VeloraProvider.apiFetch`, deduped).
- **Host SDK** (`src/services/plugins/sdk/`, resolved via import map as `@velora/plugin-sdk`)
 : root: `definePlugin`, filtered `useSessionInfo`, sanitized `usePlaybackState` /
  `useCurrentTrack` / `useLibraryPlaylists` / `useFavorites` (**`streamUrl` is stripped from
  every track crossing the SDK boundary**: on Navidrome it embeds replayable Subsonic
  token/salt auth), `useCapability` re-export, curated `playback` actions (sendCommand +
  `playTrackById`), scoped `api` client (`/api/plugins/<name>`), `useFetchExternal`
  (manifest `externalHosts` allowlist, `credentials:"omit"`), `usePluginStorage`
  (localStorage namespaced per server+plugin, 128KB value cap), `useRouteParams` /
  `useRouteState` / `usePluginNavigate`, `usePluginTranslation`. `/ui`: Button (incl. `link`
  variant), Surface, Stack/Row (token-scale spacing), Skeleton, Tabs, MediaCard,
  MediaCarousel, Toggle/Select/Slider/TextInput (the extracted bare controls), imperative
  `toast`. `/theme`: `TOKENS` + `useToken` (one shared MutationObserver + transitionend).
- **Bare controls extraction**: settingsToggle/Select/Slider/Input moved from
  `settingsView/.../settingsTypes/` to `src/assets/components/primitives/controls/` (they
  were already chrome-free; `SettingLine` owns the row chrome). SettingLine/UsersTab/
  StorageInput imports updated; no visual change.
- **Host wiring**: `PluginBootstrap` layout route inside `RequireAuth` (post-auth discovery,
  zero plugin bytes logged out, full reset on logout/server switch); `/p/:pluginName/*` route
  in MainPage (`PluginPage` with own scroll container); nav appends plugin entries (desktop
  nav only; mobile tab bar deliberately skips them for now); SettingsView renders plugin
  settings panels as a Plugins section (admin-gated panels honored; management page stays
  PH3); ArtistView renders `artistSections` (wrapped `flex-shrink: 0` so the page scrolls
  instead of squishing); `plugins.loadFailed` key in all 6 locales.
- **Author-facing package**: `plugin-sdk/` types-only `@velora/plugin-sdk` (root//ui//theme
  `.d.ts`), consumed via tsconfig `paths` until published; `docs/plugin-authoring.md` covers
  the model, manifest schema, the whole vite lib-build recipe (this replaces a
  `create-velora-plugin` generator for now: deferred), the DevSource dev loop, and the
  security rules.
- **Backend redesign** (`../velora-backend`): manifest `ui` schema is now
  `{ entry, sdk, contributes, externalHosts, locales }` (legacy `frontendBundle` tolerated so
  old plugins' backend halves keep loading, but never advertised); loader adds a **global
  `authenticate` onRequest hook** on every plugin's register scope (no plugin route can be
  public, even by mistake) and computes SRI over the new entry; descriptor (`/api/v1/server`)
  is **auth-gated** (`private` cache) and advertises `{ name, version, sri, bundleUrl
  (?v= SRI cache-buster), ui: { sdk, contributes, externalHosts, locales } }`; bundle served
  as `/api/plugins/:name/ui.mjs` (`text/javascript`, immutable+private); `/api/v1/plugins`
  registry response trimmed (no server filesystem paths). **Access-token cookie `Path`
  broadened `/api/v1` → `/api`** so cookie auth reaches `/api/plugins/*` at all (root cause
  of the first live 401: the old frontend used Bearer headers, masking it); the legacy-path
  cookie is explicitly cleared on every set/clear so a stale one can't shadow the new one.
- **ghost-catalog conversion** (`plugins/ghost-catalog/`): old `window.VeloraPlugins` IIFE
  `ui.js` deleted; new `ui/` Vite lib project builds `ui.mjs` (11 kB, react/SDK external).
  Contributes: `ArtistGhosts` artist section (partial albums / ghost albums as MediaCard
  carousels, ghost tracks list capped with show-more), `GhostAlbumPage` route
  (`/p/ghost-catalog/album/:artistId/:rgMbid`, in-library tracks playable via
  `playback.playTrackById`), admin `SyncPanel` settings panel (sync all / force re-sync +
  job polling). English strings via manifest `locales.en`; backend `index.ts` unchanged.
- Verified: backend `tsc` clean; frontend `tsc -b && vite build` clean, `eslint` 0 errors
  (6 pre-existing warnings, none in touched files); plugin `ui.mjs` builds with bare
  externals intact. Backend vitest: 5 pre-existing/environmental failures (429s from the
  Redis-persisted auth rate limiter + fulltext/external-API tests), none touching this work.

**PH2 complete: 2026-07-06** (all six remaining v1 surfaces; host SDK bumped to **1.1.0**,
additive). Acceptance plugin: **`../velora-backend/plugins/surface-sampler/`** (one
contribution per surface, 3.5 kB `ui.mjs`). Authoring guide updated with the new manifest
fields + per-surface notes.

- **Groundwork**: `PluginUiContributes` + `PluginComponents` + `VeloraPluginDefinition`
  extended (frontend `types.ts`, mirrored in `plugin-sdk/index.d.ts`); six new registry
  selectors (`selectBigMusicModes/SidebarTabs/HomeSections/PlayerControls/Commands/Themes`)
  following the `selectNavEntries` pattern; backend `manifest.ts` zod schemas for all six
  (theme token names must match `^--[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$`, values capped at 200 chars). Also fixed
  a PH1 contract typo: SDK `RepeatMode` said `"off"|"one"|"all"`, host is `"none"|"all"|"one"`.
- **BigMusic modes**: `MODE_REGISTRY` stays the typed built-in record; `useBigMusicModeOptions()`
  (bigMusicTypes.ts) merges it with plugin entries and drives the overlay's swipe cycling, the

  an unavailable persisted plugin key renders bigCover **without overwriting the setting**.
  New `PluginBigMusicMode.tsx` wrapper builds the sanitized `PluginBigMusicContext`

  toggles) and owns the `--bm-sidebar-left/right` padding so plugin modes are sidebar-safe

- **Sidebar tabs**: `SidebarView` widened to string; plugin tabs render after built-ins in

- **Home sections**: appended after built-ins in `homeView.tsx`; no capability gate needed

- **Player controls**: desktop bar's utility cluster only, the mini-player deliberately

- **Commands**: `runPluginCommand()` in `pluginLoader.ts` (lazy-loads the bundle, invokes
  `definition.commands[id]`); palette appends plugin commands to the always-visible actions

- **Themes**: metadata-only token maps. `pluginThemes.ts` applies/clears them via
  `documentElement.style.setProperty` (same mechanism as cover-accent sync, never CSS text,
  so no injection surface; `--`-prefix enforced host-side too). `useSettings.theme` widened
  to string; `applyTheme` delegates plugin keys; a module-level `usePluginRegistry.subscribe`
  re-resolves the persisted theme when plugins sync in post-auth or reset on logout/server
  switch, the setting itself is never overwritten. `useThemeOptions()` (settings.tsx) merges
  built-ins + plugin themes for the settings switcher and palette (`THEME_OPTIONS` is now
  internal).
- Verified: frontend `tsc -b`, `vite build`, `eslint` 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings,
  untouched files); backend `tsc` clean; `surface-sampler/ui` builds with externals intact.
  Backend vitest failures are the same pre-existing environmental set as PH1 (Redis-persisted
  auth rate limiter 429s), none in the plugin system.

**PH4: Desktop local plugins (folder-drop v1), done 2026-07-11, hardened 2026-07-12.** Electron owns `<userData>/plugins/` and exposes narrow list/read/path/open/rescan IPC through the platform adapter (first scan runs lazily inside the first `plugins:list` invoke, so a broken plugins dir surfaces as a Settings error instead of blocking window creation); `LocalSource` validates and registers `plugin.json` + `ui.mjs` plugins into every existing surface with source `local` and SDK tier `restricted`. Local bundles load from adapter-provided code through the shared blob/import-map path without SRI, survive server-source resets, get no scoped backend API. Cross-source name collisions are deterministic: the registry never lets a local plugin claim/replace a server/dev registration regardless of async sync order (Settings row shows a "name taken" error); a bundle load superseded by a rescan can't attach its stale definition. Settings has a distinct desktop-only Local plugins section with per-folder manifest errors, SDK compatibility, folder controls, manual rescan, and a persisted approval allowlist keyed by name + bundle revision: first enable and every `ui.mjs` change require explicit approval before code executes; approvals for vanished plugins are pruned on sync. The restricted tier is an SDK convention, not a sandbox (documented in `docs/plugin-authoring.md`). Open: host-mediated `fetchExternal` via a main-process proxy, install via file picker, storage-wide quotas (128 KB per-value limit remains).

**recommendations converted, 2026-07-07.** Full page (nav entry + `/p/recommendations/main` route) rebuilt on the host SDK: For You personal mix + taste-profile card + all 6 Smart Collections, playing via `playback.playTrackById`. Backend half untouched (`/current`, `/generate`, `/collections`, `/taste`, `/feedback`). Old `ui.js` deleted; new `ui/` builds `ui.mjs`. Added SDK **`useServerUrl()`** (host bumped 1.1.0 → **1.2.0**) so a backend plugin can resolve its own cover paths into `<img>` URLs.

**navWidgets surface + plugin activity indicator, 2026-07-07.** New `navWidgets` extension point (mirrors `playerControls`): a plugin contributes a component the host mounts persistently in the sidebar nav footer (stays mounted while enabled so it can poll in the background), rendered via `PluginSurface` in `nav.tsx`. First consumer: a plugin status pill styled like the host upload indicator, polling a lightweight backend `/nav-status` route on its own plugin. Host SDK bumped **1.2.0 → 1.3.0**. Desktop nav only, mobile bottom tab bar skips plugin nav.

**listenbrainz-scrobbler converted, 2026-07-07.** Full page (nav entry + `/p/listenbrainz-scrobbler/main` route) rebuilt on the host SDK (`sdk ^1.0.0`): Connection panel (username + masked token + count slider + history-sync toggle + history-preview) and a copy-ready recommendations list. Server-stored settings via `usePluginApi` `/settings`; backend half untouched. Dropped the old localStorage caching. Old `ui.js` deleted; new `ui/` builds `ui.mjs`. (The kit's `TextInput` ships no CSS and lacks a password type, so the two inputs are a small token-styled local `Field`.) timestamped-lyrics stays out of scope (its feature works with no frontend UI; legacy `ui.js` is only an admin backfill panel redundant with `autoBackfill`).

**ghost-catalog cross-plugin bridge, 2026-07-07.** First plugin-to-plugin integration, no host/SDK change and ghost-catalog untouched. A sibling backend plugin reads ghost-catalog's cached "missing albums/tracks" straight from the shared DB (`ghost_catalog_cache`), gated on `getRegistry()` presence + a `to_regclass` table guard, isolated in one adapter file. New backend route `GET /ghosts/:artistId` (`{ available:false }` when ghost-catalog absent). Frontend side adds a second `artistSections` contribution with one-click action buttons wired to that plugin's backend routes; renders nothing when unavailable. Pattern: no first-class inter-plugin API yet, cross-plugin work leans on shared infra (DB + registry accessor), coupling confined to a single adapter file.

**Sandbox Phase 4 step 1, frame delivery decided by measurement, 2026-07-26.** The step the plan
deliberately stopped at: what document a plugin frame loads, from which origin, and how the bundle
bytes reach it. Answer in `docs/plugin/frame-delivery.md`, harness in `scripts/frame-probe/`
(`npm run probe:frame`, an Electron main that runs the candidate frame behind the `app://`
privileges copied from `electron/main.ts`, hidden window, no network, pass/fail matrix). One static
`plugin-frame.html` loaded by a relative URL so it lands on whatever origin the shell has,
`sandbox="allow-scripts"` only, policy in a `<meta>` with no network scheme in any directive, and
the host hands the bytes over by `postMessage` for the frame to turn into its own blob and import.
Auth never crosses; the existing credentialed fetch + SRI verify in `pluginLoader.ts` is unchanged.

Measured, all holding: opaque origin (`self.origin === "null"`, while `location.origin` reports the
URL's origin and is the wrong thing to assert on), `localStorage`/`document.cookie` throw, no
`veloraDesktop`, blob import works under `script-src blob:`, and fetch/WebSocket/EventSource/
sendBeacon/remote-`<img>` are each refused with their own violation event rather than a DNS error.
Two options died on evidence: a `srcdoc` frame inherits the host policy and can only tighten it, and
no frame can import code over `app://` even when its policy allows the origin, because module
scripts are always CORS mode and that scheme has no `corsEnabled` (which is also why the single-React
import map cannot follow plugins into a frame). Three corrections to `sandbox-design.md` fell out
(all now folded into that doc):
`navigate-to` no longer exists so the **host** policy's `frame-src 'self'` is what stops a frame
beaconing out by navigating itself; `network:<host>` becomes a host-side check on the bridge with
`connect-src 'none'` in every frame, forced anyway because `normalizeCorsOrigin` throws on `null` so
an opaque origin can never read a backend response; and §1's "all four first-party UIs are built
from the declarative host kit" was false in both halves (eight UI-bearing plugins, seven take a box
surface, and three import nothing from the kit).

**Sandbox Phase 4 step 2, both policies, 2026-08-01.** The first CSP in the repo, and the two halves
of one control: the frame's policy is what leaves it with no network, the host's `frame-src 'self'`
is the only thing that stops a frame beaconing out by navigating **itself** (CSP dropped
`navigate-to`, no sandbox flag covers self-navigation). Written together in `scripts/csp.mjs` and
asserted against the two shipped documents by `scripts/check-csp.mjs`, which is the one `check:*`
that also runs inside `npm run build`, because a stale bootstrap hash refuses the frame's script on
every engine at once, silently, and reads exactly like a wrong policy rather than a stale one; on a
mismatch it prints the hash to paste. Full reasoning in `docs/plugin/frame-delivery.md` §4.5.

Host half: a `<meta>` in `index.html`, `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' blob:; frame-src 'self';
object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`. One mechanism for all four shells, because
static web hosting sets no headers and there is nothing to fall back to; Electron deliberately sends
no second policy (`serveDist` is also what will serve the frame document, and a blanket header would
put a second independently-enforced policy on it, while path-conditioning one misses every deep-link
reload through the SPA fallback). **No `default-src`, deliberately:** the backend origin is typed by
the user at login, so `connect-src`/`img-src`/`media-src` could only be scheme wildcards and
`style-src` only `'unsafe-inline'`, and a wildcard soup reads like a control without being one. What
it is: `frame-src` is real, the rest is shape and a closed URL-injection sink. It contains no plugin
today, since plugins still share the host realm. Checked before shipping: no `eval`/`new Function`/
`WebAssembly`/`new Worker` in the built bundle (so no `'unsafe-eval'`), zero iframes and no form with
an `action` or a `method` in the app or in all nine first-party plugins, and the same literal is
dev-safe, so there is no dev/prod policy skew. `form-action` is `'none'` and not the `'self'` that
"a throwing handler should still reload" argues for: four of the eight forms carry `name="password"`,
so that reload is a GET with the cleartext password in the query string and in history. Nothing in
the app submits natively, so `'none'` costs nothing. On the flag day it tightens in one move, `'unsafe-inline'` → the import map's
sha256 (which forces the meta into a build-time injection) and `blob:` drops; never as a pair, since
one hash makes `'unsafe-inline'` ignored.

Frame half: `public/plugin-frame.html` ships the measured policy with the sha256 of its own inline
bootstrap, inert until step 3 mounts it, plus one directive step 1 did not have. Workers fall back to
`script-src` rather than `default-src`, so `script-src '<hash>' blob:` alone handed a plugin a blob
worker whose network then rested on blob-URL policy inheritance instead of on the policy, which is
exactly the engine-dependent behaviour the frame exists to stop depending on. `worker-src 'none'`
closes it, and the probe grew a sixth egress channel to prove it rather than assert it: refused on
Chromium, WebKit and Gecko, while the positive control (whose `worker-src` names `blob:`) spawns one
that does reach the witness, so the strict result is not vacuous. It also closes something step 1 left as a note to a future
implementer: a shipped frame document is reachable by a **third party**, who can frame it
*unsandboxed*, `postMessage` it bytes and run them at Velora's origin with the real cookie jar, and
`frame-ancestors` is ignored in a `<meta>`. So the bootstrap refuses to boot unless
`self.origin === "null"` inside a parent, and the check asserts that guard is still present; it also
boots only on a message from `parent`, and only once. The probe's `frame.html` keeps none of those
(it is a measurement rig), but it now builds its policy from `frameCsp()` too, so it can no longer
stay green while what ships drifts. Its hostile `HOST_CSP` stays separate on purpose: `img-src 'none'`
is what makes policy inheritance visible, and the shipped host policy sets no `img-src` at all.

Two shell-level backstops with them: `will-frame-navigate` in `electron/main.ts` (fires for
subframes, unlike `will-navigate`; `about:blank` allowed because a fresh iframe commits it before its
`src`), and `/plugin-frame.html` in the service worker's `navigateFallbackDenylist`, so the app shell
can never be served into a sandboxed frame, which `serveDist` already 404s for the same reason.

**Three live plugin holes closed, 2026-07-26.** All found while establishing the above, none of them
about the frame. `createFetchExternal` / `createPluginStorage` / `createServiceContext` take the
caller's identity as an argument and were reaching plugins through `export *` in
`src/pluginRuntime/sdk.ts`, so a plugin could pass a meta that was not its own and get a fetch with
no `externalHosts` allowlist or another plugin's storage namespace; `plugin-sdk/index.d.ts` never
declared them, so moving them to `sdk/internal.ts` only makes the runtime match the typed contract,
guarded by an assertion in `hostilePlugin.test.ts`. The `app://` handler's SPA fallback answered any
missing path with `index.html`, so a wrong frame URL would have booted the whole app inside the
sandbox; `.html` paths now 404 while every other extension keeps the fallback, since app routes may
contain a dot. And `PluginBigMusicMode` handed over the queue and eleven transport callbacks with no
audit call at all, so `bigmusic-pack` and `karaoke` receive `playback.*` while declaring none: it now
records `playback.read` and `playback.control` where the capability is granted, the same way
`createPluginStorage` records storage when the object is built.

**Frame delivery verified on all three engines, 2026-07-26.** `npm run probe:frame:browsers` under
Playwright's WebKit 26.5 and Firefox 153 (playwright is a devDependency, the engines are not, install
them with `npx playwright install webkit firefox`). Each run prints the engine build it measured. Every expectation holds on both, **including the
blob import**, so the delivery path is not a Chromium convenience and WebKit's opaque-origin blob
history (bug 243996, fixed 2022) does not resurface. Playwright's Chromium stays uninstalled: the
Electron harness measures it behind the real `app://` privileges, which is the build that ships.

The run found one thing, and it was the probe's fault rather than an engine's. WebKit raised no
violation for `new WebSocket("wss://127.0.0.1:9/x")` where the other two raise `connect-src`, which
reads like an open exfiltration channel on Safari. Port 9 is a blocked port, and WebKit refuses one
earlier in the pipeline than the CSP check, so the request died before the policy was consulted and
there was nothing to report; aimed at a live port it raises the violation like everyone else.

That is why the egress claim now rests on the network rather than on the event. Exfiltration needs no
reply, the request URL already carries the payload, so `egressWitness()` in `shared.mjs` is a
loopback server that records what arrives and answers images with a real pixel; all five channels aim
at it tagged per channel and per frame, and a third variant of the same document whose
`connect-src`/`img-src` name it is the positive control. Every channel is scored twice, by the policy's word and by the network's, and
neither can mask the other: nothing from the strict or relaxed frame arrived on any engine, the
control's five arrived on all three. Both harnesses share the witness, so the desktop probe gained
the same checks.

A fresh-context audit of the harness found five more measurement bugs, all fixed and re-verified:
`frame.html` was hashed as it sits on disk, so with `* text=auto` and `core.autocrlf=true` a fresh
clone on Windows would refuse the bootstrap on **every** engine and look exactly like a wrong policy
(normalized before hashing now, and verified by converting the file and re-running); `cookie` scored
a pass on an empty string, which is also what a frame with full same-origin access would read, so it
now has to throw; the `frame-src` self-navigation row matched any `frame-src` violation among five
frames rather than the beacon's; the eval canary passed on a timeout; and a skipped engine left the
exit code at 0, so a WebKit that never launched would have reported success on Firefox alone.

A second review pass found two more. The `desktopBridge` row printed `N/A` whenever no bridge was
present, which is right for a browser but meant an Electron run whose own preload failed to load
would have silently skipped the one expectation only that harness can score: the caller now says it
installed a preload, and a missing bridge fails there (verified by hiding `preload.cjs`). And the
`frame-src` self-navigation row wanted the directive and `blocked.invalid` in the same violation but
searched the joined list for each separately, which the other host violations make reachable (Firefox
blocks its own favicon, WebKit surfaces the frames' `eval` on the host). Nine measurement bugs in
this harness now, counting the CSP placeholder that matched inside a comment and the violation array
read before the event landed.

**Phase 4 step 4, `ui.permissions` enforced, 2026-08-02.** The permission model stopped being a
label. Every capability the host hands a plugin now asks `services/plugins/pluginGrants.ts` first,
and an undeclared one is not relayed. It landed ahead of the frame rather than on it, which the
design doc had assumed was impossible: the frame makes the answer structural, but the answer is a
host decision either way, and every capability is built in host code the plugin has to call. That is
the standing the backend's Phase 3 capability object already has, so this is the same move on the
other half. The gate is deliberately not in `pluginAudit.ts`, which swallows every exception because
a bug in the bookkeeping must not be why a plugin broke; a gate cannot inherit that contract.

Denial has a shape, and it is not a throw. A plugin surface sits inside an error boundary, so
throwing out of a render is the difference between a panel that shows nothing and a panel that is
gone, and a refusal must not be indistinguishable from a plugin bug. Reads answer with their empty
shape (`null`, `[]`, `""`, a zeroed BigMusic ctx, an inert storage), actions reject. `storage.get` is
called during render by two shipped plugins, which is what makes that load-bearing rather than a
preference. The console names the missing manifest line once per permission, which is the Phase 1
audit warning doing double duty rather than a second log per refusal.

Four things the step decided that the design doc had left open or wrong:

- **One vocabulary.** `ui.externalHosts` is folded into `permissions` as `network:<host>` grants when
  a manifest is parsed, and the runtime `externalHosts` field is deleted rather than left decorative.
  The fold is what keeps every shipped manifest working; deleting the field is what stops a
  hand-built `PluginRuntimeInfo` from reading as a plugin whose declared hosts grant nothing, which
  is exactly how the test fixtures failed first. It also finally shows the user the host: the legacy
  array was never on the approval row, and a permission the user was not shown is not granted.
- **`theme` is the write side.** The audit had been recording `useToken`, a read of the page the
  plugin already renders into, and nothing at all for a `themes` contribution, so it reported the
  injection side as never used. The grant now gates `selectThemes`, the one check that runs with no
  plugin code executing at all, and reading a token needs nothing.
- **The `playback` singleton cannot be attributed, so it is held to the union**: allowed when some
  renderable plugin declares `playback.control`, refused outright when none does. That is the most a
  shared object reachable from module scope, `setup()`, a timer and a command handler can be asked,
  and a global current-plugin tracker would fake attribution rather than establish it.
  `usePluginPlayback()` (SDK 1.7.0) is the attributed path and is what the frame's RPC becomes. The
  `it.fails` on attribution stays failing on purpose: a union gate refuses without attributing.
- **`useServerUrl()` stopped being the one export mapping to no permission at all.** Any data grant
  covers it, because the origin is only worth something to a plugin already holding a relative
  `coverArt` or its own server half to resolve against it.

Two live holes closed on the way, both found by auditing the capability map rather than by the
change itself. Desktop local mode's `vmedia://` per-launch capability key rides in a `k` query param
and `resolveMediaPath` takes sequential integer ids, so that one param is a read of the entire
indexed library, and it had been crossing the SDK boundary in every local-mode track's `coverArt`
since the key was introduced. It is the same class of leak as the Subsonic `u/t/s` triple that
Phase 0 scrubbed, and it is stripped by the same set; the cost is plugin cover art in local mode
until step 5's media handle replaces the URL, and handing a credential over was not an option. And
`toast` was re-exported from the store whole, so plugins had `push` and `dismiss(id)` that
`plugin-sdk/ui.d.ts` never declared: a plugin could suppress a host toast by id or bury one under a
burst. Narrowed to the four the contract names, the same rule the `create*` factories are already
held to.

First-party fallout was two manifests, exactly the two the design doc had flagged: `bigmusic-pack`
declared nothing and `karaoke` declared neither playback grant, while both take a BigMusic ctx. Three
more dropped a redundant `externalHosts`. Dev-source plugins are granted everything, since an
authoring loop that refuses every capability is one nobody can use, and that block is compiled out of
production builds.


**Phase 4 step 5, the host halves, 2026-08-02.** Three things a plugin currently gets as an address
or a scalar, rebuilt as the shapes that survive a boundary. All three are live in this realm today,
which is the point: the frame does not change them, it only changes who is on the other end.

**The audio clock** (`services/plugins/pluginClock.ts`). BigMusic art modes read the playhead
synchronously off the audio element, and a plugin in a frame cannot. So the host stops shipping a
position and ships an anchor: where the playhead was, at which `performance.now()`, and how fast it
is moving. The consumer interpolates. This is not a slower tick, it is a correct one, which is what
lets the update rate fall from 10Hz to about 1Hz while the result gets *smoother*. Rate is in the
anchor because nothing outside MediaSession had ever read `playbackRate`, so a consumer assuming 1
drifts 15% under slowed and 25% under nightcore, and karaoke's rAF wipe was only getting away with it
by re-anchoring ten times a second. Re-anchoring runs off four seams. Three already existed:
controller emits cover play, pause, seek, track change and crossfade, audio-settings commits are the
only thing that moves the rate, and the optimistic seek broadcast fires before the controller
round-trips, which is the difference between a lyric line gliding and snapping. The fourth was added
in review, because those three are all statements of *intent* and the element is allowed to disagree
with intent: a seek deferred to `loadedmetadata`, an autoplay block, an OS interruption, `play()`
resolving a task after the emit that asked for it. So the engine grew
`subscribePlayhead()` (the audible slot's own `play`/`pause`/`seeked`) and `getEffectiveRate()`,
which reads the rate off the element and answers 0 when it is not moving. Without the pair, a blocked
or interrupted element ran the clock forward over silence and snapped it back once a second, and a
deferred seek into a *paused* track had no way back at all, since the drift interval only runs while
the playhead moves. A 1Hz interval on top is drift correction between an element clock and wall time,
not a tick. `ctx.getPosition()` is
additive: `ctx.position` keeps its 100ms tick, because a mode with `ctx.position` in an effect dep
list would visibly degrade if the tick slowed, so migrating is the plugin's move to make.

**Media handles** (`services/plugins/pluginMedia.ts`). A cover reached a plugin as a URL, and neither
kind survives: a `blob:` URL belongs to the origin that minted it, and a media URL cannot be fetched
from a frame that has no cookies and `connect-src 'none'`. The one that carried its own credentials
is the one step 4 just stopped handing over. So the host hands over an opaque per-session id and
resolves it itself: in this realm to a blob URL minted here, across the bridge to bytes. Neither the
address nor the credential crosses, an id the plugin invents resolves to nothing, and the handle is
built from the *raw* host track rather than the sanitized one, which is what makes local-mode cover
art work again after step 4 scrubbed the key out of `coverArt`. Bytes are cached under an 8MB budget
and evicted without invalidating the handle, so a plugin still holding one re-resolves rather than
showing a hole; the whole registry is dropped on logout, since a handle is a credentialed fetch
waiting to happen.

**Token piping** (`services/plugins/frameTokens.ts`). A frame inherits no `:root`, no theme class and
no accent, so the host has to send them. The piped list is hand-written as a policy rather than
scraped, because half of it is what does *not* cross: chrome geometry says nothing to a surface the
host already sizes into a rect, `--z-*` means nothing inside a frame's own stacking context, and the
`.uiContentContainer` surface tokens describe something a frame provably cannot reproduce. The
elevation tokens are the one family that survives the frame untouched (a box-shadow composites inside
it rather than sampling a backdrop it cannot see), so they cross. `--ui-density` crosses too, though
not for the reason first written here: every `--padding-*`/`--gap-*` is `calc(base * var(--ui-density))`,
but a custom property's *computed* value already has its `var()` substituted, so `--padding-md` crosses
as `calc(12px * 1)` and needs nothing else. That same rule is why no piped token depends on an unpiped
one, the list is closed by construction. The multiplier travels because a surface that paints instead
of styling has to redo that arithmetic in JS. `sdk/theme.ts` gave up its
own MutationObserver for this module's, so there is one `:root` observer for the app whichever side
is asking, and `useTokens()` exposes the whole snapshot for plugins that paint (canvas, WebGL, inline
SVG) rather than style.

What the step surfaced rather than settled, both recorded in `plugin/frame-delivery.md` §4: **nothing
in a frame can load the app's font or any of its icons.** The frame policy names no `font-src`, that
falls back to `default-src 'none'`, and `'none'` does not admit `data:` either, so `--font-sans`
crosses as a face the frame can never fetch; icons are the same one directive over, since every one
resolves to a same-origin SVG or a CDN URL and `img-src data: blob:` admits neither. The fix is one
token and a data URL, and it is deliberately not taken here: widening a shipped policy is the thing
that file measures rather than reasons about, and it wants a probe row like the worker one got. And
the host's own seekbar runs a per-frame `audioEngine` read that has no frame equivalent at all, so a
ported BigMusic mode either uses `getPosition()` or gets host-rendered controls composited over it.


**Phase 4 step 3, the RPC bridge and the frame host, 2026-08-02.** Plugin code can now run outside
the host realm. A routed page contributed by a plugin that declares SDK 2.x mounts in an
`<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` at an opaque origin and reaches the host only over `postMessage`.
`frame/frameProtocol.ts` is the wire, `frame/bridgeMethods.ts` the allowlist, `frame/frameHost.ts`
the element and the pump, `frame/PluginFrame.tsx` the `PluginSurface` twin.

**What the boundary buys that step 4 could not.** A refusal is no longer a check that answers no, it
is a method that is not there: the dispatch table is compiled from the manifest at boot, so an
undeclared capability has nothing to call. And the `playback` singleton finally has a sender. That
object grants when *any* renderable plugin declared the permission, because a module singleton
reachable from `setup()`, a timer and a command handler carries no identity; a call over the bridge
arrives on a `MessageEvent` whose `source` is one specific frame, which the sender cannot forge. The
in-realm singleton keeps its union gate for as long as a 1.x bundle can reach it from module scope,
which is why that `it.fails` still fails and why the two new assertions sit beside it rather than in
place of it.

**Two majors, not a flag day on the day the host landed.** A 1.x bundle resolves `react` and
`@velora/plugin-sdk` through the document's import map and therefore cannot run anywhere that has
neither and cannot fetch one; a 2.x bundle bundles both and can. `sdkVersion.ts` accepts either and
the declared range is the only thing that decides which mount a contribution gets. The flag day
becomes "drop 1.x", a deletion rather than a cutover, and it waits for the ports instead of blocking
on them. Registering all nine first-party plugins as incompatible in the same commit that gave them
somewhere to go was never the honest reading of "no incremental path": the design doc's point is that
a *plugin* cannot be half-ported, not that the host cannot speak two versions while the ports happen.

**Four things the build settled that the plan had wrong.**

- **The frame document needed no edit at all**, so its hash and the frame CSP are untouched by this
  step. Its bootstrap returns early on a non-`boot` message without consuming it, so a listener the
  imported bundle installs receives everything after the boot, which is where the whole protocol
  lives. The plan had assumed a second payload carrying a guest runtime.
- **There is no guest runtime to deliver.** The plugin bundle *is* the guest: `plugin-sdk/runtime/`
  ships the frame-side implementation and the plugin bundles it along with its own React. That is
  what §1 breakage 6 already implied, and it removes the bare-specifier problem rather than solving
  it. Both alternatives are worth recording as dead: an inline import map is governed by `script-src`
  and would need its own hash *and* same-origin URLs the frame provably cannot fetch, and rewriting
  specifiers inside verified bundle bytes is a regex over minified JS on a security path.
- **The clock anchor cannot cross as a timestamp.** Every realm has its own `performance.timeOrigin`,
  so sending `atMs` would put a frame's playhead a constant few hundred milliseconds out. That reads
  as a fixed lyric offset, the most visible bug a karaoke mode can have, and it would have shipped
  looking like a tuning problem rather than a bug. `ageMs` crosses instead and the frame re-bases on
  receipt, which folds the one-way latency in rather than needing a clock-sync algorithm to take it
  back out. `epoch` keeps its early-on-crossfade behaviour and is now documented as "the anchor's
  track changed", not "the music did".
- **An iframe cannot be reparented.** Moving one in the DOM reloads its document, losing the boot,
  the handshake and all plugin state, and the sidebar portals its entire docked panel into the
  BigMusic overlay when that opens. A framed `sidebarTabs` would therefore have died every time the
  user pressed the cover. The element lives in one container on `document.body` and is positioned
  over a placeholder the React tree owns, so a portal moves the placeholder and the frame follows.

**A channel is a grant, exactly like a method.** Found in review, and it is the mistake worth naming:
the first cut compiled the *methods* from the manifest and then pushed whatever state the frame asked
for. The frame realm runs plugin code, so anything pushed into it is readable off the raw
`MessageEvent` whatever the SDK returns on the far side. Degrading a value in the frame is a
contract, not containment. `playback`, `clock`, `library`, `session` and `storage` are gated on the
grants their methods are, `serverUrl` follows the same three-grant rule `useServerUrl` applies in this
realm, and an unrecognised channel name is dropped rather than trusted.

**What the host sends, and why the handshake is one big message rather than chatty.** `init` carries
the session constants (`serverUrl`, grants, the storage cap), a first-paint value for every
subscribed channel, and the two things that can never be awaited from a render: the plugin's i18n
bundle, because `t(key)` is called inline in JSX by every plugin UI there is, and its whole storage
namespace, which is what lets `PluginStorage.get` stay synchronous across a boundary where everything
else is a message. `hello` names the channels the plugin actually uses, because a library snapshot is
every playlist with every song and a playback state is the whole queue, both re-serialized on every
mutation, so a plugin that never calls `useLibraryPlaylists` does not pay for it. The English bundle
is merged under the current language, because i18next's own `fallbackLng` does not cross a realm and
a plugin with partial locale coverage would otherwise render raw keys.

The frame side is `plugin-sdk/runtime/`, plain ESM built by the plugin's own bundler so the hooks run
on the plugin's React. `hello` is sent from a microtask scheduled inside `definePlugin()`, which
lands after the module body and before anything renders, and each pushed-read hook registers its
channel at module evaluation behind a `/*#__PURE__*/` annotation, so a bundler drops an unused hook
together with its subscription. i18next itself does not cross: the host sends one flat key-to-string
bundle, which leaves backends, detection, namespaces and nesting with no input, so the runtime ships
a shim doing lookup, `{{var}}` interpolation, `Intl.PluralRules` and `defaultValue` instead of putting
the library into every plugin bundle. `requestPluginApi` and the path containment behind it moved into
`sdk/internal.ts` on the way, for the reason that module exists: it takes the caller's identity as an
argument, and exported from `sdk/index.ts` a plugin could have passed a name that was not its own.

**Phase 5, storage and files, 2026-08-02.**

**Storage kept its synchronous `get`, and that is a correction to §4** ("the API goes async"). True of
the wire, not of the API: the module's own comment already said the desktop cache "is also the seam
the sandboxed iframe bridge will call later", and the frame gets exactly that, its whole namespace at
handshake. Going async would have broken the two shipped plugins that read during render and, worse,
the *reason* a refused storage degrades instead of throwing. Writes are optimistic on both sides.
What did land: a per-namespace byte total (512KB web, 2MB desktop, keys counted, recomputed per write
so there is no second total to keep in step with four mutation paths), UTF-8 byte counting where the
cap had been comparing UTF-16 units against a label in KB, and `assertPluginValueSize` exported so
the frame side refuses with the same sentence.

**Uninstall now clears every account's copy**, which closes a tracked leak: the namespace is
`<host>:<account>:<plugin>` and the account segment precedes the plugin one, so no string prefix
could ever express "this plugin, every account", and another user's data survived an uninstall and
was inherited on reinstall. The decision the item asked for, whether one session may delete another
account's data at all: yes for an uninstall, because it is machine-level and has already removed the
plugin for everyone, and no for anything else. A plugin's own `clear()` and the new per-row **clear
stored data** action in Settings → Plugins are current-account only, and the confirm copy says so.

**Files** are two directories and a token. `plugins/<name>/` is read-only and on the load path,
`plugin-data/<name>/` is read-write and never scanned, because a plugin that could write into its own
install folder could replace its verified bundle on the next launch and defeat both SRI and the
approval hash. The handle is an unguessable per-session token rotated per document, not the plugin
name, since `protocol.handle` gets a `Request` and an opaque origin sends `Origin: null` with no
`Referer`. **`vplugin://` was not built**, and the two reasons are worth keeping: the frame policy is
`img-src data: blob:`, so an opaque origin could never load such a URL anyway, and registering a
scheme would put a plugin-controlled file one navigation from being a document. Bytes cross and the
plugin mints its own blob, the way media handles already do. The write filter is an allowlist in both
directions, extension *and* magic bytes, so `cover.jpg` cannot be a PE binary; **svg is not
writable**, because it is XML and the strongest check available is "looks like markup", which cannot
tell artwork from a script container, and that would be the one hole in a filter whose whole
guarantee is that the bytes match the name. Reading an svg the plugin shipped is unaffected. Quotas
are 8MB per file, 32MB and 256 files per plugin. The name sanitizer inside `importFile` became
`electron/safeFilename.ts` with its behaviour pinned, including one weakness left deliberately
unchanged: `CON .mp3` (trailing space, which Win32 strips) is still accepted on the *import* path,
because widening it changes what an import accepts; the full rule applies on the plugin write path.

**Phase 6, `contextMenuItems`, 2026-08-02.** Track, playlist and album menus take plugin rows. Which
menus a row joins is three `flag?` fields rather than a new list field type, because the vocabulary
has no enum and inventing one for three closed values is the same drift that kept `grants:` out of
the table. Gated on `library.read` and enforced in the selector: selecting a row hands the handler the
entity the menu was opened on, so the row *is* a library read with a click in front of it, and a
denied row is absent rather than degraded because there is no useful form of an item that may not be
told what it was invoked on. Rows sit after the host's own entries behind a divider, so a plugin can
add but never reorder or displace. Nothing blocks: label, icon and targets are manifest metadata, so
the menu opens with the rows already in it and the bundle loads on select, the `runPluginCommand`
path. Radio tracks, the favourites pseudo-playlist and the artist menu take none, having no library
entity to hand over.

**`trackListColumns`: dropped, not deferred.** It lands on the hottest scroll path in the app and
asks host code to call into a plugin per visible row, and the one bound ever proposed for it, "batch
by visible window", is not a bound: a flick scroll changes that window tens of times a second, so the
batch size is whatever the plugin makes it. Nothing has asked for it, and a reserved row for an
absent consumer is the exact drift the registry exists to kill.

**Smaller things closed in the same pass, all tracked items.** `bundleUrl` was interpolated into
`` `${serverUrl}${entry.bundleUrl}` `` unvalidated, so a descriptor value of `@evil.example/x.mjs`
parsed as userinfo rather than a path whenever the server URL was a bare origin, and got the client to
make an arbitrary off-app request; it now runs through the icon parser's containment predicate,
exported as `isContainedPath` rather than written twice. The icon grammars moved from
`electron/localPlugins.ts` into `electron/pluginPoints.ts` beside the `UI_PERMISSIONS` mirror, and
the drift test compares them behaviourally against the frontend's own sanitizers over a corpus rather
than string-matching a regex literal. `docs/plugin-system-design.md` no longer describes
`local-plugin://` as a registered scheme; it is a synthetic bundle key and the bytes cross
`plugins:readBundle` (the same claim is not in `plugin/sandbox-design.md`, which the goals item had
wrong). Plugin `nav` contributions became command-palette pages, which is the mobile entry point that
costs nothing: they are reachable by long-pressing the Search tab, an affordance that tab already has,
and they had been missing from the palette on desktop too. A permanently visible mobile surface stays
deferred on purpose: the bottom tab bar has five fixed thumb targets and a sixth breaks at 360px, and
with zero shipped plugins contributing `nav` there is nothing to shape it around yet.

**Host-drawn chrome, widened (2026-08-06, host SDK 2.3.0, 2.4.0 and 2.6.0).** Four additions on the
same seam step 6 built, each closing a case where a descriptor could not say what a shipped plugin
needed. An `artistSection` is handed the artist, not only its id (`artistSectionProps`, behind
`library.read`, capped at 300 albums and 1000 tracks and run through `sanitizeArtist` so no signed
cover url or `streamUrl` crosses): an id is only a name to something that can look it up, so a
frontend-only plugin could say nothing about the artist it was mounted on. A `rows` item carries its
own trailing button, because a block has one action to spend across forty songs. A `routes` surface
may publish a `PageDescriptor` and be drawn as one of the host's own detail views (`DetailHeader` +
windowed `Track` rows, `PluginDetailPage`), which is opt-in per render: `PluginRoute` creates the
frame through the same `usePluginChrome` every chrome surface uses and only *places* it while the
plugin publishes nothing, so a route that never publishes keeps exactly the mount it had and a live
frame is still never reparented (`useFramePlacement` is the one subscription both mounts share). And
a card's cover takes raw bytes as well as a media handle, for the card about a record the library
does not have: a handle is minted host-side from a url the host already holds, so there was nothing
to mint one from. Bytes are the stricter half, not the looser one, because the plugin still names no
address: the container is identified by sniffing the bytes rather than by the declared `mime` (SVG
refused by name *and* by content), capped per image and per descriptor, copied out of whatever view
arrived, and the blob url is the host's, minted per consumer and revoked on unmount
(`usePluginBytesUrl`).

**One network identity for every plugin (2026-08-06, host SDK 2.5.0).** Some services a plugin
talks to ask the *application* to name itself, so the identity is one app-wide setting
(`useSettings.pluginUserAgent`, Settings → Plugins, defaulting to `Velora/<version>`) rather than a
per-plugin string: per plugin, one could speak as another and spend its budget. `User-Agent` is a
forbidden header name, so setting it in `createFetchExternal` would be dead code in every browser
*and* in Electron's renderer; instead `electron/pluginUserAgent.ts` rewrites the header in main,
scoped to the hosts the enabled plugins declared (`network:<host>`), fed by
`startPluginUserAgentSync()` and torn down on logout. A bare `network:*` is deliberately not a scope,
on both sides: it is a legal grant but as a rewrite scope it is every http(s) request the app makes,
so one plugin asking for the open internet would put a user-typed line that may carry a contact
address on the backend, the icon CDN and the update feed. On web the browser's own User-Agent is what
the service sees and nothing can change that. `useUserAgent()` hands the string to a plugin that
makes the request somewhere the rule does not apply (its own server half, a companion), gated on
having declared any host at all and crossing the frame as a handshake constant. Sanitized to
printable ASCII on both sides of the IPC: it becomes a real header, so a newline in it is injection.

## 21. Context Menus
- **The jar row goes with its tab, and a long menu scrolls (2026-09-12).** The jar's sidebar tab is off by default, so the **Put in jar** row and the multi-select bar's stash button were a one-way trip for anyone who never turned it on: tracks went in and there was no panel to see them in. Both now read `sidebar.tabs`, which supersedes the always-on row described in §5. Separately, `.dropdownPanel` had `overflow: hidden auto` and no height cap, so a tall menu never scrolled, it just ran off the bottom of the screen (`positionAtPoint` clamps `top` to the edge margin and the rest is simply gone). One `max-height: calc(100dvh - var(--gap-lg))` fixes both halves at once: the placement effect measures `offsetHeight`, so capping the panel is also what makes it fit. Submenus inherit it; `.dropdownSubmenu--surface` keeps its own tighter 60dvh cap.

- **Track "Info" entry + shared `TrackInfo` (2026-08-31).** The track menu could edit a track's tags but never just show them, and the only read-only surface was the sidebar Info tab, locked to the playing song. The tab's body was lifted into a `TrackInfo` primitive (cover, artist/album links, duration, the Audio/Catalog/Analysis groups, comment) and both surfaces now compose it: the sidebar passes the playing track, the new store-driven `TrackInfoModal` (mounted once in `mainPage`, twin of `EditTrackModal`, focus-trapped, Escape/back/outside-click dismiss, and it closes itself when a link inside navigates) passes whichever track the menu was opened on. Three fields the tab never showed came along: rating, date added, mood tags. New in both: a **Playlists** chip row answering "which playlists is this song in", Favorites included as the pseudo-playlist it already is at `/playlist/favorites`, each chip navigating there. No provider answers that in one call, so `utils/useTrackPlaylists.ts` walks the user's playlists 4 at a time, prefers a detail the library already cached, and keeps a module-level id-set cache that a `useLibrary` subscription drops whenever `playlists`/`details` change, so switching songs with the tab open does not refetch the library. New keys `contextMenu.track.info` + `main.sidebar.info.{groupPlaylists,noPlaylists,moodTags,rating,addedAt,close}` in all 9 locales.

Album entry appears when the provider gave an `albumId` (absent on local rows); the artist entry always resolves, an artist with an id goes to `/artist/:id`, one without searches for the name, and a track credited to several artists gets a submenu. Two seams came out of it: `src/utils/navigation.ts` (module-level `setAppNavigator`/`navigateTo`, registered by `mainPage` while the authed shell is mounted, dismissing BigMusic first) so non-component code can navigate without threading a `navigate` through all 9 menu call sites, and `src/utils/artistSegments.ts` (`toArtistSegments`/`artistSegmentPath`, lifted out of `ArtistLinks`) so the comma-splitting rule for collapsed multi-artist names lives in one place.

- **`Dropdown` primitive** (`src/assets/components/primitives/dropdown/dropdown.tsx` + `.css`): flat items + dividers + section labels + recursive flyout submenus (hover-opens on desktop, tap-toggles on touch, sibling submenus switch instantly via shared per-group `activeId` state, no race against the hover-close delay). Viewport-clamped positioning with edge-flip. Each open panel (root + every submenu, at any depth) is portaled **independently** to `document.body`, never nested inside the panel that opened it, so the shared `.uiContentContainer` surface's `overflow:hidden`/`contain:paint` can never clip a flyout that renders outside its own box. Closes on Escape or an outside `pointerdown` (matched via `.closest(".dropdownPanel")` against every currently-open panel, regardless of which one), deliberately not a full-screen blocking backdrop, so right-clicking a different trigger while a menu is open opens the new one immediately instead of being swallowed. No animation (removed by design, twice, per explicit direction). Below 480px width the root panel becomes a full-width bottom sheet with a dimmed/blurred backdrop and a "back" row for entering/leaving a submenu, a basic CSS-only fallback, not the future shared `Sheet`/MF1 primitive (§18 tracks that migration).

One instance + one `<Dropdown>` mount per *view* (never per row/card, since several call sites are virtualized lists/grids).

## 23. Licensing / Activation Codes

- **License server (2026-07-10).** `../velora-license-server` (Fastify + TypeScript + Node's built-in `node:sqlite`, needs Node ≥ 22.13). One public idempotent endpoint `POST /api/activate` `{ code, deviceId }` → `200 {ok:true}` / `404 INVALID_CODE` / `403 REVOKED|DEVICE_LIMIT`; rate-limited 30/min/IP, CORS open (no credentials). Normal codes allow **4 devices**; `--unlimited` codes (dev) have no limit. Codes are 20 chars from a 32-char alphabet (`XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX`, input normalization ignores dashes/case). **CLI-only management** (`npm run codes -- create|list|devices|revoke|unrevoke|free|delete`), no admin endpoints. `npm run check` asserts the full activation matrix in-memory. Dockerfile + compose included (DB volume at `./data`). `TRUST_PROXY` is a hop count (`1` in compose) so rate limiting can't be dodged via a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For`.
- **Frontend gate (2026-07-10).** `useLicense` store (`src/store/license.ts`, localStorage `velora-license`: code, random `deviceId` UUID, valid) + `ActivationPage` (`src/screens/pages/activationPage/`, styled like login, i18n `activation.*` in all 6 locales). `app.tsx` renders `ActivationPage` instead of the router until licensed; re-validates once per launch. Gate is active in dev too, pointed at `http://localhost:8790` (prod: `https://license.uplift-beyond.de`); activate once against a locally running license server and localStorage keeps it.
- **Offline grace window (2026-07-19).** An explicit recognized rejection (`INVALID_CODE`/`REVOKED`/`DEVICE_LIMIT`/`TRIAL_EXPIRED`) clears the activation immediately; network failure or unknown responses (e.g. a proxy 502 or rate-limit reply) keep the device working only while the last successful check (`lastOkAt`, persisted on every successful activate/validate) is under 30 days old, past that (or with no successful check ever, i.e. forged storage) it soft-locks with `GRACE_EXPIRED`, keeping the token so one online validate reactivates without re-entering the code. Trial expiry and the grace window are measured against `max(Date.now(), maxSeenNow)` (persisted high-water mark), so rolling the clock back doesn't stretch them.
- **Trial license codes, 2026-07-15.** 7-day trial codes across license server + frontend. Server (`../velora-license-server`): `codes.trial` + `codes.trial_started_at` columns (+ migrations), `TRIAL_DAYS = 7`, clock pinned to the code's **first activation by any device** (`COALESCE` guard; new devices never restart it); expired trials return `403 { reason: "TRIAL_EXPIRED" }` from both `/api/activate` and `/api/validate`, live ones include `trialExpiresAt` (ISO) in the success body; CLI `create --trial`, `list` shows trial state (not started / expires X / TRIAL EXPIRED); `npm run check` covers the matrix (pinned expiry shared across devices, backdated expiry locks existing + new devices, non-trial responses carry no expiry key). Also added CLI `delete <code>` (permanent remove; `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` so the devices `ON DELETE CASCADE` actually fires). Frontend: `useLicense` persists `trialExpiresAt` (non-null = trial, refreshed on every validate), `TRIAL_EXPIRED` added to both known-reason lists so it **hard-locks** back to `ActivationPage` (message via `activation.trialExpired`), plus a local expiry check in `revalidate()` so going offline can't ride out an expired trial; nav shows a "Test Version" pill in the nav footer while a trial is active (`NavTrialBadge`, a `NavPill` like the update/desktop prompts: hourglass icon + days-left subtitle, click opens `GET_LICENSE_URL`). New i18n keys (`nav.testVersion`, `nav.trialDaysLeft_one/_other`, `activation.trialExpired`) in all 6 locales.
