## 24. Onboarding

- **First-run flow, 2026-07-19.** A skippable wizard, then a four-stop coach-mark tour, then a full-screen stage, mounted as a store-driven singleton (`<Onboarding />` in `mainPage.tsx`, which only renders behind `RequireAuth`, so mounting *is* the first-login trigger). Persisted per install via `useSettings.onboardingCompleted`, set on finish **and** on skip so it never re-prompts; replayable from Settings → Appearance → Interface. Wizard = 4 cards (welcome · theme · density + text scale · animation speed + blur) reusing `SettingsSwitcher` and `useThemeOptions`, each writing straight through the normal setter so there is nothing to commit or roll back. The backdrop blurs the app (`blur(calc(var(--surface-blur) * 1.5))`, forced to a heavier flat scrim under `data-reduce-transparency`), so the card carries the demonstration instead of the app behind it: a small `.uiContentContainer` specimen (accent cover square + rem-sized text bars) re-themes, re-densifies and re-scales with the live setting without a single branch. Progress is a seek-bar rail rather than dots, and Skip is the only dismiss control (Escape/back button still work). The mark card carries no shadow, the ring around the cutout is what reads as elevation. Dev affordances live in the `DevToolsPanel`'s Onboarding row (Rerun setup / Tour only / Unsee), not as on-screen chrome. Tour = scrim with the target's rect punched out (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px accent, 0 0 0 9999px scrim`, ring outside the box model, so the hole never shifts), target inert behind a full-screen click catcher, card positioned below-then-flip-above with `dropdown.tsx`'s `EDGE_MARGIN`/`clamp` math and its measure-then-`visibility:hidden` two-pass, re-measured on `resize`/`scroll` (which dropdown doesn't do). Stops anchor to `data-tour` attributes, resolved once at tour start; a missing target drops that stop and the count adjusts. Stops are settings · command palette · sidebar · BigMusic. The docked sidebar stays mounted when hidden (it slides off-screen via `sidebar--hidden-*`), so drop-if-missing can't save that stop, it would point off-screen: the tour opens the panel on mount and restores the previous value on unmount, reading it through `getState()` so flipping it doesn't re-run the effect and undo itself. On mobile the docked panel isn't rendered at all (it's a Sheet opened from inside BigMusic), so there the stop does drop. **The last stop hands off to a third phase instead of ending:** `startStage()` opens BigMusic over an empty library (`ctx.track` stays null, which every mode already handles by type; only `coverBlobUrl` is forced to `COVER_PLACEHOLDER`) and floats a low-anchored card asking for the BigMusic mode and the background style, the two most visual settings in the app, chosen where they're actually visible rather than as two more rows in a modal. The card is draggable by a grab bar (handle-only via `useDragControls`, so it never competes with the switcher buttons for the pointer) inside an invisible full-screen bounds element, since it sits on top of the very thing it's asking about. Centering uses auto margins, never `translateX(-50%)`: motion writes an inline transform for both the entry animation and the drag, which would wipe it. Done routes to `/home` via `navigateTo()`, which drops the overlay on the way. Desktop/mobile targets are declared per stop (nav button vs tab bar, topbar search vs search tab, `.playerTrackInfo` vs `.miniPlayer`); the player anchor is the **region**, not `.playerCoverClickable`, which isn't rendered when nothing is playing i.e. on a real first run. Palette copy interpolates the live keybind, never a hardcoded Ctrl+K.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/onboarding/*`, `src/store/onboarding.ts`, `src/settings.tsx`, `mainPage.tsx`, `nav.tsx`, `MobileTabBar.tsx`, `topbar.tsx`, `player.tsx`, `settingsView.tsx`, all locales

## 25. Games & Easter Eggs

- **"Guess It", 2026-08-30.** A hidden guessing game: name the song from a clip that starts at 0.1s and opens to 0.5s, 3s and 10s. Reached only by typing `guess` in the command palette (a `ValueCommand` verb beside `confetti`, so nothing lists it), never from nav. One anchor per round, drawn between 20% and 70% of the track and pulled back far enough that the 10s window still fits, so every reveal contains the one before it. Skipping and guessing wrong cost the same thing, the next clip; running out is the loss. The reveal starts the answer playing and offers favorite, add-to-playlist, play/pause and another round.
  - **The clip is gated on the audio clock, not a timer.** `audioEngine` grew a third `<audio>` slot, created on first use and routed straight into the master gain, so the two playback slots and their crossfade are untouched while the clip still follows the app volume, the mono switch and the output device (and inherits the CORS mode and `buildStreamUrl`'s quality params). Not the iOS unlock: `unlockMediaElements` blesses the two slots at the first gesture, before this element exists, so on iOS Safari the first clip rides the transient activation of the click that asked for it. Creating the slot in `initGraph` is what would bless it, at the cost of an element and a node in every session. `playPreview` schedules `gain` at `ctx.currentTime + lookahead` and back down `seconds` later with a proportional ramp on each edge; a `setTimeout` cannot hold a tenth of a second and a hard gate on one that short is a click. `preparePreview` loads and parks the element on the anchor **before** the round starts, because a window landing on unbuffered audio plays silence and reads as a broken game. An epoch counter retires a window that was cut short so it can't pause the clip that replaced it.
  - **`getTracks`'s cursor is a row id, not an offset** (see the live trap in `goals.md`). The first picker drew random offsets and returned the same song every round. `utils/randomTrack.ts` now proves the cursor's meaning before inventing one, comparing a page's `nextCursor` against its own last row's id, then draws over the id space and samples within the returned page to absorb the gaps deleted rows leave. Providers that declare `randomSongs` (Subsonic, Jellyfin, local) still just ask the server.
  - Overlay is a BigMusic-band takeover, transparent over the shared `background_overlay` (lifted by `mainPage` for the game the same way it is for BigMusic) with `<Topbar overlay />` re-mounted, so the themed background and the Electron titlebar both survive. The card is built around one square slot: during the round it holds the seconds you are allowed as display type, and that numeral **is** the play button; on the reveal the artwork lands in the same box, so the number resolves into the thing itself. Escalation is the numeral growing (a per-stage `transform: scale`, never a size, so it neither reflows the card nor animates per frame, live traps), and the four windows sit above it as an unlabelled fuse of four ticks that survives the reveal as the score. Audible-right-now is a colour swap on the numeral, not a pulse: the shortest clip is a tenth of a second and any cycle would read as a glitch. A win fires the app's existing one-shot `useConfetti` burst, which already sits at `--z-overlay` (above this overlay's band) and already skips itself under reduce-motion. `VolumeControl` was extracted out of `player.tsx` into `primitives/volumeControl/` so the game uses the same control rather than a copy.
  - **Cover blur assist, 2026-08-30.** One help, on by default. It is toggled from the game's own header, since a Settings row would list the easter egg, and persisted on its own key, `velora-guess-game`, rather than in `useSettings`, so it never travels through user-data export. On, the answer's artwork sits under the numeral behind a scrim at a heavy blur and clears one step per opened window, off the same `data-stage` attribute the numeral's growth uses; the blur is derived from `--guess-slot`, so it reads the same on the phone card. It steps on input and never on a clock, and the artwork is only fetched while the assist is on.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/guessGame/*`, `src/store/guessGame.ts`, `src/utils/randomTrack.ts`, `src/services/audio/audioEngine.ts`, `src/assets/components/primitives/volumeControl/*`, `src/utils/valueCommand.ts`, `commandPalette.tsx`, `mainPage.tsx`, `player.tsx`, all locales
- **"Puzzle It", 2026-08-31.** A hidden puzzle on the cover of whatever is playing, in two modes and four sizes (3x3 easy, 4x4 normal, 6x6 hard, 10x10 very hard). Reached only by typing `puzzle` (or `slide`) in the command palette, the same `ValueCommand` shelf `confetti` and `guess` sit on, so nothing lists it; opening either game closes the other, since both are takeovers in the same band. Self-contained: no fetch of its own, no library call, no backend. The artwork is locked at the deal, so a track change mid-solve cannot swap the picture under a half-built board, and a deal made while nothing is playing simply picks up the first cover that arrives.
  - **Slide**, one hole and n*n-1 tiles. A tap or a drag on any tile sharing the hole's row or column takes the whole run with it, which is the only thing that makes 10x10 playable with a thumb. The drag is pointer-driven end to end (a tap is just a drag with no travel in it): the run follows the finger up to the one cell a slide is worth and commits past half of that, and the live movement is written to a CSS var on the board, so tracking a hundred tiles costs no render, only crossing the tap slop does. Arrow keys drive it too, from the board itself.
  - **Assemble**, an empty grid and a tray. Drag a piece in, or tap it and then tap where it goes; drag a placed piece back off the board (or tap the tray) to take it out again. Any empty cell accepts any piece: a wrong one is not refused, it just looks wrong, which is the whole feedback loop of a jigsaw. The tray is whatever is not on the board in the deal's fixed order, so a lifted piece reappears exactly where it sat in the pile. The piece under the finger is one fixed element portalled to the body (a card transform would otherwise claim a fixed child) whose position is a pair of CSS vars, and the drop target is computed from the board's own box rather than by hit-testing what is under the pointer, which is the ghost.
  - **Shuffled by walking the hole, never by permuting the array**: half of all permutations of a sliding puzzle are unsolvable and a walk can only reach the solvable half. The walk refuses to step straight back where it came from (or it spends most of its steps undoing itself) and re-deals if it lands back on solved, which 3x3 does often enough to matter. The tray's order is a real Fisher-Yates, not a random-sign comparator, which on a 100 piece pile is a visible bias. Both, plus the run a tap moves (shared by the slide and its drag, so the gesture and the move can never disagree), are pure in `utils/coverPuzzle.ts` and covered by `tests/utils/coverPuzzle.test.ts`.
  - A piece's face is an `<img class="img_cover">` of the whole cover at the board's size, clipped to a one-cell box: the same object-fit the player's cover uses, so a cover that is not square is cropped to the square the board is rather than squashed into it. Seams are outlines, not inset shadows, because only an outline is painted after an element's children. Slide places its tiles by transform (one animated property, no reflow); assemble lays its cells out as a grid, since nothing there moves between cells on its own. Boards are remounted per deal by a key, so neither has to know how to reset itself. A solve fires the shared one-shot `useConfetti` burst, which already sits above this band and already skips itself under reduce-motion.
  - Records are per mode and size (a placement and a slide are not the same unit), and the two assists live in the game's own header rather than in Settings, which would list the easter egg: piece numbers (persisted) and a peek at the whole cover (per glance, dismissed by tapping it). All of it is on `velora-cover-puzzle`, not in `useSettings`, so none of it travels through user-data export.
  - \u21b3 files: `src/assets/components/ui/coverPuzzle/*`, `src/store/coverPuzzle.ts`, `src/utils/coverPuzzle.ts`, `tests/utils/coverPuzzle.test.ts`, `src/utils/valueCommand.ts`, `commandPalette.tsx`, `navigation.ts`, `mainPage.tsx`, all locales

- **The games stopped being easter eggs, 2026-09-01.** Both were reached only by knowing a magic word, which is a feature nobody finds. They are listed features now, and the shelf they sit on is a registry, so a third game is additive rather than another pair of edits in five files.
  - **One registry, one store, one shell.** `GAME_REGISTRY` (`ui/games/gameTypes.ts`) is the `MODE_REGISTRY` shape: name key, description key, icon, component, and an optional `useBest` for the record line. `store/games.ts` holds `active: GameId | "picker" | null`, so the per-game `open` booleans are gone and `closeOverlays()` no longer grows by one call per game. `GameOverlay` (`ui/games/gameOverlay.tsx`) is the takeover both games were already spelling out identically: the BigMusic band, the transparent root over the lifted background, the re-mounted `<Topbar overlay />`, the notch spring on the card, Escape and `useBackButtonDismiss`. `.gameOverlay` / `.gameCard` in `games.css` own the two rule blocks that were byte-identical in `guessGame.css` and `coverPuzzle.css`, including the `!important` trio that guards the card against `.uiContentContainer`'s own padding and radius, which now has nothing left to tie with.
  - **A launcher you pick from.** `<Games />` mounts once in `mainPage` and renders either the picker or the active game. The picker is a tile per registry entry (icon, name, one line of description, and its record where it has one) on the list-row grammar: neutral at rest, translucent accent fill with an accent line on hover, `auto-fit` columns so it is one column on a phone. A tile calls its own game's `useBest`, so the picker knows nothing about a puzzle or a clip.
  - **Palette rows, not hidden verbs.** `guess` and `puzzle` are out of `valueCommand.ts` (`confetti` stays, it is not a game). "Games 🎮" is always in the actions list; the per-game `Game: <name>` rows join the theme/mode/language switches that appear once you type, so typing `game guess` reaches the game the way `Export: M3U` reaches an export. Typing `guess` still lands on it too, since the row's own title fuzzy-matches.
  - **Records became data worth keeping.** Fewest-moves records moved out of the puzzle's own key into one flat `records` map on the games store, keyed `"<game>:<board>"` and lower-is-better (`recordLowest`, named so a future score game cannot silently inherit the wrong comparator). That is one shape for the export path to know, so the new `games` scope in user-data export/import carries every game's records forever: sanitized on the way in (a whole non-negative count in range, key length and entry count bounded, since the file is untrusted) and **merged, not overwritten**, taking the lower of the two, so importing a profile can only improve what is already on the device. The puzzle's old `best` map is folded in once at boot and self-heals. File version 3; every field stays optional, so a v1/v2 file still reads.
  - The assists stayed in each game's header. The reason they were there (a Settings row would have listed the easter egg) is gone, but the better reason stands: they are per-round controls next to the board they change, not a rail row.
  - ↳ files: `src/assets/components/ui/games/*`, `src/store/games.ts`, `src/store/coverPuzzle.ts`, `src/store/guessGame.ts`, `ui/guessGame/*`, `ui/coverPuzzle/*`, `utils/valueCommand.ts`, `utils/navigation.ts`, `utils/userDataScopes.ts`, `utils/userDataExport.ts`, `commandPalette.tsx`, `mainPage.tsx`, `tests/utils/gameRecords.test.ts`, all locales
  - ↳ open: the idea backlog for more games is `docs/goalsDetails/games.md` (§25 in `goals.md`)

- **"Unheard", 2026-09-02.** The first game that is not a quiz: it deals songs out of your own library that you have never picked, ten seconds at a time, and you keep or pass. Keeps land in one "Unheard" playlist that outlives the session (found by name, made on the first keep and never before it), so a session ends with something you can play. Keeping also steers the deal, the kept track's neighbourhood goes to the front of the buffer, so a session walks somewhere instead of being shuffle with extra steps.
  - **There is no per-track play count anywhere in `IMusicProvider`**, which is why `SMART_FIELDS` has no `playCount` field, so "never played" is not queryable and the game never claims it. Cold is approximated in `utils/unheardDeal.ts`: not a favourite, not in any playlist, added more than 30 days ago, and absent from `listeningStats.topTracks` where that capability exists. A provider that does not report `addedAt` cannot fail the age rule rather than failing every track. Once nothing cold is left the dealer relaxes to anything unjudged, instead of telling a small library it has nothing to offer.
  - **One walk, not a request per candidate.** `useTrackPlaylists`'s module-level membership cache grew `loadPlaylistedTrackIds()`, with the hook's per-playlist fetch extracted so both go through one `trackIdsIn`, which makes membership a Set lookup for the rest of the session. `randomTrack.ts` grew `randomTrackPool()` and `pickRandomTrack` samples it, so one page fetch feeds several cards instead of one.
  - **The steer works on every provider.** Velora resolves smart radio server-side and throws UNSUPPORTED for `getSimilarSongs`, so the neighbourhood is similar songs where the `smartRadio` capability is on and the seed's artist otherwise (`getTracksByArtist`, falling back to a search on the artist name). A provider with `createPlaylist` off keeps by favouriting instead, so a keep always lands somewhere.
  - **Two firsts for the games store.** Tracks kept is the first most-is-better record, so `recordHighest` sits beside `recordLowest` and `isHighestRecord` names the one key that counts up; import calls the store's own `mergeRecords` now, which folds each key in its own direction, rather than the export path spelling "lower wins" for every game forever. The dealt-track list is the first game state that is not a number: `seen` is a capped (500) list on the same store, persisted, and it rides the same `games` export scope, sanitized on the way in like the records because the file is untrusted.
  - **A third verdict, delete.** Not for me and not for the library either: a small destructive button beside pass and keep, behind the same gate the track menu's delete uses (the `deleteTrack` capability plus admin, so it is simply absent everywhere else) and behind the same `confirmAction` pill, because nothing about it is undoable. The next card is dealt as the delete goes out, so a dig does not stall on a server round trip.
  - The card is the shared `GameOverlay` takeover around one square slot: a blurred cover that is also the replay button, the name withheld until the header's reveal toggle says otherwise (persisted on `velora-unheard`, since turning the blindfold off is a decision about the game and not about the song on screen), `VolumeControl` for the clip, and two verdict buttons of equal weight. The clip is the preview slot the guessing game already added; `pickClipAnchor` moved out of `guessGame.tsx` into `utils/clipAnchor.ts` so both draw the anchor the same way.
  - ↳ files: `ui/unheard/*`, `store/unheard.ts`, `store/games.ts`, `utils/unheardDeal.ts`, `utils/clipAnchor.ts`, `utils/randomTrack.ts`, `utils/useTrackPlaylists.ts`, `utils/userDataExport.ts`, `utils/userDataScopes.ts`, `ui/games/gameTypes.ts`, `ui/guessGame/guessGame.tsx`, `tests/utils/unheardDeal.test.ts`, `tests/utils/gameRecords.test.ts`, all locales

A round "Resume auto-scroll" chip in the bottom-right opens into its label on hover. In the mobile sheet the lyrics view now takes the sheet's visible height (the panel publishes `--sheet-hidden` per rest), so the lyrics box is the scroller in every style (before, only focus was) and chat's newest bubble stays on screen at the low rest.

Replaces the planned font size / alignment / line-count knobs: a few drastic looks over many small sliders. BigMusic keeps its own lyric column.

## 29. Pets & Seasonal Decorations

- **Seasonal decorations + the October ghost, 2026-10-07.** `seasonalDecorations` (Interface, on, desktop) dresses the app for the season in `utils/seasons.ts` (Halloween = all of October, re-checked at local midnight). The first decoration is a pet: a hand-drawn ghost that floats in a lane just outside the player bar (below it when the bar is on top), drifting left and right at random, lingering now and then, turning to face where it goes; a click makes it say "Boo!" with little hands out. It can be dragged anywhere outside the bar (arms flailing) and drifts back down to its lane when dropped.
  - Pets are a registry (`PET_REGISTRY`, `float` / `walk`, optional `season`), so a new pet is one union member, one entry and one SVG. All motion is transforms on their own layers, outside the bar's blurred surface, and drawn at 30fps (`utils/useFrameCap.ts` pauses every animation in the lane and steps it by hand), since each frame re-blurs the panels under the pet; hidden while BigMusic is open, paused with the window, still under reduce-motion. Dev: Season override + Poke.
  - ↳ files: `ui/pets/` (`PetLayer.tsx`, `petTypes.ts`, `petWander.ts`, `ghost/`), `utils/seasons.ts`, `ui/player/player.tsx`, `store/devTools.ts`
- **Pets picker + the rabbit, 2026-10-07.** `pets` (Interface, desktop, off by default) is the list of pets shown, a multi-pick; the ghost is only offered and shown in October, and its old `seasonalDecorations` toggle is retired (`migratePets`, off keeps the ghost away). `rabbitColor` picks the fur from five swatches. The rabbit walks the bar edge (under a top bar it hangs upside down from the bar's underside): it hops on its trips, idles with a nose wiggle, ear twitches and the odd sit-up, jumps up with floating hearts when clicked (no speech bubble, `sayKey` is optional), dangles and paddles when held, and lands with a squash when dropped (walkers fall faster than the floating ghost).
  - ↳ files: `ui/pets/rabbit/`, `ui/pets/PetLayer.tsx` (the filter), `ui/pets/pets.css` (walker flip + landing), `src/settings.tsx`
